links.title: Bitcoin Will Cause Bond Prices To Go Down
links.body: ![BoomerRugpullBTC.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmRHCgWNUqpKxFr5Wah9R3JyjXsQBCN48Ctw2jLsZhmcVY/BoomerRugpullBTC.png) This is a complex topic. We will be discussing several layers of the financial industry that are all changing, and then disappearing. Bitcoin, and the like will destroy bonds, and then replace bonds, and then bitcoin will no longer be bonds, and bonds will disappear. It all comes down to, where does money come from? And this is not an easy question, nor is there an easy answer. We can look at the Fed, at fractional reserve lending. We must also look at the thought construct of the men in 1st world countries. But, in this post, we will try to comprehend bonds, and why they are important to the retiring boomers, and why they are dying, and how to save the boomers' retirement.

bonds are a place to park currency. Some place to put currency, while you are waiting for the next opportunity. But the rest of the investors are there for continuous income. For doing things like funding retirement. And thus, most retirees move their investment money heavily into bonds when they retire. And thus, the group that needs bonds to have a high yield the most is the boomers. To bad, that right now, the bonds are paying such low interest rates. Just when the retirement accounts need to make up for the lack of earnings. (difference between what they promised and what got delivered) There are stocks that pay out a very steady dividend each year, but even with these, payouts can change drastically. Retirees need more even payouts, and so, the govern-cement bond has become the go to. But, the thing that allowed govern-cement bonds to exist, is now almost gone.

> ## The life and death of govern-cement bonds Govern-cement bonds shouldn't exist; can't exist. There are two ways to pay the interest on bonds. 1. create money out of thin air. 2. charge (collect money from) someone outside of your system Early in America's life, they charged imports a fee to be allowed into the country. And after they dropped the gold standard, (with WWII) they could print money. (If you have real money, like, say, gold, when you charge interest/pay interest, it is like taking a bite out of your money supply. So, literally, over time, paying interest on bonds will leave no money in the system, and if a foreign entity bought the bond, that money doesn't reenter the system at all, making the gold disappear faster.) So, as we create a new monetary system (the Dollar is dying, and the Yuan, and the Euro…), if it is a sound money system, then you cannot have interest paying bonds. Especially if we choose bitcoin. (We will see the debt interest owed exceed 21 million and EVERYONE will know that it can never be repaid.) Bonds will not exist in the future with sound money.

> ## The dual problem of bonds 1. on one hand, we need bond interest rates to be high so that retirees can get their monthly payments (this includes Social inSecurity). But, high interest rates means the govern-cement will have to print more money to service the debt. 2. on the other hand, if we keep interest rates low, then no one (besides the Fed) buys the bonds, and then no one gets paid. Retirement accounts NEED interest rates to be higher or they will run out of money before the retirees kick the bucket. This is why these retirement accounts are going to very high risk, hopefully high yield, investments. And retirement accounts really should not be investing in high risk.

></center>\n\nSo, the financial system is pivoting to buying highly appreciating assets.  Bitcoin, Ethereum, Ripple… to name a few, where their value is going up faster than the destruction of the fiat currencies.  The plan is to buy bitcoin, then sell off a portion as its value goes up to make payments to the \

holders. They are making a new form of continuous payment monetary vehicle. And this may save the boomers' retirement. The problem is that this is just a bandage. It will work while fiat currency is flowing into the cryptos. When things level off, or people stop accepting fiat, when we accept bitcoin as the money, the thing of value all other things are priced in, then all we can do is pay out the bitcoin payments from their stash of bitcoin. But, until then, fiat currencies will go down. And the bonds that are denominated in will go down. And the younger generations will just put their fiat into bitcoin, until they are each paid in bitcoin. And then there will be no more bonds.

>\n
All images in this post are my own original creations.

links.title: Esto sucede
links.body:
This happens

It happens that the rope on which I play at balance is about to vanish: it is held by the wind and by your fingers… your fingers, yes, among my addicted hair as I wander the Malecón. Yet, before falling, I relive through your photographs, I breathe in your gaze with hope, and I know that in those eyes I would lose myself without guilt, or let myself die in ecstasy, even while falling… because I also know, all too well, that even if I close mine you will be there, here, always. Beside the wall of these eyelids that sometimes dim their lights to soften the pain, Deliriums whisper lectures. Now they hold the image of a girl running barefoot with a red balloon across the cobblestones of the Plaza de la Catedral, and there are the drawings I made upon your body without touching you, your kisses and bites are already visible on my skin from imagining them so much. But the Plaza and the work, the rope and the child, the white, the black, the wink of colour… and so much… so much time scattered like the ashes of the dead do not lessen the night, and I, a mediocre photographer for a magazine equally mediocre, did not know then that I would walk upon a rope tied to nowhere. There are very few steps left now.

Sucede que la cuerda donde juego al equilibrio está a punto de desaparecer: la sostienen el viento y tus dedos... tus dedos, sí, entre mis cabellos adictos cuando camino por el Malecón. Pero, antes de caer, revivo con tus fotografías, esperanzada absorbo tu mirar y sé que en esos ojos me perdería sin culpa, o me dejaría morir en éxtasis, incluso cayendo... porque también sé, demasiado bien, que aunque cierre los míos vas a estar ahí, aquí, siempre. Junto a la pared de estos párpados que a veces apagan sus luces para atenuar el dolor dictan conferencias los delirios. Ahora retienen la imagen de una niña corriendo descalza y con un globo rojo sobre los adoquines de la Plaza de la Catedral, y están los dibujos que te hice en el cuerpo sin tocarte tus besos y mordiscos ya son visibles en mi piel de tanto imaginarlos. Pero la Plaza y la obra la cuerda y la niña el blanco, el negro el guiño de color... y tanto... tanto tiempo esparcido como las cenizas de un muerto no hacen menos la noche y yo, una mediocre fotógrafa de una revista también mediocre, no sabía entonces que caminaría sobre una cuerda atada en ninguna parte. Ya quedan muy pocos pasos.

links.title: [ENG-SPN] Peñaranda de Duero, Castile in its purest form / Peñaranda de Duero, Castilla en estado puro
links.body:
![P1080527.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/juancar347/EpGQJjkSvbXLHsiXMuYVyMqWBpwkqxyuAdRESvEqAxawCaWndYxXYvcph3qyrAymtqT.JPG)

Not only does Juan Eslava Galán recommend it as one of those thousand places to see in Spain at least once in a lifetime, but he goes even further, describing this ancient medieval town of Old Castile—which, for better or for worse, has always been present in the meticulous pages of history—as a monument in its entirety: Peñaranda de Duero.

![P1080390.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/juancar347/242Ncw458bc91TGifvgqgQstR5gZJdLbUGb5nWiN2fuQySCmicEeXV5TrdioQ5QTpTMjJ.JPG)

Located beside a castle, over whose ancient ruins time seems to particularly enjoy playing a game of cat and mouse, and also the fiefdom of the Ximénez family, who for countless generations have served as apothecaries—and who knows if their ancestors didn't also practice the noble art of alchemy in the Middle Ages—Peñaranda, which still preserves part of the imposing medieval walls that once surrounded it, is a treasure for thrill-seekers and an adventure for lovers of the Gothic style, which, from around the mid-12th century, illuminated the darkness of the Romanesque period, at least until the 16th century.

![P1080403.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/juancar347/23yTb2JPYsnqQwHpVA8xnxmsq3dYSZuSBPNPWoEj3XkpD1JGBmYzW8PnA8q8HnD31Weti.JPG)

In this style, and as a prelude to another unmissable place located just a few kilometers away, which we will see later, we find, alongside the charming Plaza Mayor, where almost all the narrow medieval streets converge and where visitors can still find many examples of ancient architecture, including the famous inns, the imposing church dedicated to Saint Anne; that is, to the Mother of Mothers par excellence, whose striking, solid, and spectacular apse is truly admirable.

![P1080398.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/juancar347/EqFtuTvgX46adDwksS8QQksqKe6ferR42LkUaMYzKEE5E1FMBVbSMxyxii6JP8AhQzH.JPG)

No sólo nos lo recomienda Juan Eslava Galán, como uno de esos mil sitios que ver en España, al menos una vez en la vida, sino, que, además, va todavía más lejos, cuando, haciendo referencia a esta arcaica villa medieval de una Vieja Castilla, que para bien o para mal, siempre ha estado presente en las meticulosas páginas de la Historia, nos la describe como un monumento en su conjunto: Peñaranda de Duero.

![P1080438.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/juancar347/243M38Z2HCkUAVWmbTi74hgRAuiyoeHqP42oZ6cDUjWPpgS5DCbeuRK4KQ7pZSWqAyJc4.JPG)

Situada a la vera de un castillo, sobre cuyos arcaicos restos el tiempo parece divertirse especialmente agregándose al juego del gato y el ratón y siendo feudo, además, de una familia, los Ximénez, que, durante incontables generaciones han servido como boticarios y quién sabe si realmente en la Edad Media sus antepasados no practicaron también el noble arte de la Alquimia, Peñaranda, que todavía conserva también parte de las imponentes murallas medievales que la circundaban, es un lujo para el buscador de emociones y una aventura para el amante de un estilo, el gótico, que, a mediados, aproximadamente del siglo XII, fue alumbrando las oscuridades del románico, cuando menos, hasta el siglo XVI.

![P1080429.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/juancar347/23sdfXwbGJBxdM2CgzURbMmLaHRh5kB7SSTV6Jdddnd7XAXBiXqndiwcKmPoruFe58Vi7.JPG)

Precisamente, de este estilo y como anticipo a otro lugar imperdible, situado a escasos kilómetros y que veremos más adelante, nos queda, junto a esa artesana Plaza Mayor a la que van a desembocar la práctica totalidad de estrechas callejuelas medievales y donde todavía el forastero se puede encontrar con no pocas arquitecturas ancestrales, incluidos los célebres mesones, la imponente iglesia dedicada a la figura de Santa Ana; es decir, a la figura de la Madre de la Madre por antonomasia, siendo digno de admirar su sorprendente, sólido y espectacular ábside.

![P1080491.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/juancar347/23u5zYvSa5vh8kGZfjoX7CMuQSyu62PH79bXzVSksnFb5uC29jr3kkSipBWrw3AdoSEg1.JPG)

links.title: Ultimate Wrestling Season 3 - Ch.12: Empire's End: PART - 7
links.body:
![000.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmWzmvB2baP6Py67JDPbyzm9PZnkvfE3oTcWmWpxB1QMch/000.png)

The arena dimmed until the crowd became a living shadow, a low roar trapped under the ceiling like thunder refusing to break. In the center of it all, the ring sat transformed from a sacred square into something uglier, something honest, its familiar geometry violated by intent, the boundaries no longer welcoming but warning. The Death Match Championship belt rested on its pedestal like a relic from a darker religion, gold and black and bone-faced menace, and beside it the officials hovered with the careful posture of people standing too close to an animal that might lunge.

Takeshi Suzuki’s voice cut in first, calm but sharpened at the edges, as if even he didn’t want to give the night too much emotion to feed on.

**Takeshi Suzuki:** Well you Americans are in for a treat. The Japanese Death Match isn’t like the hardcore garbage wrestling you love. 

Yasuhiro Fujimoto sounded less reverent and more grimly satisfied, like a man watching a storm arrive exactly on schedule.

**Yasuhiro Fujimoto:** In Japan, we respect fighting spirit. But this… this is the kind of match that tests if your spirit is real, or just something you say when the cameras are on. 

**Chris Rodgers:** This horse shit shouldn’t even be legal! How is this even wrestling? You people in the far east are SICK!

**Takeshi Suzuki:** Hey! I we don’t come to your country and piss on your traditions! Have some respect Rodger-san!

At ringside, Kazuo Nakamura checked the ring one last time with the methodical precision of a veteran who’d seen too many “almost” become “too late.” Beside him, Bob Sigro stood with Ultimate Wrestling’s familiar sternness, jaw set, eyes narrowed, already hating what he knew he’d be forced to allow. They exchanged a brief nod, not agreement, but acknowledgment of shared burden. There would be no perfect control tonight, only damage management.

Then the house lights flared red for a heartbeat, and the big screen flashed a warning graphic: a stylized countdown clock, dormant for now, waiting. The crowd reacted to the sight of it with an uneasy cheer, half thrill, half superstition. The match hadn’t even begun and already it had a deadline.

Holly Hudson stepped into the spotlight with a microphone in hand, her voice poised and professional, but her eyes betrayed the smallest flicker of caution as she looked toward the ring, as if measuring how close she was to the blast radius of history.

**Holly Hudson:** Ladies and gentlemen… the following contest is scheduled for one fall… and it is for the DEATH MATCH CHAMPIONSHIP!

Kyōki grabbed Cassie by the hair and dragged her face-first toward the center, where the broken tube shards still lay. Cassie clawed at the mat, trying to brace, but Kyōki hauled her up and whipped her into the ropes.

Cassie came back and Kyōki caught her mid-run, snapping into Psychotic Break, the tornado DDT exploding into motion. Cassie’s head whipped down and her forehead clipped the canvas near the glass dust. The impact was sickening, a jolt through the ring.

Kyōki sprawled into the cover, blood still pouring down her face, dripping onto Cassie’s shoulder.

Kazuo Nakamura dropped.

ONE!

TWO!

Cassie kicked out, but it was ugly and desperate, more a convulsion than a statement. She rolled onto her side and coughed, and a streak of red sprayed from her mouth onto the mat.

**Chris Rodgers** Cassie Hurst is bleeding from the mouth. Kyōki’s bleeding from the eye. This ring is turning into a crime scene!

**Scott Slade:** This is what happens when you import Japan’s sickest habits and mix them with Mudcock’s circus.

**Yasuhiro Fujimoto:** No. This is what happens when pride gets wounded.

Kyōki wiped her face with the back of her hand and stared at the smear of blood on her fingers like she was reading a message. She turned, slid under the bottom rope, and reached beneath the ring.

The crowd leaned forward.

Kyōki dragged out a wooden board wrapped in barbed wire, thick coils stapled tight, metal shining under the lights like teeth. She shoved it into the ring and then followed it back in, still bleeding, still calm.

Cassie pushed up to her knees and saw the board. Her expression tightened. Not fear. Calculation. The kind that came from growing up around wrestlers who taught you exactly what to do when the match stopped being sport.

Cassie crawled, reaching for the bat again, finding it by feel, and hauled herself up with it as a crutch. She staggered toward Kyōki and swung.

Kyōki ducked and drove a forearm into Cassie’s ribs, then another, and another, forcing Cassie backward until her spine hit the ropes. Kyōki hooked Cassie’s arm and tried to whip her toward the barbed wire board.

Cassie planted her boots and resisted, face twisting. She yanked Kyōki forward instead and drove a knee into Kyōki’s stomach. Kyōki doubled over. Cassie grabbed her head and snapped her down with a fisherman’s neckbreaker, but she added something extra, twisting the landing so Kyōki’s shoulder and upper back skidded across the debris, glass dust and tube splinters biting into skin.

Kyōki rolled, clutching at her shoulder, blood now streaking down her neck.

Cassie didn’t cover. She wanted worse.

Cassie dragged the barbed wire board into the center and positioned it like an altar. Then she grabbed Kyōki by the wrist and tried to haul her up for a slam onto it.

Kyōki’s feet moved before her body fully rose, a sharp, almost inhuman adjustment. She hooked Cassie’s arm, pivoted, and suddenly Cassie was the one off balance, stumbling forward. Kyōki drove a short kick into Cassie’s knee, making it dip, and snapped Cassie down with a quick, brutal suplex.

Cassie landed hard, and the wind left her in a raw bark.

Kyōki stood, wobbling slightly, then pulled Cassie up and drove her toward the board again. Cassie fought, elbows flailing, but Kyōki’s grip tightened with cold intent. She lifted Cassie and turned, aiming to drop her back-first onto the barbed wire.

Cassie twisted mid-air.

She raked her nails across Kyōki’s already-open cut, smearing blood into Kyōki’s eye. Kyōki flinched for the first time all match, her head snapping aside. Cassie slipped free, landed behind her, and cracked the bat across Kyōki’s spine.

The wire caught Kyōki’s back through her gear and tore.

Kyōki stumbled forward, and Cassie hit her again, and again, each swing leaving more red on the bat, more red on the mat, more red on Kyōki’s body. Kyōki dropped to her knees, one hand on the canvas, blood dripping from her face in a steady line.

The crowd screamed her name like it could hold her upright.

KYO-KI! KYO-KI!

Cassie threw the bat aside, grabbed Kyōki from behind, and hauled her up. She looked at the barbed wire board. Then she looked at the crowd, lips split, chin slick with blood, and she screamed back at them like she wanted to fight the entire building.

Cassie ran.

She drove Kyōki forward and slammed her down onto the board with a full-body shove, forcing Kyōki’s shoulder blades and upper back into the wire.

The ring exploded with noise.

Kyōki arched, body spasming, the barbs biting and holding. Blood beaded instantly along her back, then ran in thin lines down her sides. Cassie dropped onto her for the pin, pressing her weight down like she was trying to keep Kyōki nailed there.

Bob Sigro slid in, eyes wide.

ONE!

TWO!

Kyōki kicked out, violent, her legs snapping up, knocking Cassie sideways off her. Kyōki rolled off the board, leaving behind streaks of blood and a few stubborn barbs that looked like they didn’t want to let her go.

**Scott Slade:** She kicked out off the barbed wire board! She kicked out while she was still bleeding into it!

**Chris Rodgers:** That’s not heart. That’s pathology.

**Takeshi Suzuki:** That is why they chant! That is why she is ours!

Cassie sat up, panting, hair wild, blood dripping off her chin. Her eyes widened in disbelief again, and then narrowed. She crawled toward the ropes, reached under the bottom strand, and pulled something out from beneath the ring.

A bundle of fresh fluorescent tubes. She slid them in one by one, stacking them like brittle bones, then grabbed two and turned back toward Kyōki. Kyōki was already rising, one knee first, then both feet, blood on her face, blood on her back, shoulders rolling like she was shaking off pain rather than carrying it. The cybernetic eye shimmered again under the lights, and the crowd’s noise sharpened into something almost feverish.

Cassie charged with the tubes.

Kyōki met her head-on.

Kyōki’s forearm smashed into Cassie’s throat, stopping her momentum. Then Kyōki grabbed both tubes, yanked Cassie forward, and drove her knee into Cassie’s stomach so hard Cassie folded. Kyōki snapped Cassie’s head under her arm and ran her forward, using Cassie’s own forward weight.

Cassie’s face hit the top rope, and Kyōki shoved her through it.

Cassie fell to the apron, scrambling for balance.

Kyōki followed her to the edge and, without hesitation, grabbed Cassie’s head and smashed it down onto the apron, the metal edge biting into flesh. Cassie’s forehead split. A thick ribbon of blood ran down her face immediately, bright and unignorable.

Cassie gasped, shaking, one hand slapping at her own forehead like she couldn’t believe it was open.

Kyōki grabbed one of the fluorescent tubes and raised it like a club.

Cassie lifted the barbed wire bat again, barely standing, both women drenched now, their blood mixing on the mat and apron in smeared, dark handprints.

They swung at the same time. The tube shattered across Cassie’s shoulder, exploding into glass dust and shards. The bat clipped Kyōki’s jaw, barbs scraping, tearing. Both women staggered. Both stayed up and the camera caught it: the canvas now dotted and streaked in red, ropes stained, hands slipping when they grabbed, every breath wet and loud.

**Yasuhiro Fujimoto:** This is no longer anger. This is a war.

**Scott Slade:** The whole arena feels different. Like the air is heavier. Like everybody’s waiting for someone to go too far.

**Chris Rodgers:** In this business, “too far” is the point. And they’re just getting started.

Kyōki turned back toward the ring, blood dripping off her chin. Cassie wiped her eyes, trying to clear the red. Kyōki stepped through the ropes first, and Cassie followed her in, bat dragging behind like a tail.

They stood again in the center, shaking, bleeding, staring.

Kyōki’s hands rose, fingers flexing.

Cassie lifted the bat one more time.

And this time, neither one looked like they planned to stop until the mat couldn’t hold any more of them.

Kyōki didn’t wrestle like a person trying to win. She wrestled like a person trying to leave an image behind The ring was already a wrecked shrine, lacquered with sweat and streaked with blood, glittering with the sick confetti of shattered light tubes. Every step kicked up a faint chalky haze, the phosphor dust hanging in the air like a bad omen. Cassie’s breathing came in sharp pulls through clenched teeth, her face painted with fresh red, one eye narrowing as she tried to keep Kyōki in front of her.

Kyōki’s smile widened anyway.

The Japanese crowd surged into a chant again, louder now, angrier, as if the building itself had decided it needed a hometown monster to cleanse the taste left behind by the stable belts slipping away earlier.

KYO-KI! KYO-KI! KYO-KI!

**Yasuhiro Fujimoto:** Listen. This is different now. The crowd wants a Japanese victory. They need it.

**Takeshi Suzuki:** They do not need it. They demand it. This is AAPW’s title. This is our ring. She is our fighter.

**Chris Rodgers:** Yeah, yeah, national pride and bloodlust. Pick your poison. Either way, somebody’s leaving this ring looking like a crime scene.

Cassie stumbled forward first, because hesitation in a death match wasn’t strategy, it was surrender. She threw a forearm, then a second, and then snapped a knee into Kyōki’s midsection. Kyōki doubled for a fraction of a second and Cassie pounced, yanking her into position and spiking her down with a hammerlock inverted DDT that drove Kyōki’s face into the canvas with a sick, wet thud.

Cassie sprawled into the cover fast.

Referee Kazuo Nakamura hit the mat.

ONE!

Kyōki kicked out so hard she nearly bucked Cassie off like a seizure.

Cassie didn’t even look surprised. She looked insulted.

She hauled Kyōki up by the hair and cracked a headbutt into her forehead. Then another. Kyōki’s body wavered, and for a moment the cybernetic eye looked wrong under the lights, the lens catching and reflecting the phosphor haze like a tiny dead spotlight.

Cassie whipped Kyōki toward the corner and chased, but Kyōki spun at the last second and launched into Reaver’s Claw, her knee snapping into Cassie’s jawline and the spinning backfist catching Cassie across the cheekbone. Cassie fell sideways into the ropes, hands scrambling, and Kyōki was already moving, already snarling, already too fast for a sane person in this much pain.

Kyōki hit the ropes and came back with Chaos Theory, a brutal storm of punches, elbows, and kicks that landed like a tantrum with a blueprint. Cassie ate it, staggered, tried to swing back, and Kyōki answered with a tornado DDT off the ropes, twisting Cassie down into the mat like she wanted to drill her through it.

Kyōki rolled through, hair in her face, blood on her lips.

And she covered.

ONE!

TWO!

Cassie kicked out, barely, shoulder rising like it was being dragged out of a grave. The crowd roared anyway, the chant turning ragged and hungry. Kyōki slapped the canvas, furious at the math of it, and leaned in close to Cassie’s face. Kyōki didn’t speak loud enough for the cameras.

But Cassie heard it.

Cassie’s eyes flashed, and she swung upward with a desperate elbow that caught Kyōki across the mouth. Kyōki snapped back, spit and blood spraying, and Cassie crawled toward the barbed wire bat like it was a lifeline.

The bat was there. Waiting. Cassie’s fingers closed around the handle and the crowd’s noise sharpened into panic.

**Scott Slade:** No. No, no, no. She’s got the bat again.

**Chris Rodgers:** Of course she does. In this match, “sportsmanship” is just a funny word people say before they faint.

Cassie rose, bat trembling in her hands, her body shaking from adrenaline and damage. Kyōki stood too, wiping her mouth with the back of her hand, and the cybernetic eye tracked Cassie’s movement with a cold, predatory stillness.

Cassie swung.

Kyōki ducked.

The bat whistled past Kyōki’s head and struck the top rope, barbs scraping and vibrating, and Kyōki snapped forward with a sudden kick to Cassie’s shin. Cassie’s leg buckled. Kyōki lunged, grabbing Cassie’s wrist, twisting, and then yanking Cassie forward into a knee strike that drove up into her face again.

Cassie stumbled backward.

Kyōki ripped the bat from Cassie’s hands like stealing a crown.

The Japanese crowd exploded.

Kyōki lifted it high.

KYO-KI! KYO-KI! KYO-KI!

**Takeshi Suzuki:** YES! This is what you wanted, Cassie! Now she holds your father’s gift!

Kyōki swung the bat downward. Cassie tried to raise her arms. The barbed wire bit anyway. Not like a cut. Like a hook. Cassie screamed as the wire scraped and caught across her forearm, tearing skin, and Kyōki yanked the bat back with a nasty little twist that made Cassie drop to a knee from the shock of it. Blood ran down Cassie’s wrist, thick and fast, and flecked the mat.

Kyōki’s cybernetic eye flickered once as the blood mist caught the lens. Just once. Nobody called it out. But a few fans near the front stopped chanting. They stared. Kyōki grinned wider, seeing their fear and liking it. She cracked the bat across Cassie’s back.

Cassie’s body jolted.

Kyōki tossed the bat aside like she was bored with it and dragged Cassie up by the hair, stepping through the light tube fragments as if they were petals. She planted Cassie, hooked her, and drilled her with the Redline Driver, snapping Cassie down in a piledriver that made the ring shudder.

Kyōki covered again, pressing her weight in.

ONE!

TWO!

Cassie kicked out.

The arena gasped like one organism.

Kyōki sat up slowly, hair hanging, blood dripping off her chin, and stared at Nakamura like he’d personally offended her by counting. Kyōki didn’t argue. She laughed. And that laugh had teeth.

**Scott Slade:** Cassie just survived the Redline Driver! How is she even moving?

**Chris Rodgers:** Spite. That’s how. Pure spite and dumb luck.

Kyōki rose and began to pace, eyes darting, body twitching with that manic, unhinged energy that didn’t come from confidence.

It came from need.

She pointed at the corner.

Then at the wreckage in the ring.

Then at herself.

She wanted the ending to look a certain way.

Kyōki slid outside and pulled two steel chairs in. She set them up facing each other, not neatly, but deliberately enough that the crowd understood she was building something. She grabbed a length of barbed wire and looped it over the chair backs like she was stringing a cruel instrument. Then she lifted the bat and bridged it across the chairs, barbs glinting.

A contraption.

A statement.

Kyōki climbed the turnbuckle, fast, hands gripping tight, boots crunching glass.

She stood at the top.

And she spread her arms like a saint in a nightmare.

KYO-KI! KYO-KI! KYO-KI!

**Yasuhiro Fujimoto:** She is going for something… something terrible.

**Takeshi Suzuki:** This is death match! This is what they came for!

**Scott Slade:** This is what she came for. There’s a difference, Takeshi. She’s not thinking about the title right now. She’s thinking about the picture.

Cassie dragged herself toward the ropes, trying to get up, trying to shake the ringing out of her head. Her forearm was shredded. Her back was welting. Her mouth was a red mess. She looked up and saw Kyōki poised above her, and for a split second, Cassie didn’t look angry.

She looked like someone staring up at a falling car.

Cassie rolled, desperate, turning away from the chair rig.

Kyōki’s cybernetic eye caught the lights again.

It flickered.

Once.

Twice.

The lens stuttered like it was struggling to focus through blood and phosphor haze, misreading the distance, misreading the angle. Kyōki blinked hard and her body tightened like she was fighting her own senses.

She saw Cassie in the right place.

Except Cassie wasn’t there anymore.

Kyōki launched anyway.

A half-beat early.

She committed to the landing because her mind could not accept the idea of not being perfect.

Her boots came down onto the rig instead of flesh.

The bat bucked under her weight, barbed wire snapping taut like a trap springing shut. The chair legs skidded on the canvas. Kyōki’s foot slipped on the glass dust and the barbs caught her boot, then her shin, then the side of her calf as the rig collapsed sideways.

Kyōki hit hard, twisting, and the bat whipped up into the side of her face.

A crack.

A flash.

And then, unmistakably, a sharp spit of sparks from the housing around her cybernetic eye.

The crowd’s chant died instantly.

Not into silence.

Into horror.

Kyōki screamed and clawed at her face, rolling, legs kicking wildly as if she was trying to stomp out an internal fire. The cybernetic eye stuttered again, sparks popping, tiny flashes crawling along the edge of the implant like lightning trying to escape skin.

Cassie froze for half a heartbeat, stunned by what she was seeing.

Then Cassie’s expression hardened into something ruthless.

She didn’t hesitate.

She climbed the ropes, ignoring the pain screaming through her limbs, and launched.

The Sundrop.

Cassie sprang and flipped, crashing down in a backflip senton across Kyōki’s chest and shoulder, driving  the air out of her and pinning her down while the cybernetic eye flickered and spat one more angry spark.

Nakamura slid into position.


![008.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmYaA75Hm7knQBeAw4m5Wts9YdeMkX4R7iqFzVv8RkxJiA/008.png)


ONE!

Kyōki’s body jerked, but it was wrong. Not a kickout. A spasm.

TWO!

Cassie hooked the leg tighter, forearm biting into her own torn skin, holding on like her life depended on the count.

THREE!

The bell rang, and it sounded like a verdict.

Holly Hudson rushed in with the championship, face tight with that ring-announcer professionalism that always looked slightly haunted in matches like this.

**Holly Hudson:** Here is your winner… and NEW AAPW DEATH MATCH CHAMPION… VANITY… CASSIE HURST!

The Japanese crowd erupted into furious boos, not the playful kind, not the “we’re mad because it’s fun” kind. This was personal. This was disbelief. This was a gut punch to a crowd that had needed a hometown victory, needed proof they hadn’t lost the night entirely.

**Yasuhiro Fujimoto:** No… no… this is not how this should end.

**Takeshi Suzuki:** This is disgusting! This is robbery by accident! By malfunction!

**Scott Slade:** It’s not robbery. It’s consequence. Kyōki built a death trap and jumped into it.

**Chris Rodgers:** She got outsmarted by her own insanity. That’s the story.

Cassie took the belt with both hands. It looked heavy in a way gold shouldn’t. She raised it anyway, breathing hard, blood dripping off her chin, eyes locked forward as the boos poured down on her.

Behind her, officials swarmed Kyōki.

Then EMTs.

A stretcher rolled down the ramp, wheels rattling over the metal grate, and the atmosphere shifted from spectacle to emergency. The medics knelt, talking fast, hands careful around Kyōki’s head. One of them shone a light near her face and the cybernetic eye answered with a jittering flicker, a weak spark that made the skin around it twitch.

The crowd didn’t chant now.

They hissed.

Horrified. Furious. Betrayed.

Kyōki’s fingers clawed at the mat as they lifted her, leaving a smeared handprint behind. When they strapped her down, her body jerked again, and the implant sparked faintly, sending a visible shudder through her jaw and neck like her nervous system had become a live wire.

**Takeshi Suzuki:** Look at her! LOOK! This is not normal! This is not human!

**Yasuhiro Fujimoto:** The fans… they are not only angry at Cassie. They are angry at the truth they are beginning to see.

Cassie stood in the corner, belt raised, soaking in the hate because she didn’t have the luxury of flinching. Not tonight. Not after what it took to survive Kyōki. The stretcher rolled up the ramp, Kyōki’s cybernetic eye flickering under the lights like a dying signal, the medics moving fast.

And the Japanese fans, for the first time tonight, didn’t feel entertained.

They felt robbed.

They felt scared.

They felt like the home monster had been dragged out of the temple and revealed as something else entirely.

Cassie didn’t celebrate like a hero.

She didn’t even celebrate like a villain.

She stood in the corner with the AAPW Death Match Championship hanging from her hands, knuckles white around the leather, chest heaving as if her ribs were still trying to remember how to breathe. The boos rained down on her from every direction, not scattered heat, but a unified, wounded roar. Japanese fans slapped the guardrail, screamed into the lights, pointed up the ramp like the whole ending was a personal insult.


![Final.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmTYxhVvqKdAjF8zkBQGpUfnCx9Kto2pKMMo4AELYRRA4p/Final.png)


Cassie just stared.

Up the aisle, the EMTs moved with grim precision, Kyōki strapped down, hair matted, blood streaked into the padding beneath her head. The cybernetic eye still stuttered with that sick little flicker, the occasional spark catching the camera like a dying star refusing to go out. Each time it jumped, Kyōki’s jaw twitched, and the crowd winced, furious and horrified all at once.

Holly Hudson hovered near the ropes, belt presentation already done, her expression carefully neutral but her eyes tracking the stretcher like she couldn’t fully look away. Referee Nakamura stayed close too, one hand raised as he kept medics and officials spaced, the other wiping at a smear of blood on his forearm that didn’t belong to him.

Cassie’s throat worked. She swallowed hard.

The bat lay in the ring wreckage, barbed wire still gleaming under the lights like a relic from another era. Cassie looked down at it, and for the first time since the bell, her face shifted. Not fear. Not pride.

Recognition.

Like she finally saw what she’d been fighting in, what she’d been willing to become.

**Scott Slade:** …That’s not a celebration face.

**Chris Rodgers:** No. That’s a I-got-out-alive face.

Cassie stepped to the ropes, slow, careful. Her boots crunched glass and light-tube dust. She didn’t pose. She didn’t throw the belt up. She didn’t soak in the moment.

She just watched Kyōki disappear.

The stretcher reached the top of the ramp. One of the medics adjusted the strap near Kyōki’s shoulder and the implant sparked again, sharper this time, and the whole arena recoiled. A fresh wave of boos rolled down like thunder.

**Takeshi Suzuki:** This is shameful! This is tragedy! This is not wrestling!

**Yasuhiro Fujimoto:** Kyōki Piero… she wanted the perfect ending. And it… destroyed her.

Cassie’s fingers tightened around the championship. She pulled it close to her chest, not like a trophy, but like something heavy you carry home after a night you’ll never brag about. Her eyes stayed locked on the ramp until Kyōki was gone, until the curtain swallowed the stretcher and the last flicker of that sparking eye vanished from sight.

Only then did Cassie exhale.

Only then did she turn back toward the ring.

The boos didn’t stop. They might never stop. But Cassie didn’t flinch from them. She lifted the title once, not high, not triumphant, just enough to show she understood what it cost. Her mouth opened like she might say something, like she might explain herself, like she might even apologize.

She didn’t.

She simply raised her free hand and wiped the blood from her lip with the back of her wrist, leaving a red smear across her skin like war paint she never asked for. Then she stepped through the ropes and walked out under the noise, under the hatred, under the lights.

Not proud.

Not broken.

Just… alive.

And as she disappeared up the ramp, the barbed wire bat remained in the ring, glittering in the aftermath, a silent reminder that some matches don’t end.

They just stop.

**To Be Continued In PART - 8\

body.title: Chłopomania Ignacego Korwin Milewskiego
body.body:
![ikm01.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/helcim/23xemxbjheYXpLCHoydsS5QaEQBPQYrZgiRzirZ2qnuc9eMBZDGUB88NXFzKXyKYJVVTF.jpg)


Fascynacja Ignacego Korwin-Milewskiego ludowością jest zadziwiająca. To nie było przelotne zainteresowanie, którego świadectwem pozostało kilka obrazów w kolekcji. To była autentyczna pasja, której źródła chciałoby się poznać, ale można tylko zgadywać skąd mogła się wziąć. Milewski miał w swych zbiorach obrazy różnych artystów malujących ludowe tematy, ale najważniejszy był zdecydowanie Wincenty Wodzinowski. Milewski nie tylko kupował jego obrazy, ale sfinansował budowę jego pracowni, której Wodzinowski miał możliwość malowania wielkich płócien nieustępujących rozmiarami kompozycjom Matejki. 


![jkm08.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/helcim/23wCDiLBehekxzk3YAJ6oZn1JJhrEdYrPX9X9GWBacGfaKpVtHd1eW8edNbL3esYNsFJJ.jpg)


![jkm04.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/helcim/23wWvt3apgJQyRo3gRnQBR9aAYVRWhdSkDkapyd5mcTuhk2t8WAyaSux2hQ698wSc7Bzb.jpg)

Takich obrazów nie ogląda się często i to niezwykły zbieg okoliczności, że niedawno można je było oglądać na wystawie monograficznej Wodzinowskiego w Muzeum Krakowa. Są na pewno dokumentem zainteresowań kulturą i życiem ludu, ale czy przetrwały próbę czasu jako dzieła malarskie? Niektóre na pewno tak. Nie ma wątpliwości, że przetrwały ją prace Ludwika Stasiaka, malarza mało znanego, chyba tylko dlatego, że nie można zobaczyć jego obrazów w wielkich muzeach narodowych, ale trzeba pojechać do Muzeum im. prof. Stanisława Fischera w Bochni. Jego obrazy przedstawiające Noc Świętojańską są ciekawą próbą przedstawienia nocnego pejzażu, co bez wątpienia lepiej się udało w  obrazie *Sobótki* z 1890 roku niż w dwa lata póxniejszej *Nocy Świętojańskiej*.

body.title: #MyHiveGoals week #16: May progress: #HPUD #HPUM and awaiting the savings system interest payments on HBD [Eng/Esp]
body.body:
> Hey Hive friends! Happy start to May, everyone! I always feel a bit nostalgic around this time of year. These are the last few weeks I'll be able to see the Araguaney trees in bloom, so I have some time to photograph one if I'm lucky enough. This month, among many other things, I'm coordinating the lab classes at the university, so I barely had time to write this report on Monday, which is the day I usually do them to make my progress week by week. But here I was, at the university, accompanied by this mischievous cat I named Diocletian, yes! Like the Roman emperor. Yesterday he surprised me because I saw him protecting his territory from other cats in the faculty, and boy, is he aggressive! He's my only companion when I arrive so early to start preparing for lab sessions. We both share a stoic nature, which is why I don't take my job for granted, because training professionals is always a rewarding endeavor. Of course, I also dedicate that time to my Hive project, which I'm definitely taking very seriously, so let's see how our progress has been this week and assess the status of #MyHiveGoals. ---
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bulkathos/23t77FvkwHZ7RwVWbngJjztEhHXvEnuxKDFb5dS7jFqFVrnDCFbYekc7Cf53wNnzXFVzQ.png) Link: [livecoinwatch](https://www.livecoinwatch.com/price/Hive-HIVE)

> These last 24 hours have been insane! Hive's price has skyrocketed by 44.4%. The truth is, with all this global chaos we're experiencing, the uncertainty is quite high, and I don't know to what extent this price will hold or if, on the contrary, it's just the first step towards a sustained bull run. I hope it's the latter, although in either scenario, my approach will be the same: creating content about my favorite projects and interacting with the various communities. In other words, continuing to grow on Hive.
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bulkathos/Eo4Ab6YHDAqaRVh7pHakA5AGvkNLYU7VLBS8c1rk9qDwzndFTYaNHBV8B4vRG9gDDam.png)
# Hive/HP

> Let's start with the most important event of these first days of May, #HPUD. As we've been doing for the past four months, on the 1st of each month we've been religiously blocking our Hives to increase our Hive Power and strengthen our contribution to this project. But we've gone beyond just powering up one day a month and have committed to powering up every day of the year. And although we haven't received the #HPUM Hive Power Up Month medal since December, I've remained steadfast in blocking at least one Hive every day, except for the 1st of each month when I power up at least ten Hives. ---
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bulkathos/23tRrJ2pAEZd2YmsZhgRwVgYW11poK3qtJ6BtaDhuq2z4PzfEmWbR1m8APB7o8WRBA1wv.png)|![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bulkathos/EoEo7DEYePe26ogtUrdWRbo1rVwdGibpVn1LmJufSNZBhqSGcb1WpDaKAdvugEbtmv8.png) --|-- --- ![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bulkathos/23t797xMXYCFjdUs6UXT2qQpG5M8ufJdoyAd54oKszx2ooZ1kMhMs5dvBhAsq6cv92Tjs.png)

> The sum of these power-ups, combined with posts and interactions on Hive, has led me to generate almost 149 HP this week! That's right, friends, we far surpassed our goal of 9,500 HP before May 1st! I still remember when we started January with 7906 HP in our first week. I was frustrated that we hadn't reached 8000 HP at the time, but looking back, and despite the drop in Hive's price, achieving over 1600 HP in the first quarter of the year seems like a remarkable improvement. Of course, we're still far from the 12000 HP I've set as my goal for 2026, but maintaining this pace, this goal is perfectly achievable.
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bulkathos/23t77MfGSNMprPt4FzUYragrz15TSZVR6tkMRC4nxubC3Ds9gssFxDa63Ze15i2nbsvz4.png)|![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bulkathos/23t7937Mo7nva5vb2BKdCtUc5n6oeo126q92bd4UwNDMWVWbdfUG3TFjhYzFeGonxDqF9.png) --|-- Link: [hivestats](https://hivestats.io/)
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bulkathos/23tbkj8mbMn9CYGJL7qVH3Zzq9mBSpZMLFAwUuy9ggaZ1KBkyRJwKGLVu3gb6pfH3bZUd.png)
# HBD Savings

> Next, let's talk about our HBD savings. Last week, I organized the posts I had already planned, and fortunately, they were well-received. Combined with the curations and interactions, we reached 7,344 HBD this week. Unfortunately, I traded those Hives to HBD on Sunday afternoon when the Hive was at $0.06. We could have made a bit more profit if we had waited until today, but as I mentioned at the beginning, there's no need to get upset about these things, just keep working on your blog and your reputation. You'll see the fruits of your labor one way or another. ---
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bulkathos/23tRvNJcWj5y29BsxSWF42pTv1AVDux2BhvbT9VrCQFjnpm8yE8eWLAworFVKGFsstTKX.png)

> We've reached a total of 1964.73 HBD, and I think that with luck we'll reach a little over 1970 HBD by the end of this week, which conveniently coincides with the collection of the interest on that 15% APR, which I estimate could be around 19-20 HBD, bringing us to about 1990 HBD. I was hoping to reach 2000 by the end of this month, but we came pretty close. The goal I set for myself of reaching 2300 HBD by the end of this year does seem quite difficult now, but there are still 7 months left. I think if I organize my time better, I can achieve this goal.
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bulkathos/23tRqtUv2HbgUu3pHREDtnyBMjZMVWZw1pQAdkGMQpG9zcN4LKLEFgFQRuP14tLnmDWi6.png) --- ![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bulkathos/23tRvSiU5m7Z9Pz4UvJB3ePpMbdip6yngvyEi5yEuBJv7RwrLB87nfr7xWjBwrL3LTqCy.png)
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bulkathos/23tGyXZoWHqdFmZ3okUbJHeoVbbUXGqH9Q7Eq9XGt2nrFidVxjieoh8GH2HD5583firb5.png)

> That concludes my report, friends. This past week I also had no activity on the second layer beyond NFT games. Only now, as I write this, am I receiving the RWA tokens: TGLD and TNVDA that I had staked. It's a shame what's happened to these projects. I need to evaluate what's best to do with them: exit them completely and accept a loss of over 90% of my investment, or hold on and pray for a miracle. In the next report, I'll tell you how things went with these tokens. Regards. ---
# Versión Español
---
![Front MHGW16.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bulkathos/23xp4ErK3whnmzDex97ZmNYWkBwDM95KoyBxcG2mMhAwg6iAp4Gyo1v95ZGMxbnCj3f9k.jpg)
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bulkathos/23zRw3SoGotiSUAysx4tbYSPR3V3jdvPQ3LTooQ4k1z4VBxtPoNchWgAq1KiuHBo874BJ.png)

> Que tal amigos de Hive! Feliz inicio del mes de mayo estimada comunidad, siempre tengo cierta nostalgia por estos días, son las últimas semanas que podré ver los arboles Araguaney florecer por lo que tengo algo de tiempo para fotografiar alguno que vea si tengo suficiente suerte. Este mes entre otras tantas cosas me corresponde coordinar la docencia de los laboratorios en la universidad, por lo que casi no tuve tiempo para realizar este reporte el lunes que son los días que me gusta hacerlos para comprar mi avance semana por semana. Pero aquí me encontraba, en la universidad acompañado de este travieso gato al que llamé Diocleciano, si! Como el emperador romano. Ayer me sorprendió porque lo vi protegiendo su territorio de otros gatos de la facultad y vaya que es agresivo! El es mi único acompañante cuando llego tan temprano para comenzar a preparar las prácticas de laboratorio, ambos compartimos el ser estoicos y es la razón por la que no desprecio mi trabajo, porque formar profesionales siempre es una labor gratificante. Por supuesto, comparto ese tiempo con mi progreso en Hive que es un proyecto que definitivamente me estoy tomando muy enserio, así que veamos como ha estado nuestro progreso esta semana y evaluar el estado de #MyHiveGoals. ---
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bulkathos/23t77FvkwHZ7RwVWbngJjztEhHXvEnuxKDFb5dS7jFqFVrnDCFbYekc7Cf53wNnzXFVzQ.png) Link: [livecoinwatch](https://www.livecoinwatch.com/price/Hive-HIVE)

> Estas últimas 24 horas han sido de locura! Hive a disparado su precio un 44,4% la verdad es que con todo este caos global que estamos viviendo la incertidumbre es bastante grande y no sé hasta que punto este precio vaya a mantenerse o si por el contrario es apenas los primeros pasos para bull run sostenido. Espero que sea lo segundo, aunque en cualquiera de los escenarios mi proceder será el mismo, crear contenido de mis proyectos favoritos e interactuar con las distintas comunidades. En otras palabras seguir creciendo en Hive.
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bulkathos/Eo4Ab6YHDAqaRVh7pHakA5AGvkNLYU7VLBS8c1rk9qDwzndFTYaNHBV8B4vRG9gDDam.png)
# Hive/HP

> Comencemos por el evento más importante de estos primeros días de mayo, el #HPUD. Como ya veníamos haciendo en estos últimos 4 meses cada 1ero de mes hemos estado religiosamente bloqueando nuestros Hive, para aumentar nuestro Hive Power y aumentar el peso de nuestra participación en este proyecto. Pero hemos ido más allá de solo hacer power up un solo día del mes y nos hemos propuesto hacer el power up todos los días del año, y aunque desde diciembre no nos están dando la medalla del Hive power up month #HPUM me he mantenido firme bloqueando al menos 1 hive todos los días a excepción del 1ero de cada més donde hago power up de al menos 10 Hives. ---
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bulkathos/23tRrJ2pAEZd2YmsZhgRwVgYW11poK3qtJ6BtaDhuq2z4PzfEmWbR1m8APB7o8WRBA1wv.png)|![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bulkathos/EoEo7DEYePe26ogtUrdWRbo1rVwdGibpVn1LmJufSNZBhqSGcb1WpDaKAdvugEbtmv8.png) --|-- --- ![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bulkathos/23t797xMXYCFjdUs6UXT2qQpG5M8ufJdoyAd54oKszx2ooZ1kMhMs5dvBhAsq6cv92Tjs.png)

> La suma de los estos power up en sinergia con las publicaciones y las interacciones en Hive me ha llevado esta semana a generar casi 149 de HP! Así es amigos, logramos superar ampliamente la meta de los 9500 HP antes del primero de mayo! Aún recuerdo cuando empezamos enero 7906 HP en nuestra [1era semana](https://ecency.com/hive-167922/@bulkathos/myhivegoals-initiative-taking-the-first), me frustraba no haber llegado a los 8000 HP en aquel momento, pero viendo las cosas en retrospectiva y a pesar de la caída del precio de Hive, haber logrado más de 1600 de HP en el primer trimestre del año me parece un avance notable. Por supuesto aún estamos lejos de los 12000 de HP que me he propuesto para este 2026, pero manteniendo el mismo ritmo esta meta es perfectamente posible.
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bulkathos/23t77MfGSNMprPt4FzUYragrz15TSZVR6tkMRC4nxubC3Ds9gssFxDa63Ze15i2nbsvz4.png)|![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bulkathos/23t7937Mo7nva5vb2BKdCtUc5n6oeo126q92bd4UwNDMWVWbdfUG3TFjhYzFeGonxDqF9.png) --|-- Link: [hivestats](https://hivestats.io/)
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bulkathos/23tbkj8mbMn9CYGJL7qVH3Zzq9mBSpZMLFAwUuy9ggaZ1KBkyRJwKGLVu3gb6pfH3bZUd.png)
# Ahorros HBD

> Luego pasamos a nuestros ahorros en HBD, la semana pasada organicé las publicaciones que tenía ya tenía planeadas y afortunadamente fueron bien valoradas y sumado a las curaciones e interacciones, llegamos a 7.344 HBD esta semana. Lamentablemente cambie esos Hives a HBD el domingo en la tarde cuando el Hive estaba en 0.06$ habríamos podido sacar algo más de ganancia si hubiéramos esperado hasta hoy, pero es lo que les comentaba al comienzo, no hay por que amargarse por estas cosas, solo seguir trabajando en tu blog y tu reputación, el fruto de tu esfuerzo y trabajo lo verás de una u otra forma. ---
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bulkathos/23tRvNJcWj5y29BsxSWF42pTv1AVDux2BhvbT9VrCQFjnpm8yE8eWLAworFVKGFsstTKX.png)

body.title: [Esp/Eng] ✨Lindo colgante con temática de conejito.   // Cute Bunny-themed pendant.✨
body.body:
<div class=text-justify>

###### <center>✨¡Hola amigos amantes de la creatividad! Espero que estén todos bien.✨</center>

<center>¡Buenas tardes, amigos! Espero estén pasando una excelente semana. Por mi parte, contenta de pasar por acá a compartir una linda idea con ustedes. En esta ocasión les comparto el paso a paso para elaborar un lindo colgante con temática de conejito. Esta vez quise elaborar esta linda idea que perfectamente puede ser un imán para la nevera, pero quise hacerlo como colgante para que pueda ser para una habitación, decoración de puerta o, como dije, un lindo imán para la nevera.</center>

**🔸Sin más que añadir, a continuación los dejo con el paso a paso:**

> ###### <center>✨¡Hello friends who love creativity! I hope you are all well.✨</center>

> <center>Good afternoon, friends! I hope you're having a wonderful week. I'm happy to stop by and share a cute idea with you. This time, I'm sharing the step-by-step instructions for making an adorable bunny-themed pendant. I wanted to create this cute idea, which could also be a refrigerator magnet, but I decided to make it as a pendant so it could be used in a room, as a door decoration, or, as I mentioned, as a cute refrigerator magnet.</center>

> **🔸Without more to add, then I leave you with the step by step:**

---

<center>![portada defii.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/valenpba/23u63LwYakxUDkvYBUqHpFshz8xHibk7mSXRMN8CwsRKcUjD2imLwtFqh5QA7x5Wu1LtV.JPG)</center>

---

<div class=\

> **♥️ESPERO QUE TE GUSTE, ¡Empecemos!**
**♥️I HOPE YOU LIKE IT, Let's start!**
---
![separador 2023.PNG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/valenpba/23uFnpKyJ7meMSyw1pqmfQu94TYy7tCuEmTPQy9gugnkC5oXaC7gcejs3b2EPAGmUMGRT.PNG)

> - Cartulina metalizada azul. - Foami azul. - Foami gris. - Foami naranja. - Foami verde. - Cinta delgada. - Pinturas y marcadores. - Pegamento. - Tijeras. - Regla. - Hoja blanca. - Lápiz.
- Blue metallic cardstock. - Blue craft foam. - Gray craft foam. - Orange craft foam. - Green craft foam. - Thin ribbon. - Paints and markers. - Glue. - Scissors. - Ruler. - White paper. - Pencil.
![separador 2023.PNG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/valenpba/23uFnpKyJ7meMSyw1pqmfQu94TYy7tCuEmTPQy9gugnkC5oXaC7gcejs3b2EPAGmUMGRT.PNG)

> ###### ✨PASO 1: Lo primero, como siempre, es tomar una hoja blanca y dibujar el diseño que desean elaborar. En mi caso, como les dije al inicio, quería un conejito saliendo de una regadera para plantas, pero, además, quería colocar algunas zanahorias dispersas en el fondo, el cual aún no tenía claro, pero al tener la idea lista en la hoja blanca, lo pasé a los colores correspondientes de foami, como explico a continuación: ✨Orejas: 2 cm x 1 cm en foami gris. ✨Cabeza: 3.5 cm x 2.5 cm en foami gris. ✨Cuerpo: 2.3 cm x 2 cm en foami gris. ✨Patas: 1 cm en foami gris. ✨Pico de regadera: 5 cm x 2 cm en foami azul. ✨Cuerpo de regadera: 4.8 cm x 4 cm en foami azul. ✨Agarradera: 3 cm x 0.3 mm en foami azul. ✨Zanahoria: 1.5 cm x 1 cm en foami naranja. ✨Hojas: 1 cm en foami verde.

> ###### ✨STEP 1: First, as always, take a white sheet of paper and draw the design you want to make. In my case, as I mentioned at the beginning, I wanted a bunny popping out of a watering can, but I also wanted to add some carrots scattered in the background. I hadn't quite figured out the placement yet, but once I had the idea sketched out on the white paper, I transferred it to the corresponding colors of foam, as explained below: ✨Ears: 2 cm x 1 cm in gray foam. ✨Head: 3.5 cm x 2.5 cm in gray foam. ✨Body: 2.3 cm x 2 cm in gray foam. ✨Legs: 1 cm in gray foam. ✨Watering can spout: 5 cm x 2 cm in blue foam. ✨Watering can body: 4.8 cm x 4 cm in blue foam. ✨Handle: 3 cm x 0.3 mm in blue foam. ✨Carrot: 1.5 cm x 1 cm in orange foam. ✨Leaves: 1 cm in green foam.
![separador 2023.PNG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/valenpba/23uFnpKyJ7meMSyw1pqmfQu94TYy7tCuEmTPQy9gugnkC5oXaC7gcejs3b2EPAGmUMGRT.PNG)
|![IMG_20260422_124917.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/valenpba/EoyTMZxaoQ6E1o2qV4Eabauwgy5iSA8BJMYfgUc1byKwSVohF7fz2HiC6x6JAm7hw4H.jpg)|![IMG_20260422_125030.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/valenpba/EokeX6mnYzehDnXUF8bnZg6fvE3qdz5T26ZRmZ6nhM9XKk6365FZb9ND7U6NfyydR49.jpg)|![IMG_20260422_125103.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/valenpba/EoK8iCpfenDGbdHZ4BmFmxNc4G5pfBRxcZ5ic7sHEqLJhUe75PkN2wJXzd4sEqtyyL6.jpg)| |-|-|-|
![separador 2023.PNG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/valenpba/23uFnpKyJ7meMSyw1pqmfQu94TYy7tCuEmTPQy9gugnkC5oXaC7gcejs3b2EPAGmUMGRT.PNG)

> ###### ✨PASO 2: Al tener listas y recortadas las piezas, es momento de dar color a los bordes, con pinturas o marcadores, ya sea con colores que hagan contraste o con colores que combinen. En mi caso, utilicé marcador negro para los bordes de las piezas en foami gris y para el resto de las piezas, sí utilicé el mismo color, pero más oscuro.

> ###### ✨STEP 2: Once the pieces are cut out, it's time to color the edges with paint or markers, using either contrasting or complementary colors. In my case, I used a black marker for the edges of the gray foam pieces, and for the rest of the pieces, I used the same color, but darker.
![separador 2023.PNG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/valenpba/23uFnpKyJ7meMSyw1pqmfQu94TYy7tCuEmTPQy9gugnkC5oXaC7gcejs3b2EPAGmUMGRT.PNG)
|![IMG_20260422_125711.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/valenpba/Ep7xTCXyjNPyeCSCKQVY7UgqtcgrrMWtf8gJmTQYXN7Fn988YpDZpYmA46Zz6a4BhMS.jpg)|![IMG_20260422_125659.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/valenpba/Ep7xYtBGmk72pN97HvyVUNHNvkjTN39mKSeoauqaxetLaDW6qXXYpwbavaJvYqkpvoE.jpg)|![IMG_20260422_125705.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/valenpba/EopxgRcdTdMu5pQnzHaw1dHLrHqckeBCzCd6uxpCHtX1RzcAMLYjGucgj1Cje5v4vPz.jpg)| |-|-|-|
![separador 2023.PNG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/valenpba/23uFnpKyJ7meMSyw1pqmfQu94TYy7tCuEmTPQy9gugnkC5oXaC7gcejs3b2EPAGmUMGRT.PNG)

> ###### ✨PASO 3: Al estar secas las piezas, es momento de los detalles extras, para definir o, como dije, detalles pequeños pero importantes, como ojos, nariz, boca, rubor, cejas; definir mejor el centro de las orejas, las patas, las zanahorias y la regadera. Al estar pegadas, es momento de dejar secar y pegar al menos las piezas por individual.

> ###### ✨STEP 3: Once the pieces are dry, it's time for the extra details, to define, or as I said, small but important details, such as eyes, nose, mouth, blush, and eyebrows; to better define the center of the ears, the paws, the carrots, and the watering can. After gluing them together, it's time to let them dry and glue the pieces individually.
![separador 2023.PNG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/valenpba/23uFnpKyJ7meMSyw1pqmfQu94TYy7tCuEmTPQy9gugnkC5oXaC7gcejs3b2EPAGmUMGRT.PNG)
|![IMG_20260422_130103.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/valenpba/EoeGrk5xAxmP3wSrfYAjP2A8haNyMx27wNFoZ5rpUWQrck6WPXsymrdYg9HPj5AL8uP.jpg)|![IMG_20260422_130746.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/valenpba/EonmsTDpLgLVecrKf3qCxnnuzks7aswtEfqWCKtaGW7W23TQnstQTpPfkmzGpGnWp87.jpg)| |-|-|
![separador 2023.PNG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/valenpba/23uFnpKyJ7meMSyw1pqmfQu94TYy7tCuEmTPQy9gugnkC5oXaC7gcejs3b2EPAGmUMGRT.PNG)

> ###### ✨PASO 4: Ahora sí vamos a tomar la cartulina metalizada azul y vamos a recortar una pieza de 10.5 cm x 11 cm y vamos a ir pegando hasta formar la decoración; en este caso, pegamos al conejo de la regadera, junto con las patitas, y luego, alrededor, pegamos las zanahorias.

> ###### ✨STEP 4: Now we'll take the blue metallic cardstock and cut out a 10.5 cm x 11 cm piece and start gluing it to create the decoration; in this case, we glued the rabbit with the watering can, along with its paws, and then, around it, we glued the carrots.
![separador 2023.PNG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/valenpba/23uFnpKyJ7meMSyw1pqmfQu94TYy7tCuEmTPQy9gugnkC5oXaC7gcejs3b2EPAGmUMGRT.PNG)
|![IMG_20260422_130816.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/valenpba/EprU9VuCRtSGPwRRwwy5QJZG1L6UnNokennr1VTEUhGLe4R891eTzaCQv56hbMpzDbj.jpg)|![IMG_20260422_130937.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/valenpba/EpLguKcxnR9QzpjWdkTVazF4UQzFTxpbct3S6DPWpFAa8cikXNRcSubC1xiTa7nzqko.jpg)| |-|-|
![separador 2023.PNG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/valenpba/23uFnpKyJ7meMSyw1pqmfQu94TYy7tCuEmTPQy9gugnkC5oXaC7gcejs3b2EPAGmUMGRT.PNG)

> ###### ✨PASO 5: Finalmente, quise darle más detalles, así que pinté en la regadera unas pequeñas flores blancas con pintura, dejamos secar y, por último, pegamos una cinta delgada en la parte superior, pero trasera, de la cartulina metalizada.

> ###### ✨STEP 5: Finally, I wanted to add more detail, so I painted some small white flowers on the watering can, let it dry, and then glued a thin ribbon to the top back of the metallic card.
![separador 2023.PNG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/valenpba/23uFnpKyJ7meMSyw1pqmfQu94TYy7tCuEmTPQy9gugnkC5oXaC7gcejs3b2EPAGmUMGRT.PNG)
![IMG_20260422_131358.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/valenpba/EpEHruxATXD6AB9rGeQXZPHoDUD3JEYTLqLTrSzhH2gCE1ESvsztAwADn5QwkPdWUFe.jpg)
![separador 2023.PNG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/valenpba/23uFnpKyJ7meMSyw1pqmfQu94TYy7tCuEmTPQy9gugnkC5oXaC7gcejs3b2EPAGmUMGRT.PNG)
✨Así es como pueden elaborar este o el colgante con la decoración que deseen elaborar. De verdad que pueden crear lo que gusten, dejando volar la imaginación y obtener un lindo resultado. Espero que les haya gustado el paso a paso y se animen a elaborarlo.
❤️Hasta la próxima publicación.
>
✨That's how you can make this or any other pendant you like. You can really create whatever you want, letting your imagination run wild and achieving a beautiful result. I hope you enjoyed the step-by-step instructions and are inspired to make it.
>
❤️Until the next post.
![separador 2023.PNG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/valenpba/23uFnpKyJ7meMSyw1pqmfQu94TYy7tCuEmTPQy9gugnkC5oXaC7gcejs3b2EPAGmUMGRT.PNG)

<Sub>[source](https://pixabay.com/photos/sapa-vietnamese-labor-labor-1531088/)<sub>








![kenznguyen-sapa-1531088_1920.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/oyebolu/23qrHpR1zvssVRiKvpdvQ4veMsgAKFDBst1o5pEcA4EFHL6cShhjxHMhWcfyohJtD3k5M.jpg)









Is not the son of none.



It is so bright that it clears the route,
In a way vivid enough for the foot,
As the blockage  couldn’t overshadow the sun's brightness,
So to say that the entire scheme is just madness.

So what about the darkness in counting,
The one that is a metaphor for comparing,
The catalogue that serves as catharsis,
It is all about domination in analysis.

As the vigintillion shadows reflect,
That kind of ambiguity deflects,
It is not a struggle,
Where search marks up Google.

For the protagonist is the same,
As the antagonist in fame,
Where the father is the everlasting light,
And the mother is the over-darken darkness in sight.

So what is proper?
It is also improper,
Only the lens shown,
And view accepted to the bone,

Fathered in light,
Mothered in total darkness in sight,
The son of a vigintillion suns,
Is not the son of none.

body.title: Technology And Artificial Intelligence Only Made Things Easy, Faster And Even More Beautiful
body.body:
# Hello learners and community 😍💕.

What a lovely prompt to commence another week of featured contents from #hiveleaners . Will AI slow down the ever known creativity knowledge of humans? 

I have always loved 🥰 questions that relates to technology and artificial intelligence because they are the two greatest things that has made a boom 💥 in our 21st century, even while controversies continued in one angle or the other. And this I believe is not a bad opinion because what ever that has an advantages , surely will have a disadvantages.

# The Era:

Im my own opinion as regards to the above question, I can tell you that technology artificial intelligence only helped made creativity easier for humans, with less time consumption when creating an art 🖼 and at the same time significantly adding more beauty to art 🖼 creativity. So here, the evolution of technology and artificial intelligence only brought to humans a new modern creativity that will help them create something that will flow with the times we are in. 

I believe that technology and artificial intelligence is never a blow to human creativity and will never be due to how humans must move with time, creating something from their own imagination 💭but only using the availability of technology and artificial intelligence to make it less stressful, cutting costing 💲that will make the art 🖼 too expensive and unaffordable, and finishing up quickly because of use of machines which is another way that will help productivity.

# Going Back With References:

We should be making references to other things that has been invented by man 👨, which has also helped humans process in life instead of making humans loose focus. One example is the calculator that has helped many students while studying mathematics. It only helped  us to put numbers together , but we humans still work out the answers by ourselves.  Its as simple as this. If you do not put your figures well into the calculator by thinking 🧐 properly, you will end up making a mistake. 

Have you seen where a Cashier at the bank 🏦 is trying to balance his ledger 📒 after the bank has closed for the day? He will go over and over again, making sure the figures on the ledger 📒 is corresponding with what he or she has entered into the calculator. J don’t know how humans would’ve been able to calculate those large sum of figures without the calculator.

So the use of technology and artificial intelligence in creativity is only helping humans to have a better presentation of art 🖼, after they have imagined the art, then will start to put them together to come out in a more better and beautiful finishing. I see this as change that goes with times and era. Time is the only thing that is bringing change which will cause a shift in many things that connects to humans.

# How Can We Still Stay Creative?

First thing we should have in mind is to keep being original. This comes from the imagination 💭 we have as humans. Before creating an art 🖼, we already picture it in our mind , which is the base work. So here the image stays original even when we use technology and artificial intelligence to do some touch ups, we still maintain the originality in the arts 🎭.

Quality arts 🎭 are never compromised when creating an art by a good creative artist 👨‍🎨 . In fact, they pay attention to this area through the experience they have, making sure the finishing looks sophisticated and not just one generated artificial intelligence products. This area is also crucial to a good artist who wants to maintain a top notch clientele.

Arts 🎭 attracts because those who love ❤️ arts knows what they want. A good creativity brings the best out from the artist. He or she should not allow artificial intelligence to dominate every part of the creativity. Your skill as an artist should be seen visibly if you must go far as a well known artist 👨‍🎨.

As humans who wants to represent ourselves in what we do, we should not be fully dependent on technology and artificial intelligence. Our impact on our work should always be visible, superseding the involvement of artificial intelligence and technology. By this, we will always retain and maintain our originality in what we do.

This is my response to the #hiveleaners featured content for week 216, edition 01

# Thanks for visiting and reading friends 😍

# Best Regards @sunshine29 🧡

body.title: RAFI 1 - F*ck Society [ENG-PT/BR]
body.body: >One of the hallmarks of the city of Coimbra, Portugal, is undoubtedly its university. Now 736 years old, it is divided into three campuses. Campus 1 is the oldest area, where the Law and Humanities programs are still located. Today, it is mostly visited by tourists. Campus 2 houses Mechanical Engineering, Computer Engineering, and new technologies. Campus 3 is dedicated to biomedical sciences; this is where Medicine and Nursing are taught. ㅤ I found this piece of street art on Campus 1, in an area behind the old Physics building that is hardly visible to tourists. Today it is inhabited by homeless people; filth reigns and the smell of urine is nauseating. But it was worth the sacrifice because I consider it a very interesting piece of graffiti. A simple technique (spray paint, direct line) that blends tagging and conceptual drawing, inspired by contemporary graphic language and punk culture. A graffiti piece closely linked to ideas of free expression and counterculture. body.title: HIVE Digital Is Playing a Different Game — And Most People Haven't Noticed Yet
body.body:
>Most Bitcoin mining stocks are a slow bleed. HIVE Digital might be the exception — and the reason has almost nothing to do with Bitcoin.
I've been watching this space for a while. And if there's one thing I've learned, it's that the most interesting plays are the ones where the company is changing the rules while everyone else is still playing the old game.

>
That's exactly what HIVE Digital Technologies is doing right now.

\n\n

>Here's the short version: HIVE used to be a Bitcoin miner. Full stop. It dug coins, sold them, and rode the market cycles like everyone else.
Then something shifted.

>
The company quietly started converting its infrastructure into high-performance computing (HPC) data centers — the kind that power AI workloads. Not pivot-as-a-press-release. Actual hardware. Actual liquid-cooled server racks. Actual GPU fleets.

>
Nine Wall Street research firms noticed. As of late April 2026, they collectively hold a \
consensus on the stock. The average 12-month price target sits at $6.16 against a recent share price around $2.35.

>
That's a 162% upside baked into analyst models. The most bullish call — from Canaccord Genuity's Joseph Vafi — goes all the way to $10.
Now, I'm not here to tell you to buy the stock. I'm not your financial advisor. But I am here to tell you what those analysts aren't fully explaining.

\n\n
>The Real Story Is in South America
>Forget the price targets for a second. Let me tell you about Paraguay.

>
In late 2025, the Paraguayan government enacted Decree 5306. In plain terms: it locks energy rates for qualifying AI and data center operators at U.S. dollar-denominated prices for 15 years.

>
That sentence doesn't sound exciting. Stick with me.
>The single biggest cost for any data center — AI or otherwise — is electricity. Stable, cheap power isn't just nice to have. It's a structural moat.
>HIVE moved fast. They planted their BUZZ HPC platform in Paraguay and started building what CEO Aydin Kilic calls \
The country runs on abundant hydroelectric power. It's green. It's cheap. And now, thanks to that decree, the price is locked in for a decade and a half.

>
Compare that to a competitor trying to build in Texas or Georgia. They're fighting for grid access, dealing with volatile spot energy prices, and sweating through every summer heat wave. HIVE's Paraguay operation doesn't have that problem.
This is the part the TheStreet article buried in a single sentence. It deserves its own headline.

\n\n
>The $115 Million Move That Cost Nothing

>On April 21, 2026, HIVE closed a $115 million private offering of senior exchangeable notes.
The interest rate? Zero percent.

>
Read that again. They raised $115 million and don't owe a dollar in interest. That kind of deal only happens when investors believe so strongly in a company's future that they're willing to accept no yield in exchange for conversion upside.

>
HIVE is now deploying that capital into two moves: quadrupling its Canadian AI capacity and funding the Paraguay expansion. The company's debt-to-equity ratio sits at a remarkably low 0.02. They have firepower and they have room to use it.

\n\n
>What the Bulls Are Missing (The Risk Side)

>Here's where I want to be straight with you, because the bullish case is easy to get swept up in.
Risk 1 — Bitcoin is still the anchor. HIVE earns meaningful revenue from mining. If Bitcoin's price drops hard, the mining side bleeds and that drags on everything.

>
Risk 2 — Dilution is real. Those $115M in exchangeable notes can convert to equity. That means current shareholders could get diluted. Cantor Fitzgerald quietly reduced its price target to $3 in April, citing exactly this kind of friction.
Risk 3 — Competition doesn't sleep.

>Marathon Digital and Riot Platforms are not standing still. They have deeper pockets. If AI data center demand becomes the obvious gold rush, they will build too.
HIVE's moat is real — but it is not invincible.

\n\n
>The TSX Catalyst Nobody's Talking About
>One more thing. Around April 30, HIVE was expected to graduate from the TSX Venture Exchange to the main Toronto Stock Exchange (TSX).

>
This matters because the TSX main board opens the door to a whole class of institutional funds — pension funds, large ETFs — that are prohibited from holding Venture-listed stocks. More eligible buyers means more potential demand. It's a quiet catalyst that doesn't make for a flashy headline.

>
But it's the kind of structural shift that can move a stock over months, not days.

\n\n

>HIVE isn't just a miner trying to survive a post-halving world. It's a company that locked in cheap power in Paraguay for 15 years, raised $115 million at zero interest, is building liquid-cooled AI infrastructure, and just upgraded its exchange listing.

>
Whether the $10 price target materializes or not, the strategy is more interesting than almost anything else happening in the mining sector right now.
>The best plays aren't the ones everyone's shouting about. They're the ones where a company quietly builds something hard to replicate — and most people don't notice until it's already priced in.

>Watch the Paraguay build-out. That's where the real answer will come from.

\n\n
>I want to hear your take on something specific:

infrastructure — data centers built in countries with cheap, stable, green energy — is the next great moat in this industry. Do you think that geographic energy arbitrage is a durable advantage? Or will bigger players like Amazon, Microsoft, and Google simply outspend them into irrelevance?

>
Drop your thinking in the comments. Especially if you've been watching any other small-cap companies running the same playbook in different regions — I'd genuinely love to dig into those examples with you.

\n\n**This is not financial advice. Do your own research before making any investment decisions.**
