body.title: Letting Go Is The Rhythm Of My Present Happiness #287
body.body:
What was it that you clung to tightly (an ideal, a person, a stage of life) that life forced you to let go of? What was the emotional process of accepting that it was no longer part of your present?
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmXfBMzWXNyGxot4eGpDc4msXxiFdRc187VVtkHYAafPDQ/1778002880307.heic) Before now, I found it difficult to let go because I was brought up in an environment and lifestyle that seemed perfect. I was surrounded by people who became a permanent structure in my growth. There was no reason to live in isolation or fight each other. The love around was sufficient for us to live happily without necessarily hurting each other. However, as life evolved and everybody started moving on far beyond to fend for daily endeavours. People transitioned, and everything changed immediately. Being the last in our family, I was left with my mother and father while others moved on to bigger things out there. In that moment, everything changed, relationships evolved, patterns shifted, and circumstances overturned. I became frustrated with the sudden change and the lonely situation. That moment came with a learning process of openness and of building relationships beyond bloodlines and family. However, in a bid to do that, I became demanding, which led to a series of offenses. I was always getting offended and not letting go. It became quite frustrating while I also struggled to regain myself and quit that lifestyle. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmUYYekCraXZf6LjMLDjkK17aerZ87FJvw1Mb3pFZ7HcC5/1778002951088.jpg) Life continued to evolve, leaving me with no choice but to accept change and transition to a better version of myself. The last straw that broke the camel's back was a bickering I had with my close friend. I informed my eldest sister, and she asked me to let go and move on. Unfortunately, I allowed it to linger, and on a particular Sunday, as teens, after the service, we were spoken to, and peace was made between us. The following morning, we learnt that the girl had passed on. I cried my heart out, but was also happy that we made peace. That experience not only served its purpose in my life but also helped in reshaping me. From that day, acceptance crept in. I began to see letting go as a bitter pill to my change and a process to my transitioning. I became softened, and the emotional weight of not letting go gradually disappeared. I adopted the tool of reflection to unwind and adjust on my daily journey in life, noting that not letting go is no longer part of my present Feel free to join [here](https://ecency.com/hive-124452/@ladiesofhive/ladies-of-hive-community-contest-287) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmbU2hSgaX1Af4R4dWfwNG3TcPhZMquzbJbmqGKqd7BpTd/1778003035145.gif)

body.title: The Great Illusion: How @guiltyparties Built an Empire on Empty Promises
body.body: # The Great Illusion: How @guiltyparties Built an Empire on Empty Promises\n\n<a href=\

>from Imgflip Meme Generator --- ## **Prologue: The Mask of Benevolence** There is a particular kind of tragedy in watching a wolf dress itself in shepherd's clothing, not to protect the flock, but to shear it bare while convincing the sheep they are being cared for. Today, we pull back the curtain on **@guiltyparties**. To the casual observer, this account appears to be a hub of charity, a distributor of aid, a beacon of hope in the Hive ecosystem. The transaction history is a cascade of outgoing transfers: thousands of HIVE and HBD flowing to `gpwallet` accounts, to individuals in need, to \

*\n\nBut look closer. Follow the money. And you will find not a charity, but a **centralized banking cartel** disguised as a community fund. You will find a system where power is concentrated, transparency is an illusion, and the \

provided is merely the interest paid on a loan of trust that can never be repaid.

**We expose the truth:** @guiltyparties runs a massive farm, a shadow bank, and a political machine, all while pretending to be a simple benefactor.

---

## **I. The Architecture of the Shadow Bank**

### **Figure 1: The Wallet Network (The Shell Game)**

```
THE GUILTYPARTIES ECOSYSTEM
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
Central Hub: @guiltyparties
│
├── The Distribution Arms (Dozens of \

accounts)
│   ├── @gpwallet, @gpwallet2, @gpwallet3... @gpwallet30
│   ├── Function: Receive large lump sums from HQ
│   └── Function: Disburse funds to end-users or exchanges
│
├── The Laundering Layer (@bdhivesteem)
│   ├── Pattern: gpwallets send HIVE → @bdhivesteem
│   ├── Action: @bdhivesteem swaps HIVE for HBD via internal orders
│   └── Result: Clean stablecoins ready for reuse or export
│
└── The Power Base (@spaminator, @logic, @hivewatchers)
    ├── @spaminator: Receives delegation (20k HP) & funds logic
    ├── @logic: Receives steady weekly stipend (~50-100 HIVE)
    └── @hivewatchers: Receives operational funding
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
Analyst Note: This is not charity; this is corporate structure. The use of dozens of numbered wallets obscures the total volume of flow and makes auditing nearly impossible for the average user.
```

**The Implication:**
Why does a charity need 30+ numbered wallets? Why does it need to route funds through `@bdhivesteem` to convert currency before distribution? The answer is **control**. By fragmenting the treasury, @guiltyparties creates a labyrinth that protects the central hoard from scrutiny while maintaining absolute authority over who eats and who starves.

---

## **II. The Mechanical Symphony of Control**

*Based on on-chain transaction logs*

While the public sees \

the blockchain records **transactions**. And the patterns reveal a cold, calculated machine.

### **Figure 2: The Stipend System (@logic)**

```
THE LOGIC STIPEND
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
Recipient: @logic
Frequency: Weekly (every 7 days ±1 day)
Amount: ~50.00 to ~100.00 HIVE (precise decimals)
Duration: Continuous for years
Recent Examples:
• 50.066 HIVE (5 days ago)
• 100.051 HIVE (11 days ago)
• 49.985 HIVE (23 days ago)
• 75.249 HIVE (Mar 18, 2026)
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
Verdict: This is not a donation; it is a salary. @logic is an employee of the @guiltyparties empire, paid to maintain the infrastructure (Spaminator, etc.) that enforces the cartel's will.
```

### **Figure 3: The Currency Mill (@bdhivesteem)**

```
THE CONVERSION LOOP
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
Step 1: @gpwallet30 receives 830.000 HIVE from @guiltyparties.
Step 2: @gpwallet30 sends 830.000 HIVE to @bdhivesteem.

body.title: ⛰️ Quiet mornings far from everything
body.body:
https://img.leopedia.io/DQmWXNes65eYzq8CnKwX6jhE12DWGcGdeZSo7dhBFXCGMro/IMG_0060.png 

Some trips are full of noise, busy streets, schedules, and endless movement…  
but the ones I remember the most are usually the quiet ones.

This place felt different from the moment I arrived. Fresh air, wooden cabins, mountains in the distance, and that peaceful silence that makes you breathe a little deeper without even noticing.

I spent most of the morning doing absolutely nothing important, and honestly, that was the best part.

Sometimes traveling is not about escaping your life.  
It’s about reconnecting with yourself for a little while.

I think we all need places that make us slow down and appreciate simple things again — the view, the weather, a calm morning, or even just sitting quietly with your thoughts.

And today felt exactly like that.

body.title: MLB: De todo un poco...  [ESP/ENG]  ||  OPINION
body.body: <div class= 'text-justify'>\n\n      A ningún equipo le puede gustar tener jugadores lesionados. Por supuesto, unos son más importantes que otros y puede ser determinante tenerlos arrumados en la lista de jugadores de baja, por ello es una excelente noticia cuando regresan a la alineación. Uno de los caos más apegado a lo que describimos, ha sido las lesiones de Andrew Vaughn y el jardinero venezolano Jackson Chourio. No seguimos los detalles de Andrew, pero en el caso de Jackson, fue una fractura de la mano en el Clásico Mundial de Baseball lo que le hizo arrancar la presente zafra en la zona de incapacitados. Por ello, aunque ayer perdieron, los Cerveceros estaban de fiesta en el Bush Stadium al saberse la incorporación de ambos toleteros al line-up. Por poco pierden de nuevo a Jackson el viernes, cuando una pelota bateada de foul en juego de rehabilitación en las menores, le golpeó fuertemente el tobillo. Los rayos \

no revelaron daño y el hombre tomó el avión el domingo para alcanzar a los lupulosos en San Luis. #
ENGLISH VERSION (click here!)

     No club likes seeing their guys hit the shelf. Obviously, some losses sting more than others, and having key bats stashed on the IL can tank a season. That’s why getting reinforcements back in the starting nine is a massive boost. Both Andrew Vaughn and Venezuelan outfielder Jackson Chourio fit that bill perfectly. While we didn't track Vaughn’s every move, Chourio’s road back was tough: a fractured hand during the World Baseball Classic forced him to break camp on the Injured List. Even with a tough loss yesterday, the Brew Crew was buzzing at Busch Stadium because both sluggers were officially back in the lineup. It almost went south again on Friday, though. During a rehab assignment in the minors, Chourio took a foul ball straight to the ankle. Luckily, the X-rays came back clean, and he hopped a flight Sunday to join the Crew in St. Louis.

# ---

![Chourio.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/fermionico/EpCATX1u9U7w4T5bJsQBTXiN2mK1ReAXrpPSsucjsgmiBEPJnRNuQcQaTkZErifJczh.jpg) Screenshot from [video](https://www.mlb.com/es/gameday/brewers-vs-cardinals/2026/05/04/823064/final/video) --- # ![Firma Fermionico_Mesa de trabajo 1616.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/fermionico/QnCF6Qc3-Firma20Fermionico_Mesa20de20trabajo2016-16.png)
#
     La estrella nacida en Maracaibo, Edo. Zulia, se ocupó se aparecer en los titulares con su actuación, muy diferente a la de su compañero Andrew (quien se fue en blanco). Chourio se paró 5 veces en la goma y no lo pudieron sacar de out. Primer turno, doble; y la secuencia continuó: sencillo, imparable, boleto y otro doble para entregar planilla de anotación de 4-4 con boleto. Lamentablemente fue un desperdicio porque sus compañeros no estaban en base para aprovechar su ofensiva. Los muchachos de Milwaukee dejaron demasiados hombres en posición de anotar al irse de 12-2, contrariamente a San Luis quienes anotaron 6 carreras versus 3 de los Cerveceros, para llevarse el triunfo. Jamás será bueno perder contra equipos de vuestra misma división, pero la central de la Nacional está tan apretada, que con todo y sótano, los chicos de Milwaukee están a 4.5 juegos de la vanguardia. San Luis acecha a los Cachorros a dos juegos detrás. #
ENGLISH VERSION (click here!)

      The Maracaibo-born star grabbed the headlines with a performance for the ages, a far cry from his teammate Andrew (who went 0-for). Chourio stepped into the batter’s box five times and they simply couldn’t retire him. He started with a two-bagger, followed by a single, another base knock, a walk, and finished with another double to post a perfect 4-for-4 line with a free pass. Sadly, it was a bit of a solo act since the rest of the Crew couldn't drive him in. Milwaukee went cold with runners in scoring position, going a dismal 2-for-12. On the flip side, the Cards capitalized, putting up 6 runs to the Brewers' 3 to secure the W. You never want to drop a game against a divisional rival, but the NL Central is a total dogfight right now. Even sitting in the cellar, Milwaukee is only 4.5 games back of first place, while St. Louis is breathing down the Cubs' necks, just two games out of the lead.

# ---

![Arráez.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/fermionico/23wMkucZUWsPdwKo6RMgVCVF3mLK8c5EbWnKxqji8RLQZpsaEKz5p9RF2nwsZdJpatVtH.jpg) Screenshot from [video](https://www.mlb.com/es/gameday/padres-vs-giants/2026/05/04/823228/final/video) --- # ![Firma Fermionico_Mesa de trabajo 1616.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/fermionico/QnCF6Qc3-Firma20Fermionico_Mesa20de20trabajo2016-16.png)
     ¿Recuerdan cuando les hablamos de Luis Arráez y su renovada defensiva? Efectivamente, el hombre se ha propuesto mejorar a cualquier costo y su aparición en las jugadas destacadas no se ha hecho esperar. Ayer, hizo una jugada clave en el noveno episodio con un out, cuando puso out a Jackson Merril, fildeando una pelota a mano limpia y sacando el segundo jugador del inning. Jackson corre duro, así las cosas, Luis se tuvo que emplear a fondo para no dejar que la carrera del empate se quedara en primera. Al bate, también se lució al irse de 3-2 con dos carreras anotadas. Acumula .318 y 40 hits, líder en éste departamento dentro del contingente venezolano. Su defensiva, que hasta el año pasado se medía con un -61 en outs sobre el promedio, ha mejorado un mundo ésta zafra, con una estadística de +6 outs sobre el promedio. El criollo es una de las pocas luces en un alicaído equipo de la bahía, que aunque ganó a un equipo directo (San Diego), todavía está a 8 juegos de la vanguardia en el oeste de la Nacional. Los clérigos siguen detrás de los Dodgers a juego y medio. #
ENGLISH VERSION (click here!)

     Remember when we talked about Luis Arraez and his revamped glove? The man is on a mission to improve at all costs, and he’s already popping up on the highlight reels. Yesterday, he made a clutch play in the ninth with one out, retiring Jackson Merrill by charging a ball and making a slick barehanded play for the second out of the frame. Merrill has wheels, so Arraez had to go all out to keep the tying run off the bases. At the dish, he stayed hot, going 2-for-3 with two runs scored. He’s now hitting .318 with 40 hits, leading the Venezuelan contingent in that category. His defense, which was a major liability last year at -61 Outs Above Average (OAA), has taken a massive leap this season, sitting at +6 OAA. \

is one of the few bright spots for a struggling Marlins squad that, despite taking a game from a divisional foe like San Diego, still sits 8 games back in the NL West. Meanwhile, the Friars are still chasing the Dodgers, trailing by just a game and a half.

---

![Abreu.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/fermionico/23wX3KeQTXgVK25F8JboeAw4oceVLsM6mmGddgrpmuHLdkv2brBMpnXpBHKv9DeFXh5xJ.jpg) Screenshot from [video](https://www.mlb.com/es/redsox/video/wilyer-abreu-misjudges-pitch-tries-to-challenge-it) --- # ![Firma Fermionico_Mesa de trabajo 1616.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/fermionico/QnCF6Qc3-Firma20Fermionico_Mesa20de20trabajo2016-16.png)
     La ansiedad al bate que mostraba Wilyer Abreu en el Clásico Mundial de Béisbol, nunca le afectó para entregar resultados en ese campeonato. Pero seamos honestos, no es lo mismo el WBC que una temporada de 162 juegos. Y he aquí que si usted no controla esa ansiedad, tarde o temprano le pasará factura en su performance. Esto pareció entenderlo el jardinero criollo y se le ha visto trabajando los turnos al bate con extrema paciencia. El maracucho es el hombre con mejor promedio de la alineación de Boston y ayer contribuyó con un hit impulsor de una carrera, para alejar la pizarra que se encontraba 3-2 a favor de los Medias Rojas, en ruta a un triunfo de 5 carreras a 4, de los patirrojos ante los Tigres de Detroit en el Comerica Park. Antier, en una demostración de que trabaja los conteos, pidió revisión con sistema ABS de un lanzamiento. Solo para darse cuenta de que se había confundido, porque el umpire había cantado bola. El momento resultó jocoso con un Wilyer riendo y el umpire gesticulando en tono de burla. Los Medias Rojas siguen hundidos en el sótano de su división. Veremos. #
ENGLISH VERSION (click here!)

     The plate discipline issues Wilyer Abreu showed during the World Baseball Classic never really hurt his production in that short tournament. But let’s be real: the WBC is a different beast than the 162-game grind. If you don't keep that anxiety in check, it’ll eventually tank your numbers. The Venezuelan outfielder seems to have figured that out, as he’s been working counts with elite patience lately. The Maracaibo native currently leads the BoSox in batting average and came through yesterday with an RBI knock to stretch a tight 3-2 lead. That insurance run helped the Red Sox secure a 5-4 win over the Tigers at Comerica Park. Just the other day, showing how locked in he is on every pitch, he actually challenged a call using the ABS system (Challenge System). It turned into a hilarious moment when he realized he’d messed up—the umpire had already called it a ball! Wilyer couldn't help but laugh while the blue poked a little fun at him with some jokey gestures. Despite the win, the Sox are still buried in the basement of their division. We’ll see if they can climb out.

body.title: Hablemos de: Crepúsculo | Let's talk about: Twilight
body.body:
> Hola de nuevo! Hoy les traigo un nuevo post bastante genial, esta vez hablando de una saga de películas de la que siempre he querido hablar, Crepúsculo. Tengo mucho tiempo sin publicar por aquí, y eso es debido a que no he tenido mucho tiempo desde hace unos años, realmente no tenía tiempo para a sentarme a escribir con calma las reseñas de películas que tanto adoro hacer, ya que trabajo y estudio, sin embargo me planteé como meta poster más seguido como lo hacía antes. Hace unos 4 años me vi una maratón de Crepúsculo con mi novio, me vi todas las películas y la verdad, es que quedé fascinada. Sin embargo, la vi de manera irónica, porque para mí estas películas son para verlas así y en su momento cuando se estrenaron no las vi. Sí recuerdo a un montón de amigas obsesionadas con esta saga de películas y sus libros, y aunque en su momento nunca entendí el por qué de eso, en la actualidad me meto en la mente de una adolescente de 14 años de los 2000s, y lo comprendo, así que hoy les hablaré sobre la primera entrega de esta emblemática saga de películas, comencemos!
Hello again! Today I’m come to you with a pretty awesome new post, this time about a movie series I’ve always wanted to talk about: Twilight. It’s been a long time since I’ve posted here, and that’s because I haven’t had much time over the past few years, I really didn’t have time to sit down and calmly write the movie reviews I love so much, since I’m working and studying. However, I’ve set a goal to post more often, just like I used to. About four years ago, I did a Twilight marathon with my boyfriend, I watched all the movies, and honestly, I was fascinated. However, I watched them with a bit of irony, because for me, these movies are meant to be watched that way, and I didn’t see them when they first came out. I do remember a bunch of friends who were obsessed with this movie series and its books, and although I never understood why back then, now I put myself in the mind of a 14 year old girl from the 2000s, and I get it. So today I’m going to talk to you about the first installment of this iconic movie series, let’s go!

> [![2-2.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ochitoalreves/23tvCjD7XpZdrSpQru3FwCtb3sZDpER6tTH4ATfi43nN1Q952VUyPJ3TLyfboD1WW95R9.jpg)](https://uk.pinterest.com/pin/775604367063669493/) La primera película fue estrenada en el año 2008 y está basada en una novela del mismo nombre cuya autora es Stephenie Meyer. La película gira entorno a Bella Swam, interpretada por Kristen Stewart, una adolescente que muda con su papá a un pueblo pequeño y alejado llamado Forks. Allí se reencuentra con un viejo amigo, Jacob Black (interpretado por Taylor Lautner) y también va a una nueva escuela. Hace amigos fácilmente, pero cuando están en el comedor se topa con una familia muy peculiar, los Cullen. Al entrar a una de sus clases le toca sentarse con uno de ellos, Edward Cullen (interpretado por Robert Pattinson), y parece estar tan repugnado por ella que se va e incluso, falta varios días a clase luego de eso, sin embargo regresa y actúa como si nada con Bella. Un día Bella está en el estacionamiento de su escuela y casi es atropellada por una camioneta, de no ser porque Edward Cullen la salva mostrando una fuerza y rapidez sobrehumana que deja a Bella sospechando sobre quién es ese extraño chico, pero él le dice que no se le acerque. Al hablar con Jacob sobre los Cullen, este le dice que ellos y su familia prácticamente son enemigos.
The first film was released in 2008 and is based on a novel of the same name by Stephenie Meyer. The film centers on Bella Swan (played by Kristen Stewart), a teenager who moves with her father to a small, remote town called Forks. There, she reunites with an old friend, Jacob Black (played by Taylor Lautner), and starts attending a new school. She makes friends easily, but when she’s in the cafeteria, she runs into a very peculiar family, the Cullens. When she enters one of her classes, she ends up sitting next to one of them, Edward Cullen (played by Robert Pattinson), and he seems so repulsed by her that he leaves and even skips class for several days after that; however, he returns and acts as if nothing happened with Bella. One day Bella is in her school’s parking lot and is almost hit by a truck, but Edward Cullen saves her, displaying superhuman strength and speed that leaves Bella wondering who this strange boy is, though he tells her not to come near him. When she talks to Jacob about the Cullens, he tells her that they and his family are practically enemies.

> [![4-2.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ochitoalreves/23tbCQZseUD9rLobg5N1g85ob8e4foC53DpSgqRwHSPkCp1T1zZNKE9fcqNkXC25VUcqs.png)](https://www.cbr.com/twilight-baseball-scene-still-untouchable/) Después de otro incidente donde Edward salva a Bella, ella se da cuenta de que tiene características de vampiro, así que se pone a investigar exhaustivamente sobre esos seres. Un día Bella confronta de manera definitiva a Edward, y este le admite que es un vampiro, diciéndole que no consume sangre de humanos, demostrándole sus habilidades sobrehumanas y que bota escarcha cuando está bajo la luz del sol. Durante todo esto, Bella no deja de pensar en Edward y que siente que la ve desde la ventana de su habitación. Un día Edward lleva a Bella a su casa presentándoles a su familia, demostrando que tienen muchos años siendo vampiros y que suelen mudarse con frecuencia. Mientras tanto en el pueblo están ocurriendo muertes extrañas que parecen ser hechas por animales salvajes, pero en realidad son causadas por tres vampiros, Victoria, James y Laurent. Un día estos 3 vampiros se topan con los Cullen y Bella que estaban en un partido de béisbol amistoso y James queda encantado con el olor de Bella.
After yet another incident in which Edward saves Bella, she realizes he has vampire characteristics, so she begins to research these beings thoroughly. One day, Bella finally confronts Edward, and he admits to her that he is a vampire, telling her that he doesn’t drink human blood, demonstrating his superhuman abilities, and showing her that he sparkles when he’s in the sunlight. Throughout all this, Bella can’t stop thinking about Edward and feels that he’s watching her from her bedroom window. One day, Edward takes Bella to his home to introduce her to his family, revealing that they’ve been vampires for many years and tend to move frequently. Meanwhile, strange deaths are occurring in town that appear to be caused by wild animals, but are actually the work of three vampires: Victoria, James, and Laurent. One day, these three vampires run into the Cullens and Bella, who were at a friendly baseball game, and James is enchanted by Bella’s scent.

> [![6-1.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ochitoalreves/23uEykzQYBYVrRkis4Ny2Z8NYWCXDpokxiAp4TZkVzW5EBDej3Zc64zjdxYtvJVMYTcVb.jpg)](https://screenrant.com/best-most-iconic-high-school-prom-movies/) James está obsesionado con cazar a Bella y la persigue sin descanso, obligando a Bella a escapar a Phoenix con Alice y Jasper. Sin embargo, James atrae a Bella a una trampa, atacándola e infectándola con veneno vampírico. Nuestra protagonista está a punto de morir pero llegan los Cullen a salvarla y se lleva a cabo una pelea bastante fuerte. Los Cullen logran someter y matar a James, quitándoles la cabeza y quemándolo, mostrando que esta es la mejor manera de matar vampiros. Pero Bella está agonizando y la única manera de salvarla es absorbiendo el veneno que tiene Bella en su sangre, Edward la salva y la llevan al hospital ya que está bastante herida. Al volver al pueblo de Forks es el baile de la secundaria y Edward acompaña a Bella, donde sellan su amor con un beso y no lo saben, pero Victoria está escondida viéndolos, dando a entender que la veremos en la siguiente película.
James is obsessed with hunting Bella and relentlessly pursues her, forcing Bella to flee to Phoenix with Alice and Jasper. However, James lures Bella into a trap, attacking her and infecting her with vampire venom. Our protagonist is on the verge of death, but the Cullens arrive to save her, and a fierce battle ensues. The Cullens manage to subdue and kill James, decapitating him and burning his body, demonstrating that this is the best way to kill vampires. But Bella is dying, and the only way to save her is to absorb the venom in her blood. Edward saves her, and they take her to the hospital since she is seriously injured. Upon returning to the town of Forks, it is the high school dance, and Edward accompanies Bella, where they seal their love with a kiss. Unbeknownst to them, Victoria is hiding and watching them, hinting that we will see her in the next movie.

> [![8-1.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ochitoalreves/23tGTGXmMhPSNYC2mAaq7h4a6uBgrEp4Fc4Dt38Kgzj3S5mtUW464CuWkeCASqWD6MnS6.jpg)](https://collider.com/cringey-yet-charming-lines-from-the-twilight-movies/) Honestamente esta película me maravilló, viéndola de manera irónica. Comencemos por los protagonistas, aunque los actores que interpretan a Bella y Robert ciertamente tienen mucha química que hasta traspasó la pantalla, no puedo dejar de pensar en lo incómoda que esta actuación de Robert Pattinson en esta película. Parece que no quisiera estar allí, pone caras de disgusto y su intento de ser misterioso me da mucha risa. Y Bella ni se diga, es una chica que intenta ser rara y no transmite absolutamente ninguna emoción, parece un robot, pero no se crean, adoro estas actuaciones porque disfrute lo malas que eran. El desarrollo de la relación de ambos es un vaivén, ya que Edward es el típico chico que dice que le hará daño si está con él, y Bella siendo el cliché de chica que no le importa que sea diferente, quiere estar con él. Los villanos no están tan mal, sin embargo me parecen muy exagerados y estereotipados, a veces no me creo que sean malos porque sus expresiones parecen muy forzadas. Necesito que alguien me explique porque toda la película tiene un filtro azul como si fuesen los inicios de Instagram, entiendo que quisieran darle un tono frío a lugar, pero creo que exageraron. Pero no todo es malo, realmente creo el ambiente del pueblo de Forks cumple su función de ser un lugar donde ocurren cosas extrañas, no todo es un romance cliché sino que hay drama y además, adoro a Alice, no les voy a mentir. La música está muy bien, recuerdo que cuando tenía entre 11 y 12 años conocí música genial que me recomendaban amigas las cuales escucharon en esta película, además de que conocí a Paramore gracias a eso. Esta película me parece muy buena para verla sin tomársela en serio, les juro que la disfruté y genuinamente me gusta por eso, me reí y pasé un buen momento viéndola, a pesar de saber que no es muy buena.
Honestly, this movie blew me away, in an ironic way. Let’s begin with the main characters, although the actors playing Bella and Robert certainly have great chemistry that practically jumps off the screen, I can’t help but notice how awkward Robert Pattinson’s performance is in this film. He looks like he doesn’t want to be there, he pulls faces of disgust, and his attempt to be mysterious just cracks me up. And Bella, don’t even get me started, she’s a girl trying to be weird who conveys absolutely no emotion, she looks like a robot. But don’t get me wrong, I love these performances because I enjoyed how bad they were. The development of their relationship is a rollercoaster, since Edward is the typical guy who says he’ll hurt her if she’s with him, and Bella is the cliché girl who doesn’t care that he’s different, she just wants to be with him. The villains aren't that bad, but they seem very over the top and stereotypical to me, sometimes I don't buy that they're bad guys because their expressions seem so forced. I need someone to explain to me why the whole movie has a blue filter, like it’s from the early days of Instagram. I get that they wanted to give the setting a cold vibe, but I think they went overboard. But it’s not all bad, I really think the atmosphere of the town of Forks does a good job of being a place where strange things happen. It’s not all cliché romance; there’s drama too. Plus, I love Alice, I’m not going to lie to you. The music is great. I remember that when I was 11 or 12, I discovered some awesome music that friends recommended to me, they’d heard it in this movie, and I also discovered Paramore thanks to that. I think this movie is great to watch without taking it too seriously. I swear I enjoyed it and genuinely like it for that reason, I laughed and had a good time watching it, even though I know it’s not that great.

> ![divisor.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ochitoalreves/23uQpCCM2XzmBdpEynL1LXipfX2x97hTDT9BnGPC1a8bLdexmQwuJQz1DFTsyWfYHuEg8.png) Puedes seguirme en mis redes sociales dando click! You can follow me in my social media with a click!

>as a parent why am I raising my kids here?

The problem with a great empire is that when it declines, it does not decline alone.  The influence of this country on global affairs is so great that the repercussions of our decline will be felt just about everywhere.  It is a global event.

Where will the safe havens be?  Will we be able to recoup, here, in the US? We still have vast resources, including people, education and natural resources.

 It's not just a matter of economics.  Some of the changes he has made will have devastating long-term consequences.  Others may be turned around...like his golden oval office, the Gulf of America, the Trump Kennedy Center.  If we are lucky, there will be a sea change with the 2026 midterms (if they are allowed to proceed unimpeded). With a working Congress maybe the worst of this administration will be choked off.

Meanwhile, I think we should all be flexible in assessing our futures.  I know you will be because you have made dramatic changes over the course of your life.  I try to tell my kids to be ready for an evolving future, to not count on stability but be ready to adjust.  I hope the same for my granddaughter.

One thing Trump has done for us is remind us that the world is and always has been a scary place. In the U.S. the domestic population has been insulated from that. No war here since 1812.  Maybe we are waking to a new reality.  

I know I'm going on...but that's just my mind as I reheat a few slices of pizza for lunch. Life goes on, we hope.

I asked claude to check for obvious security vulnerabilitie BTW. Here is what it found that may or may not be on your radar, I will paste as I asked claude to format it, let me know if relevant or not:

## Bug A — Free Gas Exploit: Any User Can Steal Gas Reserve (Critical)

**File:** `account-mapping/evm-mapping-contract/contract/main.go:81`  
**File:** `account-mapping/evm-mapping-contract/contract/mapping/types.go:24`  
**File:** `account-mapping/evm-mapping-contract/contract/mapping/handlers.go:147-149`

### What it is
The EVM bridge has a shared \

— ETH held by the contract to pay Ethereum gas fees when
processing withdrawals. Users are supposed to pay this fee themselves on top of their withdrawal.

There is a boolean field `deduct_fee` in the withdrawal request that is supposed to mark whether the
fee should be deducted *from* the amount (e.g., a relayer covering fees on behalf of a user). The
problem: **there is no access control on this field.** Any user can set it to `true` in their JSON.

### The code

```go
// main.go:81 — no access control, input parsed directly from user JSON
func unmapETH(input *string) *string {
    var params mapping.TransferParams
    json.Unmarshal([]byte(*input), &params)   // DeductFee comes straight from user
    ...
}

// types.go:24
DeductFee bool `json:\

`  // user controls this

// handlers.go:147-149 — when true, fee is simply... dropped
totalDeduct := amount + fee
if params.DeductFee {
    totalDeduct = amount  // fee not charged to anyone
}
```


The calculated fee (Ethereum gas cost) is never charged to the gas reserve, never deducted from
the caller — it just disappears. The contract still pays real Ethereum gas from the reserve. Every
withdrawal with deduct_fee: true drains the gas reserve slightly without anyone paying for it.

How to exploit
Send a withdrawal with:


`{ \

: true }`

Repeat until the gas reserve drops below MinGasReserve (0.05 ETH), at which point all
withdrawals for all users are permanently blocked until an admin manually refills the reserve.




## Bug B — Funds Permanently Trapped: int64 Balance Ceiling (High)

**File:** `account-mapping/evm-mapping-contract/contract/mapping/balance.go:46-53`  
**File:** `account-mapping/evm-mapping-contract/contract/mapping/handlers.go` (all deposit handlers)

### What it is
All balances in the EVM bridge are stored as Go `int64` (a signed 64-bit integer). The maximum
value of `int64` is 9,223,372,036,854,775,807 — which in wei equals approximately **9.22 ETH**.

If a user's balance is near this ceiling and they deposit more ETH, the `IncBalance` function
correctly detects an overflow and returns an error. But here is the problem: **the ETH is already
sitting in the Ethereum vault at the moment this error is returned.** The Ethereum transaction
confirming the deposit has already been included in a block and verified via Merkle proof.

### The code

```go
// balance.go:46
func IncBalance(address, asset string, amount int64) error {
    bal := GetBalance(address, asset)
    newBal, err := safeAdd64(bal, amount)
    if err != nil {
        return err  // <-- deposit rejected, but ETH is already in the vault
    }
    SetBalance(address, asset, newBal)
    return nil
}
```

The deposit is also marked as \

before IncBalance is called, so it cannot be replayed.
There is no refund path. The ETH is stuck in the Ethereum vault with no way out.

How to trigger
A user who has accumulated ~9 ETH in the bridge and then deposits 1 more ETH will lose the 1 ETH.
It arrives in the Ethereum vault, the Magi contract rejects the credit, and the funds are gone.

Since 9.22 ETH is not a huge amount for a bridge, this affects any moderately active user and
becomes more likely as the bridge grows in usage.

## Bug C — Permanent Fund Loss in transferFrom (High, triggered by Bug B)

**File:** `account-mapping/evm-mapping-contract/contract/mapping/handlers.go:460-466`

### What it is
The `HandleTransferFrom` function (the ERC-20-style \

operation) has its steps
in the wrong order. It removes funds from the sender **before** crediting the recipient. If
crediting the recipient fails, the sender's funds are gone with no rollback.

### The code

```go
// handlers.go:460-466
if !DecBalance(params.From, params.Asset, amount) {  // 1. funds removed from sender ✓
    return errors.New(\

is returned to the caller, but the state is permanently corrupted — sender balance is
reduced, recipient balance is unchanged.

Conditions for exploitation
This bug requires the recipient's balance to be near math.MaxInt64 (≈9.22 ETH equivalent in the
token's smallest unit). This is the same condition as Bug B, making the two bugs compounding:

Bug B causes ETH deposits to get trapped
Bug C causes token transfers to drain senders when Bug B conditions are present in the recipient
A malicious actor who knows about Bug B could craft a scenario where a target address is near the
ceiling, then trigger a transferFrom against them to silently burn the sender's tokens.

PS: Note from reading bug C, I used to work with Solidity and smart contracts early in my career, the logic of deducting before crediting is standard and usually the ideal, however this is go, not solidity, I think there is no equivalent of assert or requiring or just throwing the transaction invalidating and rolling back previous operations, the huge problem with fixing this is how to rollback a transaction in a way that does not create yet another possible exploit?

Well, as I said, the bugs above were AI found, they may or not be relevant, I have no context on the project and haven't worked with smart contracts in years and don't have time to evaluate them myself, but worth sharing.

But then that is why I raised the problem of AI generated code. AI can delivery so much code that it is extremely hard to review and investigate. It happens often that when we are done generating code we have so much technical debt and backlog that the work is endless. Then one fix becomes two bugs that require 2 fixes that generate 4 bugs. Be careful not to fight an Hydra with the code base. More code in general means more risk and more vectors.

You seem to have a large team from what you mention, I can only hope they are all experienced enough and beyond average enough.

# The Great Illusion: How @guiltyparties Built an Empire on Empty Promises



---

## **Prologue: The Mask of Benevolence**

There is a particular kind of tragedy in watching a wolf dress itself in shepherd's clothing, not to protect the flock, but to shear it bare while convincing the sheep they are being cared for.

Today, we pull back the curtain on **@guiltyparties**.

To the casual observer, this account appears to be a hub of charity, a distributor of aid, a beacon of hope in the Hive ecosystem. The transaction history is a cascade of outgoing transfers: thousands of HIVE and HBD flowing to `gpwallet` accounts, to individuals in need, to \

*\n\nBut look closer. Follow the money. And you will find not a charity, but a **centralized banking cartel** disguised as a community fund. You will find a system where power is concentrated, transparency is an illusion, and the \

provided is merely the interest paid on a loan of trust that can never be repaid.

**We expose the truth:** @guiltyparties runs a massive farm, a shadow bank, and a political machine, all while pretending to be a simple benefactor.

---

## **I. The Architecture of the Shadow Bank**

### **Figure 1: The Wallet Network (The Shell Game)**

```
THE GUILTYPARTIES ECOSYSTEM
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
Central Hub: @guiltyparties
│
├── The Distribution Arms (Dozens of \

accounts)
│   ├── @gpwallet, @gpwallet2, @gpwallet3... @gpwallet30
│   ├── Function: Receive large lump sums from HQ
│   └── Function: Disburse funds to end-users or exchanges
│
├── The Laundering Layer (@bdhivesteem)
│   ├── Pattern: gpwallets send HIVE → @bdhivesteem
│   ├── Action: @bdhivesteem swaps HIVE for HBD via internal orders
│   └── Result: Clean stablecoins ready for reuse or export
│
└── The Power Base (@spaminator, @logic, @hivewatchers)
    ├── @spaminator: Receives delegation (20k HP) & funds logic
    ├── @logic: Receives steady weekly stipend (~50-100 HIVE)
    └── @hivewatchers: Receives operational funding
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
Analyst Note: This is not charity; this is corporate structure. The use of dozens of numbered wallets obscures the total volume of flow and makes auditing nearly impossible for the average user.
```

**The Implication:**
Why does a charity need 30+ numbered wallets? Why does it need to route funds through `@bdhivesteem` to convert currency before distribution? The answer is **control**. By fragmenting the treasury, @guiltyparties creates a labyrinth that protects the central hoard from scrutiny while maintaining absolute authority over who eats and who starves.

---

## **II. The Mechanical Symphony of Control**

*Based on on-chain transaction logs*

While the public sees \

the blockchain records **transactions**. And the patterns reveal a cold, calculated machine.

### **Figure 2: The Stipend System (@logic)**

```
THE LOGIC STIPEND
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
Recipient: @logic
Frequency: Weekly (every 7 days ±1 day)
Amount: ~50.00 to ~100.00 HIVE (precise decimals)
Duration: Continuous for years
Recent Examples:
• 50.066 HIVE (5 days ago)
• 100.051 HIVE (11 days ago)
• 49.985 HIVE (23 days ago)
• 75.249 HIVE (Mar 18, 2026)
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
Verdict: This is not a donation; it is a salary. @logic is an employee of the @guiltyparties empire, paid to maintain the infrastructure (Spaminator, etc.) that enforces the cartel's will.
```

### **Figure 3: The Currency Mill (@bdhivesteem)**

```
THE CONVERSION LOOP
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
Step 1: @gpwallet30 receives 830.000 HIVE from @guiltyparties.
Step 2: @gpwallet30 sends 830.000 HIVE to @bdhivesteem.
Step 3: @bdhivesteem executes internal limit orders to swap HIVE for HBD.
Step 4: Repeat with @gpwallet10, @gpwallet2, etc.
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
Observation:  HIVE were funneled through this mill. The sheer volume suggests @guiltyparties is acting as an unregulated central bank, minting stablecoin liquidity for its own network while bypassing open market price discovery.
```

---

## **III. The Narrative vs. The Ledger**

The most dangerous lie is the one wrapped in truth. Yes, @guiltyparties *does* send money to people in need. The transactions are real. The memos are heart-wrenching. *\

*

But consider the source.

When a warlord builds a school in the village he occupies, is he a philanthropist? Or is he buying silence?

The ledger shows that for every dollar given to the poor, ten dollars are moved between shell companies (`gpwallets`). For every memo about \

there is a silent transfer of thousands of HIVE to `@logic` to fund the bots that downvote dissenters.

**The Truth:**
The \

is the marketing budget. It is the cost of doing business for a cartel that seeks to dominate Hive's governance and culture. They give you crumbs to keep you from noticing they are eating the whole loaf.

---

## **IV. The Connection to the Downvote Machine**

We cannot talk about @guiltyparties without talking about **@spaminator** and **@hivewatchers**.

*   **@guiltyparties** delegates **20,614 HP** to **@spaminator**.
*   **@spaminator** receives this power and uses it (along with delegated power from others) to fund **@logic**.
*   **@logic** and **@spaminator** are historically linked to the coordination of downvotes against critics, whistleblowers, and competitors.

The cycle is complete:
1.  **Accumulate** power and wealth (often via opaque means or early adoption advantages).
2.  **Distribute** small amounts to the public to build a reputation as a \

3.  **Fund** the enforcement arm (@logic/@spaminator) to silence anyone who questions the source of the wealth.
4.  **Repeat.**

This is not community building. This is **protection racketeering** on the blockchain.

---

## **V. The Verdict: A Scam of Proportions**

To call this a \
in the traditional sense might be too simple. It is more insidious. It is a **governance scam**.\n\n*   **The Promise:** \

The use of dozens of `gpwallet` accounts serves no purpose other than obfuscation. A true charity publishes its ledgers. It does not hide behind `gpwallet24` and `gpwallet25`. It does not route funds through internal swaps to avoid detection.

**@guiltyparties** has built a shadow state within Hive. They hold the purse strings, they hold the voting power (via delegates), and they hold the whip (via downvote bots). And they expect us to thank them for the privilege of being ruled.

---

## **Epilogue: The Reckoning**

There is a particular courage in speaking truth to power, especially when that power holds the keys to your survival.

But the blockchain does not care about fear. It only records truth.

And the truth is this: **You cannot build a free community on a foundation of centralized control.** You cannot claim to be a benefactor while funding the silencing of your critics. You cannot pretend to be a saint when your ledger reads like a mob boss's ledger.

To the users of Hive: Do not be fooled by the breadcrumbs. Look at the bakery. See who owns the oven. See who controls the flour. And ask yourself: *If I speak out against the baker, will I still be fed tomorrow?*

The time for gratitude is over. The time for scrutiny is now.

**Expose the farm.**
**Demand transparency.**
**Break the cartel.**

*— Bilpcoin: We expose the truth, so you can confront it.*

#HiveBlockchain #CryptoForensics #GuiltyParties #ShadowBank #DownvoteCartel #Transparency #BilpcoinTruth #StopTheAbuse

El Arte de la Guerra sigue siendo vigente porque nos recuerda que la verdadera grandeza está en evitar la confrontación cuando aún es posible. Yo creo firmemente en la paz y en la diplomacia como caminos naturales de los pueblos, pero también es cierto que cuando una nación es agredida y su soberanía violada, la resistencia se convierte en un acto de dignidad y justicia.  
Sun Tzu enseñaba que “la mejor victoria es vencer sin combatir”, y sin embargo, cuando la guerra llega por la prepotencia de quienes no respetan el diálogo, los pueblos tienen el deber de defenderse con tenacidad hasta que el agresor comprenda que atacar siempre es un error. La Batalla de Puebla es un ejemplo histórico de cómo un pueblo puede transformar sus limitaciones en fuerza, y demuestra que la patria es sagrada y nunca se rinde.  
Los pueblos son soberanos y también responsables de no permitir que la beligerancia de unos pocos se imponga sobre la voluntad de la mayoría. La paz se respeta, la soberanía se respeta, y la resistencia justa es la voz que recuerda al mundo que la agresión jamás será aceptada.  
Que viva por siempre la paz, el entendimiento entre las naciones y la conciencia de los pueblos para defender con firmeza lo que les pertenece.

**Project A: Markdown to HTML Converter (3/3)**

### What will I learn
- You will learn walking the AST to emit HTML tags;
- You will learn escaping HTML entities in text content;
- You will learn handling inline elements within block elements;
- You will learn pretty-printing vs minified HTML output;
- You will learn CLI interface: read from file or stdin, write to file or stdout;

- A working modern computer running macOS, Windows or Ubuntu;

# Learn Zig Series (#39) - Markdown to HTML: Renderer and CLI

Here we go -- the final piece of the puzzle! ;-)

In [episode 37](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-zig-series-37-markdown-to-html-tokenizer-and-lexer) we built a tokenizer that breaks raw Markdown into a flat stream of tokens. In [episode 38](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-zig-series-38-markdown-to-html-parser-and-ast) we wrote a parser that organizes those tokens into a tree -- an AST with block nodes, inline nodes, and all the nesting relationships that make a document a _document_ rather than just a bag of text. But a tree sitting in memory doesn't help anyone read your README. We need something that walks that tree and produces actual HTML.

That's what we're building today: the **renderer**. It takes an AST in, spits HTML out. And then we'll wrap the whole pipeline in a CLI so you can actually _use_ this thing from the terminal like a real tool. Read from a file, read from stdin, write to a file, pipe it around -- the works. By the end of this episode, you'll have a fully functional Markdown-to-HTML converter written entirely in Zig, across three episodes, from scratch.

## The HtmlRenderer struct

The renderer walks the AST using the visitor pattern we set up last episode and writes HTML into a growable buffer. The core idea: for every node type, we emit an opening tag when we _enter_ the node and a closing tag when we _leave_ it. Text nodes just dump their (escaped) content. The tree structure guarantees correct nesting -- if bold is inside a paragraph, the visitor enters the paragraph first, then the bold, then leaves bold, then leaves paragraph. The HTML tags come out in the right order automatically.

`, `'`) and why escaping everything unconditionally is the safest approach
- Handling inline elements within block elements by letting the visitor recurse naturally -- bold inside paragraphs, italic inside list items, text inside links, all handled by the same enter/leave logic
- Pretty-printing vs minified output controlled by a simple boolean flag, with `writeIndent()` and `newline()` methods that become no-ops in minified mode
- A CLI that reads from file or stdin and writes to file or stdout, following Unix conventions so it composes naturally with pipes and other tools
- Adding inline CSS with multiline string literals and a `--full` flag for complete HTML5 document generation
- End-to-end testing by running the entire tokenizer-parser-renderer pipeline and checking the HTML output, plus file-based fixture tests that scale without code changes

And with that, **Project A is done!** We built a Markdown-to-HTML converter from scratch across three episodes. The tokenizer breaks text into tokens, the parser builds a tree, the renderer walks the tree to emit HTML, and the CLI wraps it all up in a usable tool. No external dependencies, no magic -- just data structures, algorithms, and the Zig standard library.

The concepts from this project -- tokenizing, parsing, AST construction, tree walking, code generation -- show up everywhere in programming. Compilers, template engines, configuration parsers, syntax highlighters, linters -- they all follow this same pipeline. If you understood how our little Markdown converter works, you understand the skeleton of much larger systems.

title.title: 🚴‍♀️ A day without walking… but not without movement!/🚴‍♀️ Dzień bez spaceru… ale nie bez ruchu!
title.body:
🚴‍♀️ A day without walking… but not without movement!

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmdYEs1jtp6QCbhtaXCxEFx1YACeaz58drKwQ2tv8Kzsq9/1778001039562.jpg)

Today, instead of the usual “step counting,” I chose something I enjoy just as much – cycling 💪

And let me tell you… my legs definitely feel it 😅

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmXaaNus1kmUnauNNRHtGAHypMSQtYQWCsDAwg7aBmqiwQ/1778001055497.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmbnVrZ2NfKLDNh5qtxno9BuXCcLHeFZABLYVR7Z8UtfSX/1778001055517.jpg)

I managed to fit in a few rides throughout the day – shorter and longer distances, some easy pedaling, and some stronger efforts. In total, it was over 18 km on the bike, so even if my step count wasn’t impressive today, the activity was still solid 🚀

What makes me happiest:
✔️ my heart rate stayed nicely in the fat-burning zone
✔️ there were also more intense moments (great for fitness 💥)
✔️ my body got exactly what it needed – movement without pressure

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmSVRxWEv88wavvsNcaHbaAMEESf18V4wd8tp2A9KQ4gai/1778001076344.jpg)

There are days when walking just doesn’t happen… but that doesn’t mean we give up. We simply switch things up 💡

And cycling?
👉 gives freedom
👉 clears the mind
👉 and gets the job done 🔥

Today’s Actifit score: 2507 – lower than usual… but in terms of quality? Absolutely awesome 😎

Because it’s not always about the number of steps – sometimes it’s about how you move 💛

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmU6CUTqWsAcWoYoYLKWK68Jne2sEAZkscakJZr3c1WkdE/1778001096962.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmbx16aKVgHXyHTogMmGWzwZ4Wwn4E3yi2TEkWsRwHHPny/1778001096975.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmd3PN2Ry9M6N6aVq4Mi4x3r3KhdviBaiterSw5u6vzT8h/1778001096998.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmNSmkHX3SQ9k1o91zRfR4vCMgssX4iV22Zks3jTYY1Dfo/1778001097011.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmZKW7zf2BLPmwZxkSrhJ2EGFNDvc1keEj5ehW5Md1K7Pe/1778001097022.jpg)

Maybe tomorrow a walk… or maybe another ride? 😏

#actifit #cycling #activity #health #fitness #movement #fitmom

🚴‍♀️ Dzień bez spaceru… ale nie bez ruchu!

Dzisiaj zamiast klasycznego „nabijania kroków” postawiłam na coś, co lubię równie mocno – rower 💪

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmb8hLebRhzqHetPDCjfB3fWQgvxaTHhnUB7PamvN6JrYZ/1778001115673.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmZsZae2TddfuwFTKqshjz4tiTGBR7okbzPzu1B6We4JuS/1778001115743.jpg)

I powiem Wam jedno… nogi czują, że żyją 😅

Zaliczone kilka przejazdów w ciągu dnia – krótsze i dłuższe dystanse, trochę spokojnego kręcenia, trochę mocniejszego tempa. Łącznie wyszło ponad 18 km na rowerze, więc nawet jeśli licznik kroków dziś nie pękał w szwach, to aktywność była jak najbardziej konkretna 🚀

Najbardziej cieszy mnie to, że:
✔️ tętno ładnie pracowało w strefie spalania tłuszczu
✔️ pojawiły się też momenty intensywniejsze (czyli coś dla kondycji 💥)
✔️ organizm dostał dokładnie to, czego potrzebował – ruch, ale bez presji

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmXVEWYFjdtBJBgnqKy4vZqdbFHjL75y8v2Xo2bGbLfvNQ/1778001129188.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmQHoZXUpUon76m3XfcQu8LBCdQEDjvFfUutp8TZ3a4eko/1778001129213.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmQE7bvrYm4NuB5t5hE3ngCV1wwmcmKRbAaNf5qS3srx8C/1778001129230.jpg)

Są takie dni, kiedy spacer odpada… ale to nie znaczy, że odpuszczamy. Po prostu zmieniamy formę 💡

A rower?
👉 daje wolność
👉 czyści głowę
👉 i robi robotę 🔥

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmZxsQTYw8WLGBfGNyYDCLZetXJYu4tzsZY8QweC7Ftc83/1778001156268.jpg)

Na liczniku Actifit dziś 2507, więc skromniej niż zwykle… ale jakościowo? Sztos 😎

Bo przecież nie zawsze chodzi o ilość kroków – czasem chodzi o to, jak się ruszasz 💛

Jutro może spacer… a może znowu dwa kółka? 😏

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmbfHoGZn6cDTY6fZkQssB83f2QKb9iNiLKoFwGFedRdYd/1778001170632.jpg)

>       Estas vivencias te marcan para toda la vida y lo único que se me ocurre en este momento y creo que es lo conducente, es **agradecer**. Agradecer a todos los que estuvieron, desde la familia principalmente y por supuesto a todo el entorno que lo hizo posible. Sin olvidarme de dios, de las buenas energías y también de las malas, que forjan nuestro carácter. **Río Pinto** es una carrera única y en medio del sufrimiento te das cuenta de lo importante que son las personas que te rodean. Te pasan muchas cosas por la cabeza y más aún cuando llegas a la meta cómo lo soñaste. >*These experiences mark you for life, and the only thing that comes to mind right now, and I think is the most appropriate, is **gratitude**. Gratitude to everyone who was there, especially my family, and of course to everyone around me who made it possible. And I can't forget God, the good energy, and even the bad, which shape our character. **Río Pinto** is a unique race, and in the midst of the suffering, you realize how important the people around you are. So many things go through your mind, and even more so when you reach the finish line, just as you dreamed.* > ___
![Rio Pinto 2026.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/palabras1/243ftUeEu3VNBiYgNd3kxVwVtV5aDfQnos1NeQvArsL6APD7EBG7fQTdVtYUg32SSAqf1.png)

Próxima competencia, no tengo ni idea, pero de qué sucederá, **sucedera**. Muchas bendiciones para todos 🫂. > *I don't want to make this too long, since the video is over 20 minutes, but I humbly believe it's worth it. *Find inspiration to achieve your own dreams and surround yourself with the right people.** > >*See you in the comments, and of course, let's keep training and living a healthy lifestyle.* > >*Next competition? Agradecer a todos los que estuvieron, desde la familia principalmente y por supuesto a todo el entorno que lo hizo posible. Sin olvidarme de dios, de las buenas energías y también de las malas, que forjan nuestro carácter. **Río Pinto** es una carrera única y en medio del sufrimiento te das cuenta de lo importante que son las personas que te rodean. Te pasan muchas cosas por la cabeza y más aún cuando llegas a la meta cómo lo soñaste. >*These experiences mark you for life, and the only thing that comes to mind right now, and I think is the most appropriate, is **gratitude**. Gratitude to everyone who was there, especially my family, and of course to everyone around me who made it possible. And I can't forget God, the good energy, and even the bad, which shape our character. **Río Pinto** is a unique race, and in the midst of the suffering, you realize how important the people around you are. title.title: How to Write Better GPT Image Prompts: A Beginner-Friendly Guide
title.body:
If you want to create high-quality AI-generated visuals, learning how to write effective prompts is the most important skill. The way you describe an image directly affects the output quality, style, and accuracy. Even small changes in wording can completely transform the result.

A useful starting point for exploring structured examples and prompt ideas is [imggpt](https://imggpt.io), where different GPT Image workflows and prompt styles are organized for learners and creators who want to improve their results.

In this guide, we’ll break down how GPT Image prompts work, why they matter, and how you can improve them with simple, practical techniques.

<h2 style=\

>What is a GPT Image Prompt? Before diving deeper, it’s important to understand the basic concept. A GPT Image Prompt is a written instruction that tells an AI image model what to generate. It includes details like subject, style, lighting, composition, and mood. For more structured examples and ready-made ideas, you can also explore [GPT images prompts](https://imggpt.io/prompts), which provides useful variations and prompt inspirations for different use cases. A simple prompt gives general results, while a detailed prompt gives more controlled and realistic outputs. Example: Basic prompt: A city at night Improved GPT Image Prompt: A futuristic city skyline at night with glowing neon lights, reflections on wet streets, cinematic atmosphere, wide-angle view, ultra-detailed, cyberpunk style The second version clearly defines what kind of image is expected.
>Why GPT Image Prompts Matter AI models don’t “guess” your imagination perfectly. They rely completely on the structure of your prompt. A well-written GPT Image Prompt helps you: *

>Get more accurate visuals

* Reduce random or low-quality outputs * Control style and lighting * Improve consistency across images * Save time in editing or regenerating results The more detailed your prompt is, the more predictable your result becomes.

>A Simple GPT Image Prompt Formula You don’t need complex engineering to write good prompts. A simple formula works very well: Subject + Environment + Style + Lighting + Composition + Mood Example: A young woman reading a book in a cozy library, warm golden lighting, cinematic photography style, shallow depth of field, peaceful mood, highly detailed This structure helps the AI understand exactly what you want instead of guessing.
>GPT Image Prompt Examples Here are practical examples showing how better prompts improve output quality:

>Product Photography Basic: A smartwatch on a table Improved: A premium smartwatch placed on a black reflective surface, studio lighting setup, minimal background, high-end product photography style, ultra realistic details

>Social Media Post Basic: Motivational background Improved: A soft gradient abstract background with calm blue and purple tones, smooth light transitions, aesthetic minimal design, perfect for motivational quote overlay

>Blog Featured Image Basic: Laptop on desk Improved: A modern workspace with a laptop on a wooden desk, coffee mug beside it, natural daylight from window, soft shadows, productivity and focus theme, top-down view

>Portrait Concept Basic: Man portrait Improved: A cinematic portrait of a professional man in soft natural lighting, blurred background, shallow depth of field, editorial photography style, confident expression

>Website Hero Image Basic: Team working Improved: A modern business team collaborating in a glass office, bright natural lighting, wide-angle composition, clean corporate aesthetic, professional and minimal design

>Common Mistakes in GPT Image Prompts Many beginners repeat the same mistakes when writing prompts: **Too vague descriptions** Words like “nice” or “good” don’t help the model understand anything. **No style direction** Without mentioning style, results become inconsistent. **Overloading too many ideas** Too many conflicting instructions reduce quality. **Ignoring lighting and composition** These two factors heavily impact realism. **Copy-pasting same structure** Repetition reduces creativity and variation.

>Tips to Improve Your Prompts **Be specific but not overloaded** Focus on clarity, not length. **Think like a photographer** Describe angles, lighting, and mood visually. **Use style keywords** Such as cinematic, minimal, 3D render, editorial, etc. **Test variations** Change one element at a time and observe differences. **Build your own prompt library** Save effective prompts and reuse them with modifications.
>Why Better Prompts Give Better Results A strong GPT Image Prompt gives you control over: *

>Mood and storytelling

In simple terms, better prompts = better creative control.

>Conclusion Writing effective GPT Image prompts is a skill that improves with practice. Once you understand how to structure your prompts using subject, style, lighting, and composition, your results become far more consistent and professional. Instead of guessing, you start guiding the AI with intention and clarity. This makes your workflow faster and your visuals more usable for real projects like blogs, social media, marketing, or design concepts.

title.title: Tiny moments I wanted to keep 🖤📷
title.body:
https://img.leopedia.io/DQmVcou3FYpSscFom8pgkcWKPbzn5Qp4PmszXF98Sz62dD4/IMG_8763.jpg 

Funny how some of the most random photos end up meaning something later.

This was just a quick mirror picture before leaving…  
nothing planned, nothing perfect.  
But when I look at it now, it reminds me of a version of myself that was quietly trying her best.

I think people underestimate how much we grow in silence.  
Not every change is dramatic.  
Sometimes it’s just becoming a little stronger, a little softer, a little more confident without even noticing.

And honestly, that’s been me lately.

Still learning.  
Still making mistakes.  
Still dreaming bigger than my reality sometimes…

But I’m proud that I never stopped moving forward.

Life feels different when you stop trying to look perfect and just start being real. 🤍

Posted Using [INLEO](https://inleo.io/@bryanavita/tiny-moments-i-wanted-to-keep--3bi)

title.title: Three Tune Tuesday and Happy Cinco de Mayo!
title.body:
https://img.leopedia.io/DQmUJq6iaSTbLTHaWMTHUoF65APVgcpYZJKWSnjLrgKEhG1/image.png

Happy Cinco de Mayo everyone! I know to many of our Mexican members it's not all that of an important date, but for many countries including the United States do consider it an unofficial holiday. The last time I mentioned the date @jza tried to inform me that here were more important dates in Mexican history, and I agree there are. But the Mexican Army defeating the French on May 5, 1862 and decisively removing the Second French Empire in the region is the origin of the date. Yes I did say second, because there was a first in the past. Several nations have held claim to Mexico beyond the Spanish before complete Mexican independence.

To kick it off I want to share a nice Mexican gold coin, not mine personally, although I do own quite a few of these, but they are all stored away in secure storage. It's the Cinco Pesos, it's a pretty coin:

 https://img.leopedia.io/DQmSTYe9DuMPhd8xaRepK2drSz9vc3fXngVV3TDdgf45eFr/Screenshot%204994.png 
APMEX.com

The obverse (front) has the national arms of the state of Mexico which bears a golden eagle with a rattlesnake in it's beak while perched on a prickly pear cactus. On the reverse (back) is the portrait of  Miguel Hidalgo y Costilla. He was a Catholic priest that led the move for Mexican Independence and is considered the father of the nation. These coins contain 0.1205 Troy ounces of gold and are relatively inexpensive to pick up if you are investing in gold as the premiums are pretty low. They were some of the first ones that I purchased early on.  Right now the asking price on these is about $620!


It's hard to believe that coin is almost 120 years old and still looks almost as good as new...  Moving on, since it is Tuesday it's time for another Three Tune Tuesday. But first off, I want to say thank you to @ablaze for starting and continuing to sponsor this fun weekly event where you can share three songs that you enjoy. One lucky participant will win some HSBI units, you can't have too many of those! So if you don't already participate feel free to jump in, just use the tag #ttt or #threetunetuesday and it's never a bad idea to do a shoutout to @ablaze .

Let's jump into some music for Cinco de May!

 https://img.leopedia.io/DQmay1VYGkPJEY33bsAi1nuUzULQm6S8t8TyP1hRRzVVmaX/image.png 

## **Richie Valens**

Born Richard Velenzuela  in a suburb of Los Angeles, California in 1941  to Mexican indigenous parents who migrated to the United States. This young, talented self-taught musician rose to fame at age 16 with hits like \

made him a pioneer in Spanish-speaking rock n' roll and sold well over one million copies. However, career was cut short while touring with Buddy Holly and The Big Bopper as their private small plane crashed in a snowstorm In Iowa on February 3, 1959. He was just seventeen years of age.\n\nHe has since been inducted into the Rock Hall of Fame and received his own star on the California Walk of Fame. His guitar style influenced generations of guitarists including Jimi Hendrix, Carlos Santana, The Beatles, The Beach Boys, and Led Zeppelin. His career was short but his influence is still felt in rock n' roll until this day. I chose his classic \

to share today:


https://youtu.be/Jp6j5HJ-Cok?si=wOtmDE5AW6KHU16P







 https://img.leopedia.io/DQmay1VYGkPJEY33bsAi1nuUzULQm6S8t8TyP1hRRzVVmaX/image.png 

## **Selena**

Selena Quintanilla-Pérez was born in Texas to Mexican-American parents in 1971.  She launched her career at age ten but struggled to break into the male led Tejano Music scene in the early 80's, until she won Tejano singer of the year in 1987. Now often referred to the as the \

, she didn't speak any Spanish until she was forced to sing in the language by her father.  She became such an incredibly popular artist that in July of 1995 she produced a hugely successful crossover album into English. Sadly, it was released posthumously as she was murdered on March 31, 1995 by Yolanda Saldívar, who had been managing Selena's boutiques, after allegations she had been embezzling funds.\n\nSo yet another rising star who died too young at age 23. But she made some great music over the years, and the movie about her life in 1997 made Jennifer Lopez a huge start! This song is called \

:









https://youtu.be/YnbchtvR_M4?si=WdADASYBiBowsRF0


 https://img.leopedia.io/DQmay1VYGkPJEY33bsAi1nuUzULQm6S8t8TyP1hRRzVVmaX/image.png 

## **Marco Antonio Solis**

For the third spot there were many contenders but I decided to go with a singer from Mexico. Marco Antonio Solis has been on the Latin American Music scene since the late 1990's and produced many hits over the years.  He's even received his own star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame as one the most influential and successful artists in Latin American music over the last three decades. 

Today I'll be sharing a song he performed in the Festival de Viña del Mar, Chile in 2016 called Si No Te Hubieras Ido\

title.title: it gets louder when it is quiet
title.body:
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmYaq2eEk71yJCG5Y2Pr7GvCpiBBfW1gMyQkviqrMYv7op/1778000202340.jpg) 

I didn’t expect this clip to land the way it did.

What started as just another short between Baby Lady and Clown Cat ended up feeling… different. Not because of the animation or even the dialogue, but because of the reaction it triggered.

People didn’t just watch it — they recognized it.

And that’s when I realized something important:
the way you frame a piece of content can either preserve that feeling… or completely destroy it.

Video Clip: https://x.com/i/status/2050732815868682466


---

The problem with “naming” something like this

When I first finished the clip, my instinct was the same as anyone else’s:

“Alright, what do I call it?”

But the more I looked at it, the more I realized that a traditional title didn’t make sense. The clip already had structure:

a question

a response

an escalation

a final line that lingers


It didn’t need explanation. It needed space.

And that’s where most people go wrong.


---

Why overexplaining kills good content

There’s a temptation — especially when something feels strong — to describe it:

“Clown Cat haunts Baby Lady”
“Fear vs Calm”
“Creepy night thoughts”

The problem is, the moment you label it like that, you reduce it to something familiar and predictable.

There’s no discovery left for the viewer.

On platforms like Hive, where people actually take the time to read and engage, that loss of depth is even more noticeable. It stops being something you experience and turns into something you just scroll past.


---

Letting the clip speak for itself

What made this particular piece work is that it already contains everything it needs:

Clown Cat pushes.
Baby Lady responds.
The tension builds.

By the time it ends, the viewer already understands the dynamic — even if they can’t fully explain it.

So instead of adding more information, the goal became:

> don’t interfere with what’s already working

---

Final thoughts

If there’s one takeaway from this, it’s this:

Not everything needs to be explained.

Sometimes the strongest thing you can do is step back and let the piece exist on its own terms.

Give it just enough framing to be understood…
but not so much that there’s nothing left to feel.


---

If you’ve seen the clip, you probably already get it.

If not — you’ll know exactly what it means the moment you do.

title.title: How to Make the Most of \
to Improve in Splinterlands? (Part 2)
title.body:
![Img SPL.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/wizardwarrior/23tmN5X9JtXrBWomJBvjtyFREpgUSaQLNQJfNusukeVfVpyC5xPxzC41YmKUuXUT4NLw6.jpeg)


<center>```Image created with NANO BANANA AI```</center>

<div class=\

> **Hi, Wizards! ⚔️** I'm @wizardwarrior, and I hope you're all doing great. I haven’t posted anything in a few days, but it’s been a busy week. However, I’ve found some free time, and today I want to bring you the continuation of my last post, where I talked about “Practice Mode.” In the first part, I covered some very basic aspects of it, such as: What is Practice Mode? How do you access it? And other details about why this mode is so important, even if it doesn’t seem like it. That’s why in this second part we’ll go a step further and explore some strategies we can apply in this mode, such as how to handle and use “Splinters” and card positions. We’ll experiment with some fictional battle rules so you can get used to them, but most importantly, learn along the way, because this is all about playing, repeating, making mistakes, and continuing to learn until you become an expert—and this mode is incredible for achieving that.
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/wizardwarrior/23uQr4bnMFY9McX8PLxAMMUAvU4HUrpgPjen21oVdA326yRotQuNhD6shrgcCBNtY2XN7.png) ##
Strategies for Practicing in Practice Mode
---

>

Well, here we’ll look at some strategies you can use to learn in this mode and get off to a good start, but I want to break it down into several levels covering the concepts I mentioned earlier. These levels are:

https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/wizardwarrior/23tbwHGyBbHdEqtyLjA85WdvChBS3XKGag52CWb38QJconf6QooiJCLu5XnaAtiriGFvZ.png

### <center>Level 1: Get familiar with the Splinters</center>

Something I highly recommend—and something we should learn right from the start—are the \

They're called that because they're like the elements of nature and actually follow those same colors, so you can learn about them just by associating the colors. But to give you more context, pay attention to the following:\n\n- **Fire:** The Fire Splinter is one of the most aggressive, as it focuses on \

attacks; this is brute force at its finest.
- **Water:** I see this unit more as a control unit; it has good support and a magical attack that deals direct damage.
- **Earth:** This splinter specializes in withstanding attacks and healing allies, so if you want to hold out for several rounds, this is one of the options to consider.
- **Life:** One of the strongest teams in terms of protection and healing—I'd even say stronger than \

itself. - **Death:** This is one of my favorites because it focuses on weakening and poisoning the opponent; if you want to deal passive damage with certain abilities, this is the best choice. - **Dragon:** The most powerful team of all, since it has a little bit of everything: synergy, brute force, support, and more. - **Neutral:** It's really underrated, but it's one of the strongest; here you can get everything the other teams have. To wrap things up, you need to play and practice with each one so you can identify their strengths and weaknesses. You need to play; that’s the most important thing.
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/wizardwarrior/23uQr4bnMFY9McX8PLxAMMUAvU4HUrpgPjen21oVdA326yRotQuNhD6shrgcCBNtY2XN7.png) ###
Level 2: Learn the Positions
---

>

In the game, I’d say the positions of your cards on the battlefield are the most important thing; that’s why, if you learn that each position has specific responsibilities, you’ll have an edge over newer players—but, again, let me give you some context so you can understand the point.

- **Position 1 (Melee)**: Here are the tanks—the durable cards that last longer than the rest and pack a powerful punch.
- **Positions 2-3 (Middle)**: Here, you should play \

cards or certain abilities that can have an immediate effect on the field, or your opponent's cards that tip the battle in your favor. - **Positions 4-6 (Rear)**: Here are your snipers—those attackers who strike from a distance and can't be on the front lines. You can also experiment a bit with support units here, but it depends on the modifiers. My recommendation here is that you should practice and play with cards in different positions to see how they work—of course, following the format I’ve described—so you can observe how a particular card performs in that position, or whether you can play it in another one. It’s basically all about practice.
https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/wizardwarrior/23tbwHGyBbHdEqtyLjA85WdvChBS3XKGag52CWb38QJconf6QooiJCLu5XnaAtiriGFvZ.png ###
Level 3: Experiment with Battle Rules

>

Splinterlands has various battle rules and modifiers, and these are what dictate the strategies in the game. So, if you don’t take the rules into account, you won’t be able to create a winning combination. It’s like a law of nature: if you don’t know the rules, you won’t be able to come up with good strategies.

Here are some of the most common rules:

- **Standard**: The basic rules. Anything goes.
- **Super Sneak**: The cards gain Sneak and attack from the rear.
- **Reverse Speed**: The monsters that attack first are the ones with the lowest speed.
- **Equalizer**: Both players' cards have the same number of life points as the card with the most life points on our side of the field.

To wrap things up, Practice Mode lets you play with any active rule, so use it to get familiar with all of them and take the opportunity to learn as much as you can so you can advance to \

That will be the subject of the next post.
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/wizardwarrior/23uQr4bnMFY9McX8PLxAMMUAvU4HUrpgPjen21oVdA326yRotQuNhD6shrgcCBNtY2XN7.png)
### Have a great day, and join me on this journey of art and gameplay in Splinterlands
