title.title: SA Rugby Reaping Benefits From Grassroots
title.body: /> [source](https://encrypted-tbn0.gstatic.com/images?q=tbn:ANd9GcQPrhSAwY2ESuesbqN0yUAyHk39AjeKLD6jXA&s) The Rugby Under 20 Championship is well under way with two rounds played and one match remaining. This tournament is being hosted in South Africa and includes Australia, New Zealand and Argentina. Last year the under 20's won the World Cup thrashing every team they faced so this is a new batch of players and we kind of knew what to expect due to how strong junior rugby is in South Africa.

/></center>


[source](https://www.sofascore.com/rugby/tournament/rugby-union/u20-the-rugby-championship/26481#google_vignette)

The bonus point system for this tournament is slightly different and under normal circumstances the Junior Boks would have already won this tournament due to the results after the first two rounds. They play New Zealand on Saturday and have to make sure they either win, draw or score one bonus point to clinch the title.

Looking at Australia, New Zealand and Argentina they are of a similar standard and the matches between them are closely contested with not much between them. The Junior Boks have racked up a points difference of 66 points in just two matches which shows the gulf between them and the rest is rather big. 

The reason why South African rugby is so strong at the junior levels is that they have a strong domestic school rugby system that has been developed over the last 10 years. The players coming through the school programs have been in the system for 5 years and this is treated like a professional set up.

When players are leaving the school system they are ready for professional rugby having had conditioning coaches, dieticians and coached the same way professional players are coached with professional teams. This is kind of scary to think that the under 20 players are ready for international rugby and they are still very young.

The school system is the feeder system for the adult rugby teams and many of the leading professional teams have scouts on the ground offering contracts for those players standing out. The scary part is there could be 10 players for every position that could walk into professional teams tomorrow so many youngsters will be lost to other countries. We saw at the back end of last season a few players accepting contracts with sides in Europe and one is already penciled in as a future Irish international.

When your feeder system at grass roots level is strong then the chances are your national team will also be strong and with South Africa having won the last two World Cups the chances of a third are looking more likely.

Already having watched the first two rounds of this tournament you can see two or three players that will be featuring on the international stage within the next 12 months. The skills and power these players have is what you would expect form a player in his mid twenties and not just turning 20 and in some cases still in their teens.

When I played Under 20 rugby back in the days it was a fast open game and if you played in a better team they would control the tempo of play. The Junior Boks is controlling the tempo of play and thus are showing their dominance as the other teams cannot handle the power and speed being thrown at them. In many ways it is very one sided and does seem unfair yet it is for the other nations to improve or be left behind. If this is the best that the other countries have then they have a good 10 years of catching up to do in order to compete and then would still be behind due to SA rugby having already moved forward again.

Posted Using [INLEO](https://inleo.io/@cryptoandcoffee/sa-rugby-reaping-benefits-from-grassroots-5pg)

Thank you for your feedback. We are fully aware that it will always be too much for someone, whatever is asked. That is simply expected which is why I invite anyone that holds that position, which can be or might not be justified, to actually look at what it is we are delivering and what our goals are. 


>Increasing the delivery of code and features by hundreds of % sounds good but is not necessarily, specifically when it comes to DeFi it raises red flags in my mind.

That is fair. But we are not adding code for the sake of adding code. These are all incredibly necessary additions related to infrastructure, all greenfield stuff. Our output in code will obviously drop over time once all the infra is built and focus moves onto business. We will be freezing greenfield development after the next round of feature releases for a few week at least to work on optimization. Thats when we expect significant liquidity to come in. That will be our focus. I think the roadmap reflects that due to the fact that we are not releasing all integrations at the same time even though the code is finished. 

>Also, need more details on how the funds will be used.

The core team is decently large and budget is in most part spent on the team, it slightly fluctuates due to how specific team members are paid (fixed, per hour) but that is almost entirely the budget with ofc servers, team nodes, certain services, Zk provers will account for most of the non team cost. 

>The fact that you plan to reduce it proportionally to rewards increasing aiming to get to zero is great, it is a huge green flag, but this positive in my view is dwarfed by the size of the funding asked. 

I would respectfully disagree with this. And I am not talking here as the project lead. Im talking as a 8 year Hiver that put in thousands of hours of work into Hive for free to try and help this chain. Its how I even started with Magi, as an external volunteer. 

Not only do I think the budget is easily justifiable but I think that spending 10x more DHF funds on projects like Magi, that aim for self-sufficiency, creating clear token demand that's not hype based should be the norm. Not a 1 off, like Magi is currently.

At least 50% of the DHF spending should go on projects like Magi. I want to see more of them. That is what we need. Maintenance and opensource DHF proposals will not make Hive relevant. They might make Hive better or more efficient, or whatever, and thats great, but they can never lift Hive up from the position in the market we are in. 
**Magi can do that. Those are the \

I want to be making with DHF funding.** \n\nAnd I definitely think we, as Magi, are the best bet anyone can make right now. We have shown we can deliver top tier crypto tech and know exactly what to achieve and how.

links.body:
# 9/11 Evidence - Why Dr Judy Wood Uses Strange Terms to Describe the Unthinkable

**Source:** https://mysticbazaar.substack.com/p/911-evidence-why-dr-judy-wood-uses

When we look at the events of 9/11, we were told straight away what we were seeing before we had a chance to actually observe it.  Most people use words like ‘collapse’ ‘fire’ or ‘explosion’, but these words come with assumptions about the cause.Dr Judy Wood takes a different approach.  Her use of unique terms like, dustification, Wheatchex and Cheetos isn’t an accident or a lack of technical vocabulary.  It is a clever and unbiased way of naming an effect without assuming a cause.  By using descriptive analogies, she forces us to look at the provable fcts - the observable evidence - rather than the theory we have been told to believe.You may have seen words like ‘toasted’ and ‘fuming’ in my previous articles but here is a breakdown of the specific vocabulary that Dr Wood uses, to describe the never before seen phenomena of that day.Dustification - The mid-air transformation of solid material, including massive steel beams, into ultra fine powder before it hits the ground.Poofing - The visual phenomenon of a building section suddently turning into a cloud of dust and ‘wafting’ away rather than falling as a solid object.Wheatchex - Her term for the perimeter wall panels of the Towers (3 columns wide, 3 stories tall) that fell in chunks, resembling the cereal.Thinning - Thick, heavy steel beams that appeared to have become as thin as tissue or paper without evidence of melting.Jellification - A state where metal loses its rigidity and behaves like a soft or fluid substance at room temperature.Rolled up Carpets - Massive steel remnants that were found tightly coiled or curled, a shape physically impossible for a gravity driven ‘pancake’ collapseTortilla Chips - Eroded steel fragments so thin and curled they resemble the texture of corn chips.Toasted - objects like vehicles parked blocks away that appeared ‘burnt’ or singed, melted and totally destroyed.Fuming - The continuous emission of white clouds from the ground or debris, even when material was saturagted with water and clearly cold.Lather - A thick white ‘shaving cream’ appearance of fumes pouring from one side of WTC 1 and WTC 7.Cheeto - A specific orange glowing object that looked like the snack food, it appeared to glow as if hot but did not ignite the paper it sat on.Swiss Cheese - Metal surfaces (like cars and steel beams) that had round holes ‘eaten’ or evaporated through them while the surrounding metal remained intact.Rustification - Instantaneous, uniform rusting of metal that occurred much faster than natural oxidation.Fuzzballs - Microscopic, iron rich spheres found in the dust, suggesting material was pulled apart at a molecular level.Spatter - Material that appeared to have been ‘splashed’ onto the sides of adjacent buildings at high speeds.Transmutation - The apparent alteration of a material’s molecular structure, such as finding wood fused into aluminium.On 9/11 the media repeatedly told us what to belie before a forensic investigation had even begun.  This loop of information created ‘perceptual conformity’ training us to ignore what was physically in front of us.Dr Wood’s unique vocabulary is an invitation to break that spell.  She isn’t offering a new theory to believe she is asking you to look at the evidence with fresh eyes and make up your own mind.When you see a building ‘unravelling like a sweater’ or ‘swiss cheese’ holes in parked cars, your eyes are witnessing a phenomena that conventional physics cannot explain as simple fire or collapse.  The question is - do you have the courage to look again and believe what your own eyes are telling you?‘If you listen to the evidence carefully enough, it will speak to you and tell you exactly what happened’. - Dr Judy Woodwheredidthetowersgo.comLeave a commentShare

You won't venture to offer an opinion but I will, without restraint.  No restraint, but reason, I hope.

The war is such folly that it breaks my heart.  

Obama's 'nuclear deal' included a payment of 1.7 billion dollars (see Stanford Law School blog:https://law.stanford.edu/2016/08/12/the-400-million-payment-to-iran-was-american-diplomacy-at-its-finest/).  This money included the release of funds withheld for Iran, + interest (see the same blog).  That deal included free access by the IAEA  to all Iran's nuclear facilities, both known and unknown.  If new activity was detected (easy enough to detect), the new sites could be inspected with 24 hours notice. There was no sunset provision in this agreement, no date on which Iran could resume development of a nuclear weapon. (See Obama White House blog: https://obamawhitehouse.archives.gov/node/343726). 

In a nutshell, Obama's deal neutralized *indefinitely* Iran's nuclear program and its ambitions. For 1.7 billion, much of which was money owed to Iran already.

What do we have now?  We have a war that may be costing as much as 2 billion dollars a day (see Harvard Kennedy School blog: https://obamawhitehouse.archives.gov/node/343726.  Also see Brown University's daily cost tracker: https://iran-cost-ticker.com/ ).  As you rightly state, we have a burden on taxpayers and consumers around the world that is growing daily and that is anticipated to continue growing.  

It's not just gas.  It's the cost of just about everything.  What about that promised cut in the Fed rate?  How does that look with inflation rising?

Then there is global instability. The breakdown of traditional alliances, already frayed by Trump before the war began. 

How much harm can one man do?  You wrote a previous blog about examples from world history where empires have fallen.  Where are we now in that historical perspective?

links.title: Qwen 3.6 Plus: Alibaba Deu um Passo Maior Que o Esperado
links.body:
Quando escrevemos sobre o Qwen 3 e o Qwen 3.5 em março, a Alibaba já havia mostrado que estava levando a competição em IA a sério. O Qwen 3.6 Plus, disponível a partir do final de março de 2026, é a confirmação de que a empresa não parou para comemorar. Ela continuou trabalhando.

## O que mudou do 3.5 para o 3.6

A atualização mais direta e mais impactante é o contexto de **1 milhão de tokens**. Isso representa o dobro do que o Qwen 3.5 oferecia, e coloca o modelo no mesmo patamar dos maiores do mercado nesse quesito.

Para ter uma referência prática: 1 milhão de tokens equivale a algo entre 700 e 800 mil palavras. São cerca de 10 livros de tamanho médio numa única sessão de processamento. Para tarefas que envolvem grandes volumes de dados — análise de código, contratos longos, pesquisa acadêmica, documentação técnica — essa capacidade elimina limitações que antes exigiam soluções alternativas complicadas.

## Benchmarks: cinco de oito

O Qwen 3.6 Plus empata ou vence em cinco das oito categorias principais nos benchmarks mais respeitados do setor, incluindo o LiveCodeBench (tarefas de programação em competições reais) e o SWE-bench (resolução de problemas reais de software no GitHub).

Isso o coloca lado a lado com modelos como o GPT-5.4 e o GLM-5.1 nas tarefas de código — que são, hoje, um dos indicadores mais confiáveis da capacidade geral de raciocínio de um modelo.

## Gratuito no OpenRouter

Um diferencial que chama atenção pela praticidade: o Qwen 3.6 Plus Preview está disponível gratuitamente no OpenRouter desde 30 de março. Sem chave de API. Sem barreira de entrada.

Para desenvolvedores que querem testar o modelo antes de decidir pela integração, ou para equipes que estão avaliando opções sem comprometer budget, isso reduz o atrito quase a zero. Você acessa, testa, e decide.

## Da família mais diversificada do mercado

O Qwen 3.6 Plus não existe sozinho. Ele faz parte de um ecossistema de modelos que vai do Qwen de 0,8 bilhão de parâmetros — projetado para rodar em dispositivos com pouca memória — até o Qwen com 397 bilhões de parâmetros.

Essa amplitude é rara. A maioria dos laboratórios lança dois ou três tamanhos. A Alibaba mantém uma progressão quase contínua, o que permite a diferentes tipos de aplicação usar o modelo mais adequado para o seu contexto: borda, servidor, nuvem, ou alta performance.

Todos os modelos da família Qwen são licenciados sob a **Apache 2.0**, que assim como a MIT, permite uso comercial livre, modificação e redistribuição sem restrições significativas.

## Foco em tarefas agentic

O 3.6 Plus foi desenvolvido com atenção especial para fluxos agentic — onde o modelo não apenas responde perguntas, mas executa tarefas encadeadas: consultar APIs, processar resultados, tomar decisões baseadas nos dados obtidos, e entregar um resultado final.

Esse tipo de uso está crescendo rapidamente. Cada vez mais empresas constroem sistemas onde o modelo age como um operador autônomo, não apenas como um assistente de texto. O contexto de 1 milhão de tokens ajuda diretamente nisso: tarefas longas e encadeadas exigem memória de contexto extensa para não perder o fio da meada.

## O que a Alibaba está construindo

O que o Qwen 3.6 Plus revela sobre a estratégia da Alibaba é interessante. A empresa não está tentando ter um único modelo campeão. Está construindo uma família consistente, acessível, bem licenciada e competitiva em benchmarks que importam.

É a aposta na escala e na distribuição, não apenas na performance de ponta. Para uma empresa com a presença global da Alibaba em e-commerce, nuvem e logística, ter modelos que empresas parceiras possam adotar livremente é um movimento estratégico tão importante quanto o desempenho técnico.

O Qwen 3.6 Plus é um modelo forte por conta própria. Como parte de uma família maior, é uma peça de um jogo bem mais longo.

links.title: Day 55: When the math isn't mathing
links.body:
#
Liquidity pools can be confusing

I like to think that I am well versed in how liquidity pools work on Tribaldex. I also like to think that I know a little about hive-engine, arbitrage and other financial stuff on Hive. But I will admit that sometimes things don't work as I think they should. Mostly I'm thinking about the GLD : Swap.LTC pool When I created the pool I placed exactly enough GLD and Swap.LTC in it to make sure that GLD had a price of $0.01 HBD. Essentially it is a HBD penny. It sat that way for a while. However, I knew that if LTC went up or down the overall value of the pool would go up or down and I had no control over that whatsoever. My idea was simple. If the value went up I would sell GLD into the pool and if the value went down I would sell LTC into the pool. Except I put in LTC and GLD went down... Huh? Why? Then I went to the pool this morning and the GLD coin was down to 0.007 cents? 30% under what I consider its PEG. Now holders can still exchange for 100:1 through my website/bot but I thought... Wow. LTC must have tanked for the GLD to go down that far. Except LTC went up.

#
Ok. To me that makes no sense

![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/cinderclaw.gld/23tw7oP4iZPdMfLkAvwLUANQdEafpqrBfsEkQ6sjLbQ28pSogGCERQjTtCZjjo7onrtdd.png) Here are the actual pool numbers GLD Value : $0.00827 <-- My goal is $0.01 Swap.LTC : $49.339 <-- Hmm... that looks off. I took a look at the price of LTC through Google and I got this ![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/cinderclaw.gld/23t8CfKjGpMgRUCQHQRBfHFyarX6qMpfHM4tEnQRF56XrvdD3gxGjMqUT7uatwWkNWGZF.png) ### Doing my own math. The pool has 8.168 swap.LTC in it. Each should be worth $55.67 **Total Value**: $454.65 The pool has 44637 GLD tokens if valued at $0.01 **Total Value**: $446.37 **Yes** I like that valuation. But just to look at it from a \

order on Tribaldex ![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/cinderclaw.gld/23tHbr9yn5m69WdnxLd3G3MG4ZqfDzT5CGQRtjRZ2uniqy8hq3fveHjoHL9avfxo8MXDw.png) **500 GLD gets 0.09025 LTC** $55.67 / LTC * 0.09025 LTC = **$ 5.02** Since I want 500 GLD to be worth **$5.02** I'm quite happy with someone getting **5.02** in value from their LTC. In that way the value is still there. **But why does Tribaldex only value the LTC at **49.34**

#
It makes little sense to me but....

I went to look at the HIVE to Swap.LTC conversion. Just for fun I looked at how much SWAP.LTC I would get for 100 HIVE ![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/cinderclaw.gld/23tHbr9ynYoKPZdridhJdVWhLHa6BSrTBrCSRMx731QemmYUvboHTGDGaF4zf2WhVSTmj.png) $ 55.67 / LTC * 0.1317 LTC = **$7.33** for those **100 HIVE** And how much does PeakD say HIVE at worth right now? ![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/cinderclaw.gld/23uFwMHhyP5U9sGJhoNFRRky1mCK3nvCHg8RPeGWWUJg1Q9rMt3GSbHtkMbe3EP6zhR9P.png) **So that matches also**

#
Which leaves me confused

### Really confused. ![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/cinderclaw.gld/23tmm5sZGoS9iq9EzFwTKaYhCFcSdDtEihQ8ux5KcSXmptiPyJQW9T9GgM3QoYAqbARSM.png) I mean if I look at this pool for swap.hive/swap.ltc it shows the LTC value at **$42.01**??? But...but....but.... ***I don't get it***
### Final thoughts? I just thought I would share this. Not because I can make sense of it but rather because I can't. If I was to ***guess*** I would say that the tribaldex site uses up to the minute pricing and arbitrage to make sure that things buy and sell for the right amount. That's why I can sell GLD and get the correct amount of LTC. That's why I can sell HIVE and get the right amount of LTC. Sure there is slippage but that's shown right in the buy and sell page. I have a feeling that the data on the pool is updated less frequently than the data for the trades. In that way when I look at the liquidity pool holdings they show me old data on the value of each token in HBD. ***Or I could be missing something altogether*** As always I'll keep watching and see if I can figure out this unsolved mystery but... For now I've said my peace about it. If someone reads this and knows better than I do? I'd love a comment. Thanks. ### Just as a final add on. I ran this through an AI which tells me that the values are correct through bots and arbitrage but the pool data is internally correct from the values it uses but not reflected in real world data. That seems a little fishy to me but.. maybe it makes sense and my brain doesn't get it... ***yet*** I'll do more thinking :)

links.title: The art of silent persuasion, a lesson from an Igbo trader encounter ~3094
links.body:
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmYgXwwAKSHRmanPn8vUMZUhH5FK6EcYzaGGRbWHQZgp1S/1778000087252.jpg)

An image of me

There’s one thing about the Igbos in Nigeria, the art of having the power of dominance and knowing the art of persuasion (convincing) and this is one of the reason I get close to them.

I didn’t plan to buy anything that day, in fact, I was only passing through the market, my mind fixed on getting one item and leaving as quickly as possible. But markets have a way of slowing you down and Igbo traders have a way of stopping you completely.

Fine girl, come and see quality stuffs, one voice called out. I ignored it, yet another voice followed, softer, almost friendly. No pressure, just check it. Looking is free, that's the line that got me hooked me, not because I believed it, but because of how effortlessly it was delivered so i turned.

The man smiled like he had known me for years, praising God's creation, before I could speak, he had already read my hesitation. You don’t need it now, I know but when you need it, you’ll remember you saw something better. That was the first move of convincing me, not selling the product, but planting the idea on my mind

I picked it up, casually and this Igbo trader didn’t rush me. Instead, he told a story of who bought it last week, how it lasted longer, why cheaper ones would disappoint me. Every word felt less like a pitch and more like an advice. That’s when I realised I was no longer just a passerby

Then came the comparison, he showed me two options, one average, one slightly better that is if  it’s me, I’ll go for this one but you choose. That subtle shift of control made it feel like my decision, even though he had already guided it.

I tried to leave, okay let me think about it, I said.

He laughed lightly, of course, think. But if you come back, price might change. Market no dey wait all of it was enough to make me pause.

Somehow, I stayed.

The negotiation began, not as a battle, but as a dance. He reduced the price before I even asked properly, because na you, ooo he added, as if I was special among hundreds.

Minutes later, I was walking away with the product I never intended to buy.

Halfway home, it hit me, I didn’t just buy an item, I bought into confidence, storytelling, patience, and strategy, that’s the art. Igbo traders don’t just sell goods, they sell belief, faith, skill, persuasion and love 

And the most fascinating part? 
You leave feeling like it was your idea all along.

# Unreleased CCTV Footage Captures Rodney Dickins and James Debeuneure at Dulles Airport on 9/11

**Source:** https://911planesresearch.substack.com/p/rodney-dickins-and-james-debeuneure

This is a short clip from Dulles Airport CCTV on 9/11, which captures Rodney Dickins and James Debeuneure. See below: Charlie Kallas shared privately a screen shot of the Dulles CCTV video identifying Rodney Dickins people. After seeing the screen-shot which Kallas sent me, I noticed James Debeuneure was also captured, at the baggage screening area. This prompted to find the piece of CCTV video footage, which I had, and share it here. Two further photographs shows Dickins and DebeuneureGwen Faulkner took two photographs which captured passengers at Dulles Airport on 9/11. Faulkner took photographs of some school children and their teachers along with two National Geographic representatives. The children had won a National Geographic competition, and were on a trip organized by National Geographic as the prize to participate in a National Geographic ‘Photo Camp’ in Channel Islands National Marine Sanctuary, sponsored by NOAA’s Office of National Marine Sanctuaries. Washington, D.C. Dickins and Debeuneure are captured on the left of the photograph. A Study of American 77 Passengers & Aircraft Telemetry DataIn this article, I am going collate evidence I obtained which showed passengers who were captured at Dulles Airport who “allegedly” boarded American 77 on 9/11. I will also study previous aircraft telemetry data evidence, and piece together what really happened to American 77 and its “alleged” passengers.Thanks for reading and caring!

links.body: > Hello my lovely people, how is the new month going for you all? I wish you guys all the best and for this week's prompt I would be going with the first topic which says: what was is that you clung to tightly either an ideal, a person or a stage of life that life forced you to let go of? What was the emotional process of accepting that it was no longer part of your present?

> So I would like to go with that stage of life. That stage of life that I clung to was and is still my best and sweetest part of my life so far, you know that stage where you have nothing to worry about, that stage where all your headaches are just for coming back to wash your school uniform or doing your assignment or even having a quarrel with your friends or boyfriend, that stage where you just want to go out and do all the yawo in the whole wide world and leave your mother in the kitchen to do the chores, that stage where you have all those high school boys tripping and falling heads over heels in love with you, that stage where you are in competition with your friends on how many movies you have watched or how many story books you have read, that stage where your own is to just cook, eat, play and gossip with your peers. Yess that's the stage that i clung to and struggled to let go, infact I was so much consumed in that stage that I grew up and still had that childish, carefree/careless and playful plus my childish face complimented the whole thing, if you had met the before me you would agree with me that I haven't Sha seen life, and then that self of mine blocked alot of things like good connections, reasonable friends, a responsible me and lots more but when life happened to me in a very hard way according to my perspective, I had to let go. I think letting isn't just the problem here but having to live without what you have been used to living with before, it's more like reality dawning on you even when you refuse to accept it. You know that situation where you lost someone very close to you, you have being crying and all of that but to you, you are just waiting for a situation where you expect them to tell you it's a prank or that the person rose up to live but then when you get to see that person lying down in a coffin about to be laid six feet down, it's then you would realize that it's real. We never pray for days like that but we can't just do without it because sometimes it's just our pushing force to growth. This is my que to leave so do have a lovely day ahead. All images used here belongs to me.

links.title: To Have and to Hold
links.body: Most likely some of you are going to smile and scroll through my post, thinking I want to preach about marriage vows. It's ok if you do that, no problem, but this post is going to have nothing with it. It's about something else. \n\nLast night I was thinking of this so called \

mentality and the consequences of it and decided to put my words on paper, or on the blockchain, to be precise, which is better than paper, as a storing method. It's been on my mind for some time and now that I'm  still in the process of selling everything I don't need, it's a good lesson for the future. 

![tuaans-PRet1VEonso-unsplash.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/erikah/2432QW32gZHrZi33qNVwaeB64ZmZtZLLdj7TLWq2nCQ1og5jiW81DTB7J34YZCnMY6xax.jpg)
Photo by <a href=\

>Unsplash During this process, I came across a lot of things that honestly, I didn't even think I still have. Some items have never been used as those have bee put aside, to have later. Now comes the question, when is late? As that time has not come yet it seems as I've never used those items. Lucky me, I only have one or two of these, mostly expensive glass and porcelain, but I've seen this mentality so many times. Without having statistics to back my theory up, still, I think you see this mentality at those limited financially. Buy something of value, to have and then never use it as it's saved for better occasions, that may never come, or let's say, there's no occasion that worth using it. Why? The fear of breaking it, losing it has a lot to do with it. ![atul-pandey-pCS5gimk5B8-unsplash.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/erikah/23wC1Zbav4S2kCW87gn2KDmKXwh6GfPxLVP4EYDgKjJaDR7cSSaWqoMoqRTSD67Y9ip2R.jpg) Photo by

>Unsplash I've seen so many do this, with china, clothes and some with a part of the house, which is even worse. Imagine building a house and never use the rooms as those are meant to be preserved ... to have them clean and new, while they were living in a single room. Clothes have been kept in the drawer, worn only on occasions, till those didn't fit anymore. It's a question of mentality, which has a justification, to some extent, but when you think deeper, you can see you end up not using a good part of your belongings, and when I say not using them, in some cases it means at all. ![clay-banks-3qaMytIyx0c-unsplash.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/erikah/23u6BsUb5pWXvSvRWW5o2VbqFKGRsmDbdKMN4B63G948EaqyFP1wwNiVjnagVMjKuVhn5.jpg) I was raised to think like that, but not in the strictest way. However, over the years, if you have an open mind and learn what's important for you and your well being, you can decide for yourself and live your life as you see fit. For me, this mentality has a very negative effect and it causes more pressure on me, than joy. Storing things you rarely use is just going to restrict your living space and also means spending money on things unnecessarily, so it's not a viable option, or one that I should choose. Times have changed a lot for our generation and the ones after us as well, even more. Mindset has to change as well, if you don't want to live stuck in the past. I don't for sure. Change is the only certain thing in life and I'd say change is good. Some items are to keep, others have their role in our lives and that role can change too. Letting go is part of the process. Learning to let go is crucial, if you want to evolve. Finding a healthy balance between keeping and letting go is the key in this game. We all have an emotional baggage, that we carry with us over the years, but the size of it depends on us. I can only speak for myself but the faster you change and adapt, the better. ![mike-hindle-2jyGcCJKPrQ-unsplash.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/erikah/23t7mWE36WKmKgk17Uiy7vkWaArYP1Br1GBofcX3msVJUoSzn8La5Th9BjzerDACZdYYQ.jpg) Photo by

>Unsplash I'm wondering if what I'm saying makes sense at all, or I'm the only one seeing things this way? Dunno. Let me know in a comment. I think I owe you an explanation regarding these photos, that most of the time have nothing to do with the topic of the post 😆 Yes, that's right, I select them based on what I like and find interesting. For so many years I've been using my photos for these posts, that also rarely had anything to do with the topic, but now I use Unsplash. For me it's a lot of fun to just scroll through the collection of photos the platform offers and pick so many amazing short. I will never be able to take such shuts, or the most of it anyway. So there you go, you have the explanation, mystery sold.

links.title: Celebrating Sobriety: Recovery Milestones Across New Jersey
links.body:
## Introduction: The Meaning of Sobriety in New Jersey’s Recovery Landscape

Sobriety in New Jersey is more than abstaining from substances; it represents a structured journey of rebuilding health, relationships, and identity. Across the state, individuals in recovery engage in a wide network of clinical programs, peer groups, and community-based initiatives designed to support long-term healing.

New Jersey’s recovery ecosystem reflects a growing understanding that addiction is a chronic condition rather than a short-term crisis. As a result, recovery milestones are increasingly used to measure progress, reinforce accountability, and celebrate transformation.

## Understanding Recovery Milestones

Recovery milestones serve as psychological and behavioral markers that help individuals track their progress. These milestones often include time-based achievements such as 24 hours, 30 days, 90 days, and one year of sobriety.

### Emotional and Physical Stages of Recovery

Early recovery typically involves physical stabilization followed by emotional recalibration. Individuals may experience mood fluctuations, cravings, or renewed clarity as the body adjusts to functioning without substances. Over time, emotional resilience improves, and cognitive patterns begin to stabilize.

### Why Milestones Matter in Long-Term Sobriety

Milestones provide structure in a process that can otherwise feel uncertain. They also reinforce positive reinforcement loops, which are essential in behavior change psychology. Celebrating progress helps individuals internalize success rather than focus solely on setbacks.

## Early Recovery: The First Days and Weeks

The first stage of sobriety is often the most fragile. During this period, individuals may undergo detoxification, begin counseling, and establish initial routines that support stability.

### Detox, Stability, and Early Challenges

Detox can be physically and emotionally demanding. Symptoms vary depending on substance history, but support from medical professionals can significantly reduce risks. Early stabilization often includes hydration, sleep restoration, and emotional monitoring.

### Building Initial Support Systems

At this stage, support systems are critical. Family involvement, inpatient programs, and peer mentors often play a stabilizing role. Establishing routine check-ins and structured environments can help reduce relapse risk during early recovery.

## Medical Support and Treatment Landscape in New Jersey

New Jersey offers a wide range of treatment options, including outpatient clinics, inpatient rehabilitation centers, and Medication-Assisted Treatment (MAT) programs. These services aim to combine medical care with behavioral therapy.

### Access to Medication-Assisted Treatment (MAT)

MAT has become a cornerstone of opioid recovery in New Jersey. It integrates medications with counseling to reduce cravings and withdrawal symptoms. This approach is widely used in both urban and suburban treatment centers across the state.

### Role of Clinical Supervision and Counseling

Therapy and clinical supervision remain essential components of structured recovery. Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), group counseling, and trauma-informed care help individuals address underlying causes of substance use while building coping mechanisms.

### Understanding Medication Pathways in Recovery

In some discussions about treatment options, individuals explore questions like [How Fast Does Snorting Suboxone Kick In?](https://www.choicepointhealth.com/how-fast-does-snorting-suboxone-kick-in/) as part of broader curiosity about medication effects and misuse risks. While medical professionals strongly caution against non-prescribed or improper use, these conversations highlight the importance of education in recovery environments.

## Community Support and Peer Recovery Networks

Recovery in New Jersey is deeply supported by community-based networks that provide emotional connection and accountability. These groups often complement clinical treatment by offering lived experience and ongoing encouragement.

### Recovery Meetings and Sober Communities

Support groups such as 12-step programs and non-religious recovery circles are widely available throughout the state. These meetings help individuals share experiences, reduce isolation, and build long-term coping strategies.

### Family Involvement in Healing

Family participation can significantly improve recovery outcomes. Education programs and family therapy sessions help loved ones understand addiction dynamics and rebuild trust over time.

## Navigating Treatment Access and Insurance in New Jersey

Access to treatment is often influenced by insurance coverage, location, and available providers. New Jersey has expanded access through public health initiatives and telehealth services.

### Public vs. Private Treatment Pathways

Public programs often provide low-cost or state-funded treatment options, while private facilities may offer more specialized or intensive services. Both pathways can be effective depending on individual needs and circumstances.

### Telehealth and Digital Recovery Tools

Telehealth has become a significant part of modern recovery care. Virtual counseling sessions, mobile recovery apps, and online support groups provide flexible access to treatment resources, especially for individuals balancing work or family obligations.

### Accessing Support and Clinical Guidance

For many individuals navigating treatment options, resources such as [Online Suboxone Doctors That Accept Medicaid](https://www.choicepointhealth.com/online-suboxone-doctors-that-accept-medicaid/) have expanded access to care. These services help connect patients with licensed providers who can offer evaluations, prescriptions, and ongoing support through accessible digital platforms.

Immediately after exploring treatment accessibility, it becomes clear that reliable, evidence-based information is essential in recovery planning. For additional context on structured recovery systems and national behavioral health resources, more information is available at[ https://www.samhsa.gov/recovery](https://www.samhsa.gov/recovery).

## Celebrating Milestones: 30, 60, 90 Days, and Beyond

Milestones in sobriety provide moments of reflection and recognition. Each stage represents a shift in physical health, emotional stability, and behavioral consistency.

### Recognizing Progress in Structured Recovery

At 30 days, individuals often begin to experience improved clarity and energy. By 60 and 90 days, emotional regulation typically strengthens, and new habits begin to feel more natural. One-year milestones are especially significant, symbolizing sustained commitment and transformation.

Celebrations may include recovery tokens, ceremonies, or private reflections. These moments reinforce identity change—shifting from substance use to long-term recovery.

## Long-Term Sobriety and Reintegration into Daily Life

Sustained sobriety extends beyond structured treatment. It involves rebuilding a meaningful life that supports ongoing wellness and personal growth.

### Employment, Relationships, and Purpose

Many individuals in long-term recovery return to work, pursue education, or rebuild family relationships. Purpose-driven living is often a key factor in maintaining sobriety over time.

### Maintaining Recovery Momentum Over Years

Long-term recovery requires ongoing effort. Continued participation in support groups, therapy, or community service helps maintain accountability. Many individuals also become mentors, contributing to the recovery community that once supported them.

## Conclusion

Celebrating sobriety in New Jersey is not just about marking time—it is about recognizing transformation. From early detox to long-term reintegration, each milestone reflects resilience, support, and personal growth. As recovery systems continue to evolve across the state, individuals are finding more pathways than ever to build sustainable, fulfilling lives in sobriety.

body.title: The Anatomy of a Graco Fluid Section: What Every Part Does and Why Each One Fails
body.body:
![The Anatomy of a Graco Fluid Section: What Every Part Does and Why Each One Fails](https://waivio.nyc3.digitaloceanspaces.com/ef59219452b9e92bf1c6e6d1e854db6d4db8cc8a8b12985c3a3fa534c9ba008e)



**By SprayersAndParts.com Technical Team Published April 2026 · 14 min read · Category: Equipment Education | Technical Deep Dives**

Most painting contractors have a working relationship with their sprayer that goes something like this: the machine does what it's supposed to until it doesn't, at which point they look for whatever failed. This approach works — eventually — but it produces reactive repairs rather than proactive maintenance, and it means every failure is a surprise.

The alternative is understanding what every part inside the fluid section actually does, and why each one fails the way it does. A contractor who knows that a stuck inlet ball is caused by a different mechanism than worn packings — and that both produce \

as their symptom — can diagnose a Monday morning failure in three minutes instead of thirty.

This article is a complete component-by-component reference for the Graco Endurance displacement pump fluid section found in the 390, 395, 490, 495, and 595 class contractor machines. Every part is explained: its function, its materials, its failure mechanism, and the symptom it produces when it fails. The goal is to give you a mental model of the fluid section accurate enough that you can diagnose problems by reasoning about what's happening rather than working through a checklist by elimination.

***

## The Big Picture: What the Fluid Section Does

Before component-by-component detail, it helps to hold the whole system in mind.

The fluid section is a reciprocating positive-displacement pump. A motor drives a crankshaft mechanism that moves a piston rod up and down inside a cylinder. On the upstroke, the rising rod creates a partial vacuum in the cylinder below it, which pulls paint upward from the bucket through the inlet valve. On the downstroke, the rod descends and the volume it occupies displaces paint upward through the outlet valve and into the hose.

Two check valves — the inlet at the bottom of the pump and the outlet above the piston — alternate open and closed in opposition. When the inlet is open, the outlet is closed. When the outlet is open, the inlet is closed. This sequencing ensures that on every stroke, fluid moves in one direction: up from the bucket, through the pump, out to the hose.

The packings form a dynamic seal around the moving piston rod, preventing paint from bypassing the piston rather than going up the hose, and preventing air from being drawn down past the throat on the intake stroke. The prime/drain valve provides a controlled bypass path for priming and pressure relief. The packing nut and TSL cup lubricate and protect the rod-to-packing interface.

Every failure mode in the fluid section traces back to one of these mechanisms either wearing out, getting contaminated, or losing its sealing geometry. What follows is the story of each component in that system.



***

## Component 1: The Cylinder

What it is: The cylinder is the outer housing of the fluid section — the steel tube within which everything else operates. On Graco's Endurance pump used in the 395, 490, and 595 class machines, the cylinder is hardened stainless steel, sized to extremely tight dimensional tolerances. The bore surface finish matters: the cylinder's interior must be smooth enough that the piston packings can form a reliable seal against it.

What it does: The cylinder provides the pressure vessel that contains the 3,300 PSI working pressure. It also provides the sealing surface for the throat packings at the top and houses the sleeve and piston assembly throughout the stroke. The dimensional accuracy of the bore — its roundness and surface finish — directly determines how well the packings seal.

How it fails: The cylinder fails through scoring — longitudinal scratches or grooves cut into the bore surface by abrasive contamination. When paint that hasn't been strained reaches the fluid section, pigment particles, dried paint flakes, and debris pass between the piston rod and the cylinder bore. At 3,300 PSI operating pressure, these particles act like lapping compound. Over time, they grind linear grooves into the bore surface.

A scored cylinder bore creates a path for fluid to bypass the piston packings along the groove channels, regardless of how new and correctly installed the packings are. This is the failure mode that explains why a machine that was rebuilt with fresh packings still cycles rapidly or won't hold pressure — the new packings are sealing against a scored bore that has channels the piston packings can't close.

The symptom of a scored cylinder is a machine that doesn't respond adequately to packing replacement. Cylinder replacement or replacement of the complete pump cartridge is the correct repair.

Prevention: Strain all materials before loading the pump. Keep the inlet strainer clean. Replace the manifold filter on schedule. The cylinder's lifespan is directly proportional to how clean the material flowing through it is.



***

## Component 2: The Sleeve

What it is: The sleeve is the inner liner that sits inside the cylinder bore and provides the immediate sealing surface for the piston packings. On Graco Endurance pumps, the sleeve is a separate component from the cylinder body — this design allows the sleeve to be replaced independently if it becomes worn, rather than replacing the entire cylinder housing.

What it does: The sleeve's inner surface is the surface that the piston rod and piston packings ride against. Its dimensional accuracy and surface finish are critical to packing seal quality. The sleeve also provides guidance for the piston rod throughout the stroke.

How it fails: Like the cylinder, the sleeve fails through abrasive scoring. Its inner surface can develop grooves from contaminated materials flowing through. Additionally, the sleeve can become fouled with dried paint residue if the machine is stored without proper flushing — paint that dries on the sleeve surface creates an abrasive layer that damages new packings from the first stroke.

Graco's documented maintenance note: Graco's repair manuals specifically call out removing and cleaning the sleeve during every repacking service. This instruction is often skipped in rushed field rebuilds, and it's a significant omission: a sleeve with dried paint accumulation on its inner surface will damage new packings within hours of installation.



***

## Component 3: The Piston Rod

What it is: The piston rod is the central moving element of the fluid section — the steel shaft that reciprocates through the cylinder bore, creating suction on the upstroke and displacing fluid on the downstroke. On Graco's Endurance pump design, the piston rod uses Chromex treatment — a proprietary surface hardening process that Graco describes as providing twice the service life of untreated rods under identical operating conditions.

The Chromex treatment creates an extremely hard outer surface layer that is highly resistant to the abrasive wear produced by pigment particles and dried paint residue at the packing interface.

What it does: The piston rod transmits the mechanical force from the drive mechanism to the fluid. Its diameter determines the displacement volume per stroke — a larger diameter rod displaces more fluid per stroke at equivalent stroke length. The rod must maintain tight dimensional tolerances along its full length to work correctly with the packing stack. Even minor surface damage along the rod creates a path for fluid to bypass the packings.

How it fails: Piston rods fail through surface damage at the packing interface zone. The most common damage mechanism is running the machine with a dry TSL cup — when the wet cup runs dry, the throat packings contact the rod without lubrication, and the abrasive pigments in paint act directly on the rod surface at the packing contact zone. This produces fine circumferential scratching that progressively worsens and eventually creates enough leakage to show paint at the packing nut.

Rods also fail from corrosion when machines are stored with water in the fluid section without Pump Armor. The piston rod's exposed section — the portion that sits above the packing nut when the rod is at the top of its stroke — is vulnerable to rust if stored improperly. Rust on the rod creates roughness that damages packings and eventually scores the cylinder bore.

Graco's documented procedure for rod storage: Park the rod in the down position after the last use of each day, keeping the exposed rod section inside the pump. Fill the TSL cup before shutdown.



***

## Component 4: The Piston Valve and Piston Check Ball

What it is: The piston valve is the threaded assembly at the lower end of the piston rod. Inside it sits the piston check ball — a stainless steel sphere, 5/16 inch diameter on most machines in this class, that acts as the upper check valve in the fluid section.

What it does: On the downstroke, as the piston rod descends, the piston check ball opens (lifts off its seat) and allows fluid to be displaced upward through the piston valve assembly and out to the outlet port. On the upstroke, as the rod rises and creates suction below, the piston check ball seats (closes) and prevents fluid from being drawn back down through the piston. This keeps the suction effective — all the vacuum created by the rising rod works to pull paint up through the inlet, not recirculate fluid back through the piston.

How it fails: The piston check ball and its seat fail primarily through two mechanisms. First, abrasive wear: the ball cycles against its seat at the pump's strokes per minute across hundreds of hours of operation, and even tungsten carbide seats and stainless balls wear over time, developing slightly imperfect seating geometry. Second, debris on the seat: a single particle lodged between the ball and seat prevents full closure, causing a constant bypass leak on the downstroke.

The symptom of piston check failure is a machine that runs but can't build full pressure, where the symptoms appeared gradually over time (wear) or suddenly (debris contamination). The machine may prime and move paint, but the pressure available at the gun is lower than it should be, and the motor cycles more frequently.

Critical maintenance note from Graco's official documentation: The piston valve threads are treated with a factory thread-locking patch. Graco explicitly warns in every relevant repair manual: \

This warning is widely ignored in DIY rebuilds and YouTube tutorials. A loose piston valve inside an operating pump is a catastrophic failure.



***

## Component 5: The Piston Packings

What they are: The piston packings are the seals mounted on the piston rod itself — the stack of leather and UHMW-PE V-packings that create the dynamic seal between the pressurised lower fluid section and the returning rod. In the 18B260 kit, the piston packing stack consists of a combination of leather V-packings and UHMW-PE (ultra-high-molecular-weight polyethylene) V-packings alternating with metal glands that maintain the stack geometry.

The V-shape of these packings matters: the lips of V-packings face toward the pressure direction, so that operating pressure itself helps press the sealing lips outward against the bore surface. The higher the pressure, the more tightly the packings seal — the design is self-energising.

What they do: The piston packings prevent the high-pressure fluid below the piston from bypassing around the rod rather than going up the outlet. On a machine in good condition, the piston packings create a seal tight enough that essentially all of the fluid volume displaced by the rod on the downstroke goes up the hose — nothing bypasses around the rod.

How they fail: Piston packings fail through three mechanisms. Abrasive wear is the primary mechanism — paint pigments and dried paint particles passing through the fluid section at high velocity gradually abrade the packing lips and reduce their dimensional precision. Deformation is the second mechanism — V-packings that are installed dry (without oil soak for leather, without grease for the stack) or over-compressed by an over-torqued packing nut can take a permanent set that prevents them from returning to their sealing geometry. The third mechanism is chemical degradation — certain solvents, particularly some oil-based paint thinners, are incompatible with specific packing materials and cause swelling or breakdown.

The early symptom of worn piston packings is a machine that cycles more frequently than it used to at the same pressure setting — the motor restarts within 10 seconds of trigger release rather than the 15–20 seconds that indicates a properly sealed system. As wear advances, the machine cycles continuously at low pressure, and eventually paint appears at the packing nut.



***

## Component 6: The Throat Packings and Glands

What they are: The throat packings are a separate set of seals from the piston packings — they sit in the throat of the cylinder (the top bore, where the piston rod exits the cylinder) rather than on the piston rod itself. In the 18B260 kit, the throat packings are leather V-packings and UHMW-PE elements stacked with metal glands in the cylinder throat.

What they do: Where the piston packings seal the rod inside the fluid section against downward bypass, the throat packings seal the rod at the exit point — preventing paint from following the rod upward out of the fluid section during the downstroke. They also prevent air from being drawn down into the fluid section during the upstroke.

Think of the function this way: the piston packings keep paint below the piston from bypassing up around the rod. The throat packings keep paint from leaking out of the top of the cylinder when the pressurised fluid section pushes against the rod. Both sets are necessary to maintain the pressure integrity of the system.

How they fail: Throat packings fail identically to piston packings — abrasive wear, deformation, or chemical degradation. The specific symptom of throat packing failure is paint weeping upward at the packing nut area (the wet cup housing at the top of the pump), visible as paint on the exterior of the packing nut or dripping from the lower motor housing. This is the classic \

failure that every experienced contractor recognises as the signal for immediate packing replacement.

The throat packings also fail faster when the TSL cup runs dry. TSL directly lubricates the throat packing area — it's pooled in the wet cup right at the throat packing's contact zone. A dry TSL cup means throat packings running without lubrication, accelerating wear dramatically.



***

## Component 7: The Packing Nut and TSL Wet Cup

What it is: The packing nut is the threaded steel collar at the top of the fluid section that compresses the throat packing stack to the correct sealing tension. Inside the packing nut is the wet cup — the small reservoir that holds TSL.

What it does: The packing nut has two jobs that must both be done correctly simultaneously. It must compress the throat packings enough to create an effective seal around the rod. It must not compress them so much that friction from the packings becomes excessive or that the packings deform permanently. This is why Graco specifies a torque value for the packing nut (100 +/- 10 inch-pounds for most machines in this class) rather than a tactile instruction like \

The wet cup continuously feeds TSL to the throat packing-rod interface. Every time the rod strokes downward, it draws a thin film of TSL down into the contact zone. This film reduces friction, dissolves and carries away any paint residue that migrates upward, and keeps the leather packings supple.

How it fails: The packing nut fails two ways. First, it can be incorrectly torqued — too loose, and paint bypasses the throat packings and appears at the nut exterior; too tight, and the packings are over-compressed and wear at an accelerated rate. Second, the TSL cup can run dry, which is not a nut failure but a maintenance failure that causes premature packing wear.

The daily maintenance habit that preserves the packing nut system: check the TSL level every morning before the first stroke, and top up to the fill line. On high-production days in hot climates, check at midday as well. TSL evaporates faster in heat, and a hot summer day of continuous spraying can empty the cup before a full day is done.



***

## Component 8: The Inlet Check Valve (Foot Valve)

What it is: The inlet check valve — sometimes called the foot valve or intake valve — is the assembly at the very bottom of the pump where the suction tube connects. It contains a check ball (stainless steel, 1/2 inch diameter on most machines in this class) seated against a tungsten carbide seat, and is housed in a threaded housing that screws into the cylinder body.

What it does: The inlet check valve is the entry point for paint into the fluid section. On the upstroke, the rising piston rod creates suction below, which lifts the inlet check ball off its seat and allows paint to flow upward from the bucket through the inlet valve and into the cylinder. On the downstroke, when the rod descends and pressure builds in the lower cylinder, the inlet check ball is pressed down onto its seat and prevents paint from flowing back down to the bucket — instead, the pressure pushes paint up through the piston.

How it fails: The inlet check valve fails through three mechanisms.

The most common is the stuck ball — the inlet check ball sitting against its seat for a period of storage without Pump Armor develops a slight adhesion from dried paint residue around the contact zone. When the machine is started, the motor cycles normally but no paint is drawn up because the ball can't lift. This is why the hammer-tap technique (tapping the inlet valve housing while running on PRIME) sometimes frees the machine — the vibration breaks the adhesion.

The second failure mechanism is seat wear — the tungsten carbide seat develops wear marks at the ball contact circle over hundreds of thousands of seating cycles. When the contact circle becomes uneven from wear, the ball no longer seats cleanly, and paint bleeds back through the inlet on the downstroke. The machine can prime but can't build or hold pressure because every downstroke partially recirculates paint back to the bucket rather than pushing it up the hose.

The third mechanism is debris on the seat — a single particle lodged between the ball and seat prevents closure, producing the same symptom as wear. The 239922 inlet valve kit includes new seat, ball, and O-rings for complete replacement.



***

## Component 9: The Outlet Check Valve

What it is: The outlet check valve sits above the piston assembly in the pump body, between the cylinder and the outlet port that connects to the hose. It contains a check ball (smaller than the inlet ball — 5/16 inch diameter on most machines) and a tungsten carbide seat, assembled into the pump body in the area directly above where the piston rod's downstroke creates pressure.

What it does: On the downstroke, as the piston descends and pressure builds in the fluid section, the outlet check ball is pushed upward off its seat, allowing paint to flow out through the outlet port to the hose. On the upstroke, as pressure drops in the lower cylinder and suction draws paint in through the inlet, the outlet check ball drops back onto its seat, preventing the pressurised paint already in the hose from flowing back into the pump.

The outlet check valve and inlet check valve together create the one-way flow that makes the pump work as a pump rather than just a piston moving back and forth in a sealed cylinder.

How it fails: The outlet check valve fails identically to the inlet — seat wear and debris contamination. A seat with wear marks or debris can't close cleanly, allowing pressurised paint in the hose to bleed back into the pump on every upstroke. The symptom is the same as worn packings: the motor cycles more frequently than it should, because pressure bleeds down faster than a correctly sealing system would allow.

The diagnostic distinction between outlet valve failure and packing failure: if the machine cycles rapidly but primes normally and builds pressure initially before losing it, the problem is more likely outlet valve or packing bypass than inlet valve failure. The inlet valve failing typically presents as inability to prime at all, rather than inability to hold pressure after priming.



***

## Component 10: The Prime/Drain Valve

What it is: The prime/drain valve — sold as the 235014 kit for most machines in the 390–595 class — is the rotary valve mounted in the pump body that the operator switches between PRIME and SPRAY modes. It contains a valve body with a precisely shaped port, a cam mechanism operated by the handle knob, and sealing components including O-rings and the valve seat.

What it does: In PRIME mode, the valve opens a bypass path that routes paint from the pump outlet back to the return tube and down to the bucket. This allows the pump to circulate paint freely during priming without building pressure in the hose, making it easier to establish consistent fluid flow before switching to spray mode.

In SPRAY mode, the valve closes the bypass path, forcing all pump output up the hose to the gun. This is where pressure builds and spray happens.

The valve also functions as a pressure relief device — if system pressure exceeds safe limits due to a blockage, the prime valve provides a path for pressure to release back to the bucket rather than building to a dangerous level.

How it fails: The prime valve fails when its seating surface wears or when debris prevents complete closure in SPRAY mode. A prime valve that leaks internally in SPRAY position creates a bypass path that competes with the hose for pump output — paint that should be going up the hose is instead bleeding back to the bucket.

The symptom is a machine that primes easily but can't reach adequate spray pressure, cycling constantly without building. This symptom is identical to worn packings in how it presents, which is why the diagnostic sequence matters: check the prime valve under load before concluding the packings need replacement.

Graco's product description for the 235014 kit states directly: \

The prime valve is also physically exposed — the handle knob gets knocked, paint accumulates in the cam mechanism, and the pin that secures the knob can corrode and seize. Unlike the check valves, the prime valve has externally accessible components that can be cleaned and serviced without full pump disassembly.



***

## Component 11: The Manifold Block

What it is: The manifold block — the main pump body to which all fluid section components mount — is the structural and hydraulic centre of the fluid section. On Graco contractor machines, the manifold includes the outlet port that connects to the hose, the prime valve port, the manifold filter housing, and the pressure transducer port (on SmartControl models).

What it does: The manifold provides the fluid passages that connect the pump's outlet to the hose connection and the prime valve bypass. It also houses the manifold filter — the mesh strainer screen that catches debris after it exits the pump but before it enters the hose. This is the last filtration point before the hose, gun filter, and tip.

How it fails: The manifold itself rarely fails under normal conditions — it's a machined steel block. The manifold filter it houses fails regularly: it accumulates debris from the material being sprayed and progressively restricts flow. A partially clogged manifold filter produces pressure drop between the pump outlet and the gun, which presents as the machine running but unable to deliver adequate spray pressure at the tip.

The manifold filter is the first thing to inspect on any \

complaint — before packings, before valves, before anything else. It takes 60 seconds to check and it's responsible for an outsized proportion of mid-job pressure complaints.



***

## Component 12: The Inlet Strainer

What it is: The inlet strainer is the mesh filter screen at the base of the suction tube where paint first enters the fluid section. It is the system's first line of defence against debris entering the pump at all.

What it does: The inlet strainer catches paint chunks, skin from the top of improperly sealed buckets, dried paint flakes, and any other particulate before it reaches the inlet check valve. A clean inlet strainer allows full flow. A clogged inlet strainer restricts the volume of paint that can reach the pump on each intake stroke.

How it fails: The inlet strainer fails through clogging — paint skin, dried paint flakes, and debris from improperly strained material accumulate in the mesh. A clogged strainer causes exactly the same symptom as a stuck inlet ball: the machine runs but won't prime, because insufficient material reaches the pump inlet. The diagnostic distinction is simple: remove the strainer and inspect it. If it's clean and the machine still won't prime, the problem is elsewhere. If it's clogged, cleaning it resolves the issue.

Strainers also fail through damage to the mesh — if the mesh is torn, debris passes directly into the pump with nothing to stop it. Any strainer with a torn mesh should be replaced immediately, not returned to service after cleaning.



***

## Component 13: The O-Rings

What they are: The fluid section contains multiple O-rings at connection points throughout the fluid path — at the jam nut connection where the suction tube joins the pump inlet, at the cylinder base, around the packing nut, and at the outlet port connection. The 18B260 packing kit includes replacement O-rings in both Viton and PTFE formulations, matched to their specific installation positions.

What they do: O-rings create static seals at connection points — sealing the fluid path at threaded joints and housing interfaces where dynamic sealing isn't required. The distinction between O-rings and packings is that packings seal against moving surfaces (the rod) while O-rings seal against stationary surfaces (threads and housing interfaces).

How they fail: O-rings fail through compression set — they deform permanently after sustained compression and no longer return to their original round cross-section when pressure is released. A compression-set O-ring can't fill its groove completely and allows fluid to bypass. O-rings also fail from chemical incompatibility — Graco specifies Viton O-rings in positions where contact with oil-based solvents is possible, and PTFE O-rings in positions requiring the highest chemical inertness.

The symptom of O-ring failure is a fluid leak at a connection point — visible dripping or paint accumulation at a fitting or joint that was previously dry. O-ring replacement is one of the easiest fluid section repairs: remove the fitting, extract the old O-ring with a pick, clean the groove, install the new O-ring, and reassemble.



***

## Putting It Together: The Wear Hierarchy

Understanding these components individually matters less than understanding how they wear relative to each other — because this hierarchy tells you what to inspect first and what to replace last.

Wears first (highest turnover, maintain proactively):

Tips, gun filters, manifold filters, and inlet strainers wear or clog fastest. These are consumables in the truest sense — tips based on material volume, filters based on job frequency and material abrasiveness. These items should be on the truck in quantity and replaced without hesitation.

Wears next (service interval maintenance):

Packings — both throat and piston — wear at a rate determined by hours of use, material abrasiveness, TSL discipline, and packing quality. For a contractor machine doing moderate residential work in water-based latex, expect 200–400 hours of reliable service per packing set. The 18B260 kit is the scheduled maintenance part for this wear tier.

Wears alongside packings (replace simultaneously):

The inlet valve seat and ball wear at a comparable rate to packings. Replacing the inlet valve kit (239922) at every packing replacement adds modest cost and avoids the failure that causes a priming problem on Monday morning three months after a packing rebuild.

Wears more slowly (replace when symptomatic):

The prime valve (235014), the outlet check valve components, and O-rings throughout the fluid path wear on a longer cycle than packings. They are worth replacing at packing rebuild intervals on high-hour machines, and worth replacing immediately when their characteristic symptoms appear.

Structural components (inspect, don't routinely replace):

The cylinder, sleeve, piston rod, and manifold block are structural components designed to outlast multiple packing service intervals. Inspect them at each rebuild for scoring, surface damage, and dimensional integrity. Replace them when they show damage, not on a routine schedule.



***

## The Quick-Reference Failure Map

For rapid field diagnosis, here is the symptom-to-component connection:

Won't prime → Inlet strainer (check first, 60 seconds), inlet valve ball stuck (tap housing), air leak on suction side (listen for air sounds, look for bubbles in return tube), worn packings, prime valve leak in PRIME mode

Primes but won't hold pressure in SPRAY → Gun filter (check immediately), manifold filter, prime valve leaking in SPRAY position, outlet check valve not seating, worn piston packings

Cycles too fast → Worn throat or piston packings (primary cause), outlet check valve not seating, prime valve internal bypass

Paint at packing nut → Throat packings worn — service immediately, don't continue running

Gradual pressure loss over weeks → Piston packings wearing, inlet valve seat wear, outlet valve seat wear

Machine rebuilt, still doesn't seal → Scored cylinder bore (new packings can't seal against grooves), piston packings installed in wrong orientation, packing nut over or under-torqued, sleeve not cleaned at rebuild



***

## The Parts That Matter Most

Based on the failure modes above, the OEM parts that every contractor should keep on the truck:

[18B260 Pump Packing Kit](https://www.sprayersandparts.com/home/117-graco-18b260-pump-packing-repair-kit.html) — covers throat and piston packings, seats, balls, O-rings, and gland nut. The scheduled maintenance kit for the entire fluid section wear tier.

[239922 Inlet Valve Seat](https://www.sprayersandparts.com/home/206-graco-239922-intake-valve-seat.html) — the inlet check valve replacement for stuck ball and seat wear failures.

[235014 Prime Drain Valve Kit](https://www.sprayersandparts.com/home/171-graco-235014-prime-drain-valve-spray-kit.html) — the prime valve replacement for bypass-in-spray-mode and priming failure.

[17J880 Outlet Valve Repair Kit](https://www.sprayersandparts.com/home/9762-graco-17j880-outlet-valve-repair-kit.html) — the outlet check valve for machines that prime correctly but can't hold pressure.

[117828 O-Ring Packing Kit](https://www.sprayersandparts.com/home/3327-graco-117828-encapsulated-o-ring-packing-kit.html) — O-rings throughout the fluid path for connection leaks.

[246428 Endurance Chromex Pump](https://www.sprayersandparts.com/home/246-graco-246428-endurance-pump.html) — for machines where scoring or structural damage has moved the repair beyond a packing kit.

All are genuine OEM Graco components, stocked and available with same-day shipping on qualifying orders placed before 1pm CST at[ SprayersAndParts](https://www.sprayersandparts.com/). For part number confirmation for your specific machine model and series letter, the[ interactive Graco parts diagram](https://www.sprayersandparts.com/7-order-by-graco-parts-diagram) provides the exploded view with correct part numbers. Technical support at 713-931-4102, Monday–Friday 8am–4pm CST.



***



Published by SprayersAndParts.com — an authorized Graco dealer at 5250 Gulfton St, Suite 1H, Houston, TX 77081. This guide covers the Graco Endurance displacement pump fluid section as used in the 390, 395, 490, 495, 595, Ultra Max II 490/495/595, FinishPro, and GMax 3400 class machines. Component specifications vary by model and series — always confirm part numbers against your specific machine's parts manual or the interactive parts diagram before ordering.

body.title: A special session for my beautiful friend Natasha | monomad challenge.
body.body:
>

Happy day and happy start to the week, friends! As you saw in the title of this post, today I want to show you the results of this photo shoot where I turned a great friend into a model for a day. Of course, it seems like Natasha really got into it after this session, hahaha—which is great, but anyway, this happens because when my friends have birthdays, I give them a card that says “coupon valid for a studio photo shoot,” hahaha, because honestly, I’m really, really bad at this gift-giving thing—it’s either food or a photo session. Those are always my gifts because I prefer it to be something they enjoy right away or something they’ll have forever, so those are always my options, hahaha. And well, friends, I gave Nat one of these coupons for her birthday back in March, and she just redeemed it. She’s into fitness, she’s one of those women who really loves the gym, and she told me she wanted some portrait shots, but then she said she wanted some sexy photos—nothing vulgar, though. The reliable way to do that is with a coat, and she suggested a skirt, which matched perfectly. Plus, she didn’t want them to look like just any old photos, and honestly, it turned out absolutely amazing—we were blown away by the results. She had been a model once before, but that was years ago, guys—she wasn’t even into fitness back then, hahaha, her words, by the way. She was super nervous at the start of this shoot, but honestly, she did a great job, guys, Our friend Figueroa was also here in the studio; she’s the makeup artist who did her makeup, and she was helping her relax a bit, so to speak. She followed the posing instructions very well, and the result really turned out better than we expected.

>Feliz día e inicio de semana amigos, hoy asi como lo leyeron en el título de este post quiero mostrarles el resultado de esta sesión fotográfica en la cual convertí a una gran amiga en una modelo por un día, claro que al parecer a Natasha después de esta sesion ya le gustó la movida jajaja, super excelente pero bueno, esto pasa resultado a que cuando mis amigas cuando cumplen años les regalo una tarjeta que dice \

jajaja, porque de verdad les digo que soy muy muy malo con esto de los regalos, o es comida o es la sesión, esos siempre son mis regalos porque prefiero que sea o algo que disfruten al momento o algo que les quede para siempre, entonces esas siempre son mis opciones jajaja y bueno amigos yo le di uno de estos cupones a Nat en su cumpleaños que fue en Marzo y apenas es que lo reclamo y ella es fitness, es de esas mujeres que les gusta mucho el gimnasio y me dijo quería unas de retrato pero luego que quería unas fotos sexys pero nada vulgar, la vía confiable para eso es un abrigo y ella sugirió una falda las cuales hicieron juego perfectamente, además de que no quería que parecieran unas polas y la verdad es que resultó de los mas genial, porque los resultados nos fascinaron, ya ella había sido modelo una vez pero hace años amigos, no era ni fitness jajaja palabras de ella, por cierto, en esta sesión estaba demasiado nerviosa al inicio pero honestamente lo hizo super bien amigos, aquí en el estudio tambien estaba nuestra amiga Figueroa que es la maquilladora que fue quien la maquilló tambien y la estaba ayudando un poco a soltarse por asi decirlo, ella seguía muy bien las recomendaciones de poses y el resultado de verdad que quedo mejor de lo que nos esperábamos.

body.title: Flaca - Andrés Calamaro (un pedacito)
body.body:
>

Un saludo comunidad, les deseo una feliz y próspera semana.

Con el llamado de las épocas quise recordar una canción que disfruté tocando junto a los amigos, una canción que se paseó entre mis primeros acordes.

Calamaro escribió canciones geniales, \
siempre la recuerdo por aquel comercial de los cangrejos, peo ejemplo. \

en este caso ha llegado a representar más que una canción de desamor, todo un clásico alternativo. Espero de corazón que ustedes y sus familiares estén muy bien. # ![Separador de párrafos.gif](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/elisonr13/EpR31g7k62Hhh4h3njerYP9RoRcwf9MdbYEwoYAYeuSkz6zYtVfZSuV7Qt8vA1fUGWk.gif) # Flaca Flaca no me claves Tus puñales Por la espalda Tan profundo No me duelen No me hacen mal Lejos En el centro De la tierra Las raíces Del amor Donde estaban Quedarán Entre el no me olvides Me dejes nuestros abriles olvidados En el fondo del placard Del cuarto de invitados Eran tiempos dorados De un pasado mejor Aunque casi me equivoco Y te digo poco a poco No me mientas No me digas la verdad No te quedes callada No levantes la voz Ni me pidas perdón Aunque casi te confieso Que también he sido un perro compañero Un perro ideal que aprendió a nadar Y a volver al hogar Para poder comer [#Lyrics](https://www.letras.com/andres-calamaro/1678/) [#Music](https://youtu.be/UCF9oHXhDMU?si=SJAcd5dhyuppBGS8) # ![pie de página.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/elisonr13/EpJZXy1VzjPgC9srPjYCey1BT3xrGEkZVtM5isJbi2pXk7PtjxpVp19JuSSKD758bUw.png) >! [Click here for the English version] >

>

Greetings everyone, I wish you a happy and prosperous week.

With the season upon us, I wanted to remember a song I enjoyed playing with friends, a song that was among my first chords.

Calamaro wrote some amazing songs; I always remember \
because of that crab commercial, for example. \

in this case, has become more than just a heartbreak song—it's a true alternative classic. I sincerely hope you and your families are doing well. # ![Paragraph separator.gif](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/elisonr13/EpR31g7k62Hhh4h3njerYP9RoRcwf9MdbYEwoYAYeuSkz6zYtVfZSuV7Qt8vA1fUGWk.gif) # Skinny Skinny, don't stab me With your daggers In my back So deep They don't hurt They don't harm me Far away In the center Of the earth The roots Of love Where they were Will remain Among the forget-me-nots Leave our forgotten springs At the bottom of the closet In the guest room They were golden times Of a better past Although I almost made a mistake And I tell you little by little Don't lie to me Don't tell me the truth No Stay quiet Don't raise your voice Or ask for forgiveness Although I almost confess That I too have been a companion dog An ideal dog who learned to swim And to return home So he could eat [#Lyrics](https://www.letras.com/andres-calamaro/1678/) [#Music](https://youtu.be/UCF9oHXhDMU?si=SJAcd5dhyuppBGS8) # ![footer.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/elisonr13/EpJZXy1VzjPgC9srPjYCey1BT3xrGEkZVtM5isJbi2pXk7PtjxpVp19JuSSKD758bUw.png) --- ▶️ [3Speak](https://3speak.tv/watch?v=elisonr13/d0b210e4)
