body.title: Hive to $150
body.body:
<center>
There are so many tokens out there that have no utility at all.

<u>Why should Hive not be worth $150?</u> Give me a good reason.

# 0.00183922 BTC / HIVE
would give HIVE a market cap of
$81,255,700,200 billion


![1000hiveBEE9bee1-500rb1.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/darkflame/23vspBQQ182NBegos4Z95MQWMVBvZz9LdzroSRWEJEed7ungRBT9vr2DzUYKJRERVmPUW.png)


Unrealistic, perhaps. There are 541m Hive tokens and only 21m Bitcoin, but it's possible.

McDonalds has a market cap of $202.45 B but it also has a globally recognized brand that people line up for 24 hours a day. This year people will buy Cheeseburgers, and next year, and the year after.

> *\

*

What are Hive's earning, if we look at it in this light?

What is it that Hive serves its customers?

Where are our Chicken Nuggets?


![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/darkflame/23uQrpTxUKhSrWZHGwbKxHAKhMMqkCRYFuQV7XhHLVJp4RTXNS6CcvvuLvxV3BAHzEMxQ.png)


I often talk about how it's a better web host, but it's users are its greatest asset.

Although we have dApps and HBD is ideal for payments, (who is using recurring payments?) 
There still is no active Hive Marketplace for Products and Services.

Someone walks into Hive, and their starting place is to post, 
but as soon as they get a downvote, its all over.

<u>Where are Hive's Customers?</u> How can we build a Brand that serves people?
And if we had a Products and Services Marketplace, what might that look like?

The mechanism for adding value to the Hive coin would need to be there. 

What does Hive make? What are our resources? Our equipment and our to-go boxes?

Brainstorm with me please, how can we make Hive more appealing to Customers?

What would a more successful Hive look like, in 10 years? What things would we need to do today to make it somewhere that people want to go, daily, and what would get they?

Could they buy home made stuff? Shipping costs makes it difficult. Digital goods makes sense. Hiring Devs for their coding talents, perhaps. But the risk of AI automation replacing both coding and writing work is unfolding. Human meaningful efforts are recognized on Hive, because it takes a Human eye to give that upvote and judge a post and user with Merit.


![iminpOB1-360.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/darkflame/23y9213fwad1VoZXHpvy1XtXvxAaPMJs9nVL8PxuWBaSpkYWySwqjwStq34KTj3bLxzCo.png)


I have had several ideas for Front ends I would create, smart contracts for tokens, and more.

What is really worth doing? Are we determined to keep Hive small, with a low price? Or do we want to see the value of the entire chain rise and see everyone thrive? Hive flipped HBD once, it can do it again. When Hive is worth more than HBD, then the HBD created inflation won't be so high.

Mainly I am asking is, what does a new user come here for, and why would they come back?

<u>Please take the time to leave your Proof Of Brain in the comments and brainstorm some ideas.</u>

**If Hive was a Service and Product focused Business**, what would new users come here for, and why would they spend their Crypto here? How could they do it? How can we encourage, not discourage?

Does everyone need a Shop that donates 2% to a Pool? Could there be user/HBD liquidity pools? 

Should there be automatic BTC and USDT reserves built up to back the HIVE token? 

Can Hive diversify and secure it's place as the ultimate decentralized web3 platform?


![surfingnetscape.gif](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/darkflame/AK2C8Rp3X5q2V5aMMaQiTCT7j1SrqmZZLnqiSMqRwTyZZo1K6h76pCgrr2FGwzX.gif)


What are the top 10 most important issues of the year?

#### **Can we continue to innovate, or does Hive burn out?**

These are just some of my thoughts over Breakfast and Coffee.

------------

https://images.hive.blog/0x0/https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/cvault/23wBg83V7B2u3t4feGGEmoTsWq9pmvoSdHGzFCGFr8sCLpPNk7EwUpXq68gnBRGw14YT1.png

@Darkflame

</center>

body.title: \n\n\
\n\n(Between Waves and Smiles: A Glimpse of Our Honeymoon at Los Canales Beach, Lechería)
body.body: /> ¡Hola, amigos! 🌟 Dicen que los mejores planes son los que no se fuerzan, y nuestra visita a Playa Los Canales fue exactamente eso. Mientras disfrutábamos de los días mágicos de nuestra luna de miel en la hermosa ciudad de Lechería, nos encontramos con un pequeño espacio de tiempo libre. Estábamos esperando a que una gran amiga nos buscara para recorrer la ciudad, y en lugar de esperar encerrados, decidimos que el sol y la brisa marina eran mejores anfitriones.

/> No hay nada como el calorcito de las playas orientales de Venezuela. Nos sentamos en la arena, bajo la sombra de las palmeras, a simplemente ser. Fue un momento de paz total, de esos que te permiten procesar la felicidad de haber comenzado una vida juntos.

/>\n\nSi algo hace que estas fotos sean perfectas para mí, es la sonrisa de mi esposa. En cada toma, su alegría refleja exactamente cómo nos sentíamos: libres, enamorados y agradecidos. A veces, en medio de los viajes, corremos de un sitio a otro queriendo verlo todo, pero este \
en la playa nos recordó que los momentos de espera también pueden ser el corazón del viaje.\n\n

/>

¡Gracias por ser parte de nuestros recuerdos!

\[ENG\]  
Hello, community! 🌟

They say the best plans are the ones that aren't forced, and our visit to Los Canales Beach was exactly that. While enjoying the magical days of our honeymoon in the beautiful city of Lechería, we found ourselves with a small window of free time. We were waiting for a dear friend to pick us up to explore the city, and instead of waiting indoors, we decided the sun and the sea breeze were much better hosts.

There is nothing like the warmth of Venezuela's eastern beaches. We sat on the sand, under the shade of the palm trees, simply being. It was a moment of total peace, one of those that allows you to process the happiness of having started a life together.

If anything makes these photos perfect for me, it’s my wife’s smile. In every shot, her joy reflects exactly how we felt: free, in love, and grateful. Sometimes, in the middle of trips, we rush from one place to another wanting to see it all, but this \
at the beach reminded us that the moments of waiting can also be the heart of the journey.\n\nThank you for being part of our memories!

body.title: Frente al Espejo
body.body:
by Hilaricita on Hilaricita 
View my bio on Blurt.media: https://blurt.media/c/hilaricita [![Frente al Espejo](https://blurt.media/lazy-static/previews/63efc9a8-ec71-443f-b8ff-7dfc8024f857.jpg)](https://blurt.media/w/ewnah8hU6dhEKWoR7xnmjp) 
 
 ![Versión español.png](https://img.blurt.world/blurtimage/hilaricita/0c2eef4b843038ffa91c5c76126870fbaa369559.png)

Martes 5 de mayo, 2026

Hace miles de años, en las tierras que hoy conocemos como Egipto, hombres y mujeres por igual comenzaron a delinearse los ojos con kohl. No lo hacían simplemente para verse más atractivos ante el espejo de bronce; buscaban protección. Esa línea negra alrededor de la mirada actuaba como un escudo contra el sol implacable del Nilo y, según creían, contra el mal de ojo y las infecciones. Era una barrera física y espiritual.

Pero la historia no se queda solo en el valle del Nilo. Mientras tanto, en otras latitudes, las tribus utilizaban arcillas, bayas trituradas y grasas animales para pintar sus rostros antes de la caza o la guerra. El color rojo de la tierra o el blanco de la cal servían para intimidar al enemigo o para camuflarse entre la vegetación. Aquí, el maquillaje era lenguaje, identidad y estrategia. Con el paso de los siglos, esa función práctica comenzó a transformarse en símbolo de estatus. En la Grecia clásica y luego en Roma, el uso de cosméticos se volvió más sofisticado, aunque también más controvertido. Las mujeres de la élite romana usaban polvos blancos de plomo para aclarar la piel, un ideal de belleza que, irónicamente, las enfermaba lentamente. 

Durante la Edad Media en Europa, la Iglesia miraba con recelo cualquier alteración de la creación divina, por lo que el maquillaje pasó a la clandestinidad, reservado para actrices y mujeres de mala reputación. Sin embargo, el renacimiento trajo consigo un resurgimiento explosivo. La reina Isabel I de Inglaterra, con su rostro empolvado de blanco ceruso y sus labios pintados de un rojo intenso, marcó tendencia en toda la corte. Ese palidez extrema no era solo moda; era una declaración de que no se trabajaba bajo el sol, distinguiendo a la nobleza del campesinado. 

No fue hasta el siglo XX, con la llegada del cine mudo y posteriormente el hablado, que el maquillaje democratizó su acceso y cambió su propósito una vez más. Los actores necesitaban rasgos definidos para ser visibles bajo las luces intensas de los estudios, y ese estilo exagerado filtró hacia la calle. Marcas emergentes comenzaron a vender la promesa de glamour accesible. Ya no era solo para la realeza o las prostitutas; era para cualquier mujer que quisiera sentirse poderosa, moderna o simplemente visible. Hoy, cuando alguien se aplica una base o un lápiz labial, está repitiendo, sin saberlo, gestos milenarios. Es una conexión directa con aquella mujer egipcia que se protegía la mirada del sol, o con la actriz de los años veinte que buscaba liberarse de las restricciones victorianas. 

La primera gran división que cualquier profesional hace al evaluar un rostro es la textura y la cobertura. Por un lado, están las bases ligeras, como los tintes hidratantes o las BB creams, que buscan unificar el tono sin tapar la porosidad natural de la piel. Son ideales para esos días en los que se busca frescura, esa apariencia de \

que, paradójicamente, requiere mucha precisión. Por otro extremo, encontramos las coberturas completas, máscaras densas diseñadas para ocultar imperfecciones, manchas o cicatrices, creando un lienzo perfecto, casi artístico, aunque a veces a costa de esa transparencia vital que tanto valoramos en la piel sana.

Más allá de la base, el juego de luces y sombras define la estructura del rostro. Aquí entran en escena los correctores, los iluminadores y los contornos. No se trata solo de poner color, sino de esculpir. Un buen estilista sabe que un iluminador bien colocado en el pómulo puede despertar una mirada cansada, mientras que un contorno sutil puede afinar una mandíbula sin que parezca artificial. La clave está en la sutileza; el maquillaje moderno ha abandonado esas líneas duras de décadas pasadas para abrazar técnicas de difuminado que imitan cómo la luz golpea naturalmente los huesos del cara. Es arquitectura facial, pero hecha con cremas y polvos.

Los ojos siguen siendo el protagonista indiscutible de la expresión. Desde las sombras mates que aportan profundidad hasta los brillos metálicos que capturan la atención, la variedad es infinita. Pero quizás el producto más transformador sea el delineador. Una línea fina y negra puede endurecer la mirada y aportar sofisticación inmediata, mientras que un difuminado en tonos tierra ofrece calidez y cercanía. No hay que olvidar las pestañas, donde las máscaras han evolucionado desde simples cepillos hasta fórmulas que alargan, curvan y dan volumen sin apelmazar, buscando siempre esa apertura de mirada que comunica alerta y vitalidad.

En los labios, la revolución ha sido equally notable. Hemos pasado de los barras tradicionales, a menudo secos y rígidos, a texturas líquidas, tintes que tiñen la piel del labio desde dentro y bálsamos con color que hidratan mientras embellecen. El rojo clásico sigue siendo un icono de poder, pero los tonos nude, terracota y berry permiten una versatilidad diaria que se adapta a la ropa y al estado de ánimo. 

Las fórmulas waterproof para quienes sudan o lloran, los productos no comedogénicos para pieles propensas al acné, o las bases con protección solar que integran el cuidado dermatológico con la estética. Incluso ha surgido el concepto de \

, una tendencia que prioriza la salud de la barrera cutánea sobre la cobertura, utilizando ingredientes activos que tratan la piel mientras la embellecen. Un profesional no impone un estilo, sino que selecciona, combina y adapta estas herramientas para resaltar lo que la persona ya tiene, potenciando su belleza única sin disfrazarla.\r\n\r\nExiste una creencia antigua y persistente de que maquillarse es un acto superficial, una máscara para ocultar inseguridades o engañar a los demás sobre cómo nos sentimos realmente. Sin embargo, la psicología moderna ha comenzado a desentrañar capas mucho más profundas en este ritual cotidiano. Para muchas personas, aplicarse maquillaje no es un acto de vanidad, sino una herramienta de regulación emocional y empoderamiento. Estudios recientes sugieren que el simple acto de cuidar la apariencia puede mejorar significativamente la autoestima y la confianza en uno mismo, un fenómeno que los expertos a menudo denominan el \

. \r\n\r\nCuando alguien se toma unos minutos frente al espejo para delinearse los ojos o uniformar el tono de su piel, está estableciendo una rutina, un momento de pausa intencional en medio del caos diario. Este ritual puede actuar como una transición psicológica, marcando la diferencia entre el yo privado, vulnerable y descansado, y el yo público, listo para interactuar social o profesionalmente. Es una armadura suave. En entornos laborales competitivos o situaciones sociales ansiógenas, sentirse \

puede reducir la ansiedad social y aumentar la percepción de competencia propia. 

Además, hay un componente interesante relacionado con la atención plena, o mindfulness. La aplicación precisa de un producto requiere concentración, coordinación mano-ojo y una conexión física con el propio rostro. Para muchas mujeres y hombres, esos minutos son de los pocos momentos del día en los que se miran a sí mismos con detenimiento, no con crítica, sino con cuidado. Es un acto de autocuidado tangible. Tocar la piel, masajear suavemente las cremas, observar los rasgos propios; todo ello fomenta una relación más compasiva con el cuerpo. Lejos de ser un rechazo a la apariencia natural, puede convertirse en una celebración de ella, una forma de destacar lo que ya existe en lugar de ocultarlo.

La investigación también ha tocado el tema de la percepción social y cómo esta retroalimenta nuestra psique. Sabemos que, lamentablemente o no, la sociedad tiende a atribuir ciertos traits positivos, como la organización, la salud o la profesionalidad, a las personas que presentan una apariencia cuidada. Cuando una persona recibe ese feedback positivo externo —una mirada de aprobación, un trato más respetuoso—, su estado emocional mejora. Esto no significa que el valor personal dependa del maquillaje, sino que este puede actuar como un catalizador para acceder a esa confianza que ya reside dentro, pero que a veces necesita un pequeño empujón externo para manifestarse.

Por supuesto, la clave está en la motivación. Los beneficios psicológicos son más robustos cuando el maquillaje se elige desde el deseo de expresión y placer, no desde la obligación o el miedo al juicio. Cuando deja de ser una exigencia para convertirse en una opción creativa, libera. Permite experimentar con diferentes facetas de la identidad: hoy puedo ser audaz con un rojo intenso, mañana sutil con un toque de brillo. Esa flexibilidad identitaria es saludable. El mayor beneficio psicológico no es la belleza estética resultante, sino la agencia. La certeza de que tenemos control sobre nuestra presentación ante el mundo, y que ese pequeño acto diario de creación puede ser un ancla de estabilidad y amor propio en días turbulentos.

Como ya casi se acaba el número de caracteres de la caja de información, les dejo con la canción que le pedí a SUNO, esperando que esta publicación les haya servido, no solo como entretenimiento, sino que les haya aportado un poco, una chispa de contenido que genera valor.

🎵 🎶 🎶 🎶 🎵 🎼 🎼 ♬ ♫ ♪ ♩

Esta fue una canción e información útil de martes.

Gracias por pasarse a leer y escuchar un rato, amigas, amigos, amigues de BlurtMedia.

Que tengan un excelente día y que Dios los bendiga grandemente.

Saludines, camaradas \

body.body: My major target in 2026 is to attain stability. This is because in the last one year my hive account has suffered some significant loss and I will like to use this year to recover. It’s not something that would be very easy to do, in fact if I must admit it has not been easy, but I am happy to have come a long way. By now I should have been at 6,000 HP or close to 7,000 HP especially with my level of posting and engagement, but currently I am just over 2,000 HP because of the huge blow my account has suffered in the last 1 year.\n\n

/> [SOURCE](https://chatgpt.com/) But then again, I do not regret any of it because at the end of the day I needed the money desperately and that was the only place it could have come from. But right now I want to try to recover everything I have lost and try to maybe bounce back to my glory days. It’s not been easy and to be honest I haven’t even been doing anything differently. This is because long before now I have put effort into growing my engagement and posting on hive. It's now a part of me, so much so that I would say it has even become a habit. I mean I can’t even go a day without posting and engaging just to show how much of a habit I have formed. Right now I want stability, I want my HP to grow. I am targeting 5k by the end of the year, and with the level at which I post and engage, I know that would be achievable and if I get lucky, I might even surpass it so long I do not touch my HP at the end of the day. I want stability in my finances and this will require a lot of discipline. The discipline not to power down no matter what happens. I've actually changed my view over the last few months. Originally, I was a bit sad when the interest rate was dropped down from 20%.

But now I think an interest rate of around 6-10% would be ideal. It's high enough to keep up with current real world inflation (at least where I am - I appreciate every country is different !). But it's low enough to help reduce Hive inflation.

Most importantly, if the inflation rate is lower, it could encourage more use of HBD for what it is ideal for; a no-fee stablecoin for transactions, not just something to stack and earn interest on.

body.title: San Antonio de la Eminencia Castle is a must-see destination
body.body:
>There are places in the world where time seems to have stood still, not because they lack life, but because their presence is so imposing that the present yields to the weight of the centuries. At the summit of Pan de Azúcar Hill, zealously guarding the city of Cumaná in Sucre State, Venezuela, stands the Castle of San Antonio de la Eminencia. #
![1000530331.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mayifiestas/EqFssBvfnPXV9KertrtJyBSEmaxvUUYnBKpby58aXtfWaXyZu69crETKWTYSjhaVYiW.jpg)
#
![1000530329.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mayifiestas/EpxqoqXPGhbNz4C7bbRTSS1Bb7EE7XnKUGruvXq6dVJ3zyoxm7sJ1HpBVHMx9oxEacR.jpg)
#

>Visiting this stronghold is not just a tourist outing; it is a journey to the roots of the Americas, an encounter with 17th-century military architecture, and, above all, a sensory experience where the Caribbean wind tells tales of pirates, battles, and freedom. #
![1000530342.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mayifiestas/EprTcUbJeXSn2NwD4zcVcFmy62VfXJQqyQGGRvWm3hqGCL5baew22J96wbjo6wBm2M5.jpg)
#
![1000530343.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mayifiestas/Eq3822iSXZJhV9hB4tXU1XmUjtpa254hAaEY4iZh521nmXwEJ7f6X11c7FAGjFDvZDq.jpg)
#

>Cumaná, the city where I live, holds the title of the “Firstborn of the Continent,” as it was the first city founded by Europeans on the American mainland; therefore, maintaining its defense was vital. #
![1000530338.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mayifiestas/Ep1XtD6R63VBPHH2uVhdt4GGua8X7dHwpsF6xoQmCQ5esvfKJpymqQGUM8SmyzHAFnt.jpg)
# ![1000530335.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mayifiestas/EpJZbgZo78TvU3MobmWnCBGFNdC16E2DG6LT2wJqDQNYGzh7TYCwwQXUKHh5SgnJAmG.jpg) # ![1000530337.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mayifiestas/EpLgSo8ocXDsMZhA5zdYJGnEWvnRuFqBVftp7xdLAyczwr8rpsQW2WL2foynf4ALb5a.jpg) #

>The Castle of San Antonio de la Eminencia was built with coral stone and lime, designed in the shape of a four-pointed star—a jewel of Spanish military engineering intended to leave no “blind spots” against enemy attacks. #
![1000530325.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mayifiestas/EqSWQjb21eHgTmGQaUkyKSCcCJE97Q1kZ6SwZ3PXnxcdNm9cKUvjfgd68oYYKhU6X7n.jpg)
#
![1000530332.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mayifiestas/EpnDmSwjGPzukuHYyt1vCYtyMjj58enYwHCkKJmMJTMZY2Lsjkrx9byfkwPFy1KjjRn.jpg)
#
![1000530323.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mayifiestas/EpQwFAJpFQzgFZ2xXveYf3HbpkwNaJwMmg4kobzqb7zwwsU2wGac4VU2sABpYXiZfQP.jpg)
#

>As you walk along its walls, as seen in the images of its imposing structure, you can feel the rough texture of history; it is evident in every sentry box—those small watchtowers protruding from the corners—which served as lookouts against the pirate ships that lurked along the coast. Today, those same sentry boxes provide the perfect vantage point for appreciating the area’s unique geography. #
![1000530324.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mayifiestas/EqSWSUPLkUDm9GBqbLQajWXejkSuFQb8j6CT664YCcjyD9EPLWpXTjnjrH59YnRbJcu.jpg)
#
![1000530321.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mayifiestas/EprVTWAuS3Tvaiyz8qqZSehZmMAKdaJ6shdLimdYLLn8k32PFHnxtmGtzFByg5ibPUD.jpg)
#
![1000530323.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mayifiestas/EpQwFAJpFQzgFZ2xXveYf3HbpkwNaJwMmg4kobzqb7zwwsU2wGac4VU2sABpYXiZfQP.jpg)
#

>If there is one emotional reason to climb up and visit the San Antonio de la Eminencia Castle, it is for its sunset. As can be seen in the photographs, the sun does not simply set in Cumaná; it performs a farewell ritual that bathes everything in a deep orange and liquid gold. From the top of the castle, the view is panoramic: #
![1000530313.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mayifiestas/Ep7v7M47f7pnVic2LyAeYNyXh3N3JPriYFNi9rvC2UH9bVECH33qwUKSHkMgo5ivSGd.jpg)
#
![1000530314.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mayifiestas/EpEJHGzmzoNkXWF9i7MpgmVmVbjyMbmBynX8ejHYCoBwZ4PeFU9YqYtkQgFndah4hCo.jpg)
#
![1000530312.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mayifiestas/EpT5gdSzChGkh9mKfSPv56J4JSzoqtZoktRzovkxWp98vMvEfpwvLYpHqpRFgrwKXo6.jpg)
#

>If you look west, the sun sets over the Gulf of Cariaco, creating a dazzling and beautiful reflection on the waters of the Caribbean; to the north, you can make out the silhouette of the Araya Peninsula, another land of salt and castles, Now, if you look down, the city of Cumaná spreads out with its red roofs and the majestic Cathedral of Santa Inés standing out among the foliage. #

>The evening light filtering through the decorative structures of the viewpoint creates a play of shadows that invites reflection, creating moments when visitors often fall silent to simply admire how nature and history merge in a single embrace. #
![1000530285.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mayifiestas/Ep7v9QjSAf6gJp1xwv1XeNA1tg7sPi13AZTFqgCji8Uga1aisGmQedR7NsHLbojKwnx.jpg)
#
![1000530310.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mayifiestas/EqQR5aPdBbQbkFJw5m6vLjtJpdMRaKAos3wed9874VKX7Kasjwa3vaf1DsDUAz6SwmB.jpg)
#
![1000530299.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mayifiestas/EqDnTk37z2FAm7nys23DQ2JvdXnnryEMH7CpeAs3mSyWh7nSSLcRH97QJv7764Dqhvv.jpg)
#

>You may wonder why you should visit this majestic place. Beyond its aesthetic beauty, the Castle of San Antonio de la Eminencia offers profound reasons to be included in any travel itinerary: ​Connection to the Emancipatory Struggle: this castle was not only a Spanish fortress; it was also a prison for patriots. In its cold, dark vaults, illustrious figures from our history were imprisoned, such as General José Antonio Páez. So, when you walk through its tunnels and corridors, you can begin to grasp the sacrifice of those who dreamed of our country’s independence. #

>Now, when it comes to its architectural value, we can say that it is truly unique, since—unlike other forts—its star-shaped layout is exceptionally symmetrical. Furthermore, the use of local materials, such as fragments of seashells and coral mixed into the mortar, makes it a structure that literally rose from the sea to protect our land. #
![1000530329.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mayifiestas/EpxqoqXPGhbNz4C7bbRTSS1Bb7EE7XnKUGruvXq6dVJ3zyoxm7sJ1HpBVHMx9oxEacR.jpg)
#
![1000530315.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mayifiestas/EpGRi873uN6D9tBqeh26311QQcEZBkZ7ozxJfndRUyj9KCzaAnMVbuBzJkRyqbAAeDL.jpg)
#
![1000530300.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mayifiestas/EptcPNza9vwYUmAo551zvDGihJu2VcHFJaHWRnvfegMRsuwS5tVSN7yvzyUj9cWHLM3.jpg)
#

>Today, the castle has ceased to be a place of war and has become a park of peace, so it is common to see local families, couples, and photographers enjoying the esplanade. It is very safe, and its height and the spaciousness of its outdoor areas make it ideal for educational recreation. #

>The beauty of the place lies in the contrasts—between the gray of the ancient stone and the shifting blue of the sky; it is the difference between the silence of its inner vaults and the bustle of the city growing at its feet. #
![1000530350.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mayifiestas/EpQuNpYisnxWc5ydqG6iCzrrFe9x5yGL5NzpPYW8iJgWJaBjNogbeAgxEQinrnYaVnR.jpg)
#
![1000530344.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mayifiestas/Eq3822nqSCnVLymAZ7QZzo2iwnwocmMjc9HCeRfkFsvL1GtDiZ8adUFpF3BTcCjYxV8.jpg)
#

>In the shared photos, a special harmony is evident: the presence of the national flag waving vigorously, the cacti growing on the arid slopes of the hill, and the human warmth emanating from those who visit. The smile of someone taking a selfie with the sun in the background isn’t just for the photo; it’s because of the energy that fills a place that has withstood earthquakes, attacks, and the passage of time. #

>To fully enjoy this architectural marvel, you should arrive at 4:30 p.m. That way, we’ll have time to explore the grounds and get you settled in for the spectacular sunset. We should also make sure our phones are fully charged—unlike mine, which died—so we can capture the textures of the walls and the natural lighting, which are a dream come true for anyone who loves photography. #
![1000530301.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mayifiestas/EpxriFC96zT5c3iHh49CXB515jNB9MRRbZQA6EueCNjRJ1N7eT6maTseLBnMg8f6nxg.jpg)
#
![1000530296.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mayifiestas/EqLAEtxCk2GRo1oj94rU22aH1vqsEQsu2cJroLRi2rQvx7BfcgDkDTisHHioMsmGeg2.jpg)
#
>Up on the hilltop, the wind blows with a steady force that cools the tropical heat and adds a mystical atmosphere to the place—though if you ask me, it’s a little scary, hehehe. #

>Visiting the Castle of San Antonio de la Eminencia isn’t just a simple stroll; it’s about reconciling with the past to understand our present. It sounds cliché, but it’s still true. It’s also about realizing that cities aren’t just asphalt and modern buildings, but also the stones that protected them when everything was uncertain. #
![1000530285.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mayifiestas/Ep7v9QjSAf6gJp1xwv1XeNA1tg7sPi13AZTFqgCji8Uga1aisGmQedR7NsHLbojKwnx.jpg)
#
![1000530291.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mayifiestas/EpnEnmRfsnuVNJqJcHgZRnpnXMw4wow7SdSLs7u3Cu4D6mLJ1yHnXDNgf9AnCbw2VQu.jpg)
#

>If you’re looking for a place that combines heroic history, classical engineering, and one of the most beautiful views in all of Venezuela, Cumaná and its castle are waiting for you. Remember, it’s not just a monument; it’s the soul of the city turned to stone, waiting under the Caribbean sun to tell you its secrets. #
![1000000527.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mayifiestas/23xpVkf7G3mrnzXzVUmem5v7waQ1HtpzauGt7LvLEqgzhzXsyeb3HmHYPcTWyTpPDfN5e.png)
#
>All the photos are my own and were taken with my Xiaomi 14 Note Pro Plus.\nI used the Polish program and the Deepl translator.

body.title: Technology is a useful servant but a dangerous master
body.body:
There was a time when my family members were good in mathematics. Be my Dad my uncle, my brother and to some extent me too were good in solving math problem. Be it unit conversion or remembering the formulas or mathematical tables, all were quite good in finding the solution orally But the introduction of calculators have seen a little degradation to the new generation. The new generation were heavenly relying on calculators in solving math's. There is a member who not at all good in simple math calculation. She used to take help of calculators. Certainly the ease of machine simply spoiled the art and the legacy that was carried so far in our family.


![IMG_20240316_060053(1).jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/steemflow/23tbRPqN6tFudh1jyY79PaM6keq7YdX5owsvmbB6Y5HjK1jAH1Ui5NKjtvM6sc9VqjPj8.jpg)
*(own edited image)*


> ***Escaping the algorithm***

It is always been said that techonolgy has its own pros and cons. Technology offers immediate answers and shortcuts (e.g., AI tools, templates), which diminishes the patience and deep thinking required for creative processes. Just as in case happening in my family. The legacy of solving maths with ease has diminished. The ease at which those simple day to day calculation were done orally is now dependent on machine. Calculators has now becomes an inbuilt application on every smartphone. So anybody carey it with them and take help of it rather than making use of own skills. Technology diminishes creativity by encouraging reliance on algorithms and instant, automated solutions rather than fostering original thought. There was a time when we used to spend time in solving a maths problem but now kids were ready to search them over the internet to get to an immediate answer. The keys is manking is losing their skills to machine. 

> ***Technology should improve our life...not become our life.***


These days most of the human being is relying on technology in easing their job. Be it writing content or taking a picture or solving any problems. Even now the national television is promoting the use of #chatGPT in resolving complicated issue. All these is simply killing the natural way of human thinking. The way people were directed and motivated towards technology means the use of art and creativity is at the end. The more we rely on technology, means less creativity. In other words the humans were simply losing their capability to do things of their own. And the question always lurk over individual head is this end of mankind. 


Seeing the high dependency upon calculator, I have strictly remove all the calculating machine from my home. I even deleted calculators from my mobile. I personally belive. It is better to keep the thinking proces going on rather than allowing it to dump. Remaining creative amidst rapid technology evolution requires treating technology as a tool for collaboration rather than a replacement for human ingenuity. The \

behind a project.raised from human experience is irreplaceable. Use technology to serve this purpose, rather than doing tech for tech's sake.

In an era of infinite AI-generated content, unique human creativity is the rarest, most valuable commodity.





**In good faith - Peace!!**



![1000037470.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/steemflow/Eo8M1obna2cYnnMAc2ZC3wWMW9ZqZHvk9StEga6aY2cTsKmweW7zFBDm7D13YHVoC5N.png)

body.title: A Quick Practice Game
body.body:
<center>![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmdPUa6hqQiz5NXXkxCzDYWk2XBp6xBrnTJrE7wbRveyrm/image.png)</center>

Greetings to all chess fans! I haven't written about my practice games (for Saturday Hivechess) lately. This is one game I enjoyed so much. I had an attacking plan in the middlegame that I followed and executed well.

The game started as a Center Counter Defense and was converted to a Caro-Kann Defense. 1. e4 d5 2. e5 Bf5 3. Nf3 h6 4. d4 e6 5. c3 c5 6. Bd3 

<center>![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmTzLY9JzPYpga223hEwdULroLvuiuhotDyG56EQGnMmmG/image.png)</center>

I decided to exchange my light square Bishop since his is more active. I was thinking after he moves c4 then my Bishop has few good squares so better to trade it now. 6. ...Bxd3 7. Qxd3 c4 8. Qc2 Nc6 9. Nbd2 b5 10. a3 Nge7 11. O-O Ng6 

<center>![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmVbhMqsRaVcJuxzGBqd1nTmp2bkbZpeAGZWa76RNW4Pfh/image.png)</center>

We reached the position. Conventional wisdom says to attack in the side you are stronger. In this case I'm stronger in the King side due to my advanced e pawn. So I planned to push f4-f5 to begin the attack. 12. h3 

<center>![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmbSBevqkCuiG37zyvigqhBakhYyqvSn9T8ctqXPTpkEyo/image.png)</center>

I was planning to play Nh2 eyeing the g4 square. It also prepares f4 to attack in the King side. 12. ...Be7 13. Nh2 O-O 14. f4 Nh4 15. Ndf3 

<center>![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmSrZZp9nbx77uw5KrFfY3RXKZ2xzQxC9DodvYHPfEVxo9/image.png)</center>

I offered to trade Knights to reduce his pieces and defenders in the King side. 15. ...Nf5 16. g4 Nh4 17. Nxh4 Bxh4 18. Nf3 

<center>![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmXCfbvm1K7m4DEcVXrw6Bd1FxwuKjHwGY2QhTFULdNzsn/image.png)</center>

After this, I'm ready to push f5. 18. ...Be7 19. f5 exf5 20. gxf5 Re8 21. Qg2

<center>![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmekt2HmQ9y9jT7JFGkLBpRFx8kdmrjunVEakMBLa6MjnL/image.png)</center>


White is already winning. There are many threats that's not easy to parry in a blitz game. It's easier to find moves if you're attacking since the moves come naturally. 21. ...Kh8 22. Kh1 Bf8 23. Rg1 

<center>![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmZ7nNCn9GBudaUVFY6DrfdMRM5JqBiQ1TFDxMN8K9Tvis/image.png)</center>



Threatening to win the pawn on h6. Recapturing with gxh6 will result to a mate on the g8 square. 23. ...Qe7 24. Bxh6 f6 25. Nh4 

<center>![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmQQrH9AkshKggr8ZQp3g1iaVsMopAWdMtDmqohHgAH5z4/image.png)</center>

The Knight joins the attack threatening to fork the King and Queen. 25. ...Kg8 26. Ng6 Qc7 27. Nxf8 Kxf8 28. Bxg7+ { Black resigns. } 1-0


<center>![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmRhX7E7ia8TwTYioE9wqHntK6pN1mitikKXe929z5oxA8/image.png)<center>

Black resigned since his King is bare and will be mated in a few moves.

Game link: https://lichess.org/dDyHcG7n

body.title: Shutting Down Stress / #monomad challenge / [ING/ESP]
body.body:
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmbEsVr6RrXKL2B3nn1mLmJqbmQgMeqm2evjgDzEUKSSUk/_7504439_copia_2.jpg)


* * *

The photos 📸 are my entry to the #monomad contest from @monochromes and @brumest.

* * *


Greetings hivers.

A few days ago, a neighbor saw me with my camera and joked that I’m not into anything serious, that all I do is take photos and stay happy.

It made me laugh, but he’s not entirely wrong. Photography frees me from stress in an almost magical way. Problems fade away with the sound of the shutter, it’s a very effective kind of therapy. When I have to stay at home, I go out to capture hummingbirds stopping by to feed, along with dogs and cats. The important thing is not to end the day without pressing the shutter at least once.

Today I’m sharing some of the photos I take without leaving home. The models are Kymi 😽 Michi 😹 and Pitufo 🐶. Hope you like them.



![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmQhKf27RApuQR165pg9MQVgU8h4Eisrus4traSob6JA7r/_7504459_copia_2.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmUWRtVMBKPBYSsr2VZN92K9ovEor2MeCoqT47BFuLnMuB/_7504491_copia_2.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmS18AXsQk1J7cmNq7TDgftahQTBfFDseNKY4SYhCaNbef/_7504498_copia_2.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmY3t9qWbdzrmrZf2jjNrfY9xXRFjiy83YjNqq46zTHFE4/_7504501_copia_2.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmc8bHxrw4jUhEUjuMgp9XDtTe7XxXbWqHKhA1hpY6C4xG/_7504504_copia_2.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmS5ttqWEdtftjEj1sgoZi8fP1sMxEedR95C87V17opzJS/_7504423_copia_2.jpg)

Saludos hivers.

Hace unos días un vecino que me vio con la cámara en la mano me dijo en broma que yo no estaba en nada, que lo mío era tirar fotos y vivir feliz.

Me dio mucha gracia, pero no deja de tener razón. Fotografiar me libera el estrés de una forma casi mágica. Los problemas desaparecen con el sonido del obturador, es una terapia muy efectiva. Cuando tengo que quedarme en casa salgo a cazar los zunzunes que vienen a libar, los perros, los gatos. Lo importante es no terminar el día sin disparar la cámara, aunque sea una vez.

Hoy les comparto algunas de las fotos que hago sin salir de casa. Los modelos son Kymi 😽 Michi 😹 y Pitufo 🐶. Espero que les gusten.

* * *

\

* * *

body.title: The Weight of Regret, The Light of Growth | LOH #287
body.body: ![](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/zoe01/23wXGNKLaZrvE46Ew7H4ein3qbxvGkzAKxAjpCvJTBMqv6ca6pfsjU8u16cP9WdQNaw6Z.png) When I don't keep myself busy, I overthink a lot. It feels overwhelming because I regret many things in life. So even if I'm sitting quietly but my mind it's still talking. But it is not that distracting, I can ignore it whenever I want to, the problem is that it doesn't feel good at all. In the beginning I always think of the good memories, but the people in it brings out the bad memories. It starts with things I did not do then I start to think about how many opportunities I have missed for silly things. I also think of the situations which I could have handled better. Those memories keeps coming back to me it's on a loop mode inside my mind. To describe it firmly I was always afraid to speak up and hated myself for staying silent even if I wanted to say something. It feels like I'm cursing myself for not speaking up at the right time. Those memories make me feel like I was a failure. So, those regrets will often catch up to me and it stops me from enjoying what is in the present timeline. To be honest it's not easy at all, it becomes harder to focus. But it's not possible to change the past but still my mind won't stop going back to the past. For example, “Why did I reject that opportunity? What if I had accepted it? Would that make any difference?” or “What if I did not waste my time with wrong surroundings?” thesr thoughts will only swallow my brain but not change anything, like it would only take away my good energy. My anxiety will sky rocket and becomes harder to stay happy for a long time. I also feel guilty for not being the person I should have been which I am now. Also, I didn’t love myself before. As if I hated myself out of others influence. These things has already created a weight inside me. Still I'm glad that I can least understand thar it was in the past and I cannot change it. So, even if I think about it now those moments are already gone. So, the only change can be made is in the present. I can change myself and try to be a better person, I can treat myself better, and start loving myself slowly. I feel like I'm already healing so I wanna forgive myself. And I will begin with acceptance, that I'm a human being and I'm supposed to make mistakes, not only me everyone else does that too. So, it doesn’t mean that I'm a bad person, it can only mean one thing which is that I am learning slowly. I wanted to be kinder to myself and not be harsh. I don't wanna feel regret about what should I have done before, I will just follow the lead to doing better next time. After all these years, I would say I'm still not the same person, if I was then I would be not able to forgive myself. I have changed a lot and started to heal my inner self. I wanna keep it in practice which is being in present and not worrying about the past. ____ The images are created with [Gemini](gemini.google.com) and edited with [Canva](www.canva.con) ____

body.title: Topic: Why Many Nigerians Struggle With Unemployment Beyond Just “No Jobs”**
body.body:
In Nigeria, unemployment is something almost everybody has talked about at one point or another. It is no longer a distant issue you only hear on the news. It is inside homes, among friends, within families. Almost every graduate knows someone still searching for work months or even years after school.

When I was younger, I used to think once you finish school and get your certificate, the next step was simple: get a job. That was the normal picture many of us were given. Study hard, graduate, find work, settle down.

But reality has a way of changing that picture quickly.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmT4aQTotB3fXbbRot75ca7AvReT4H7qcwfkoT1TZFzom4/1777996473108.jpg)[source](https://unsplash.com/photos/a-man-in-a-cap-and-gown-holding-a-blue-folder-LIZcm-mxpOE)

After school, many people begin to face a different kind of confusion. You have the degree, but the opportunities are limited. And even when opportunities show up, the competition is high. Sometimes thousands applying for one position. It can be discouraging.

But I’ve come to realize that the issue is deeper than just saying “there are no jobs.”

Part of the challenge is how education and practical skills often don’t align. Many people leave school with knowledge, yes, but not always with skills the market is currently demanding. The world is changing faster than many systems are adapting.

My father used to say, “Education opens your eyes, but skill puts food on the table.” At first, I didn’t fully understand it. Now it makes more sense.

Another issue is dependency on traditional expectations. Many people are still raised to believe success only comes through certain paths, mostly formal employment. So when those paths become crowded or limited, frustration increases.

Of course, the economy also plays a huge role. Businesses struggle, inflation rises, companies reduce hiring or shut down completely. These are realities people can’t ignore.

But I also think mindset matters. Not in a blameful way, because the environment is genuinely difficult. Still, adaptability has become more important than ever. Learning new skills, exploring digital opportunities, freelancing, entrepreneurship, and creative problem-solving are becoming necessary.

My mother always believed in resourcefulness. She would say, “Use what you have before complaining about what you don’t have.” That mindset is useful now more than ever.

This does not mean every unemployed person is lazy or not trying. Far from it. Many are trying very hard.

But I think unemployment in Nigeria is a mix of system problems, economic pressure, outdated expectations, and skill gaps.

It is frustrating, yes. But I believe adaptation is becoming part of survival.

The world is changing, and many Nigerians are slowly learning that waiting alone may no longer be enough. Sometimes, you have to create your own direction while still hoping for better systems ahead.

body.title: Mom Life: Devotional Breakthroughs Over ....Potty Training?
body.body:
https://img.leopedia.io/DQmVyxXdKaYu5dshVzY4ttwpg1i1eKGzLoGk6btuB6KqYgb/potty.png 


I'm learning, slowly. Each and everyday. I thank God for sanctification. I don't always remember to thank Him for that because sometimes the process is exhausting and I simply forget. But today, He reminded me why I need to thank Him.

Over the years, I have come to learn that the most important ministry God has given me is the ministry of Motherhood. I am raising 3 girls and my prayer is that they will grow up to know, love and serve Jesus.

To be completely transparent, it's an area in my life that I struggle with...often. I can share that honestly because I know that there are SO many parents that can relate. Sometimes life just bogs you down! Sometimes it's hard to see the blessings amongst the chaos that is life.

I have a 14, 7 and 4 year old. My 4 year old is still struggling with potty training. An up and down battle for the last couple of months - and just when I think she's got it down, she regresses. It's frustrating. There is no other word for it!

Yesterday, I had a bad day. I snapped over it all. Raised my voice, spoke out of turn and went to bed feeling like a big old pile of guilt and shame. I felt like a failure. I knew I could have done better. I knew my kids deserved better.

Today, I woke up and made a conscious choice to praise God. For the beauty of life; the birds were chirping. For the blessings of my family; the kids were happy and off to school. My husband, handsome as ever, off to work. For simply waking me up; thank You, Lord.

I settled in to do a morning devotional and this is where God hit me right in the feels....because I KNOW He was speaking to me. He was speaking to me on the very thing I pray about most - motherhood! The struggle, the heaviness, the guilt, the worry....all that comes with Motherhood.

I read a line in my devotional that said, *“Do not declare something dead that God is still forming.”*

You guys, never forget that **God can meet you right where you're at.**

This is when I started to cry. Like, ugly cry. I realized the way that I was speaking over my daughter yesterday, in frustration and anger over what felt like the 114th time of not making it to the potty....was awful. I wasn't speaking life. I was speaking to her like it would never get better. In fact, I declared that...\

I mumbled as I changed her clothes....again. 

Horrible. It came out of me and that's instantly how I felt. Horrible.

What God is saying through that very simple sentence in my morning devotional was profound in my life. **My little girl is still forming.** She's learning, just like me. If I haven't got it sorted out at 42, why should she at 4? **He's still working on her, just like He's working on me.** Rather than declaring the situation to be impossible, I brought it to Him. Right there in that moment, through tear filled eyes, crying over...potty training. Listen, that's how you can tell you're a Mom...when one of your biggest breakthroughs with God comes to you over potty training fiascos!


Thank You Jesus for Your grace. What more can I say? I cried. I asked for forgiveness. I understood in that moment that I was failing the ministry God gifted me by using those words. 

So tonight, thanks to Gods infinite grace, I will hug my girls; I will choose to speak life over them. I will declare that even in the frustration of missing the potty and having accidents...that it's okay! Because God is still working on us. He's working through me and my temper. He's working through her and her ability to control her body.

My heart is overjoyed this morning with a new perspective. I love You so much, Jesus!

body.title: The Hidden Danger: Why Forlorn Geomant Must Go First
body.body:
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmPpAxgZCyztoYs8QKVbqQzCusi5dPgq9tTncczdF2uuQ7/thumbnail_battle_of_the_day.png)

Hello Splinterlands warriors,

back again with a small story from the arena—one that sometimes feels more like a life story than just a game. This time I want to share a **battle of the day** that honestly left an impression on me—not just because of the drama, but because of one figure who quietly became a major threat: **Forlorn Geomant**.




The ruleset in this match wasn’t particularly “noisy.” You couldn’t use legendary monsters, and the mana cap was 55. But the strategies that emerged made it feel sharp and intense. I chose to play quite aggressively with a mix of magic attacks and poison effects from the Archon I used. My goal was simple: weaken one main threat early, then let the effect do the work over time.

And my target was immediately clear—**Forlorn Geomant**.

<center>![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmSCRmzFzna7sUxdN6HFk46tj999FHvwrBmAmhBZWMFzhi/stats.png)</center>

At a glance, this monster doesn’t look flashy. But once you realize it has **5 magic attack**, along with solid durability from its armor and HP, it becomes obvious: this isn’t a monster you want to leave alive for long.

I started with a fairly balanced formation. **Ulundin Overseer** was my main tank, supported by units like **Quilliun Legionary**, **Thanalorian Blade**, and **Mindless Thrall** to apply steady pressure. The combination felt solid—defense, damage, and finishing potential all in place.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmQHiHE9wYN99VozWYa91p1xn12hdexGg2YNyVXm3mBfCT/round_1.png)


The first round began quite “calm,” if you could call it that. Both tanks held their ground. My Ulundin Overseer was still standing, as was my opponent’s **Doomshield Warden**. But something important was already happening—the poison had started working on Forlorn Geomant. Slowly, but surely.

And that’s when I started thinking, “okay, this could be the path.”

Going into round two, things began to shake. My tank was getting critical. And before the round ended, Ulundin Overseer fell. Honestly, I had my doubts at that moment, especially since the opponent’s Doomshield Warden was still holding strong.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmaTxvYURJxdfCGeeb8gVicoM44UpLcM6Wj6mPpJBmMSgG/round_3.png)


But in Splinterlands, one round can change everything.

Round three became the turning point. The poison bit into Forlorn Geomant again. And finally, Doomshield Warden fell. At that moment, I saw the opening.

Forlorn Geomant’s HP was already on the brink.
And that’s when **Thanalorian Blade** came in like an executioner.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmQi8u1hoXWa7SBNLJfbs6D6ZqykQen8NnK8fcUqUXBtBo/execute.png)


With the **Execute** ability, it finished what the poison had started. One strike… and Forlorn Geomant—who had felt like such a huge threat—was finally taken down.

Honestly, that was a satisfying moment.

The following rounds moved faster. The opponent’s **Dread Tafarian** didn’t last long either—once again falling victim to Execute. And in the end, only one enemy monster remained: **Quilliun Legionary**.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmaHbx5foPsu4wdobPctq8gPvAwbZFTZjrD2sv3dzFDhH8/round_4.png)


It had **Void**, making my magic attacks less effective. But at that point, numbers spoke for themselves. Three against one. Slowly but surely, we finished it off.

And the victory went to my team.

You can watch the battle here:
<center> 👉  [**LINK BATTLE**](https://splinterlands.com/battle/sl_30956c6355c6a5a1a2cc0824691cf3b2?ref=rqr4)  👈</center>


What made this battle most interesting was how a small decision at the start—targeting Forlorn Geomant with poison—had such a big impact in the end. If it had been left alive longer, the story might have turned out very differently.

My honest opinion about Forlorn Geomant?
It’s the type of monster that’s “quiet but deadly.” If not handled quickly, it can become a major source of damage that’s hard to stop. That **5 magic damage** is no joke, especially in mid-to-late game.

Strategically, this battle reinforced something for me:
sometimes you don’t need to defeat every enemy—just neutralize the most dangerous one first.

For new players, this is an important lesson:
don’t just look at damage—look at which unit has the biggest impact on the opponent’s team.

As a closing note, here’s my simple advice:
**if you face a monster like Forlorn Geomant, don’t wait for it to show its full power—take it down first before it’s too late.**

See you in the next arena story.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmXuXxp6GBhwB1HpXvoabLn8Dt8QaRKSe1WNYDzqX1v6Vk/chaos_logo.png)



Talk about Splinterlands,
If you haven't tried out this fantastic game called Splinterlands yet, I invite you to [**Join**](https://splinterlands.com?ref=rqr4).
It's free, but you'll need to invest in a beginning deck or buy gaming cards to gain real assets like cards and tokens.

I love these fascinating ideas about generating the income needed to bring these ideas to life in a meaningful way; all of this holds enormous potential from which we can learn and feel confident in ourselves. 

## Seeing is believing!

body.title: How New Jersey’s Faith-Based Programs Support Recovery
body.body:
## Introduction to Faith-Based Recovery Programs

Faith-based recovery programs are structured initiatives that integrate spiritual principles with addiction recovery practices. Often hosted by churches and community religious organizations, these programs aim to help individuals rebuild their lives through a combination of moral reflection, accountability, and supportive relationships.

For many participants, spirituality offers a sense of meaning that can be missing during addiction. While these programs do not replace clinical treatment, they frequently complement it by addressing emotional and psychological needs that traditional methods may overlook.

## Addiction Challenges in New Jersey

New Jersey continues to grapple with substance use disorders, particularly involving opioids and prescription medications. Communities across the state—urban and suburban alike—have experienced the widespread impact of addiction, prompting a multi-layered response.

Faith-based organizations have stepped in as accessible and trusted resources. Their presence within local communities allows them to connect with individuals who may be hesitant to seek formal medical treatment, offering a less intimidating entry point into recovery.

## Key Elements of Faith-Based Recovery Programs

### Spiritual Counseling and Mentorship

Spiritual counseling is central to faith-based recovery. Participants engage in guided reflection, often exploring themes such as responsibility, forgiveness, and personal growth. Mentors or faith leaders provide consistent guidance, helping individuals navigate both recovery and life challenges.

This approach can foster resilience. By encouraging individuals to reconnect with a sense of purpose, these programs create a foundation for long-term change.

### Peer Support Networks

Group support is another critical component. Participants share experiences, offer encouragement, and hold each other accountable. These peer networks reduce isolation, which is a common barrier to recovery.

Unlike purely clinical environments, faith-based groups often feel more personal. The relationships built in these settings frequently extend beyond the program itself, creating lasting support systems.

### Structured Living Environments

Many programs provide structured daily routines that include work responsibilities, group meetings, and spiritual practices. This structure helps individuals rebuild discipline and establish stability.

Routine is particularly valuable in early recovery. It replaces harmful habits with healthier ones and provides a clear framework for daily living.

## Education and Early Intervention

### Correcting Misconceptions About Substance Use

Education plays a vital role in preventing substance misuse and supporting early intervention. Faith-based programs often host informational sessions to address common misconceptions about drugs and treatment methods.

For instance, questions like [How Fast Does Snorting Suboxone Kick In?](https://www.choicepointhealth.com/how-fast-does-snorting-suboxone-kick-in/) may arise in discussions, reflecting confusion about medication use and risks. Addressing such topics openly allows programs to provide accurate information and discourage unsafe behaviors.

### Outreach and Prevention Efforts

Outreach initiatives extend beyond program participants. Many faith-based organizations collaborate with schools, local agencies, and community groups to spread awareness.

These efforts may include workshops, public events, and support hotlines. By engaging the broader community, programs help identify individuals in need and guide them toward appropriate resources.

## Holistic Healing and Personal Growth

### Addressing Mental and Emotional Health

Addiction often stems from underlying emotional or psychological challenges. Faith-based programs typically incorporate counseling that addresses trauma, stress, and mental health concerns alongside spiritual development.

This holistic approach recognizes that recovery is not just about abstaining from substances. It involves building emotional resilience and developing healthier coping mechanisms.

### Rebuilding Family and Social Connections

Recovery is more sustainable when individuals repair relationships with family and friends. Many programs offer family counseling and workshops to support this process.

Participants may also receive assistance with employment, education, and housing. These practical supports help individuals transition back into everyday life with greater confidence and stability.

## Addressing Complex Substance Dependencies

### Role of Medication-Assisted Treatment

In recent years, some faith-based programs have begun incorporating medication-assisted treatment (MAT). This approach uses approved medications to manage withdrawal symptoms and reduce cravings.

The inclusion of MAT reflects a shift toward more comprehensive care. By combining medical and spiritual strategies, programs can better address the complexities of addiction.

### Managing Emerging and Alternative Substances

Modern recovery programs must also address less traditional substances, such as kratom. These cases often require tailored approaches and informed guidance.

Questions like [Can I Use Suboxone For Kratom Withdrawal?](https://www.choicepointhealth.com/can-i-use-suboxone-for-kratom-withdrawal/) highlight the evolving nature of substance use challenges. Faith-based programs that stay informed on these topics are better equipped to provide relevant and effective support.

## Effectiveness and Challenges

### Measurable Outcomes and Success Stories

Faith-based recovery programs have demonstrated positive outcomes, particularly when integrated with clinical care. Participants often report improved mental health, stronger support networks, and higher levels of personal satisfaction.

Success stories frequently emphasize the importance of community and purpose. Individuals who feel supported and valued are more likely to maintain long-term recovery.

### Limitations and Criticism

Despite their strengths, these programs are not without limitations. Some critics point to a lack of standardization or clinical oversight in certain settings.

Additionally, not all individuals are comfortable with religious frameworks. Ensuring inclusivity and offering alternative options remains an important consideration.

## The Future of Faith-Based Recovery in New Jersey

### Policy Support and Integration

Government agencies increasingly recognize the role of faith-based organizations in addressing addiction. Funding opportunities and partnerships can help integrate these programs with formal healthcare systems.

Such collaboration enhances the overall effectiveness of recovery efforts, ensuring individuals receive both medical and community-based support.

### Expanding Accessibility and Inclusivity

Looking ahead, expanding access will be essential. This includes adapting programs to serve diverse populations and belief systems.

Inclusivity does not mean abandoning spiritual principles. Rather, it involves creating environments where individuals from different backgrounds feel respected and supported.

## External Perspective and Research

Research continues to highlight the value of combining community support with evidence-based treatment approaches. According to the National Institute on Drug Abuse, integrating behavioral therapies with strong support systems can significantly improve recovery outcomes ([Link](https://nida.nih.gov/publications/drugs-brains-behavior-science-addiction/treatment-recovery)).

---

body.title: Persuasion That Changed My Path
body.body:
I am a university student and I have chosen Computer Science as my field of study. This decision wasn’t just based on my personal interest but also involved the guidance and experience of my parents. They convinced me to choose a field that is not only important in today’s era but could also guarantee success in the future. At first, I may not have fully realized it but over time I felt that there was deep truth in what they said.

Computer Science has become the foundation of today’s modern era. Every field in the world, whether it’s education, healthcare, business or entertainment, is connected to technology in some way. Fields like software development, artificial intelligence, cybersecurity and data science are not only advancing rapidly but are also creating countless opportunities for young people. This was the very aspect that drew me further toward this field.

My parents believed that the coming era would be completely digital and only those who understand technology will succeed. They also explained to me that Computer Science is not just a degree but a skill that can make a person independent. Opportunities like online work, freelancing and starting your own company are more available in this field. Their words became a strong source of motivation for me.

Today, as I continue my education, I am confident that I have chosen the right path. Computer Science is not only expanding my knowledge but also preparing me for the practical world. I am grateful to my parents who convinced me and guided me toward a bright future. Now my goal is to gain expertise in this field and achieve success by using my abilities in the best possible way.

body.title: Hive and AI – a combination that could become quite interesting
body.body:
>

For a bit more than a year, I learned to work with AI and I even wrote an [e-book](https://achim03.gumroad.com/l/yjzui) about my discoveries. The one thing that I realised is that working with AI has its own challenges and limitations. The more I learned, the more I realised that in a world of AI agents and AI software, Hive could actually play an important role. But instead of making theories, I want to try things out for myself.

## Vibecoding a chatbot using Hive
When I started vibecoding, first with Google AI Studio and then later with Claude Code, I realised that the favourite output of these tools where solutions that required databases, logins and somewhat complicated deployments. Since I'm not a developer, I needed to figure out a way to make things deployable fast in an uncomplicated manner. So I simply asked the tools to translate the code, into stand alone html/js pages. The big advantage is that such pages can be opened in any browser. This made things so much easier for me. 

I can now do things that are deployed in minutes and can be tested very easily. Also I started to play with free API calls from platforms like open router, cerebras and groq.com. Suddenly, I had my own AI tools. I created a hook tester for reels, I created a thumbnail evaluator for youtube videos, I created curation filter for hive posts and other things. With each tool, I learned something new and started to put things together. 

For my newest tool, which is a chatbot, I integrated hive into the tool. 

You can try the tool here: https://www.ref-hunters.ch/lioteschatbot/index.php

> The tool is for testing purposes at the moment with very limited context.

## A hive post as a RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation)
When using AI tools, it's often necessary to give the tool a knowledge base. This is a text that the AI should be considering as source of truth. This makes a lot of sense for example if you want to define in which area the AI should be proficient. For my chatbot, I created [a hive post](https://peakd.com/liotes/@liotes.learn/liotes-your-hive-blockchain-adventure) with an account that has not curation trail and declined the payout. The post sums up more or less what Liotes is and the different facets of the project (not extensively). This post becomes the source of truth for my chatbot. 

> What is fantastic is that I can simply use a tool like ecency or peakd to update my post and the information of the chatbot are updated in real time!

## Hive login system to access the admin panel
For the tool, I created an admin panel that can only be accessed with my hive account and keychain. The tool generates a message with keychain that needs to be signed, to confirm that I'm authorized to access the admin panel. 

In this admin panel, I can set the api keys for the AI models and also define the CSS of the tool. 

## Multilingual chatbot
The great thing is that the user can chose his language and ask the bot questions about Liotes. The knowledge base is for the moment very limited for testing purpose. The AI checks the hive post and tries to answer the question of the user in his language. Thanks to an API that lives on most computers, the user can even listen to the answer. 

## Free API's
For this tool, I'm using only free API calls from groq.com and cerebras that are pretty fast. The thing is that I could also link open router API keys to my tool and I could give access to almost any model that are supported by open router. 

## Further development
In my opinion, this opens amazing potential for Hive. This tool alone could be used by any type of business that wants to have a chatbot. It's free to run and gives very quick answers. Now we could take the same tool and simple change the hive post to which it relates and we have a totally different chatbot. It could be used to create a hive bot that answers all the questions that newbies have....

The tool could be adapted so that it could offer AI services of any kind. 

## How Hive could be used for AI
- Posts as knowledge bases (RAG)
- Account system for login, user management, authorisations, etc...
- custom_json to store settings, database, progress, logs, licences for the projects
- memo key with hash to store AI API keys on chain so that people could use their own keys for services provided. Also with second layer password coding
- free transactions so that AI services can be paid directly while submitting the prompt. Even with very small amounts.
- access gating through hive payments
- credit gating through hive payments
- subscriptions with hive subscriptions
- marketplace for AI services
- marketplace for AI agents
- Reputation system with Hive power and age on blockchain
- Distribution and marketing of tools through the hive blockchain blog system and short form messages

Hive brings a lot of things to the table that AI apps need to be working. It offers a playfield for vibe coders where they don't need an expensive or complicated environment to develop working tools. I think this could be something that differentiates hive and could bring new users and investments.

body.title: WHEN FREEDOM BECOMES OVERWHELMING ... Kiss Blog Idea Week #210
body.body:
I vividly remember that particular day, not because anything sensational occurred on that day, but because nothing occurred.

I got up and had a whole day to look forward to... no pressure.
I said to myself today I am going to be productive.

I had options.


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmXbLQ7dH4qwK4pLz7VQD7ei3Lyy1HAdZbdeni8NkwJg5m/img_20260505_wa0010.jpg)

I had the opportunity to practice my writing.
I could study.
I could go out.
I could rest.
I would even attempt something different.

Everything was open.

And somehow that was the thing.

I had begun with my phone.

To check something really fast.

One application gave rise to another. Then another. Before I knew it, almost an hour had passed and I hadn’t done anything meaningful. So I attempted to reboot.

I said to myself, okay, now we have to concentrate.

However, another choice came.

What is it specifically I should pay attention to?

Writing?
Learning?
Planning?
Resting?

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmY2ZdYU5xC2che1pwqaBpW3XfF5W1jYL8krso3AaBUipr/snapchat_1905909585.jpg)


Each of the options was legitimate.

All the options seemed significant.

And, as it were, on account of that none of them felt clear.


I went to my laptop, opened a document, gazed at it a few minutes then shut it.

Not that I was unable to write.

But since I was not able to determine whether that was the most appropriate thing to do at that time.

So I changed once more.

Tried watching something. Didn’t feel right.

Tried reading. Couldn’t concentrate.

Tried resting. Felt guilty.

It was evening and I had made so many almosts.

Almost worked.
Almost rested.
Nearly liked the day.

But not fully.

And that was when it struck me.

It was not the issue of time.

It wasn’t laziness either.

Excessive options were too many.


It was one of the lessons that I learned that day, which I did not anticipate.

The freedom of the unlimited options does not mean that you are free.

In some cases, it generates stalling.

Since when everything is possible your mind begins to seek out the ideal choice.

And in endeavoring to seek perfection... you postpone action.


Since that time I have begun to do something easy.

I narrow down my choices even before the day has arrived.

I choose one or two out of five things that I would have given myself to choose.

That’s it.

No back and forth.

No overthinking.

Just a straight direction.


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmaMLW2oP96cuB6XSKMp8cNxmNV3Xq8QFkjRncteB1Lpep/img_20260115_wa0040.jpeg)


And, unexpectedly, life began to seem lighter.

Not that I now had less to do, but because I had less to determine.

And there is a peace that is in the knowing:

That is what I am doing to-day.

No internal debate.

No constant switching.

Just clarity.


There is one other thing I have noticed.

When you are not able to make any choices, then you are more present.

Instead of thinking about what you can be doing, you give more attention on what you are doing.

And that alters all.

I would believe that the peace was a result of choice.

I believe now that it stems not only out of not having to have so many.

The reason is that, not all decisions are value adding.

There are some which simply make noise.

That day revealed to me that More freedom is not always necessary.

Sometimes…

you simply require less choices.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmVPJpkfrMGrWVz94MGvnt6TBC2Fpems2Y8LHiURkmGTyq/img_20260421_wa0000.jpg)

body.title: We are still stuck!
body.body: # We are still stuck!\n\nSo its been more two months since the US-Israel alliance started the war with Iran (started on Feb 28). I have written a few posts about the importance of strait of Hormuz, [here](https://peakd.com/hive-180505/@azircon/traffic-through-me), and [here](https://peakd.com/hive-180505/@azircon/strait-of-hormuz-its-importance-in-energy-transportation). This war have been significantly [asymmetric](https://peakd.com/hive-180505/@azircon/cost-pyramid) and the main reason that US a pausing its activity is not because there are no targets, but simply because we ran out of ammunitions a little bit! Funny as it may sound, it is the United States who is running low on ammunitions because of the strong asymmetry of this war. Also, the war will continue to remain highly asymmetric to a factor of about 200:1 to perhaps 400:1. As I mentioned in one of the posts before, there are several nations in Asia which are hitting the storage limit now, and therefore, the time for the \

that I discussed in one of my post is now imminent. So let us talk about the potential scenarios at hand now. 

![image.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmSGFGUC5ZPfQNFVrc8KSzLvvZp3u8DjLXC7r5JnV992BC/image.png)

[Source](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/5/5/map-of-dominance-why-iran-cant-afford-to-give-up-hormuz-control)

The image above is the current Iranian \
for their version of the control of Hormuz and they want a \

from every ship! Well, I have promised in the past that I don't want to drift into opinions on this matter, so I will try my best to keep this post factual.

# Can't US Navy do the Escort?

Sure, they can. They are saying they will have to. Currently nearly 2000 ships are stuck on either side. Yet, there will be problems:

- Insurance: The insurance companies currently declining to insure any ships and their cargo going through the strait of Hormuz. This is the fundamental problem, and there is very little you are reading about it in the news

- Geography favors Iran: The strait is very narrow—about 21 miles (34 km) wide, with shipping lanes only ~2 miles wide in each direction. Ships are forced into predictable paths, making them easy to track and target. Iran sits on the northern shoreline and nearby islands (Qeshm, Abu Musa, etc.), giving it: 
	- Short response times
	- Ability to hide launchers, boats, and missiles along the coast

This creates a classic “chokepoint advantage” or a \

where a weaker local force can threaten a stronger navy. This will be true to any vessels that will be escorted by US Navy and the Navy ships. Iran can potentially hit targets from shoreline, and the mountains near shores. Hell, it is so close that a shoulder mount weapon can do damage to a ship. It doesn't have to be sunk, just a minor damage will be enough.

# Asymmetric warfare tactics

Iran does not need to defeat the U.S. Navy head-on. Instead, it uses asymmetric tools that are hard to counter simultaneously: Fast attack craft & swarm tactics

- Hundreds of small, fast boats armed with:
	- Rockets
	- Machine guns
	- Anti-ship missiles


- They can attack in swarms, overwhelming defenses

- Naval mines: 
	- Cheap, hard to detect
	- Even a few mines can:

		- Damage tankers
		- Shut down traffic due to insurance risk


- Clearing mines is slow and dangerous

#  High volume of civilian traffic and Escalation Risk

- ~20% of global oil supply passes through Hormuz
- Constant flow of:

	- Oil tankers
	- Cargo vessels


- This creates:

	- Congestion
	- Limited maneuverability
	- Risk of misidentification

The Navy must operate in a crowded civilian environment, making engagement rules complex. So, in other words, this can't possibly be a long term solution. There must be \

between the Iranian government and International community at some point in time. If that requires a different govt. or present govt. that is up to the complexity of the deal. Bottomline, the U.S. Navy can escort ships and keep the strait open, but  it cannot do so easily, cheaply, or without significant risk—especially against a determined Iran using asymmetric tactics. So, ultimately this leads to a final item, cost! Who pays for it? To whom?

Cat is out of bag ladies and gentlemen. Someone got to pay! Most likely, it will be you and I!

body.title: Cleanliness is key; Chidera's story
body.body:
In the quiet bustle of Ilorin, just behind a busy bank building, there stood a public toilet most people tried not to notice. It wasn’t hidden, but it wasn’t respected either. Customers rushed in and out, often holding their breath, eager to leave as quickly as they came.

To them, it was just a place of necessity.
But to Chidera, it was something more.
Every morning, before the bank doors opened, Chidera arrived with her bucket, brush, and quiet determination. She unlocked each door carefully, stepping into a space many would avoid. The smell didn’t surprise her anymore. The dirt didn’t discourage her either.
What others saw as filth, she saw as duty.
She wasn’t just cleaning toilets—she was preserving dignity in a place where people had forgotten it existed.

Public toilets carry silent stories.
There was the woman who rushed in, her face tense, only to come out moments later adjusting her clothes and her confidence. There was the elderly man who came every morning, moving slowly but grateful. There were students, traders, and bank customers each leaving behind traces of their lives in a place no one wanted to claim.
One afternoon, a sharply dressed man stepped in, clearly irritated.
“Why is this place always like this?” he muttered, covering his nose.
Chidera, who had just finished rinsing the floor, replied calmly,
“Because many people use it, but only a few people care for it.”

The man paused, but like many others, he walked away without truly understanding.
Days turned into weeks.
And then, slowly, Chidera began to feel it.
At first, it was just discomfort. A slight irritation she ignored, thinking it was nothing. But it didn’t go away. Instead, it grew burning, persistent, and quietly painful. The kind of pain that doesn’t shout but refuses to be ignored.
Still, she kept working.
Because missing a day meant losing money.
Because no one was waiting to replace her.
Because survival doesn’t always give you the luxury of rest.
But the truth was simple and heavy: the environment she worked in was affecting her health. The same place she cleaned daily, the same place she tried to make better for others, had begun to take something from her.
The female body, delicate in its own way, had limits.
One morning, she couldn’t ignore it anymore.
She sat outside the toilet, her cleaning tools beside her, her strength reduced to silence. For the first time, the place she had cared for so faithfully felt like it had betrayed her.
And yet, it wasn’t just the toilet.
It was neglect.
It was a system where people used what was provided but never protected it. Where workers like Chidera were expected to endure conditions no one else would tolerate. Where cleanliness was demanded, but support was absent.
That day, something changed.
A small sign appeared again on the wall:
“This place serves you. Respect it. Someone’s health depends on it.”

This time, the message carried weight.
Because behind every public space is a human being.
And behind every act of carelessness is a consequence someone else may have to bear.
In that small corner behind the bank in Ilorin, Chidera’s story became more than just a routine it became a reminder.
That dignity is not just about having access to public facilities.
It is about how we treat them.
And how we treat the people who care for them.
