body.title: the union between Egypt and Italy in the Temple of Ellesiya
body.body:
![IMG_3442.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/butterfly-jt9/EoeEsQNNxq3znuATiWLfpDyJ3km1ZauKjSjL7MQy7mhARfzBeoFZ4jdhrdH6qTPvDvR.JPG)


Today friends, I want to talk to you about a very beautiful thing, something that people manage to do, that they have managed to do and that if they want to do things together they always manage to achieve them, today I will talk to you about my visit to the tomb of Ellisiya, which is located near the Egyptian museum, in fact it has a lot to do with Egypt and can be visited completely free of charge, just take and book the ticket online on the website of the Egyptian museum of Turin


![IMG_3501.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/butterfly-jt9/Eoc84Y2JipT5FKZQ3W17ch73urSMBqoJxJumk8wxw5RaWQYSKGx598R6GsiEpsKdGkQ.JPG)

It is basically a Nubian temple that was carved into the rock in Egypt, it dates back to around 1450 BC, and it is a place of worship dedicated to Egyptian deities. In the 1960s, a very important event happened: Egypt had to build a dam because it needed water, but this would have led to the flooding of many museums, and so Italy participated in the rescue of these Egyptian temples. It is a wonderful thing when people participate in something truly cultural. As a thank you, Egypt donated the temple to Italy, and it was made available to all people to visit for free, as it was a gift.


![IMG_3440.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/butterfly-jt9/EoEo8CuX86w4oMP9kFyg9Xb8BdUvuM8Yx7ExEYpAsL8W5iVRiHTKmpM6sL45YnDqMro.JPG)

![IMG_3434.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/butterfly-jt9/EoEp1seL4gZArCRKPXd8KaZcZLoBpoukUsUyLhbtoshiCQmQuMsHE9xYDQnonxgL2zX.JPG)

![IMG_3439.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/butterfly-jt9/EoChZiGodz8rrCHXCUptrrRBX6BDktBicqrX9tutXBHRXw9eJDvaTPoGQMwkybM6qbj.JPG)

So basically in 1966 it was dismantled, transported and rebuilt in Turin, but this is one of the last installations which was inaugurated last year, because it took many years to be able to reassemble this structure with this central corridor and two lateral rooms partly decorated with ritual scenes and pharaoh offerings. But the real surprise is that this place was also used as a Christian place. In fact there are crosses engraved in the stone inside this Temple.


![IMG_3450.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/butterfly-jt9/EokdaPUTCjst6ND9EzumKFaZfUFzLShF8n3VmFaNs69Ft5DPsVEGmwhiGCvpZz1cHBN.JPG)


It's very beautiful because now there is an interactive part, which explains the whole history of this temple, and it was very moving for me to understand the history and see the collaboration between different peoples to save this monument that belongs to the world, if you pass by Turin, stop by because it's a visit. It's very short because it lasts about 20 minutes, but in my opinion it's very beautiful to see it live and to be able to understand the history behind this important monument.


![IMG_3485.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/butterfly-jt9/23wC2xxfBumUEy76TCeQzeBxdPouDXZbZe74whnqbmSSLpaRGVNZyGkdXUapCajkDKKZm.JPG)

![IMG_3486.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/butterfly-jt9/23u62sxtUrEVNQMKNnxGvuZrC1hLLP4ar8t8DMZKjfSfSfgLK8xWbdQwFgtmDc9BAt1T8.JPG)

![IMG_3492.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/butterfly-jt9/23vhsGhLXf2Uw3JNQBdJsSjfi6ErqpfxsGmYKdZ4kkAQgJLDU6Y7Ypx83HYG9h4TjGWYa.JPG)

![IMG_3487.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/butterfly-jt9/23vsNTzbdLbF3UgtGmDmScjteuj4ZbEB7j7atQ9ukXXzkSbH4oPneeMeR84qDN5StHafZ.JPG)

I hope my photos and my story were interesting, see you next time and I wish you all a good day

body.title: THE REALITY OF LIFE- LIFE IS UNCERTAIN
body.body:
**LIFE IS UNCERTAIN**
In a world that has two faces, the physical and digital world, it is the same that life is uncertain. we don't know what tomorrow will bring. We keep struggling, we keep moving, we chase our dreams but along the way, we encounter maybe challenges, shortages, or unexpected struggles. Our government always reminding us to be resilient and one thing becomes clear, we must learn and learn for us to keep standing, moving and learn to make use what we have.

We see in social media, fancy living like sometimes,I keep thinking, am I the one struggling? Why this people seems in all good terms? When will be the time, I will experience eating in a fancy restaurant, cooking delicious like some are featuring in their social media?

But later on, I realized looking at our simple meals, I am reminded that food does not have to be expensive to be meaningful. A few vegetable in the backyard, cooked with care, can already feed my family. These dishes may look ordinary, but htey carry something important, being ***resourceful***, ***patience*** and ***gratitude***. God really bless a grateful heart. 

Last Sunday, a family from lowland came to visit us here in our place, and they appreciated the vegetable planted in our backyard. They said, it is really a blessing in our place because we have space to plant, we have plenty of water and the weather is good but in their place, they can't plant this season due to no enough water supply. So, before they went home, they enjoy picking vegetables. 

In times of crisis, having a small source of food in our home is really a great blessing not only for us but to others, too. 

So, I can say that a backyard garden can become a quiet answer to uncertainty. It reminds us people that while we cannot control everything in life, we can prepare, adapt, and provide for ourselves in simple ways and even extend our helping hands to others by sharing what we have.

Yes life is uncertain, but we have a choice being prepared, adaptive and resilient.

God bless everyone!

body.title: Prepping Various Chicken Freezer Meals - by Sunscape
body.body:
![foodiesbeehive-tandori-chicken.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmSPteQ29JENQ77xi7syWRZYfCmSrKnWgR7pnth1pBhHAU/foodiesbeehive-tandori-chicken.jpg)

It took me two entire mornings to prep these freezer meals.  It was a lot of standing at the stove, but I'm happy to have so many meals prepared.  Below is a Tandori marinade I used with spices I had on hand.  
##### Tandori Chicken
2 pounds chicken quarters or a mix of thighs and drumsticks
1 inch ginger, minced
2 cloves garlic, minced
1 tablespoon olive oil
1 cup plain yogurt
1 teaspoon cumin
1 teaspoon cinnamon
1 teaspoon smoked paprika
1 teaspoon ground coriander
1 teaspoon turmeric
1 teaspoon black pepper
1 teaspoon salt
1/2 teaspoon of ground nutmeg


![foodiesbeehive-tandori-chicken-1.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmQJ8EEqtHkoxE62Yw4k3JioujLWewQMkv7MXvg4XpEuqd/foodiesbeehive-tandori-chicken-1.jpg)

Combine all the spices with the oil and yogurt and mix very well. Add the marinade to the chicken, coating well, and let it marinate for a few hours.  Then bake the chicken at 375°F until thoroughly cooked. 

I had enough marinade to do three different meals.  One for that night's dinner, and the rest went into the freezer. 

![foodiesbeehive-tandori-chicken-.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmPUmsVDeq4BXPAb8NgAZVjoMnwy8NngH2H4Q9bXUhPVFx/foodiesbeehive-tandori-chicken-.jpg)

Up next, I had two family-sized packages of chicken breasts to do. It took a while to trim off excess fat and slice the breasts into thin pieces.  Then I pounded each slice to make cutlets for Chicken Parmesan, Cordon Bleu, and Chicken French.    

![foodiesbeehive-food-prep-chicken-cutlets.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmXAxrGCofF8TumevYeeUZmUd9zm3J1Y3YTC5xD6tMpybR/foodiesbeehive-food-prep-chicken-cutlets.jpg)

Four Chicken Parmesan.

![foodiesbeehive-food-prep-chicken-parmesean.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmVTR4VB2eLGhrnAza1mXooE421Yc9hpvYg5FGWvrZnzsi/foodiesbeehive-food-prep-chicken-parmesean.jpg)

Five Chicken Cordon Bleu.

![foodiesbeehive-food-prep-chicken-4.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmd6KcBPzb6XJCNZcxeusoupEKRJtXC3rrYAmDdbNmVzay/foodiesbeehive-food-prep-chicken-4.jpg)

I made a sauce for the Cordon Bleu and put enough for each meal into 1/2 pint mason jars and froze them, too.

![sauce (1).jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmPksHVDi3UZdqmegG1RDLxyAX8zoKbQQfkLuEaM3jg3fp/sauce%20(1).jpg)


Four Chicken French.

![foodiesbeehive-food-prep-chicken-french-.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmUJtT3VonGPeKsGzqLAMboqYNxzh82JwTMXfVAyD7D69L/foodiesbeehive-food-prep-chicken-french-.jpg)

After dipping the cutlets into egg, then flour, I let them rest while preparing the sauce. 

![foodiesbeehive-food-prep-chicken-french.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmbnqiHKNfphYVsPPVoqWaZztWJ4a8GxvcX4LYSntWsqTw/foodiesbeehive-food-prep-chicken-french.jpg)

Chicken French is probably one of my favorites, and it freezes so nicely.  Making large batches at a time really pays off. Plus, cleanup is easier when I do marathon cooking.


![chicken french.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmXgVhVampn6JXQjbRYziyFAv2sWPBuUS5i6FYaoSH9msz/chicken%20french.jpg)

Can you smell the lemony sauce? It smells divine.


![chicken french freezer meals.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmcdgnBPiREFxyu5dUMFLbgNaQDhQWNHputd73nC3iSoiL/chicken%20french%20freezer%20meals.jpg)

Three meals for the freezer and one shared with a neighbor for his dinner.  He was so happy with a homemade meal.

Altogether, I put 15 meals into the freezer by prepping the chicken one morning and frying the cutlets the second day.  It will be a huge help to have meals on hand when I have to take care of my hubby when he has shoulder surgery soon.  

There will be more meals to prepare, but I'm taking a break and playing in the garden this week.  


![banner-sunscape-2.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmYr3stqM7yx8cpipf8v6F4YgkM2aD282NSQrGYzJZqCxE/banner-sunscape-2.jpg)

body.title: The Night I Chose a Different Path
body.body:
/>

  
  
  
Sometimes in life a night comes when everything has been going along with your routine, and then suddenly a voice starts speaking from within: what would happen if you did something different today?

The question that arises is why such thoughts come into our minds. As far as I can tell, these thoughts occur because our same old problem—the same recurring thoughts—keep hammering the same point over and over in our minds: “What if that happens? What if it happens? What will happen if I do this? What will happen then?” …what will happen if I do that? All these things become part of our routine fatigue. As soon as we fall asleep, our mind keeps repeating them over and over, and we start having strange thoughts in our sleep.

Along with that, our heart and our mind are locked in a strange battle where our mind wants to go to a peaceful side and our heart wants to follow our desires, which creates a strange fear, and in that our situation is… It comes down to making a decision: what should we do now? We've never felt this way before.

Now what happens is that the path doesn't seem safe to us. The biggest fear we have is what people will think: “What if I fail? What if I succeed?” We can't fully let go of those thoughts, but that very struggle is the path to growth that makes it hard for us to get started. is the biggest fear that's holding us back.

We're faced with new experiences we've never seen before, about which we've never expected how we'll struggle against or for them. We don't even have clarity for ourselves. What mistakes will we make in learning? We haven't learned from every mistake. A person improves themselves. What does it take to understand? We haven't learned everything, so all these fears keep repeating the same thing over and over inside us. I work…

In the end, I'll just say this: every night a new battle rages in our hearts and minds, and in it we're filled with countless questions—which path to take, which one will benefit us, which road will lead to success, whether we'll end up failing if… …that if we fail, what will people say? That fear really holds us back. It's just that we don't have the courage to take that step. If we could find the courage to believe in ourselves—to say “I can do it”—then we would succeed, and it's always those who say… “We don't know whether we can or can't, so always count yourself among those who think, ‘I can.’”

body.title: WOO’s Mayday Mayhem: When Chaos Becomes Opportunity
body.body:
A Big Hello to all WOO Fans! 🥳🥳🥳 WOO! 

There’s a certain kind of energy that only WOO can create. It’s not just about matches, not just about cards, and definitely not just about rewards. It’s that feeling when something new drops and you immediately know you’re going to be logging in more, thinking more, planning more. That’s exactly the vibe I got when I saw the announcement for Mayday Mayhem.

>*Don't miss out on yet another limited time event from WOO, \

, taking place from 1st May 2026 till 31st May 2026! Go to [THIS LINK](https://play.wrestlingorganizationonline.com/event) to join and get another chance to win even more WOO Jobber packs now!*

---

![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/blitzzzz/23tbttwkJApisCbEfQu4ioTAv2BuLQqoroWFKLr667tUgU4i5UN8VM8qbVvDwZEfzTj8M.png)

---

This isn’t just another event thrown into the calendar to keep things ticking over. This feels deliberate. It feels like WOO is doubling down on something that has been quietly building momentum over the past few weeks, and that is the Jobber system. If you’ve been paying attention, you’ll know that Jobbers are no longer just filler or side content. They are slowly becoming a core part of the ecosystem, and Mayday Mayhem is proof of that shift.

A full month-long event dedicated to Jobbers is not something you casually roll out. This is WOO telling us that this system matters, and more importantly, that players who engage with it now are going to benefit the most in the long run.

---

## Here's what's happening!!!

* **A Full Month of Mayhem Changes Everything**
  
One of the first things that stood out to me was the duration of this event. Running from May 1 to May 31, this is not a quick weekend grind or a short burst of activity. This is a sustained event that requires consistency, planning, and long-term engagement. As a fan, I actually appreciate this more because it allows for pacing. Not everyone can grind daily, but over a month, you can find your rhythm and still feel involved.

* **750 Jobber Packs Is Not a Small Number**
  
Let’s be honest, when we see numbers like this, it’s easy to gloss over them. But 750 packs is significant. That is a lot of potential new wrestlers entering the ecosystem, and more importantly, a lot of chances for players to pull something meaningful. From a fan perspective, this creates excitement because every single pack has potential. It is not just about participation anymore, it is about anticipation.

* **Every Pack Matters More Than It Seems**
  
Each WOO Jobber Pack contains one Jobber NFT Wrestler, and that might sound simple on the surface. But when you think about it, every single pack is a roll of the dice. You are not just opening a pack, you are potentially pulling a Common, Rare, Epic, or Legendary. That unpredictability is what keeps me hooked. It is the same feeling you get when opening card packs in real life.

* **The Growth of Jobbers as a System**
  
I have been watching how WOO has been developing the Jobber system, and it is clear that this is not a temporary feature. By building an entire event around Jobbers, WOO is reinforcing their importance. As a fan, this makes me rethink how I approach collecting and strategy. Jobbers are no longer background characters. They are becoming assets.

* **Consistency Over Burst Play**
  
What I like about this event is that it rewards ongoing participation rather than one-time effort. This changes how I personally approach the game. Instead of rushing everything in a short period, I can spread out my activity, stay engaged, and still feel like I am progressing.

---

## So... to round up!

Mayday Mayhem feels like one of those turning points that we might look back on later and say, “that was when things started to shift.” It is not flashy in the sense of introducing completely new mechanics, but it is impactful in how it strengthens an existing system.

From a fan perspective, this is exactly the kind of event I enjoy. It gives me a reason to log in consistently, a reason to care about every pack, and a reason to keep building my collection.

The mayhem is not just in the name. It is in the possibilities that every single pack brings.

---

Well, that's it for today. We will continue again tomorrow! 😁 WOO! 🎉

body.title: When ease rises, will creativity fall?
body.body: This prompt evokes a very strong thought on the recent trend of things especially with the rise and hike of AI. The question is will the use of AI stall human creativity? Well, in my opinion, I’d say that the emergence of AI is not a blow on human creativity but its definitely changes the rules of the creating games. With time we have seen that every major advancement in technology has triggered this same worry. When photography was invented, we thought painting was going to die. When calculator became common, we thought that we were going to loose mathematical thinking but in all these developments, we saw that creativity didn’t die rather creativity was shifted. What we are seeing is another shift with Ai and not extinction. The real risk here is not that Ai creates things but that humans may stop trying to be deep in their creativity. There’s a price for ease. When something becomes too easy or convenient, human may be tempted to avoid struggling and take the easy route. But we know that it’s in the face of struggles, trials, errors frustrations and etc that our creativity is better forged. If we rely on Ai blindly, our creativity will be weakened. Not because Ai exists but because we stopped exercising our creativity muscles. But there’s another side to this. So we can actually expand our creativity. It can help someone who doesn’t have design skills to visualize an idea. It can help to speed up the time we spend on executing things so we can spend more time on thinking and strategizing. So the question is not about whether technology is killing creativity rather it’s about how we are choosing to use technology. These are ways we can stay creative: * Stay the origin and do not be just an editor. We should not allow Ai do all the thinking for us. We can start our own ideas even if we don’t have it all figured out. We can use tools to refine our ideas and not replace our thinking. * We should build taste and not just output because creativity is not just about production, it’s about judgement. The ability to say that this works and the other doesn’t is deeply human. Machines can generate options for us but taste comes from the experiences we live. * We should intentionally embrace constrains and sometimes try to create something without AI. We can decide to write from scratch, design with fewer tools as these can helps us to sharpen our originality. * We can choose to focus on story telling perspective. Ai can recreate patterns but it cannot live our lives. Our experiences, voices, cultures and our emotions are our creativity advantage. It’s makes our works unique. * We can use Ai as a collaborator and not a crutch. We should see it as a fast and helpful assistant but not the visionary. We are still the director. In fields like architecture. Machines helps to optimize structures and reduce costs but the soul of the designs, the emotions it evokes and the meaning behind is still from human intents. Therefore our most powerful creations will be as a blend of human imaginations and the precision from machines. Therefore creativity isn’t dying, the real treat is the rise of passive consumption. body.title: The lesson AI can’t solve [EN/PT]
body.body:
>



“Dad, can I skip school?”
“Why?”
“Because I was supposed to have done an assignment to turn in today, but I forgot.”
“Okay, but we’re going to talk about this later.”

I’m the kind of father who eases up, who tries to understand the situation. That assignment was supposed to be turned in that morning, but he forgot, even though he had three days to do it. Lack of responsibility? Yes, but I wasn’t going to scold him. I gave him a second chance, the lecture came later.

I found out he was doing the assignment with the help of Chatgpt, and then the lecture came. Not aggressively, without yelling or showing anger, but rather to make him understand that this is cheating and that using artificial intelligence to do the work was just a form of regression for his learning, that he was harming himself.

The assignment was math, exercises and assignments exist for learning through practice, and I explained that to him. His response was that he already did this same type of calculation at school almost every day.

So my agreement with him was to delete everything that had been done up to that point with the help of his artificial intelligence friend and redo everything manually. Double the work to understand that he needs to follow the rules and that shortcuts only delay progress when used dishonestly.

He was upset, of course. In the mind of an almost teenager, things are a little different. So to ease the tension, I made him a snack and gave him a 20 minute break.

I sat down at the computer and asked Chatgpt to generate 10 more exercises similar to the ones it had been providing answers for to my son, twice as many as his original assignment required, and told my son to complete the tasks generated by his AI friend.

In the end, a lesson was taught. The second chance was given and, even then, he still wanted to do things the easier way. He needed to understand that too much convenience, when used the wrong way, gets in the way more than it helps. Technology is there to assist, explain, and teach, but never to replace the effort that learning requires.

In the end, he did everything. The assignment plus twice the number of exercises. I was inclined to make him spend the whole day doing even more, but deep down I knew that would not have sent a good message. I think what I truly wanted to teach in that moment was accomplished. I tried to be understanding, but I was firm when the opportunity was not used the way it should have been. I know every mother and father has their own way of educating, but this is the way I try to teach him, through how we respond to mistakes and even through showing leniency in certain situations. Maybe the biggest lesson that day wasn’t about math after all.

\

Sou o tipo de pai que alivia, que tenta entender a situação. Esse trabalho era para entregar naquela manhã, mas ele esqueceu, mesmo tendo três dias para ter feito. Falta de responsabilidade? Sim, mas eu não iria dar uma bronca. Dei uma segunda chance, a bronca veio depois. Descobri que ele estava fazendo o trabalho com a ajuda do Chatgpt, e então a bronca veio. Não de forma agressiva, sem gritos ou demonstração de raiva, mas sim uma bronca para fazê-lo entender que isso é trapaça e que usar inteligência artificial para fazer o trabalho era apenas uma forma de regressão para o seu aprendizado, que ele estava se prejudicando. O trabalho era de matemática, exercícios e trabalhos servem para o aprendizado através da prática, e expliquei isso para ele. Sua resposta foi dizer que já fazia esse mesmo tipo de conta na escola quase todos os dias. Então, meu acordo com ele foi apagar tudo o que foi feito até então com a ajuda da amiga inteligência artificial e refazer tudo manualmente. Trabalho redobrado para entender que deve seguir as regras e que atalhos servem para atrasar se for de forma desonesta. Ele ficou chateado, claro, na cabeça de quase adolescentes as coisas são um pouco diferentes. Então para aliviar a tensão, eu fiz um lanche para ele e dei um descanso de 20 minutos. Sentei no computador e solicitei que o Chatgpt fizesse mais 10 exercícios similares àqueles dos quais ele estava fornecendo a resposta para o meu filho, o dobro do que sua tarefa exigia e disse para meu filho fazer as tarefas que foram geradas pela amiga IA. Por fim, uma lição foi dada. A segunda chance foi dada e, ainda assim, ele queria fazer as coisas pelo caminho mais fácil. Precisava entender que facilidade demais, quando usada da forma errada, atrapalha mais do que ajuda. A tecnologia está aí para auxiliar, explicar e ensinar, mas nunca para substituir o esforço que o aprendizado exige. No fim, ele fez tudo. O trabalho mais o dobro das lições, fiquei inclinado a fazer ele passar o dia fazendo mais exercícios, mas no fundo exagero não iria passar uma boa mensagem. Acho que o que de fato eu queria ensinar ali foi feito, tentei ser compreensível, mas fui duro quando a oportunidade não foi usada da forma que deveria. Sei que cada pai e mãe tem uma forma de educar, mas essa é a maneira que eu tento ensina-lo, através da postura diante de erros e até mesmo em aliviar em alguma situação. Talvez a maior lição daquele dia não tenha sido sobre matemática.

body.title: The Revolving Ghost
body.body: <center>\n\nThere is a particular kind of exhaustion that comes from a revolving door. When someone enters your life only to leave again without a word, they don’t just leave a void—they leave a mountain of questions that you are forced to answer alone. It is the cruelty of \
being used as bait, pulling you back into a cycle that feels less like love and more like a trap. Eventually, the heart stops asking \

***

The Revolving Ghost

He was there for a fleeting season,
A sudden light, a hollow reason.
I thought the roots were sinking deep,
But he left in silence, secrets to keep.
He walked away with no goodbye,
Leaving me a list of \

Then he returned, a familiar flame,
Whispering hope and calling my name.
I opened the door, I let him in,
Believing this time the story would win.
But the light went out, the air turned cold,
And once again, the same ghost took hold.

Now he stands at the threshold once more,
Waiting for me to unbolt the door.
But I am haunted by the questions I face:
Is there any magic left in this place?
Is it worth the weight of the dark to follow,
When every promise rings so hollow?

Should I hold the spark until it burns,
And wait for the lesson the heart never learns?
Or should I break the wheel and finally see,
That the only way out is to set myself free?
The loop is a cage where the spirit grows thin,
And I am tired of letting the winter back in. *** The magic is no longer magical when it is used to keep you suspended in uncertainty. I am realizing that \

isn't a loss of love, but a gain of peace. To break the loop is to choose a path where the ground doesn't disappear beneath my feet every time he decides to leave. I am trading the flickering light of his return for the steady, quiet warmth of my own freedom.\n\n</center>

- Iran zaatakował wczoraj cele w Zjednoczonych Emiratach Arabskich. Irańskie pociski i drony uderzyły w rafinerię w mieście Fudżajra, wywołując duży pożar i raniąc trzy osoby. Emirackie władze poinformowały, że obrona przeciwlotnicza zestrzeliła dodatkowo 12 pocisków balistycznych, 3 pociski manewrujące i 4 drony.

- Władze Iranu oświadczyły, że do zaognienia sytuacji doprowadziło \
. Atak był odpowiedzią na amerykańską operację \

, która zdaniem Iranu stanowi złamanie zawieszenia broni.

- Póki co nie doszło do wznowienia walk. Irański atak został jednoznacznie i ostro potępiony przez państwa Zatoki Perskiej, ale też m.in. przez Pakistan, który wyraził solidarność z władzami ZEA i stwierdził, że działania Iranu podkopują proces dyplomatyczny.

- Abbas Araqczi napisał na X, że amerykańskie działania i wczorajsze zaostrzenie sytuacji pokazują, że konflikt USA z Iranem nie ma rozwiązania militarnego i można zakończyć go wyłącznie drogą dyplomatyczną.

- Pete Hegseth powiedział, że z perspektywy USA zawieszenie broni z Iranem nadal trwa. Określił wczorajsze ataki jako \

do wznowienia walk. Jednocześnie ostrzegł, że Stany Zjednoczone stanowczo odpowiedzą na jakikolwiek atak wymierzony w ich statki handlowe.

- Abbas Araqczi wyruszył dziś z oficjalną wizytą do Pekinu. Spotka się z nim chiński minister spraw zagranicznych, Wang Yi.

body.title: Trip to Miličinica - a hidden hilly village above Valjevo
body.body: Have you ever made your family tree and how far back did you get in your research? 🌳 A few years ago, I was gathering information about my ancestors, some from stories, some from census records and some from church books. I created a tree starting from my direct ancestor Raja Babić, who was born way back in 1798. He is my **_askurđel_**, meaning the seventh male generation back. Isn't it interesting to know that? I loved trying to research even further, to reach earlier centuries, but I couldn't find anything beyond that information... Maybe, like most Balkan peoples, we moved from place to place over the centuries. Anyway, this time we went to a village called _Miličinica_ in search of information about my fiancé's distant ancestors. Some books say that about two centuries ago they most likely moved from that charming little hillside village above Valjevo. Sunday was a really beautiful spring day, so the two of us, together with his sister and aunt, headed out to that area.

/>We wandered around a bit at the beginning, but that turned out to be such an interesting part of the trip because along the way we met wonderful people who pointed us in the right direction. The man who gave us directions turned out to be a retired professor from the Faculty of Agriculture. He had spent the previous winter researching his ancestors with his wife, so he gave us better insight into how to look for information in historical archives. While we were chatting, he mentioned that in the place we were heading to, his roommate from his student days has vineyards and runs a winery, so we ended up bringing greetings to him as well. Just imagine how cool that is, after driving around some 20 kilometers to reach our destination, we were carrying greetings from one old man to another, without knowing either of them. 😀\n\n

/>While we were driving to that village, we were amazed by the view on both sides of the road. Such a cute little hills, mostly covered with orchards and the occasional vineyard, and here and there we could come across a flock of sheep, cows freely walking across the meadows, and we even saw a small deer that ran across the road in front of us. So adorablee. There are not many houses, just like in any hilly village today, cause over time people have moved down to the gentler plains. So that village, which is actually the third largest in Serbia by area, now has a little under 500 inhabitants. It is about 40 kilometers from Valjevo and about 11 kilometers from Koceljeva. The largest and oldest landmark of this village is a wooden church, dedicated to the Holy Apostles Peter and Paul.

/>It is located next to a four-year primary school, surrounded by beautiful dense forests and small hills. The villagers who were working on the yard there welcomed us warmly and shared the information they knew, that the foundation of the church was laid in 1791 and the builder who started the construction was Ignjat Petrovic. In 1792, the church was fully built and the interior decoration was completed in 1794. The wooden church was in use throughout the entire 19th century. Over time, due to the increase in the number of believers and their economic strength, the construction of a new church began at the start of the 20th century. The new church is located in the same churchyard as the wooden one and is dedicated to Saint George.

/>They also said to us that the Services are no longer held in the wooden church, except on Petrovdan. Also, at the request of the locals, a priest can perform a wedding in the old church and it is a very beautiful event that in a way brings the wooden church back to life, as it is the pride of the village of Miličinica and its residents.\n\n

/>The interior decoration of the church was also made of wood. A wooden iconostasis, the choir area, a wooden false vault that beautifies the roof from the inside, everything made of wood, hand carved with great patience, faith and love. The icon of the Mother of God with Jesus, as well as the icon of Jesus, which I think by rule always stand to the left and right of the entrance to the altar, especially amazed and enchanted me. I have never seen icons painted like this, not in any church, temple, in any book, on the internet, nowhere.

/>Beautiful, truly unique sacred works of art. ❤️ This is what the wooden church looks like from the entrance to the churchyard, where on the right side is the new latge church of Saint George, and the wooden one is on a slightly smaller hill above. It is a wonderful feeling to walk along these old stone steps and to know how far back all of this dates. I hope its appearance and authenticity will never be changed, considering it is one of the rare wooden churches in such a well-preserved condition that have survived to this day. According to books, there used to be more of them, but over time they were demolished so that new churches could be built in the same places.

/>As for the reason we went there, guess what, we didn't find anything. But we had a really nice time talking to wonderful people, breathing in the fresher mountain air and enjoying the beauty of these cultural monuments and sacred places. And then we of course went to the winery. We got a bit lost there too, because there are two of them, bigger one was closed and we didn't even know exactly what we were looking for, forgetting name of a man we were supposed to visit, the one we had been directed to by that man from the other village. 😀 Anyway, another kind local helped us find our way to the lovely Dragić Ranković, where we tried white and red wine, Tamjanika, bought a few liters, chatted a bit and said his old student friend sent greetings.

/>On the way back, we of course stopped to eat something, and again at Ranković, though this was a place owned by a different man with the same surname. (: The restaurant is closer to Koceljeva, called Ranković Winery, also in a beautiful location, surrounded by forest, a small vineyard and a few fig trees. Homemade barbecue, mixed meat, a bit of everything, kajmak balls, cabbage salad, young red onion, everything was absolutely delicioooous! The atmosphere was also lovely, although I only took a photo of this wall with the Kosovo Maiden and of course the icon of Saint Tryphon, the patron saint of all winemakers, which is celebrated here on February 14th.

/>I will also leave here one single slightly blurry photo of a landscape captured through the car window. I was so amazed by the view on both sides of the road on the way there and on the way back that I didn't take any more photos. Just this flock of sheep, and even they disappeared behind the bushes while I was reaching for my phone to snap a pic.\n\n

/>If you ever visit Western Serbia, specifically the Kolubara District and the surrounding area and have a few days to explore nearby villages, this route is my recommendation. Nature, kind and friendly people and delicious food. 😍 An ideal Sunday trip. Thank you very much for reading all of this, until the next Wordmapping blog, I'm sending you all sunny greetings and a rain of good mood!

body.body:
The trip hammer you opened with is one of the earliest tools that began the industrial revolution.  The specific tool you posted is one of the most primitive I have seen, something you could make with a chipped rock and fallen logs.  The basic design was fundamental to mechanizing forging in the early industrialization of the production of metal like iron and similar tooling materials.

The fall of the four horsemen is overdue IMHO.  While the acerbic wit of Richard Dawkins is belied by his incomprehension of how AI actually works, and he clearly projects his thought processes into the source of the text he interacts with.  AI does not work like our consciousness does, but plagiarizes vast volumes of human thought to string together it's output by weighting text via complex algorithms.  It does not understand what the text means at all.  It finds that '2+2' is almost always followed by '=4', so it's algorithm supplies that statement in response to prompts.  It does not know what it means.  It does not understand the quantity of two, nor of addition - unless it has subroutines that enable it to do math.  Peterson's bloodthirst is blatantly Zionist, mere pandering, as thoughtless of human rights as AI is.  He just grovels to his paymasters.  Altman is without substance similarly.  IIRC the fourth is Molyneux, whom at least has a foundation of principles, but his inability to connect them coherently (perhaps because he strives to produce advice people will accept) leaves his foundation riddled with holes and instability.

I can understand the craving for snacks, but, frankly, am aghast at the pringles sammiches.  I guess an occasional lapse in your nutritional quality can't be helped, as we have to enjoy our lives, after all.  I was exposed to potato chips on tuna sandwiches in Texas, but generally resist such glop mostly through frugality.  I almost exclusively eat boiled veg and hunks of meat (although I am prone to using prepared meats, like sausage, which isn't high quality food due to the crappy ingredients used).  Generally my fare is buttered veg and meat, salt, turmeric, and black pepper, slathered in sour cream.  This is pretty nutritious and lacks ultraprocessed additives like maltodextrin, sodium glutamate, and etc. that most prepared foods include.  US Right To Know recently published a report showing that reducing store bought personal care products has an almost immediate beneficial impact on health, and I make my own toothpaste and deodorant from baking soda, coconut oil, and essential oils for flavor or scent (with a bit of corn starch to keep the coconut oil solid at room temperature), and this eliminates things like guar gum, aluminum, and etc from being absorbed by my tender tissues. Chicks say I 'smell like a man' and bury their noses in my pits, so that's good enough for the girls I go with, and better than being poisoned daily, anyway.

I reckon the avarice of Big Tech is behind the majority of demonetization.  The money Goolag and Meta aren't paying to their creators is money they keep, and the specific censory is mostly an excuse to take their money, IMHO.  These people aren't principled.  They're greedy.  You might be interested in the webinar that the makers of Graphene OS are holding in a couple days.

>\

I'm over being tracked and surveilled by my phones, have just dropped one, don't use wifi, and want to know how to degoogle my everything because I think Goolag is an appropriate name for what that company intends for us.  If biometric ID becomes unavoidable for using a phone, I'll quit using a phone altogether and buy meshtastic radios for local folks I need to stay in touch with.  If the internet becomes KYC Imma ditch it too.  The imposition of AI social media tyranny is not tolerable to me, and I'm just not going to do it.  

I hope you're getting to enjoy Fall, opposite to the bursting of blossoms and babies out of the woodwork here Spring brings, but with it's own charm.  

Thanks!

body.title: The Lie of Optimization
body.body: Everything must be faster. Everything must be better. We are obsessed with efficiency. We treat our bodies like machines. We track our sleep. We track our steps. We track our calories. We have become managers of our own lives. But where is the joy? You cannot optimize a sunset. You cannot quantify a laugh. The system demands we be productive units. We are cogs in a giant engine. If we stop moving, we are replaced. So we run faster. We optimize our breakfast. We optimize our commute. We optimize our downtime. It is a sickness. We are optimizing ourselves into extinction. The best moments of life are the ones that were not on the schedule. The messy moments. The surprise interruptions. That is where life happens. Throw away the spreadsheet. Live inefficiently.

body.title: A Beautiful Paradise : Isla de Gigantes (Islands of Giant) Experience
body.body:
![White Blue Modern Summer Instagram Post.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/choiscxel01/AKAq4gvyXCTTiB22t1TeTdLuUr9b1BNRyFQ18R3mkeCB8Xf5SLQcpfh1QCfDtFo.jpg)

Gigantes Islands is located in Carles, Iloilo, Philippines. ***Isla de Gigantes*** (Giant Islands) originally named *sabuluag* after a tree species found on the islands and later renamed by spanish colonisers after a local legend which spoke of gigantes human bones within the island's caves. This place is stunning chain about ten islands, clear blue waters, powdery white sand and cloudless skies.

Its about an hour ride going to Isla de Gigantes, no signal at all, It's a little bit scary being unreachable in the middle of the sea. But it's good thing since no distractions at all. You can spend your whole time together with your family and friends and enjoy the phenomenal beaches and craggy rock formations of Gigantes islands. 

Tips before going to this Island
- Make sure you made all important calls and messages before going there because there is no signal there.
- Bring extra cash because there is no ATM there, plus you need cash to buy scallops at the cheapest price.

![Isla de gigantes.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/choiscxel01/48Zb4dahBVGn3neLu5woi4MfJttgxtQjyg2wukruYSQuxER2YmzBMZckBfMRDfpffz.jpg)



This picture is taken at Cabugao Gamay Island, an iconic island referred as \

with stunning panoramic view. Cabugao is the most photographed part of the island



![51513521_2257272931198891_3112164187791425536_n.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/choiscxel01/48bWsinh4sb8AtvenjLkZBGjqBYmDVyHbHQK71dbV6y3StzmFNjDYXcS6RpCdFzT5S.jpg)

*(Together with my youngest brother and his wife.)*


![Keep calm and relax.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/choiscxel01/AKRD9QxeGncPMftgtempmP5aNrnTcYF252VcUtGmrYEQGP2y2E6sptdMRnw8Peg.jpg)

*(Keep calm and relax)*
 
After the non-stop photo shoot , it's time for lunch. Freshly cooked crabs, fish soup and the popular scallops (unlimited). Food tastes much better when you eat with your bare hands.

![Blue Illustrated Seafood Pitch Deck Presentation.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/choiscxel01/23wCGAvDeUtUuSwV5RmMf8XCB98mdgoP9wDHwZjqNRt2uqgrT7XSASKJzd3VE3HqNmGh8.jpg)

Isla de Gigantes is one of the breathtaking island getaway that God has blessed us. The scallops you can pick them live from the seabed just on the edge of the beach, the turquoise lagoons, plenty of coconut trees, unique huts and a good vibes from local community.
Every moment there feels like a dream.

body.body:
<center>
![up-green-candle-wojak-candle.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/edicted/23ynHdGVQv2UqkQBZFTy8HxFq2nzYHBkADWVy1xQw3UkRyFHNPQyjppLRzcgzVTn5FAbj.png)
</center>


![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/edicted/23swcKB9giM8vBAvFvx3js5HPZLoWZAVFvhSyk9FkWq9W3HqcA1W3fjki4AcpYvuwHQPC.png)


### Hm that's interesting...
So I wake up this morning and Hive is up 50% on some random god-candle.  Not that this is anything to write home about in the grand scheme of things considering the price is still well below 10 cents, but certainly it is a bit of a burden lifted to see a little green in a sea of red and the continued threat of the bear market year 2026.

I \
a little at 8.8 cents just to make sure I capture a tiny bit of this move.  Of course by \

, which isn't exactly selling when all I'm doing is trading my volatile asset for the on-chain stable debt derivative.  Buying or selling HBD can't really affect the price of Hive itself as the real exchange rate is determined by the worldwide market (of which there are zero HBD pairs).  It would be interesting if this was somehow proven wrong in the future given exponentially more liquidity between Hive/HBD, but my theory is that more liquidity on that pair would just make the price even more stable and harder to move.  Real liquidity on [Altera](https://peakd.com/altera/@edicted/a-bit-more-tinkering-on-altera) would change things considerably but that is yet to be seen. 

![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/edicted/Eoc1JsevxSe7S4N6Ei7xrAR4zjkH7LNEWcouz2PBWTNSuRSnFN7WhQ73uz8d92sCg6U.png)

#### Debt ratio?
The first thing I thought to do when I saw this pump was take a look at the debt ratio.  It hasn't changed yet because the number is based on the median price of Hive over 3.5 days.  That average still sits at 6 cents because this pump has had no time to affect the average. However, we can clearly see from these numbers that if the median price was double the haircut price of 4.3 cents then the scary ratio would drop from 23.5% to 15% on a single pump that materialized within an hour, which is pretty crazy to consider.  It's a good reminder that it doesn't take a whole lot of demand to ensure our debt stays in check even with high APR in the savings accounts.  


![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/edicted/Enyo5HJdXks37LRJ8k5fUQcxPGzNGRVwSXQhSJAcJ9HkqVhbtSHKUvpquVHdjNCXeuy.png)


-----

#### What's the corn doin?
Bitcoin itself is still looking good, but \

vibes are clearly significant.  It's appears as though a summer rally is locked in but the peak could be in May, June, or even July at this point.  Hopefully it's July as this would make farming that potential Bitcoin fork airdrop in August very easy to achieve.  Weirdly enough a similar thing happened last year as well, with the relevant golden cross occurring in May and the rally extending into July 2025.  This time the [25/100] golden cross happened on April 25th so we might be gearing up for a similar situation. 

That being said the MA(200) is still hanging at $83400 near the top of the critical liquidity band.  It's unclear how much resistance these lines are going to offer, but also we theoretically have a lot of time to shatter them, as a summer rally should last 2 or 3 months.  

#### Questioning the 4 year cycle
Many analysts are coming to the conclusion that the 4 year cycle on Bitcoin is either shattered or, at the very least, acting very strangely this time around.  Personally I think it just might be cope and everyone just wants number to go up so they spin a story for themselves.  At the same time the peak of 2025 was muted and sad considering the insane level of institutional adoption.  Thus it makes sense that the bear market would also be muted as well.  Either way I think buying at the end of September 2026 is going to be a huge win in multiple scenarios.  My only question is what to do in the meantime. 

#### Could something have spiked this Hive pump?
The most glaring fundamental gain Hive has gained recently was the MAGI network and the ability to pair multiple tokens to HBD.  Checking the liquidity pools there is still only 4-figures of worth total sitting on the network, but you never know what kind of hidden speculation is going on in the background.  I look forward to seeing if this is just a totally random thing or if there's something to it.  Leaning toward \

considering Steem also got boosted 20% during the exact same hour, but you never know. 

### Conclusion
Could the bear market really be over 6 months early?  Or was this not even a bear market at all like many analysts are now claiming?  Obviously it's nice to see the green but we all know how common pump and dumps are.  We've all been victim of getting our hopes up just for the price to crater right back to where it was before.  Personally I'll be much more emotionally secure once we get past September and have had a full year go by after the heartbreaking breakdown of 2025.

body.title: Is Being a single mother acceptable in the eyes of God?//Mcgi Topic Review
body.body:
https://youtu.be/l13EhMBseRY?si=M_DrbOluY6DIApyF

Romans 2:11 teaches that God does not show favoritism; He treats everyone equally. When we speak about God the Father and our Lord Jesus Christ, it means there is no discrimination with them. Likewise, James 2:1 instructs believers not to show partiality in their faith in Jesus Christ, the Lord of glory.

We should not practice favoritism because every human being is created by God. In His eyes, everyone has value. This is why the Bible makes it clear that God desires all people to be saved. As stated in 1 Timothy 2:4, He wants everyone to come to the knowledge of the truth.

If God’s will is for all people to be saved, then it shows that His love extends to everyone. In 2 Peter 3:9, we see that God is patient and not willing for anyone to perish, but for all to come to repentance.

God does not want anyone to be lost—not even one person. His love is for all humanity. So, there should be no question about accepting someone based on their situation, such as being a single mother. There is no reason to reject anyone. Although some people may experience discrimination, this should not be found in the true church of God. In the body of Christ, everyone should be treated equally and cared for with love.

1 Corinthians 12:25 emphasizes that there should be no division among believers, but that all members should care for one another equally.

In the early church, Mary Magdalene is a good example. She once had a difficult past and was delivered from evil spirits, yet she was accepted and became a valued member of the church. She played a significant role in spreading the gospel and supported the ministry of Jesus Christ. According to Luke 8:2, she was among those who were healed and transformed.

This shows that no matter a person’s background or past, they can be accepted, valued, and used for God’s purpose

**Thanks for reading.**

<center>ESPAÑOL</center>

Permitirnos ver las cosas tal y como son, con menos etiquetas y juicios nos ayuda a ver \
nuestra realidad. \nEn ese sentido, la mente puede estar modo \

. En el primer caso, predomina el análisis, la racionalización y la comparación. En el segundo, el registro, a través de nuestros sentidos de todo lo que nos rodea. 
Necesitamos de ambas, por supuesto. Pero un beneficio importante de observar es que volvemos a lo único que tenemos, el aquí y el ahora. 

_________

<center>ENGLISH</center>

Allowing ourselves to see things as they are, with fewer labels and judgments, helps us see our reality “clearly.” 
In this sense, the mind can be in “thinking” mode or “observing” mode. In the first case, analysis, rationalization, and comparison predominate. In the second, we register, through our senses, everything around us. 
We need both, of course. But an important benefit of observing is that we return to the only thing we have: the here and now.

body.title: [ESP/ENG] Échame el cuento: La luz que otros dejaron en mí / The light that others left within me
body.body:
El agradecimiento es una forma de memoria luminosa. No solo recuerda lo que otros han hecho por nosotros, sino que reconoce la huella que dejaron en nuestra manera de ser, de mirar el mundo y de caminar por él.



![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmUFPtg2RbNKiG5nYhzq8jaLknpHGSsn3PCuPRHqTzurNV/1777985473529.jpg)



Agradecer es un acto de justicia afectiva: es decirle a la vida que no hemos pasado por ella distraídos, que sabemos quiénes nos han sostenido, quiénes nos han levantado cuando flaqueamos y quiénes han celebrado nuestras pequeñas victorias como si fueran propias.

En mi historia, como en la de muchos, el agradecimiento tiene nombres concretos, rostros que no se borran y presencias que han moldeado mi crecimiento personal y profesional. 




![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmSFZ4HefQPq2oaa1YRY3CPJukFRJd6RE9oJ9m3nuH96qa/1777987199988.jpg)


Mi madre, por ejemplo, es la raíz más profunda de esa gratitud. De ella aprendí que la fortaleza no siempre hace ruido, que el amor verdadero se expresa en gestos cotidianos y que la dignidad se sostiene incluso en los días más duros. Su manera de cuidarme, de orientarme y de creer en mí cuando yo mismo dudaba, es una herencia que no se agota. Agradecerle es reconocer que una parte esencial de lo que soy nació en su mirada y en su entrega.



![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmYJ4XH4nZNhLj9nUf5H8FJdUpoyRxXm4FLxfPtRWu4sAa/1777986853423.jpg)



Mi esposa es otro pilar de esta gratitud. Con ella he descubierto que el amor adulto no es solo compañía, sino impulso, espejo y refugio. Su presencia me ha enseñado a ser más paciente, más sensible, más humano. Agradecerle es reconocer que su apoyo ha sido brújula en momentos de incertidumbre y celebración en tiempos de logro. Ella ha sido testigo y cómplice de mis búsquedas, y su confianza ha sido un motor silencioso que me empuja a ser mejor cada día.



![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmQUv1t6JCPCuZy54rhLD2VQtXUSyCvwuaW34xaDgrue8E/1777986882908.jpg)


La familia, en su sentido más amplio, también ocupa un lugar sagrado en este mapa del agradecimiento. Hermanos, tíos, primos, seres que comparten sangre o historia, todos han aportado algo a mi crecimiento: una palabra oportuna, un consejo, una risa compartida, un espacio donde descansar el alma. La familia es ese territorio donde uno puede volver sin explicaciones, y agradecerles es reconocer que su existencia ha sido sostén y raíz.






Y están las amistades, esos compañeros elegidos que la vida coloca en nuestro camino para recordarnos que no estamos solos. Amigos que escuchan sin juzgar, que celebran sin envidia, que acompañan sin condiciones. Ellos han sido faros en noches difíciles y alegría en días luminosos. Agradecerles es honrar la lealtad, la complicidad y la ternura que han puesto en mi vida.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmTwPQ4wNbJbidRCBNbSwr782Nq3Qo6Wgcueiox1nwsQ3o/1777986798303.jpg)


El agradecimiento, al final, es una forma de crecer hacia adentro. Nos hace más humildes, más conscientes, más sensibles al valor de los otros. Nos recuerda que nadie llega lejos solo y que cada paso que damos está sostenido por manos visibles e invisibles. Agradecer es un acto de amor, pero también de madurez: es reconocer que somos, en buena medida, el resultado de quienes nos han amado bien.

Y por eso agradezco. Agradezco a quienes me han formado, acompañado y querido. A quienes han visto en mí posibilidades que yo no veía. A quienes han sido hogar, impulso y abrazo. Agradecer es mi manera de decirles que su presencia no pasó inadvertida, que su amor dejó raíces y que mi vida es más plena porque ellos existen.

Para todos ellos y los que faltaron dejo estas décimas espinelas, como muestra de amor y agradecimiento.




Gratitud como raíz

A quienes fueron mi escuela,  
mi sostén y mi camino,  
les doy gracias: mi destino  
se hizo luz bajo su estela.  
Mi madre, fuerza que vela,  
mi esposa, abrazo y farol,  
mi familia, mi arrebol,  
mis amigos, compañía.  
En todos hallé alegría  
y un modo más noble al sol.



Cada gesto que ofrecieron  
fue semilla en mi jornada;  
su ternura, bien sembrada,  
dio frutos que me crecieron.  
Por ellos hoy me prefiero,  
más humano, más consciente;  
su amor firme y persistente  
me enseñó a ser quien he sido.  
Agradezco lo vivido:  
su huella es mi mejor puente.




Antes de concluir invito a participar a @ericvancewalton, @palabras1, @advesin y @palomap3, para que nos dejen sus ideas en torno a este importante tema.


Nota: Utilicé el traductor DeepL Translate.
Las imágenes son de mi propiedad.




ENGLISH 


The light that others leave in you

Gratitude is a form of luminous memory. Not only does it remember what others have done for us, but it recognizes the mark they left on our way of being, of looking at the world and of walking through it. 



![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmUFPtg2RbNKiG5nYhzq8jaLknpHGSsn3PCuPRHqTzurNV/1777985473529.jpg)


To be grateful is an act of affective justice: it is to tell life that we have not gone through it distracted, that we know who has sustained us, who has lifted us up when we falter, and who have celebrated our small victories as if they were our own.

In my story – as in that of so many – gratitude has specific names, faces that are not erased and presences that have shaped my personal and professional growth. 


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmSFZ4HefQPq2oaa1YRY3CPJukFRJd6RE9oJ9m3nuH96qa/1777987199988.jpg)



My mother, for example, is the deepest root of that gratitude. From her I learned that fortitude does not always make noise, that true love is expressed in daily gestures and that dignity is sustained even on the hardest days. His way of taking care of me, of guiding me and of believing in me when I myself doubted, is a legacy that is not exhausted. To thank him is to recognize that an essential part of who I am was born in his gaze and in his dedication.


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmYJ4XH4nZNhLj9nUf5H8FJdUpoyRxXm4FLxfPtRWu4sAa/1777986853423.jpg)



My wife is another pillar of this gratitude. With her I have discovered that adult love is not only company, but impulse, mirror and refuge. His presence has taught me to be more patient, more sensitive, more human. To thank him is to recognize that his support has been a compass in times of uncertainty and celebration in times of achievement. She has been a witness and accomplice to my searches, and her confidence has been a silent engine that pushes me to be better every day.


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmQUv1t6JCPCuZy54rhLD2VQtXUSyCvwuaW34xaDgrue8E/1777986882908.jpg)



The family, in its broadest sense, also occupies a sacred place on this map of gratitude. Siblings, uncles, cousins, beings who share blood or history, all have contributed something to my growth: a timely word, advice, a shared laughter, a space where the soul can rest. The family is that territory where one can return without explanation, and to thank them is to recognize that their existence has been support and root.

And there are friendships, those chosen companions that life places in our path to remind us that we are not alone. Friends who listen without judging, who celebrate without envy, who accompany without conditions. They have been beacons on difficult nights and joy on bright days. To thank them is to honor the loyalty, complicity and tenderness they have put into my life.


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmTwPQ4wNbJbidRCBNbSwr782Nq3Qo6Wgcueiox1nwsQ3o/1777986798303.jpg)


Gratitude, in the end, is a way of growing inward. It makes us more humble, more aware, more sensitive to the value of others. It reminds us that no one gets far alone and that every step we take is supported by visible and invisible hands. To be grateful is an act of love, but also of maturity: it is to recognize that we are, to a large extent, the result of those who have loved us well.

And for that I am grateful. I thank those who have formed, accompanied and loved me. To those who have seen in me possibilities that I did not see. To those who have been home, impulse and embrace. Gratitude is my way of telling them that their presence did not go unnoticed, that their love left roots and that my life is fuller because they exist.

For all of them and those who were missing, I leave these tenth spinels, as a sign of love and gratitude.

Gratitude as a root

To those who were my school,  
my support and my way,  
I thank you: my destiny  
there was light in its wake.  
My mother, a watchful force,  
my wife, hug and bluff,  
my family, my arbol,  
my friends, company.  
In all of them I found joy  
and a nobler way in the sun.

Every gesture they offered  
it was a seed in my journey;  
his tenderness, well sown,  
it bore fruit that grew for me.  
For them today I prefer,  
more human, more conscious;  
His firm and persistent love  
It taught me to be who I have been.  
I am grateful for what I have experienced:  
Its footprint is my best bridge.

Before concluding, I invite @ericvancewalton, @palabras1, @advesin and @palomap3 to participate, so that they can leave us their ideas on this important topic.

Note: I used the DeepL Translate translator.
The images are my property.

body.body: > https://youtu.be/oAcMa8zhQgY?si=QMVzQHbbGMO2S2kO I have realized that forgiveness of sin is a very important element in my life. On several occasions, I have acted wrongly and have committed acts that I am not fond of. At times I experience a heavy feeling in my heart due to my sins. But I thank God, because He is always ready to forgive me, when I go to Him with a sincere heart. According to the Bible in 1 John 1:9 it is written that, in case we confess our sins, He is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us of all unrighteousness. It brings me to the hope that regardless of anything I might have done, God can still forgive me. In my life, I experienced a moment when I was so guilty of something that I have done. I was also unable to even pray well since I was ashamed. However, one day, I choose to open my heart to God and request Him to have mercy on me. I wept and shared everything with Him. Now I was at peace in my heart, after that prayer. It was as though a load was taken off me. The experience also helped me to realize that God does forgive. Forgiveness of sin is not just about saying sorry. It also implies that I would have to reform my ways and attempt not to revert to that sin in future. The Bible says in Proverbs 28:13, “He that covereth his sins shall not prosper: but whoso confesseth and forsaketh them shall have mercy.” This teaches me to be sincere with God and also to repent my misdeeds. I also got to know that the way God forgives me, I also need to forgive others. This is not always easy, but, this is what God wants. The bible says in Ephesians 4:32, Be kind and compassionate to one another, forgive each other, just as you were forgiven by Christ God. Peace, freedom, and new beginning are the results of forgiveness. I also thank God that He never seems to grow weary of forgiving me when I really repent.

body.title: Summoning Spirits                       ...Finale               ...The Goddess Descends
body.body:
*She is a wild, tangled forest with temples and treasures concealed within ― John Mark Green*


![The Goddess Descends.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmR5onhyRW47xzEuq4L2RF24FEUiW4yMWV7jDb6o7PJeLy/The%20Goddess%20Descends.png)
*The Goddess Descends*


Astrid and I are on an archeological dig to uncover the sanctuary of the dead in the hopes that Perry Landers, the financier of our expedition, will be able to contact the spirit of Susi, his dead wife. It seems a fool's errand but Astrid and I are touched by the depth of Lander's grief and we've thrown common sense to the wind in the hopes of easing his sorrow. Yes, I resisted at first, but in the end common humanity prevailed.

So, two days later, we’re excavating on a tiny hillside near Phyra in a location I would never have dug had not Landers uncovered the ancient manuscript. As it is, I have my doubts. None of the details mentioned in Herodotus’ description of the sanctuary location match the site. Astrid, again, is oblivious of any discrepancies, however, and continues on, tossing spadefuls of dirt onto an ever-growing pile. I remove myself from her a short distance and begin pulling away loose stone from the hillside. One rock in particular is firmly wedged and as I strike at it with my mattock, I hear an iron clang. Astrid hears it too, and scrabbles over loose rock to get a look. It’s an iron gate. The look on her face is ecstatic.

It takes several days to clear the rubble that blocks the entrance to the sanctuary—no doubt, an earthquake buried the site centuries ago, and it’s arduous work removing some of the larger boulders. At last, the entrance is cleared enough to allow us to squeeze into the tunnel, and what we see is amazing.

The sanctuary is built into a hillside and consists of a series of labyrinthine tunnels. The faithful follow these winding subterranean corridors through several sets of iron gates until they arrive at the central room of the temple. We can hear running water—an underground spring trickles through cracks and crevices and some of the water is diverted into a huge, stone pool. Around the edge of the pool are tiny alcoves with candle sconces. Apparently the seekers lit candles and stared into the sacred waters and beheld the shades of departed loved ones.

Landers is moved to tears when we lead him into the central room of the sanctuary. “Just think, for centuries the secret of this temple lay buried beneath rubble, under the noses of unsuspecting archeologists—and now, we’ve found it.” I nod. “I think the honour of announcing it to the world should go to you, Perry—you uncovered the manuscript and financed the expedition.”

He shakes his head. “I’m not concerned with that. I have a favour to ask of you both. Could you delay the announcement—say for a month? I would like to spend some time here alone, communing with Susi. I’ll gladly finance your stay.” I glance over at Astrid—eyes shining in candlelight—skin bronzed as when we slept in the land of Nod. I know her answer. This will be our Aegean vacation. We both agree.

It’s different this time sleeping out on the beach with Astrid, beneath Aegean stars. This is where she descended to earth as Queen of the Stars—this goddess I can never fully possess. It’s also cool those nights after the sun goes down and so, we always build a fire. Astrid is inevitably curled up beside me and I can easily whisper in her ear. On one particular night, I’m feeling reflective, acutely aware of the briefness of the tiny lives we share.

“We don’t choose our time,” I say softly. I’m thinking of Landers and Susi separated by the Great Divide. She turns over to face me, hair backlit by the fire. “But we do get to choose our stars,” she says dreamily, holding my hand in hers. “What do you mean?” “I’m thinking of one faint star I see from your rooftop terrace—it’s mine, and I could dwell upon it, but I’d rather be here in your heart.”

She touches her hand to my chest and I feel a familiar warmth. It spreads to my limbs and suffuses throughout my whole body. I whisper in her ear. You know what Joseph Addison said,—*when a man becomes familiar with his goddess, she quickly sinks into a woman.* Her eyes grow huge. “Have I come down to earth?” I kiss her. “That hasn’t happened yet.”

body.body:
![IMG_20260428_191419_183.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/tiptop97/EoeFRWhN4EJSbP313UfeB3cJUi2ffnK9tqrVeRNigc4K3CG6SndLUvSqqx7e6Z3D22T.jpg)






*Hello everyone, dear friends. Today is a wonderful day. It feels like spring has finally woken up, although it's so hot outside today that I could have thought that summer had already arrived. The weather is a strange thing. Today it could be sunny, and tomorrow it could be hail or heavy rain. I don't know if the weather will surprise me again this year because a few days ago the temperature dropped below zero and it made me a little nervous. Why exactly nervous? Because it was very interesting to me and important. But probably the most appropriate word for this situation is I was scared. I was scared for my flowers, plants, bushes and trees. As soon as the blossoms appeared and everything started to bloom, the frost is not good at all. That's why every morning I went to the garden to check how my flowers and plants in the garden are doing. And so, every time one of them died, it was actually very sad, I didn't expect it to be like this. Although every year brings different weather surprises. Probably like I said before, my pears, apples, cherries, and cherries won't produce a crop this year. It's sad, well I hope that at least what hasn't frozen will bear some fruit, it's a shame about this work. But we are powerless against the weather.*



*What do we have today? I want to offer you a new look at my garden. This is my purple flower called dream grass and red decorative tulips. They are the heroes of today's post. The tulips also didn't bloom for very long this year because the weather changed very quickly, sometimes it was warm, sometimes it was cold. I'm really disappointed. But as for the dream-grass flower it is more resistant to temperature changes and I am pleased that it is blooming so beautifully this year, besides the purple one, i also have a white one, it also recently bloomed, i will show photos later. Some of them I may have already published before , when it was just starting to bloom. You can also see a small bug on a dandelion here. By the way, dandelions are already stopping blooming and accordingly there are even fewer bees in my garden. Well, there will be something new soon. I believe that there is still strength left in my flowers, plants and trees to pleasantly surprise and please me with something this year.*

body.body:
Today we have for you guitar picks from the band called 

 Machine Head 

![](https://usermedia.actifit.io/5f06233b-e93f-4629-9f4b-21746e329c9b.jpg)


---

Machine Head is a foundational force in the American heavy metal scene, emerging from Oakland, California, in 1991. Formed by vocalist and guitarist Robb Flynn, the band is widely credited with helping to bridge the gap between traditional thrash metal and the groove-laden \

sound of the 1990s. Their debut album, Burn My Eyes, remains a landmark release in the genre, praised for its raw aggression and technical precision. Over the decades, the band has successfully navigated various sonic shifts—from the more experimental textures of the late 90s to the complex, epic thrash compositions found on their critically acclaimed 2007 masterpiece, The Blackening. Known for their blistering live performances and Flynn’s signature roar, Machine Head has maintained a loyal global following and continues to be a heavy-hitting influence in the modern metal landscape.

This collection is a remarkable physical record of rock history, featuring a diverse array of guitar picks gathered from some of the most legendary North American tours. Each piece represents a specific moment in time, coming directly from the hands of the most influential touring bands of the last 20 to 40 years. From the thrash metal precision of Megadeth to the grunge-era icons like Eddie Vedder, these picks are more than just gear—they are tangible artifacts from the high-energy arenas and stadiums that defined a generation of music.
The significance of these picks lies in their connection to the peak of live performance culture across the continent. Over the past four decades, touring reached a massive scale, and these picks were used by artists who headlined the most iconic festivals and venues in the world. Whether it's a specialty \

design or a classic tour-stamped plectrum, having items from bands that shaped the sound of the 80s, 90s, and 2000s makes this a curated chronicle of modern rock’s touring legac. I'm putting this guitar pic together. Alphabetical order over the next few weeks and months. --- Thanks for stopping in today! 🎸⛏️

body.title: A habit that can make you special
body.body: Hello guys how are you I hope you are all doing well so today topic is getting a bit interesting its about our daily habits \n \n

/>

Image Credit : [https://pixabay.com/](https://pixabay.com/)

What is a habit a habit is basically something we do every day something we practice until we cant live without it now how can these habits be they can turn the ordinary into the extraordinary they are a mindset that highlights the need to take steps to change your life but its not mandatory in fact small habits actually turn out to be game changers

The topic of Meraaj is the same I am repeating through habits we can bring changes into our lives that improve our lifestyle help us succeed in front of others and over time enhance our personality so much that people see us and want their children to be like us give examples

The real difference is not talent or looks but the right mindset and discipline that turn an ordinary person into an extraordinary one

Now the question arises how can we improve our habits there are some steps we can follow to make our habits better for example when we start anything we should not begin with something big that we know nothing about always take small steps taken slowly then once you get the chance to steady yourself you can take a bigger step goals work the same way always build your habits with small things and strengthen your steps do not ignore the boring parts because there are things that at first feel very boring but in reality they are the first step toward our success

Once we take the first step we can figure out how to do it repeating those things again and again and failing does not mean your life is over or that your work is done instead it helps you learn you only realize your mistake after you take action and then you learn from it

You have also noticed that people at first motivate you a lot saying do this you will get this benefit you will get that benefit but no one tells you that you need to be consistent with the same thing when you stay consistent with one thing you learn from it and that will be the key to your lasting success

Along with this you have probably heard that English idiom a man is known by the company he keeps a person is recognized by his company good friends and good habits can all contribute to your success if you sit with intelligent people you will become intelligent yourself you will gain something from there if you start hanging out with unproductive people you will get nothing but failure so your success and your standing are closely tied to your friends and your environment

Improve your routines the tasks you complete on time always give good results while those you delay thinking I will do it later always end up harming you therefore time management and good habits are beneficial for you and they always pay off

We keep thinking we will start tomorrow but tomorrow never comes always start today if for some reason you miss a day do not think that day will come back but you will have the next day and by working hard on it you can recover what you missed if you keep leaving things with the hope that tomorrow will be better and you let that day pass too then it becomes your habit and later these habits can harm you a lot

So guys how did you like this post comment and let me know in the comments

(aka improve knowledge on) the importance of being ready for these situations, where most of the time we are basically supporting the stabilisation of the HBD peg, or making sure people don't get a bad deal for whatever transaction between a pegged coin and its main token is about to happen.

The top 20 Witnesses have a huge importance here because the HIVE price vs USD value gets updated, and depending on how quickly this happens, values will flow.

I can't say it's good or bad because there are so many things at stake at these times and on the Hive specific markets (not that I am any pro at this), but in my honest opinion, I think we just either don't take these moments as an opportunity (because we have had too many experiences with it, and often, bad experiences) or we are not enought motivated or knwoledgeable about knowing how to expand on the subject.

of arriving home and having the time for it...

body.title: Freewrite - \
body.body:
From the earliest of my memories when I was young, I remember Mom used to tell me to not look towards a particularly dark corner in the room. 

This was her strategy to make me sleep quickly, but it would end up having the opposite effect, as my overly active imagination would create all sorts of scenarios that would not let me sleep, so it was kind of ironic for her to keep trying the same thing.

Eventually though, I kind of became curious about the thing that lived in the corner and would actively go there to get a reaction. 

I think it was probably the earliest. interest I had developed in horror. Which would later influence me to read horror and actively seek out the macabre.

---
This freewrite was inpired by  [this](https://ecency.com/hive-161155/@daily.prompt/23-april-2026-freewriters-community-daily-writing-prompt-day-3082-dont-look-in-the-corner) prompt here.

body.title: Home Depot, DOH!, 31.35 Mile/50K Bike Ride, Flowers and Blooms - Monday
body.body:
<b>I was at the tool shed when I noticed a mass of bees around the garden shed. I walked up to see a number in the hive, though they are all likely just robbers and not a hive that took up residence. Debating closing it off to not allow the robbing.

![IMG_20260504_081223.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/flemingfarm/23wgKUwLqMwCdZPMTKGgLTeZ24zbxeLuEzsMh2qhJMWo6ZvHu5G5ejdhdBuHqHUdhNVUc.jpg)

I measured a few times and I would have been able to fir the door in the sled but as I stood at Home Depot browsing I realized I needed to get the 6\

depth. I bought the supplies and headed out to the car where I found I was an inch off from it fitting. So I had to have @stryeyz come over with her car so it is sitting in there until I install this afternoon. ![IMG_20260504_092914.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/flemingfarm/23vi671EpAjf69egzJ1wgaFXfuLc5TyHYymhCgh3hXq3zTQnjB3smNd6TtJfuFFLuatrd.jpg) Back home I got ready and was out on the road by 11am. Hardly any traffic on the back roads and I got in some climbs. It was warm but I felt pretty strong so ended up going past the Deer Park airport which I haven't been on those roads. ![IMG_20260504_112401.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/flemingfarm/23uFWDF54i2ix7rbmgZtAFttu69WFJuuncSeZdvSFGbSr6xte9jLQipoMyL8pP6cJkyWB.jpg) Ended up heading north to Eloika Lake road which was the high point of the ride. I tend to NOT ride the road as the hills are long from the lake output to where I hooked in. Downhill was fine as I am going faster and the vehicles were able to pass okay. ![IMG_20260504_112404.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/flemingfarm/23zRwA8wDjLyxLvLBTyAZSdPdLXbn47LiQF8yfhr2WG1thxzJZrdoTKxFkA4fNPH6zK2w.jpg) Nearing home I was close to a 50K so made sure to get it and hit 2 hours exactly. This was my third 50k+ ride in a row... One hell of a step up from where I started just a few months ago! 12 days until my 50 mile ride. ![bike 5-4 - 50k.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/flemingfarm/23tGZw4S7CnxhuGXEJzE83pshbnftpU8pFmLtwXz7RhP7ioY3SfvQNyW7eF6sRSr5tS3g.JPG) Out checking on the garden I saw our apple tree is exploding in blooms. This should be a very appley late summer. ![IMG_20260504_143102.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/flemingfarm/23tvcMa3EGwqpagjzdSvXnPjYZqzGQFc3vj2GdiMXbzcj5BPkXoxPjYwcZRsPRWh76cbh.jpg) By the highway there is a tree that has daffodils and tulips that grow. I noticed the tulips about to bloom the other day so made a pass by again and popped them out for @stryeyz. Really cool how they are all different colors. ![IMG_20260504_145045.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/flemingfarm/23wMaobBzedac9KfFSwQrYFc4H4em9wHJd4NP3xdUC5fAQerVhqodGVzroExRDvp1fSAR.jpg) After I got dinner made and we ate we went out to soak for a bit. I ended up getting another job which is scheduled for Saturday afternoon and is freeing an attic access and adding hinges and likely a latch to it. ![IMG_20260504_194919.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/flemingfarm/23t7cma7J5RNGiFJm85g5ukxC2ZTKgwhrmk4zgoZvGghcE5B1YAfjvGyFCN9cKhe1KfEj.jpg) This is a super busy week with jobs everyday now. Today I have my session this morning, @stryeyz leaves for a trip to Seattle, boys have school, then at Noon I go to remove a door and frame and install the prehung one I bought. Wednesday I have a session in the morning then work for Michelle getting her planter boxes built before J's track meet that afternoon. Thursday I have the start of the gate install which I will finish Friday, then Saturday the attic job. ---
