title.title: La Bahía de La Habana: Pulso Marítimo y Vida Cotidiana/Havana Bay: Maritime Pulse and Everyday Life[Spa/Eng]
title.body:
La Bahía de La Habana no es solo un puerto natural, es el corazón marítimo de Cuba. Durante siglos ha sido la puerta de entrada y salida de mercancías, ideas y culturas, sosteniendo la economía y conectando al país con el mundo. Su estrecho canal ha visto pasar flotas coloniales, barcos mercantes y modernos buques que mantienen viva la arteria comercial de la nación.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmWARBMevTfAD2Do8WtsSU73RJSsGTZ7Mde1eNq7W8U73g/1777983560983.jpg)

Pero más allá de su dimensión estratégica, la bahía es también escenario de vida cotidiana. En sus aguas tranquilas, los pequeños pescadores lanzan sus redes y líneas, buscando sustento en la riqueza marina que aún ofrece. Sus embarcaciones humildes contrastan con los grandes barcos, recordándonos que la bahía no solo pertenece al comercio global, sino también a quienes dependen de ella día a día.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmYJT7q6obE49SbSfLB2z9K44yD4ZVvfAcYRgL6GQWjqnL/1777983560644.jpg)

La Bahía de La Habana es símbolo de dualidad: un espacio de poder marítimo y, al mismo tiempo, un refugio para la tradición pesquera. Es allí donde se cruzan la historia nacional y la vida sencilla de los pescadores, mostrando que la grandeza de Cuba también se sostiene en las manos de quienes trabajan en silencio sobre sus aguas.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmdYS95jUgq6zDqrxLT9hFnb9Bk5mCR5zctcMsMVRbqvY9/1777983560819.jpg)

Havana Bay is not just a natural harbor—it is the maritime heart of Cuba. For centuries, it has served as the gateway for goods, ideas, and cultures, sustaining the nation’s economy and connecting the island to the wider world. Through its narrow channel, colonial fleets, merchant ships, and modern vessels have passed, keeping alive the country’s commercial lifeline.

Yet beyond its strategic dimension, the bay is also a stage for everyday life. In its calm waters, small fishermen cast their nets and lines, seeking sustenance from the marine wealth it still provides. Their modest boats stand in contrast to the large ships, reminding us that the bay belongs not only to global trade but also to those who rely on it daily.

Havana Bay embodies a dual identity: a space of maritime power and, at the same time, a refuge for fishing tradition. It is where national history meets the humble work of fishermen, showing that Cuba’s greatness is also sustained by those who labor quietly upon its waters.

title.title: Drawn Back to the Sea (Even When It’s Restless)
title.body: Hello everyone! No matter how much we travel around Thailand, somehow we always end up drifting back toward the sea. It’s a bit ironic, honestly — I’m not even much of a swimmer. You’d think I’d be the type chasing mountains or shade somewhere inland. But no… the sea has this quiet pull that’s hard to explain. |||| |-|-|-| |![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmSthJFt5FWvmg6YDnaMsXyyjxjD6Sp3392FFs9HZiGdcN/dsc05285.jpg)|![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmWV27SdPYhXpcSQe9dVF7xfxayNBntW7zW7vzrefDJuQE/dsc05221.jpg)|![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmSL4k13jTeT1JFzRmvUgNvmVvTx1Jj7CYj4kWKEzqtbPV/dsc05279.jpg)| -------------------------------------------------------------------- Most of the time, it gives me a sense of calm. The kind where you sit still, stare at the horizon, and your thoughts just slowly dissolve somewhere between the waves and the sky. But this time, it was different. This time, the sea wasn’t calm at all — it felt alive, restless, almost moody. It’s off-season now, and during the day the tide retreats far from the shore, exposing a completely different world. The water had taken on a deeper blue tone, and the waves were strong enough to rock a small boat anchored not too far away. The whole scene felt dynamic, constantly shifting, like it couldn’t quite decide what mood to settle into. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmS29WcfCrTKsDHamywPbdMtWSh87ojcSsNXNNis4jE8m4/dsc05222.jpg) Meanwhile, I was doing what I do best under the tropical sun — absolutely nothing. The heat turns me into jelly. Slow, lazy, and completely unmotivated. Moving feels optional at best. But kids? Different species. My son, as always, was full of energy and curiosity, completely unaffected by the weather. That’s when we noticed an old man not too far away. He was standing in the shallow water, holding a long stick with something unusual attached to the end. From a distance, it looked like he was drawing patterns on the surface of the sea. Naturally, we started guessing what he was doing. Fishing? Cleaning something? Just passing time? None of the guesses made much sense. Curiosity won — at least for my son. He headed straight toward the old man without hesitation. Along the way, he picked up a companion — a girl he had just met, as kids effortlessly do. Within minutes, they were both standing next to the old man, fully involved in whatever mysterious activity was happening. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmQBzi3ToYnu3vibRQu2xB3vuWeBtWngJoYnjSnMqx92iA/dsc05217.jpg) ||| |-|-| |![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmS6rsXk9UVtpk8g1JoEZq5eD2uwGVR4AgWJt1M3LEiS5L/dsc05209.jpg)|![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmSHCCadVgWHM2YxH25WwEVaU7iETfFJgSb5CbX4SBu2Mv/dsc05250.jpg)| ----------------------------------------------------------------- From my sunbed, I watched like it was some kind of slow documentary unfolding in real time. The old man wasn’t just holding a stick — it was more like a homemade tool. Imagine something between a rake and a spear, with metal rods attached at the end. He was dragging it through the shallow water, methodically combing the seabed after the tide had pulled back. ||| |-|-| |![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmZt134zmp6btHtyM3HzFLsTcJFtf2ddCebH3K1amoACiY/dsc05256.jpg)|![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmaQtPFaqWzEs9Wn2RC7JvcofckeTEoNSzcNsWubLd2Bvw/dsc05247.jpg)| ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmeXTZBDHgrfAqLCeMQcCaVMqTjDQUDH5eUf217aZGfAJq/dsc05273.jpg) Every now and then, the kids would bend down and pick something up, carefully placing it into a plastic bag. Still, from where I was sitting, I couldn’t quite figure out what they were collecting. I had a suspicion that low tide reveals all sorts of marine life, but the idea of catching something edible with what looked like oversized metal claws? That was new to me. About half an hour later, my son finally made his way back, holding something in his hand with a look of quiet triumph. Shells. Or maybe snails. Honestly, I’m still not sure what the correct name is. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmV78WBSFcNwp6YWZk7k8trA3jEfBL5kywf2awwNj47gdM/dsc05274.jpg) He explained — with the confidence only a child can have — that the old man told them they were edible. Not just edible, but something he collects regularly and sells. That’s when it clicked. I had seen these before — at local markets, already cooked and served as street food. But I had never actually tried them. Something about it always felt a bit unfamiliar, maybe even slightly strange. But then again… that’s part of traveling, right? You come across things that feel unusual at first, and slowly they stop being strange. They just become another experience. So maybe next time, when I find myself wandering through a Thai market again, I’ll stop, take a closer look — and finally give them a try. Seems only fair. Thanks for reading. * * * Thank you for your likes, your comments, and your time. It never goes unnoticed. * * * _I write my texts myself, correct mistakes and translate via ChatGPT (which is not a violation on Hive)! All photos were taken by me personally - I am a beginner photographer, so I ask professionals not to judge strictly._ * * * **_Thank you for sharing these moments with me! Until new stories and new holidays!_** ✌️. * * * **Camera** 📷: Sony Alpha 7 IV full-frame **Lens** 🔭: Sony FE 70-200mm F: 2.8 GM OSS II **Lens** 🔭: Sony FE 90mm F2.8 Macro G OSS **Lens** 🔭: Sony FE 24–70mm f/2.8 GM II **Processed** 🛠: Lightroom

I called that because this garden I have here contains full of love. Love to work and do inspired to others that has already successful in their lives because of gardening. Hope means I have full of hopes that this garden I have here will leads me to success. 

This few pineapple plants contains already lots of pineapple fruits, I really not intend to plant here but I kept trying to plant here to see if it is applicable and grows stabled here in sandy areas. My string beans plants also produced beans. Everytime when I watched this vegetables, I also remembered the child story titled jack and the beanstalk. I also only tried to plant this here in sandy areas and luckily it grows stabled producing beans. But I only planted only few beans plants but I did plans to propegate lots of it here in my simple garden. 

![Messenger_creation_7E143E0B-7B9B-49EE-9E86-BBDD8D2B0E3C.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmVPUCeciAxYkUVvG1NZccoNKx7yAEbKSMLsxDrBFzWrEd/Messenger_creation_7E143E0B-7B9B-49EE-9E86-BBDD8D2B0E3C.jpeg)

I also started to replant Alugbati vegetables here because the first alugbati vines already dried. </center>
My Garden extension is ready to use, I cleaned it for a few days and now it is ready to occupied by vegetables and root crops. Since we do not used synthetic fertilizers instead we used organic one those dry leaves are very useful. While cleaning this areas, I also kept myself busy putting those decaying materials at the pit so it will decomposed very fast.

#### *The Secret to have a successful gardening is Love and Hope, the best combination to gained a good achievement*.

Until next post, have a nice day to all of us.

title.title: A Brighter Side of Rainy Days
title.body:
The rainy season has officially begun, and with it, the garden is starting to feel alive again. After several days of rain, I noticed that more flowers are beginning to bloom, and the plants around the area are becoming lush once more. I took this chance to capture some of these flowers in black and white, hoping to show their simple beauty in a different way. ![1000130665.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/funtraveller/Eo6CFSA55aZgbz5EMQ9E83fwJUtVUCmj3xXbEcuwcgWYmPP6bim2BNFPWPpeYC3NJ33.jpg) Rainy days can sometimes feel gloomy and depressing, especially when the sky stays dark and the air feels heavy. It can slow down our plans and make the day feel less cheerful. But when I looked closely at the garden, I realized that the rain also brings something beautiful. It gives life to the plants, refreshes the leaves, and encourages flowers to bloom again. That is what I wanted to capture in these photos. Even without color, the flowers still carry a soft and graceful presence. The contrast between the light petals and the dark background makes them stand out more clearly. It reminds me that beauty does not always need bright colors to be appreciated. Sometimes, black and white makes us notice the shape, texture, and quiet character of a subject even more. I guess life is also like that. Some seasons may feel heavy, but they can still bring growth in ways we may not immediately see. We just have to look at the brighter side of things and allow ourselves to appreciate what is still beautiful around us. Thinking positively does not mean ignoring the gloomy parts of life. It simply means choosing to notice the small blessings that come with them. Have a good day ahead. *** ![1000130665.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/funtraveller/Eo6CFSA55aZgbz5EMQ9E83fwJUtVUCmj3xXbEcuwcgWYmPP6bim2BNFPWPpeYC3NJ33.jpg) ![1000121771.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/funtraveller/Eoc1GvEP3yi1wYzEN94uPz2gv9jpDv1BYiBQebrQE9DKQp2RMTuD3WcgT6sS2DX9p2n.jpg) ![1000131068.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/funtraveller/Eo44QG6xi3249Y6xff5Pq72DQgXdj5HqYH2ue6TsgbHMyUXJPyddV7yPXkQQyxhYwQj.jpg) ![1000120942.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/funtraveller/23tH1MBVaXrLuqkxo3SJM2MC8zUTm9jsY3VeSCfA8qEqMpxEMjDBMa5VBsWoe1AQvfdnH.jpg) ***

title.title: ¿Ves el mundo al revés o solo me pasa a mí? [Es-En] Do you see the world upside down, or is it just me?
title.body: ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmTgzKf23GqwVwNA1UGdwwdw1tHm3YbdZKkBfUbEaNzf2N/image.png) Son las 7:20 y aún no amanece; mientras preparo el café, observo la calle por la ventana, reparando en un transeúnte que viene caminando a buen paso; por el andar deduzco que es una mujer, pero antes de llegar a la esquina cuando pasa bajo un frondoso arbol desaparece. Espere y espere verla pasar al otro lado o cruzar la calle hacia la parada sin que la volviera a ver. Pasó el autobús, pasó otro viandante en sentido contrario que, al pasar bajo el árbol mencionado, reapareció a los pocos segundos, pero aquella mujer de pelo largo, nada. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmXCFaqMtTnJbajfFV68LueSppqbw7nbKrEexiaT1gyFbh/image.png) Puede ser que se montara en un automóvil estacionado en el lugar y arrancara mientras miraba el bus, o puede ser que se tratara de un agente del cambio dirigiéndose a ejecutar alguna misión. Vivimos tiempos complejos que muy bien podemos llamar el gran tiempo, y sin caer en sospechar de cualquiera, la verdad es que todos tomamos partido por algún bando en particular. Ya se organiza el Axis Mundi y un hombre en llamas se va elevar en el valle de Black Rock en medio de las llanuras de Nevada. Pasará otra vez sin dejar rastro de suceso y, como si no hubiera pasado, seguiremos como si nada; solo unos pocos como Fritz se percatarán de lo que sucede y hasta nos lo van a contar, pero ¿quién le hace caso a un soldado en delirium tremens? La guerra del cambio descubierta por Liber en los 50 puede ser anterior a la misma que aseguran enfrenta el bien y el mal. Me pregunto si puede ser realidad que las fuerzas implicadas son capaces de reclutar en sus filas a los mismos agentes que, manipulados, lo mismo luchan por un lado que por el otro. Convencidos de que es su lado o que es el ganador, acaso que tienen en su mano la verdad. En cada asalto lo dan todo y luchan sin cuartel sin saber, si antes estuvieron del otro lado. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmaTovBpBa7aPDYNPhmVtXBWw6rNDmJ4wVee51JKmSDEJE/image.png) Desde mi visión particular del mundo veo las noticias que nos lanzan en las redes, hace tiempo que no veo noticieros y veo las series con que nos entretienen, como esta nueva de Un Hombre en Llamas, inspirada en la pelicula de 2004. Me encantan las pelis de acción, y otras nuevas y viejas donde se enfrentan los que por lealtad están en un bando, mientras quienes los mandan negocian amistosamente con el otro bando. La misma idea de El Gato Pardo en El Gran tiempo. Estilos y tiempos diferentes, puede que a otros les parezca que nada tienen que ver, pero yo lo veo así. Reyes, alfiles y peones sobre el tablero defendiendo un lado para al terminar la partida caer en la misma caja sin saber de que lado estaremos en la siguiente. >#### Como cada día, escribo en español, mi lengua natal, y comparto la traducción al inglés generada por Google. Las imágenes son de mi propiedad y, por si sienten curiosidad, les cuento que los bloques son piezas de jabón artesanal muy rustico en proceso de elaboración. Actividad que disfruto tanto como escribir. # Do you see the world upside down, or is it just me? ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmTgzKf23GqwVwNA1UGdwwdw1tHm3YbdZKkBfUbEaNzf2N/image.png) It's 7:20 and it's still dark; while I make coffee, I watch the street through the window, noticing a pedestrian walking briskly. From her gait, I deduce it's a woman, but before reaching the corner, as she passes under a leafy tree, she disappears. I wait and wait to see her cross to the other side or cross the street towards the bus stop, but I never see her again. The bus passes, another pedestrian passes in the opposite direction who, after passing under the aforementioned tree, reappears a few seconds later, but that long-haired woman is nowhere to be seen. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmXCFaqMtTnJbajfFV68LueSppqbw7nbKrEexiaT1gyFbh/image.png) He might have gotten into a parked car and driven off while looking at the bus, or he might have been an agent of change on his way to carry out a mission. We live in complex times, which we can very well call the great times, and without suspecting anyone, the truth is that we all take sides. The Axis Mundi is already being organized, and a man in flames will rise in the Black Rock Valley in the middle of the Nevada plains. It will happen again without leaving a trace, and as if it hadn't happened, we will carry on as if nothing had occurred; only a few, like Fritz, will notice what is happening and even tell us about it, but who listens to a soldier in delirium tremens? The war of change, as described by Liber in the 1950s, may predate the one that supposedly pits good against evil. I wonder if it's true that the forces involved are capable of recruiting the same agents into their ranks who, manipulated, fight for either side. Convinced that it's their side, or that it will win, perhaps even that they hold the truth. In each battle, they give their all and fight relentlessly, without knowing if they were once on the other side. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmaTovBpBa7aPDYNPhmVtXBWw6rNDmJ4wVee51JKmSDEJE/image.png) From my particular worldview, I see the news that's thrown at us on social media. I haven't watched news programs in a long time, so I watch the series that entertain us, like this new one, Man on Fire, inspired by the 2004 film. I love action movies, and other new and old ones where those loyal to one side clash, while those in charge negotiate amicably with the other. It's the same idea as in The Great Time of the Cat. Different styles and times; others might think they have nothing to do with each other, but that's how I see it. Kings, bishops, and pawns on the board defending one side, only to fall back into the same box at the end of the game, not knowing which side we'll be on next. As usual, I'm writing in Spanish, my native language, and sharing the English translation generated by Google. The images are my own, and if you're curious, the blocks are pieces of very rustic, handmade soap in the process of being made. I enjoy making soap as much as writing.

title.title: Learn Creative Coding (#55) - L-Systems: Realistic Botanical Structures
title.body:
# Learn Creative Coding (#55) - L-Systems: Realistic Botanical Structures

![cc-banner](https://images.hive.blog/DQmSSx4SxC5nEmP89ZcekbPtexYXBqntCzVnfv8hpeUbXHA/cc-banner-teal.png)

Last episode we built L-systems from scratch. String rewriting, turtle graphics, push/pop branching, fractal curves, stochastic rules. All the fundamentals. The trees we drew looked... tree-shaped. Branching structures that read as botanical. But they were wireframe sketches -- every branch the same thickness, every segment the same length, no leaves, no weight, no life. A skeleton without flesh.

Today we put flesh on those bones. Parametric L-systems where symbols carry data (length, width, age). Tapering that makes trunks thick and twigs thin. Tropism that bends branches under gravity. Leaves at terminal nodes. Flowers with probability. Wind animation. Multiple species from different grammars. By the end of this episode your L-system trees will look like actual plants, not abstract diagrams.

The core mechanism is identical to episode 54 -- iterate a string with replacement rules, interpret it with a turtle. What changes is HOW we interpret the string and what extra information we attach to each symbol.

## Parametric L-systems: symbols with data

In episode 54, `F` just meant \

But real branches aren't all the same length. A trunk segment is long. A twig is short. And the width matters -- trunks are thick, branches thinner, twigs barely visible. We need F to carry parameters.\n\nThe idea: instead of bare characters, each symbol can carry numeric values in parentheses. `F(100, 8)` means \

after each step. The rotation scales with branch thinness (thin branches bend more). A single float parameter transforms a geometric tree into a weeping willow or a sturdy oak
- Leaves at terminal branches (below a width threshold) use simple Bezier oval shapes with randomized green tones. Flowers get placed with probability -- 15% flowers, 85% leaves gives a tree in light spring bloom
- Wind animation modifies the turtle heading by a time-varying offset scaled by depth. The string never changes -- only the interpretation during rendering. Outer branches sway more than the trunk, matching real physics
- Species are defined by 6 parameters (angles, shrink factors, tropism). Same grammar structure, different numbers, wildly different trees. Oak vs pine vs willow vs bush -- the parameters ARE the genetics
- Forest generation: grow multiple stochastic trees at random positions sorted back-to-front for depth overlap. A dozen trees with mixed species fills a convincing scene
- Growth animation pre-generates all generation strings and interpolates branch extension over time. Watch the tree grow from seed to full canopy as each iteration adds a burst of new branching at the tips

Sallukes! Thanks for reading.

X

title.title: Sometimes, no decision… is the right decision. 🧡
title.body:
Sometimes, no decision… is the right decision. 🧡

A proposal that had been on the table for months is now off the table: the obligation to declare self-hosted crypto wallets will not be implemented (in France, at this stage of the bill). 

Let’s rewind quickly, because the idea was simple: require individuals to annually declare their self-custodial wallets. 

Does someone think about better oversight or stronger fight against fraud? On paper maybe. 

In practice? serious questions around effectiveness and security. 

Because this is the uncomfortable truth:
- Self-custody ≠ bank account
- Wallets ≠ custodial platforms
- Collecting sensitive data ≠ always improving safety

The debate was never about being “for” or “against” regulation. It was about how to regulate.

Where do you draw the line between fighting fraud and increasing risk exposure for users?

This decision suggests something important: policymakers are starting to understand that not all solutions translate well into the crypto world!

Credit where it’s due: industry actors who engaged constructively, institutions that listened and a process that didn’t rush a complex topic. 

Because in a space like this… bad regulation can be worse than no regulation. 
The real challenge ahead remains: building frameworks that are effective, proportionate and adapted to how the technology actually works. Step by step.

Let’s keep moving in the right direction. 🧡

title.title: My Actifit Report Card: May 5 2026
title.body:
![IMG_20260505_123019.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmXrzfVvJjiGb7Xvw2Zx4mMXEiRHJxFvyFytK9nbGxP8XE/IMG_20260505_123019.jpg) ![hive dividers-04.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmdvc788wxsBSQHY3z21o3wSTU7hqRnyYc2JFEn2pEYSev/hive%20dividers-04.png) The day began with a simple yet warm atmosphere. I enjoyed my wife's homemade fried rice breakfast, accompanied by a cup of hot coffee, which felt just the right way to start the day. From that simple kitchen, I seemed to gather energy to tackle the activities that awaited me. After breakfast, I immediately resumed my routine work, delivering bread to my favorite shops around Lhokseumawe. The morning journey was pleasant, navigating the streets that were starting to bustle with activity. Finally, I arrived at Pusong, where the fishing boats were moored. The scenery there always held its own charm—rows of brightly colored boats, neatly arranged nets, and a refreshing sea breeze. As the afternoon approached, my activities shifted to more peaceful pursuits. I spent some time sewing caps for religious purposes. Although seemingly simple, this work brought a sense of serenity and was a way to unwind after a long day of outdoor activities. I also took the time to visit the rice fields. There, I observed the condition of the rice plants, some of which had already been harvested, while others were still waiting for their turn. The cloudy sky adds to the unique atmosphere, as if reminding us that every process has its own time. Today may seem ordinary, but it's full of meaning. From work, family, to the natural world, everything teaches us lessons about patience, hard work, and gratitude. ![hive dividers-04.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmdvc788wxsBSQHY3z21o3wSTU7hqRnyYc2JFEn2pEYSev/hive%20dividers-04.png) ![IMG_20260505_123021.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmS9AbsqgKfffjTBeWBZq5n6dAzPJ59cB1c765SdttR2zh/IMG_20260505_123021.jpg) ![IMG_20260505_123025.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmRVtbru21autVyJYzqfjNEfodqXwHgyPBhTMcBd762zKW/IMG_20260505_123025.jpg) ![IMG_20260505_123043.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmdF3M7HwbA8DmfgNYRJaeK2af3Zvxm1MsfMUv5YErfZ2L/IMG_20260505_123043.jpg) ![IMG_20260504_182426.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmNPZBA5cZDnkqVJL7N2MEPc1onceqmvPTjgswfy28aDw5/IMG_20260504_182426.jpg) ![hive dividers-04.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmdvc788wxsBSQHY3z21o3wSTU7hqRnyYc2JFEn2pEYSev/hive%20dividers-04.png)

title.title: Beautiful Dravidian style temple with an amazing location on the island of Mauritius
title.body:
>Almost in the center of Mauritius you will find the Sri Shiv Subramanya Temple. It is also called the Mountain Temple because of the location at the slopes of a mountain. A hundred steps are leading to this beautiful Dravidian style temple. It is seen as divine architectral wonder, dedicated to Lord Murugan, the Hindu god of war. It's an important pilgrimage site on the island. The location of the temple is on the mountain side of the Corps de Garde mountain. Not only is the temple beatiful and a great example of South Indian architecture, but the panoramic view is breathtaking. It is definitly worth the walk up the stairs to enjoy the view.
https://images.ecency.com/DQmakvQsxSaSnNcC19SpBSYT5UaArjBU1PpVnSAfLdKpbo5/02.jpg https://images.ecency.com/DQmTonZFXytc9RNAE8GCLWSzSjXPzZj5p1Zs1HZUuwChVcc/03.jpg https://images.ecency.com/DQmVz2b4hp9a8Y1JMrhiNKEq7MmvJgtPoCJ67372HBCEokQ/04.jpg https://images.ecency.com/DQmXXYpfq1XmPCKCrqcD98Z2ik72ncHLEoXhfErVQBe3NdS/05.jpg To get here, I took the metro from Port Louis to Quatre-Bornes. From the metro station it's a few kilometer walk. Before I started to up the stairs I noteced other buildings. There were quite a lot of people working around the entrance. They were cleaning, setting up tents, chairs ets. I supposed they are preparing for an event to be celebrated here.
https://images.ecency.com/DQmdhbnSkRUboSrmWqQP1f8gaNVdxw9fV5wfY7ghCVH1LYN/06.jpg https://images.ecency.com/DQmdz3hNfhjyMbPyvkU2eu4fXcSrLNaESaZb5CbNetkYhMu/07.jpg https://images.ecency.com/DQmbxhNDav9qN2eT8d35uJ2a3xEKPefbaqtUopTTvuYV9gp/08.jpg https://images.ecency.com/DQmTWTNEEgXnT5gPCcGMNhpFMoZkowNspfzQY17Exc4sx9g/09.jpg I decided to go up to the main temple first. I met quite a few Indians on their way up or down the stairs. The couple I met at the entrance told me that the priest was at the temple. It was a hot day, even though the sun did disappear now and then. On my way I did stop a couple of times to enjoy the view before I reached the entrance. Then I removed my shoes and took a walk around the temple itself and enjoying the vivid colors and the figures. I did look into the temple for a few minutes. (photographing not permitted).
https://images.ecency.com/DQmdKt8MQRHtJvkkvBZcBWUndeP7b83CBD6XeHh5wQR7yNa/10.jpg https://images.ecency.com/DQmVuqrTDSF8Fm8ZHKo33jQG62KbEZ8mKaKiw2DPNi8Rqij/11.jpg https://images.ecency.com/DQmcsktzGj5s2BQEPKRncNYSWkbefipnhqm5ndT6j2QSvff/12.jpg https://images.ecency.com/DQmVpfz9A7AftFwgoiJY7nRM8pqkLyymi79JU2Hm3hHB82z/13.jpg This beautiful temple was built in 1907 based on the wish of an Indian worker. He had a wish to built the temple on this particulary mountain side. All of the important festivals of Hinduism are also celebrated here. But the Thaipoosam Cavadee festival is maybe the one that is most important to the temple. It was here that the first festival on the island was held. Lots of people come to the temple to pray during the days of the festival. But it's not the only festival that are celebratet here. Devotees will climb these steps during the festival to worship Lord Murugan, making the temple a significant pilgrimage site.
https://images.ecency.com/DQmau7j9b1PPYxXkFBdLMrK4pvXTTH23DTQVQqDivSGK5zC/14.jpg https://images.ecency.com/DQmTBtTZ2nLw2qYhhvStuNLzNZcS36oKbK5rjMUnMpa7Jec/15.jpg https://images.ecency.com/DQmV8CQ3DkEZHPiaTQmkSiwHqk7zELKYEU13RoDGa9Rs7z1/16.jpg https://images.ecency.com/DQmPd2QWD3MM5G1vy1VXx2LZN4AsxxYYvKozcDYgvoCuhui/17.jpg Lord Murugan in the middle ## The history of the temple It all started when a devotee desided to build a shrine. In order to get the money to buy the property, he had to spend all of his earnings. This man who was called Velamurugan (1852-1913) had immigrated from India. I think he might have come to Mauritius as an indentured labourer, because I have red that he setled in Quatre Bornes when his contracted ended. Usually the indentured laboures were supposed to return at the end of their contract, but I think many must have stayed. Around 60 percent of the population in Mauritius are Indian origin.
https://images.ecency.com/DQmWVgXFmxihuRWGkpLV3PqZ8S6PpQEDULjwotX3xeFtweH/18.jpg https://images.ecency.com/DQmQu49o1G6MEiNtiTHb3tTWasJ81DNtzrBWwvw8h8zX5yp/19.jpg https://images.ecency.com/DQmWZsMvYUNVovSu7cmWZZv7zedsGe5SSoBbgkrR7BZZhBX/20.jpg https://images.ecency.com/DQmZJp3XUPhtVV5WDa5LNQvyuUeBCJPtNYxXnAxKgEeEVZP/21.jpg The temple has experienced problems caused by erosion. The result of all the work involved to find a solution, was to pull down the original structure and instead built a new. The decition was made in 2000 and the work started a year later. What they have done about the erotion is not clear to me. But they must have done something, because the new structure is built at the same place as the original one. This one is also larger than the original, but otherwise many of the items from the original temple are placed here.
https://images.ecency.com/DQmUMYsf8sMb73HxJbjXU65PGCPKAN4ELwejGMAtPQSb4tj/22.jpg https://images.ecency.com/DQmXh4LmSjDWtwMPySv9ovjZadszAWkM1HfHhcu7zJoBbCL/23.jpg https://images.ecency.com/DQmXxXqPgccWpXS7eUn5Q7vLpWbEKVsozyZLYYGWTQ7XCNU/24.jpg https://images.ecency.com/DQmbRbjBEcPsRKzKMQf8JTDpwJPf6g5ZnWPcDvNrtXLhVSW/25.jpg https://images.ecency.com/DQmYiPzfaBfc1Y1z7DdFQJpEz9Ta4BXwB2Hmn2R5EdVxNKY/26.jpg After a tour of the temple, I went down to the base and spend some time looking at two of the other buildings. I tried to get a good view of the temple and the mountain top, but vegetation is in the way. Instead I looked at two of the other buildings. I was here on the 30th of April and now I found out why there were so much going on at the yard near the entrance! They were preparing for next day event, Sittirai Cavadee.
https://images.ecency.com/DQmfYobEtNatF8GYVFusWTQTfKtm8kTJcrHsFR4UJrWJVBg/27.jpg https://images.ecency.com/DQmNiWyGDaYAoCHREbbKW7CFps7Zvy2bYEQYq9MPDUNQ13G/28.jpg https://images.ecency.com/DQmQe76esGmgkBvsq4hjatUmHRrntiC9jkrwxAy352gUA4K/29.jpg https://images.ecency.com/DQmQDd56Jnx3wbxYzLrENZXRKUqSzohcSsSrdg1korm3z7p/30.jpg https://images.ecency.com/DQmbNx8WHfZ48yjtjHurNPRy48RQ3b1BwVwmFiND3qo3ZVR/31.jpg https://images.ecency.com/DQmTjbqk1WJ1691TF7bkGufe8bpYW1WCB7TUaoKsunC8jSs/32.jpg At the entrance there is a very small building.There were noone here, except a woman who placed the insence sticks here and then she left. I think the figure on the back of it is Lord Murugan. I left the temple with a last look at the mountain. I have had this visit planned for last year. Now I am glad I finally made it. https://images.ecency.com/DQmWKG7UDMLeERAy9cfkviEGKZ66eGh42is1bxSiZqSnaeG/33.jpg

title.title: Kids Tooth Emergency: Birmingham Clinics Open Right Now
title.body:
Kids Tooth Emergency: Birmingham Clinics Open Right Now

Picture this: your child falls during a game in the park, and their tooth comes out completely. Blood stains their shirt, and they're in tears. That moment hits hard as a parent. You need fast help to save the tooth and ease the pain. In Birmingham, several clinics stay open for [kids tooth emergencies](https://www.robinhooddentalpractice.co.uk/kids-dental-health-tips-birmingham/) like this. Quick action matters a lot for good results in paediatric dental care.

Identifying a True Paediatric Dental Emergency

Parents often worry when their child has mouth pain. Not every issue needs a rush to the dentist. You can spot real emergencies by looking at signs of serious harm.

True paediatric dental emergencies happen fast and need prompt care. They include injuries that could lead to infection or tooth loss if ignored. Delaying help might mean bigger problems down the line.

Defining Urgent Dental Trauma in Children

Kids tooth emergencies often stem from accidents. A knocked-out tooth counts as one. Loose teeth from a hit also require quick attention.

Fractured teeth expose the inside, which can cause swelling. Severe gum or face swelling signals an abscess. Uncontrolled pain from an infection demands immediate care too.

These cases affect young mouths differently than adults. Children's teeth are still growing. Acting fast helps prevent long-term issues.

When to Head to the ER vs. The Dentist

Not all dental woes need A&E. Go to the emergency room only for life threats like trouble breathing from swelling. Unstoppable bleeding or bad head injuries also go there first.

For most kids tooth emergencies, head to a dentist. They handle tooth reinsertion and pain control better. Call your dentist's emergency line right away if you can.

If it's after hours, search for open Birmingham clinics. This keeps your child from unnecessary ER waits. Dentists focus on oral fixes that save teeth.

Finding Open Birmingham Clinics Now: Your Immediate Action Plan

In a crisis, you need a plan to find help fast. Birmingham has options for kids tooth emergencies open right now. Start with simple steps to locate them.

Use your phone or computer for quick searches. Focus on places that take walk-ins or same-day spots. Time is key, so pick the closest one.

Utilising Emergency Dental Hotlines and Directories

Dial NHS 111 for advice in the UK. They guide you to open clinics in Birmingham. Tell them it's a children's dental emergency for the right direction.

Search online with terms like \

. Sites like the British Dental Association list local spots. Check Google Maps for hours and reviews.

Local directories show which clinics handle kids. Look for ones near you, like in the city centre or suburbs. This cuts down travel time during stress.

Criteria for Selecting an Open Clinic

Pick clinics that see children regularly. Many family dentists do, but confirm it. Ask if they take emergency cases for kids tooth emergencies.

See if they have spots available today. Call ahead to check wait times. Short waits mean less pain for your child.

Look for positive feedback on child care. Clean, welcoming places ease nerves. Verify they're registered with the General Dental Council for trust.

Step-by-Step Care for Common Kids' Tooth Emergencies

While you head to the clinic, give first aid at home. These steps stop worse damage. Stay calm to help your child feel safe.

Basic care buys time until pros take over. Use clean items from your home. Avoid rough handling that could harm more.

Managing a Knocked-Out Permanent Tooth (Avulsion)

Time counts in the first hour after a tooth knocks out. Hold the tooth by the white crown, not the root. Rinse it gently in milk if dirty.

Store it in a small pot of whole milk or salt water. Never put it in tap water, as that kills cells. Get to the clinic fast for reinsertion.

Success rates drop after 30 minutes out of the mouth. Keep your child comfy on the way. This simple hold can save the tooth.

If it's a baby tooth, don't try to put it back. Just control bleeding with a clean cloth. Head to the dentist to check for other damage.

Handling Acute Tooth Pain and Suspected Abscesses

Rinse the mouth with warm salt water to clean it. Mix half a teaspoon of salt in a glass of warm water. This reduces swelling a bit.

Give pain relief like paracetamol if your child is old enough. Follow the dose on the box for kids. Skip aspirin, as it thins blood.

Don't put heat on the face if swollen. Cold packs help more for comfort. Professionals need to drain pus or give drugs.

Watch for fever or more swelling. These signs mean hurry to the clinic. Home care only holds things over till help arrives.

Addressing Chipped or Fractured Teeth

Rinse the mouth with cool water first. This clears bits and soothes. Save any large tooth pieces in milk.

If edges are sharp, cover them with clean gauze. Or use wax from braces kits if you have it. This stops cuts inside the mouth.

Control bleeding by biting on a cloth gently. Most chips need a quick fix at the dentist. Go soon to avoid infection.

For deep fractures, watch for nerve pain. Your child might need a cap later. First aid keeps it stable till then.

What to Expect at the Emergency Paediatric Appointment

Arriving at the clinic calms the storm a bit. Staff know how to handle scared kids. They make the visit as smooth as possible.

Expect a wait, but it's worth it for expert care. Bring a toy or book to distract your child. The team works to fix things quick.

The Initial Paediatric Triage and Examination

They start with basic checks like temperature and blood pressure. Tell the dentist what happened in detail. This helps them spot issues fast.

A quick look inside the mouth follows. They might take X-rays to see roots. Pain control comes early with gels or shots.

Kids often get a gentle exam. The dentist explains steps in simple words. This builds trust right away.

Treatment Options for Immediate Stabilisation

For knocked-out teeth, they clean and replant it. A splint holds it in place for weeks. Follow-up visits check healing.

Chips get smoothed or filled temporarily. Abscesses might need drainage and cleaning. Antibiotics help fight infection if needed.

Pain relief and advice wrap up the visit. They plan next steps, like a full check later. Most kids leave feeling better.

Prevention: Reducing the Risk of Future Dental Trauma

Emergencies hurt, but you can cut chances of them. Simple habits protect young smiles. Teach kids safe play from early on.

Regular dentist visits spot risks ahead. Cleanings and check-ups keep teeth strong. Mouthguards change the game for sports.

Essential Gear for Active Children

Get a mouthguard for contact sports like football or rugby. Custom ones from the dentist fit best. They absorb hits to the teeth.

Boil-and-bite types work too if the budget is tight. Check them yearly or after hard knocks. Replace if cracked or loose.

Helmets pair well with guards for bike rides. Kids in active clubs should always wear them. This gear saves trips to emergency clinics.

Teach face-away falls in play. Soft surfaces in gardens help too. Small changes add up to safer fun.

Creating a Home Dental First-Aid Kit

Build a kit for quick response to [kids tooth emergencies](https://www.robinhooddentalpractice.co.uk/kids-dental-health-tips-birmingham/). Include saline solution in a small bottle. Add clean gauze pads for bleeding.

Pack antiseptic mouthwash and a kids' pain reliever. Write down your dentist's number and NHS 111. A mini torch helps see inside mouths at night.

Store it in an easy spot, like the kitchen drawer. Review it every six months. Ready kits mean less panic next time.

Conclusion: Peace of Mind in Birmingham Dental Crises

Kids' tooth emergencies shake any parent. But in Birmingham, open clinics provide fast relief. Act quickly to save smiles and cut pain.

You now know the signs of real issues and first aid steps. Use hotlines and searches to find help now. Prevention tools keep future risks low.

Before trouble hits, note local [emergency paediatric dental services](https://www.robinhooddentalpractice.co.uk/kids-dental-health-tips-birmingham/). Call your family dentist for routine care too. A healthy mouth starts with you. For immediate kids tooth emergency support in Birmingham, reach out to NHS 111 or search trusted clinics today.

title.title: (EN-FR) How to ensure your safety in a taxi when traveling abroad as a student-Comment assurer sa sécurité dans un taxi lors d'un voyage à l'étranger en tant qu'étudiant
title.body: was originally uploaded by_ [_USAG- Humphreys_](https://www.flickr.com/photos/usaghumphreys/) _on Flickr and is reused here under the terms and conditions of the Creative Commons_ [_Attribution 2.0 Generic (CC BY 2.0)_](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/2.0/) _license_ (English version) Tips of advice to stay safe when using a taxi as a student traveling abroad Using a bus or a taxi is a necessity when you are on holiday, especially if you travel on your own and the holiday package does not include a guided tour. The national income of many countries depends heavily on visitors spending on various locally produced goods and services, therefore, a tourist is considered as a valuable source of money. As a result, it wouldn’t come as a surprise the fact that, local people, will go to any length, in order to attract tourists to buy whatever they may sell. It is not an unusual situation even in wealthy and economically developed countries that locals who are literally “jacks of all trades” to attempt to exploit, and even “rob” any unsuspecting victims who visit those countries, with student travelers being on top of their list. One of the possible scenarios where student holidaymakers may be taken advantage of is when they try to get on a taxi. Since it will not be possible for students who visit a country for the very first time to know the shortest way to drive from point A to point B, the taxi driver will be tempted to choose the longest itinerary, and make more money, as a result. A good piece of advice would be to ask the receptionist of your hotel if they could show you the fastest route; then you have to insist on the taxi driver following it. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=m8uySVbeOuk Another great tip would be to only use the services of well-established and reputed taxi companies, even if they are more expensive and charge you more, because, in this way, by choosing them you will end up saving you much more money and time. Again, you can usually find them at the reception of the hotel you are staying in, and, even better, you can use one of the taxi companies that serve the hotel’s guests on a regular basis. You are also highly advised to never try to stop and use an occasionally passing taxi, right in the middle of the street. Chances are that the driver might not be officially licensed to carry passengers in a professional manner, and in other words, he/she might be a fake and illegal taxi driver and you might end up having an unpleasant “adventure”. When female students who go on holiday to a foreign country use a taxi, they should remember not to get in it without any friends accompanying them. The majority of taxi drivers are decent professionals but you might run into one or two odd drivers, who may attempt to make sexual advancements, particularly if you had a couple of drinks and you have started losing contact with reality. It is a good habit to have your mobile phone on you at all times, so you will be able to phone someone for help as soon as possible. You shouldn’t forget that you are abroad, and this is the only way to get vital assistance in case of an emergency. Getting on a taxi with a driver that you don’t know how professional he/she is, could be such a case. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=b1MHuW00BuQ Most of the hotels provide their guests with safety deposit boxes and it would be wise to rent one of them, where you can keep your valuable personal objects and documents, such as traveler’s cheques, passports etc., if you don’t need them immediately. You should avoid showing your money or credit cards in public, whether in a taxi or anywhere else in a foreign country, because this will make you an easy target for people who set an eye on them. When getting on a taxi, you should try and get into the habit of writing down the name of the taxi driver on a piece of paper, or his/her license number, and keep it in your wallet. Actually, anyone is entitled to do this by law, and you can apply this practice even in your own country. In this way, if a problem arises, you will always have the details of the driver available, and you can use them as a proof or point of reference. This might sound funny to people who come from most countries of the western world; you should not forget to use the safety belt when using a taxi, especially in countries where the enforcement of road traffic laws is not as strict as it should be. The majority of drivers, and not just taxi drivers, in those countries, would be simply described as “dangerous” under the U.S. standards. Before getting on-board, the general appearance and condition of the vehicle that will take you to your destination should be immaculate, both outside and inside. This might sound as a joke again, but it is certainly not advisable to get on a taxi that looks like a rattletrap. You could be putting your life at risk, regardless of any “official” certification that the driver might carry, which could be false documents signed and sealed by a corrupt government official. Finally, do not hesitate to ask the taxi driver for an approximation of the total cost to carry you to a specific destination. The distance tariffs are officially set and the price per mile is standard. Again, the hotel reception can be an invaluable source of information in this area. (Version française) Conseils pour voyager en toute sécurité en taxi en tant qu'étudiant à l'étranger

_ a été initialement téléchargé par [_USAG- Humphreys_](https://www.flickr.com/photos/usaghumphreys/) _sur Flickr et est réutilisée ici conformément aux termes et conditions de Creative Commons_ [_Attribution 2.0 Generic (CC BY 2.0)_](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/2.0/) _license_

Prendre le bus ou le taxi est indispensable en vacances, surtout si vous voyagez seul et que votre forfait ne comprend pas de visite guidée.

Le revenu national de nombreux pays dépend fortement des dépenses des visiteurs en biens et services locaux ; un touriste est donc considéré comme une précieuse source de revenus.

Par conséquent, il n’est pas surprenant que les populations locales fassent tout leur possible pour attirer les touristes et les inciter à acheter leurs produits.

Même dans les pays riches et économiquement développés, il n’est pas rare que des locaux, véritables touche-à-tout, tentent d’exploiter, voire de voler, les touristes naïfs, notamment les étudiants.

L'une des situations où les étudiants en vacances risquent d'être victimes d'arnaques est lorsqu'ils prennent un taxi.

Comme il est impossible pour des étudiants visitant un pays pour la première fois de connaître le chemin le plus court entre deux points, le chauffeur de taxi sera tenté d'emprunter le trajet le plus long afin d'augmenter ses revenus.

Un bon conseil serait de demander à la réception de votre hôtel s'il peut vous indiquer l'itinéraire le plus rapide ; vous devrez ensuite insister pour que le chauffeur de taxi le suive.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=m8uySVbeOuk

Un autre excellent conseil serait de n'utiliser que les services de compagnies de taxis reconnues et réputées, même si elles sont plus chères. En les choisissant, vous économiserez ainsi beaucoup de temps et d'argent. Vous les trouverez généralement à la réception de votre hôtel, et encore mieux, vous pouvez faire appel à l'une des compagnies de taxis qui desservent régulièrement les clients de l'hôtel.

Il est également fortement déconseillé d'arrêter un taxi qui passe au milieu de la rue. Il y a de fortes chances que le chauffeur ne soit pas autorisé à transporter des passagers de manière professionnelle ; autrement dit, il pourrait s'agir d'un faux chauffeur de taxi, et vous risqueriez de vivre une mauvaise expérience.

Les étudiantes qui partent en vacances à l'étranger doivent se rappeler de ne pas monter seules dans un taxi. La plupart des chauffeurs de taxi sont des professionnels corrects, mais vous pourriez tomber sur un ou deux chauffeurs bizarres, qui pourraient tenter des avances sexuelles, surtout si vous avez bu quelques verres et que vous commencez à perdre le contact avec la réalité.

Il est judicieux d'avoir son téléphone portable sur soi en permanence, afin de pouvoir appeler à l'aide au plus vite. N'oubliez pas que vous êtes à l'étranger et que c'est le seul moyen d'obtenir une assistance vitale en cas d'urgence. Prendre un taxi avec un chauffeur dont vous ignorez le professionnalisme pourrait être une telle situation.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=b1MHuW00BuQ

La plupart des hôtels mettent à disposition de leurs clients des coffres-forts. Il est donc conseillé d'en louer un pour y déposer vos objets de valeur et vos documents importants, tels que chèques de voyage, passeport, etc., si vous n'en avez pas besoin immédiatement. Évitez d'afficher votre argent ou vos cartes de crédit en public, que ce soit dans un taxi ou ailleurs à l'étranger, car cela vous rendrait vulnérable aux personnes mal intentionnées.

Lorsque vous prenez un taxi, prenez l'habitude de noter le nom du chauffeur ou son numéro de permis sur un papier et de le conserver dans votre portefeuille. Toute personne est en droit de le faire, même dans son propre pays. Ainsi, en cas de problème, vous disposerez toujours des coordonnées du chauffeur et pourrez les utiliser comme preuve.

Cela peut paraître étrange aux yeux des Occidentaux, mais n'oubliez pas d'attacher votre ceinture de sécurité en taxi, surtout dans les pays où le code de la route est moins bien appliqué. La plupart des conducteurs, et pas seulement les chauffeurs de taxi, dans ces pays, seraient qualifiés de « dangereux » selon les normes américaines.

Avant de monter à bord, vérifiez que l'état général du véhicule qui vous conduira à destination est impeccable, tant à l'extérieur qu'à l'intérieur. Cela peut sembler anodin, mais il est fortement déconseillé de prendre un taxi en piteux état. Vous risquez votre vie, quelles que soient les « certifications » que le chauffeur pourrait présenter, qui pourraient être de faux documents signés et scellés par un fonctionnaire corrompu.

Enfin, n'hésitez pas à demander au chauffeur une estimation du prix de la course. Les tarifs kilométriques sont fixes. La réception de votre hôtel peut vous fournir de précieuses informations à ce sujet.

(Cet article a été traduit de l'anglais vers le français avec Google Translate)

_Further reading:_

[Studying Abroad-Travelers’ Health](https://wwwnc.cdc.gov/travel/page/studying-abroad)

[Guidelines for students travelling overseas](https://www.auckland.ac.nz/en/students/forms-policies-and-guidelines/student-policies-and-guidelines/student-travel-guidelines.html)

[Safety tips for traveling off campus](https://www.keiseruniversity.edu/pdf/safety-traveling-off-campus.pdf)

[Staying safe and healthy abroad](https://international.missouri.edu/health-safety-security/staying-safe-and-healthy-abroad/)

[6 Safety Tips for Taking Taxis When Traveling](https://www.nerdwallet.com/article/travel/taxi-safety-tips)

[Taking a Taxi Abroad – 8 Tips for Travellers](https://www.taxihull.co.uk/taking-a-taxi-abroad-8-tips-for-travellers/)

title.title: WhatsApp: Tu Puente de Conexión Directa con los que Amas
title.body:
<div class='text-justify'>

<center>
![image.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmUWa9YLMbozoLdbbjLVVMu3R3Hdp2X79kdsSgsb3DgKst/image.png)
</center>
<center>[Fuente](https://segurossura.com/co/blog/revista-5-sentidos/consejos-para-el-uso-de-la-tecnologia-en-la-tercera-edad/)</center>

Si hay una herramienta que ha cambiado las reglas del juego en la comunicación, esa es WhatsApp. Lo que empezó como una simple forma de enviar mensajes de texto, se ha convertido en una plataforma completa que nos permite compartir momentos en tiempo real. Para muchos, es el \

con hijos, nietos y amigos. Aprender a dominarlo no es solo saber escribir; es saber estar presente a pesar de la distancia física.

# El Poder de la Voz: Más allá del Texto
A veces, escribir puede ser tedioso o nos preocupa no expresar bien el tono. Aquí es donde los mensajes de voz son tus mejores aliados.

- El truco del \

: No hace falta que mantengas el dedo pulsado sobre el icono del micrófono todo el tiempo. Si pulsas y deslizas hacia arriba (hacia el candado), el audio se grabará solo. Así puedes hablar relajado y con naturalidad, como si estuvieras tomando un café con la otra persona.

-  Escucha antes de enviar: Recuerda que puedes pausar la grabación y escucharla antes de darle a enviar. ¡Se acabaron los audios con ruidos inesperados!

# Compartir es Vivir: Fotos y Vídeos
No hay nada que le guste más a un abuelo que recibir una foto de sus nietos, y viceversa.

- La cámara de WhatsApp: Puedes hacer una foto directamente desde la app para enviarla al instante.

-  Estado de WhatsApp: Esta es la \

de tus contactos. Puedes subir una foto de tu jardín o de tu paseo diario y todos tus amigos podrán verla durante 24 horas sin que tengas que enviársela uno a uno. Es una forma maravillosa de decir: \

. - Videollamadas: El Rostro de la Felicidad Si una imagen vale más que mil palabras, una videollamada vale más que mil mensajes. Poder ver la sonrisa de alguien mientras te cuenta su día es una medicina para el alma. - Consejo de experto: Busca un lugar con buena luz (frente a una ventana es ideal) y apoya el móvil en algo estable para que no se mueva. ¡Verás qué diferencia! - Llamadas grupales: ¿Sabías que puedes hablar con varios hijos o amigos a la vez? Es como hacer una reunión familiar virtual sin tener que limpiar la casa antes. # Un Pequeño Detalle: La Prudencia Digital WhatsApp es maravilloso, pero también requiere su etiqueta. No te sientas obligado a responder al segundo; cada uno tiene sus ritmos. Y recuerda: si recibes un mensaje que te genera duda o miedo (como premios que no has ganado o alguien pidiendo dinero de forma rara), lo mejor es borrarlo y preguntar a alguien de confianza. La tecnología debe traerte paz, no preocupaciones. # ¡Tu opinión nos guía! Ya somos casi expertos en WhatsApp. Para nuestra tercera entrega, ¿qué te genera más curiosidad? ***A) YouTube y el Entretenimiento: Cómo encontrar películas viejas, tutoriales de cocina, música y ejercicios adaptados sin pagar nada.*** ***B) Seguridad y Privacidad: Cómo configurar tu móvil para que nadie te moleste y para navegar por internet con total tranquilidad.*** _¡Escribe tu opción en los comentarios y sigamos explorando este mundo digital!_

title.title: DIY process of a beautiful dinner dress
title.body:
# Hello Hive 


It’s a beautiful day to be here again to share with the community my latest creation. I have been away from sewing for about 2weeks now and it feels so good to be back. 


![BF8941F3-268A-444F-A57C-44623CBBEDA2.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/monica-ene/23y8wwkekJWUiKJ6U7g3bywGfZtwHTnAHTqmNBokSVAx3e3TbnEHnZH1SUywR2htD8UrR.jpeg)


Today I decided to make a very simple dress but because of the nature of the fabric it turned out so beautiful and would be useful for any dinner outing. It’s a yellow net like fabrics that’s very soft and nice in the skin. The fabric is only a meter length leaving me with a challenge of sewing a dress that will be long and and decent. 

I like 
![B92B44D2-D92B-476C-8BDB-686F08C852B6.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/monica-ene/23wX3o2rYrNWKcXZ6Yiup3gCWtHhecrshapGczx7Cak5FRsWLvYeAyndbXXSfqWccGE9P.jpeg)
 I love off shoulder outfit but because of my collar bones I can’t wear them instead of that I decided to sew me a dress with some gathers at the know 



I started with marking the fabric here with a size 6 measurement and cut out the front block and the back block 
The front had a lower neckline 


![146129A9-A1E1-474D-B3BD-14F0113369E4.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/monica-ene/23u6JEAGFpBtzEKhE6szPXEKNzxehMmoeiaPiVhfNuqTGP3vzFyVNHqG8DGT48yJDsm3E.jpeg)

![706619E2-A116-4B97-BED6-DF2A0D7B3A66.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/monica-ene/23tSooAshWBawYRART6HModdZym3BL6AD2x9aTx4Zc9qzy8HwKyEiWtVvn5LcfHLdhTvi.jpeg)



Next I cut out separate sets of flair to add to the base of the dress. By the time I was done cutting that the fabric was exhausted leaving me with no option of what to use as sleeves



![88821510-0CCA-481C-848F-A85BB092D27B.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/monica-ene/23x1DUN1346GNgyNyHqAga3UGxTHuLbJtK3mQQHkyMCCiDqAm7iSouVms9TXxmn1Yw1pX.jpeg)

![0E0FCBF7-5AD3-4AA9-B698-49BC527CD4B0.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/monica-ene/23vsYzFTNudvYH4KwewnSnEQf4fiFVi2drkCCUekQbDq9g5xNBoUsZ2U4GH51j1BDDZSp.jpeg)

I have thought that I will manage this fabric well but that didn’t happen 


I moved next to sewing joining the shoulders first. Then I joined the side seams 



![327EBED7-BBE2-4B0E-A542-5086FA4722BB.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/monica-ene/242NitdcCdtpJj9SdrRLoAPR4efFTWbHwivHaYotzDM1fPZxSkyp8qAykpfNjjKbYKwrq.jpeg)

![1F9A6AAF-7BD5-44E6-9DBE-B39357890DC6.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/monica-ene/23x171o1odoP4gBrvrAGhgQsMSXnzSh9mnekQkvxpb7EfUZ2u7aLb4SHR1EEN38iosVrX.jpeg)


And the flair was the next that was joined to the dress. 


I like the outcome of the finished dress as this is simple enough to be worn for a night outing if you have a glittery camisole to wear within it.

A good idea would be to get another type of fabric with a similar color to be cut and attached to this as the sleeves or to wear it as sleeveless with some jacket or inner that has a sleeve.  

![7D8BE5E4-D154-4149-8F3A-A32CAF70AC75.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/monica-ene/23vsYuMrDP8RkefjUSUyDsAjdXCokFfWzfpwSf2tF8a2pxc8XvRP5PcUr3mjTwvkooJf1.jpeg)

![D0EB3945-D063-4225-A2B5-5D9D00C26FAC.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/monica-ene/23xVPTQfFi7Es6fVBhykk4g8hs28mYvgqTmY1VpUtJgjwu7zfwYBBPaCLhsFc2pTcBBek.jpeg)


The nature of a fabric can most times dictate what we sew of such fabric and this is exactly why I chose a simple design for a fragile fabric

title.title: Crypto Cooking - My 3-Minute Shiitake Magic Is Better Than Take-Away
title.body:
Cooking and mushrooms share some surprisingly rich similarities… both demand the right ingredients, perfect timing, and just enough experimentation to keep things interesting.

One day you’re sizzling shiitake in a hot pan, the next you’re exploring earthy porcini or delicate enoki. Ever notice how balancing flavors in a mushroom dish feels like walking a tightrope?

Too much heat and they lose their texture, too little and they never develop that deep umami. Today I made the best shiitake mushrooms in under three  minutes!

It’s all about the transformation! I watched them go from raw and spongy to golden caramelized perfection. In the end, it’s simple... you either nail that rich, savory depth… or you don’t! 

It started with a hot frying pan. Properly hot as the kind that sizzles the moment anything touches it. Into that went sliced shiitake mushrooms, followed by chopped leek, half an onion, and a mix of spices.


![image.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmP2hJ3fADmhxYLjhsHQEMnY6wWJKprtGSCLtcBQbBAtxY/image.png)


Nothing fancy, just flavors that complement each other naturally! No overthinking, no complicated prep, just heat, instinct, and a handful of  leftover ingredients that work.

That’s exactly what happened when I threw together what might be the quickest, most satisfying shiitake mushroom dish I’ve ever made. Sometimes the best meals come together in a flash! 

From there, it was all about movement and timing. For three minutes straight, I kept everything in motion... tossing, stirring, letting the ingredients catch just enough heat to soften.

The mushrooms began to release their moisture, the onions turned slightly translucent, and the leeks added that subtle sweetness. Then came the alpha element ... the soy sauce.

Not all at once but in small dashes. Each splash hit the pan and instantly sizzled, coating the mushrooms and vegetables while helping everything caramelize.

That’s where the magic happened! The sugars in the soy sauce and the natural umami of the mushrooms combined, creating a deep, rich glaze in just moments.


![image.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmP8f4nCoSw7GwBYqZ5XrxvKFKMrFiuKXRGV3sEyMw4Jp2/image.png)


By the end of those three minutes, everything had come together perfectly. The mushrooms were tender but still meaty, the onions slightly crisp at the edges, and the whole dish coated in a glossy finish.

No long cooking time, no complicated technique! PVM needs just heat, timing, and a few good ingredients. Here's the poof that the simplest dishes hit the hardest.

Whether it’s the kitchen or crypto charts... it’s all about reading the moment, trusting your instincts, and knowing when to let things ride. May the mushrooms fill your belly and feed your brain!

title.title: We're BACK?!
title.body:
### Nothing like some good old FOMO

So I have to admit, the Hive CEX whales are hard to predict. They just randomly pump HIVE by like 50% like it is nothing. Just some days ago we were sitting at rank 550+ and are now back over one hundred places at #422 with a MC of 46M. 


![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/tobetada/Eo6Bdd9CszCa11bwqqiyuJJ2YEuibRfqjhwoctAneLmv45mt4M6iWbo5uf8ZEBj9qhw.png)


Volume is up by 1000% with 17M, although the big caveat is that CMC does not include Upbit's volume for some reason. Upbit itself has 18M... so that puts us to 35M which is like 76% of our entire MC. 


![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/tobetada/23tGW1X9wTXseFMkokaKyLBKjf33mzYSSX8bLR2ud9QShEaDYWybkHKRaGzZaCAipXsrF.png)

Of course the unpredictability is only partly true, since we have known for years that the whales almost always pump Hive at 00:00 UTC! Why? Who knows... But this time is no exception.


![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/tobetada/23tcNeS8ToC4AsiBGYnAz3J7fnnuNaqMuuYcZrtydqzoFxZRuF3rDPWMfqHTtveRcDYY8.png)

The candle itself is preposterous, but nothing we haven't seen before. It's a solid candle - the one we have seen **that signals trend change**. It happened in 2021 and 2025. Volume overall is actually still low (red box). However, we still have some days left in the week and it's clear that it's still a biggy. 







![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/tobetada/23sxozwpR7YAPkTs2ayAT8pPpvWAv2KWNcNWciM2d9nwZmcdzFBLUNoKD3ziRX1okzTYt.png)

### Time to Sell?

Generally speaking, these pumps have always been good for selling. Personally, I just sold a ton of SPS for Hive, but used it to buy RUJI... seems like I always just miss the opportunity.

Anyway, if you have some spare Hive lying around, it might actually be a good idea to sell some (if you can resist the FOMO). But if this is really a trend change, it might also be quite risky...

The bottom line, I suppose, is that HIVE hasn't been forgotten by the big players. While we know that they are only in it for profits, **pumps like this do have a tendency to revive the hype and ecosystem as well as the activity.** 

---

title.title: Hive Open Days: Día 3 // Hive Open Days: Day 3
title.body: ![IMG_2270.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/palomap3/EpCAM5E1nG4nZW5z7TiM27hUuwDZpizsCxYaKguA6zvcvWd8vFABKzYKGM6un7opUBU.JPG) [Click here to read this post in **English**](#english)

> Hola querido hiver. Continúo con el relato de lo acontecido en las últimas jornadas. Esta vez escribo ya de regreso en mi hogar, con la comodidad del ordenador en lugar del teléfono móvil. Tengo cientos de fotos por revisar y que más adelante darán para publicaciones exhaustivas sobre algunas de las experiencias que te cuento en este de hoy. ![IMG_2228.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/palomap3/EowJXVmpN6yGHPNYwEsS3GhBdYZBgsP3bkg8eBPivtfHAjJY4gqhunyN87QWKK8Ruwy.JPG) ![IMG_2230.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/palomap3/EogNJuVA837SoNByXpWNagRKT6SoMwvpZv2k1ap1TJMsSGBvT8zWwYAfpuKC6BKRSyX.JPG) Empecé el tercer día con este delicioso desayuno en [Swallow Specialty Coffee](https://www.instagram.com/swallow_specialtycoffee/). Me gustó mucho el ambiente tranquilo y acogedor de esta cafetería y el servicio fue inmejorable. Desde allí acudimos al punto de reunión para caminar juntos hasta el puerto. Antes de llegar al embarcadero me detuve un instante para fotografiar el paseo más conocido de Alicante. ![IMG_2231.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/palomap3/EqFsWYpJM4H5tFVUa6cq1j9UxmcmtniEeNKoe9tUTZrfZdNKkbTcQFwrQ9nXUbPCbGW.JPG) ![IMG_2244.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/palomap3/Ep5nG9wKwQ6QAhnUfQ3QUfDDhk49QUif9jEYxYukW68weCndRZBzwnSW7fZTNzxxw4B.JPG) Esta imagen de @ninaeatshere resume bien cómo nos sentíamos durante el viaje, emocionados por estar navegando y disfrutando de unas vistas fascinantes. El viento amortiguaba como podía el ruido del motor de la embarcación y nuestra emoción por navegar hizo que el viaje de una hora se pasara volando. ![IMG_2255.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/palomap3/EqUdp94u8Kh2FsZwgToDYeaX6bqpfSxmtwq5rt5whG8CfvbUFy9QoWRPqWFQpiPYtz4.JPG) ![IMG_2267.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/palomap3/EqhQkLgHUp9Kydca34zVns6ZgkSCWYrfjeaoP5F5Fq79FT8bs9Uf5YRU8L4oSKa4qGB.JPG) ![IMG_2269.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/palomap3/Eq9Vo9qApJ55xF81Y5fKVvcYDQZRFCC1nEErwty6KPoYzmHxdbYVFjqKhCkDa4Nxkmi.JPG) Hivers desembarcando en la isla de Tabarca, pendientes de documentar lo que sus ojos estaban viendo. Lo primero que hicimos fue comer en el restaurante donde habíamos reservado y después nos divertimos mucho con un juego de Trivial organizado por @ninaeatshere. ![IMG_2273.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/palomap3/Eq9WAML4fKn1YVpfFbyGmejrPSeyzUHzgRqoJKar7H37gvSSbPvFMsNFey3JAJiVAkG.JPG) Este fue mi equipo, quedamos los terceros, ¡medalla de bronce! Fue fácil de conseguir... ya que solo había tres grupos. 🤣 Lo importante es que nos echamos unas risas y aprendimos cosas nuevas. De izquierda a derecha: @juanmatrader @gissse @ninaeatshere @livinguktaiwan @edje @enraizar @sinochip @igormuba Paula @palomap3 y @ratona Después de esto había programado un visionado de un audiovisual en el Museo Nueva Tabarca, pero la responsable de atendernos no se presentó. 🤷‍♀ De ese modo tuvimos más tiempo para participar en la siguiente actividad, el paseo dedicado a la iniciativa @cleanplanet ![IMG_2282.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/palomap3/EopvMeyooMdJZqN36dP6EkVbhC7cxYcLQy6DgjbKcjucojb89deFvHaxFzu63GyxNbQ.JPG) Hice equipo con @ratona y la verdad es que no fue una tarea fácil encontrar basura. Nos sorprendió lo limpio que estaba la isla para ser un lugar que se dedica al turismo de forma prácticamente exclusiva y por el que pasamos tantas personas a diario. ![IMG_2283.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/palomap3/EpGSCWirJfYSQxUDAKcXb7B8CW6YRjmXkUMzPAz8zyKjKixz2jz1km4aRmVQf7aJq5P.JPG) @igormuba y @edje en plena faena. ![IMG_2286.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/palomap3/Eq9XG24g1B6U6ch64kQrJvgMfRzZZ1XRFEANxJ3hRN5UTqm1NctgoUGPhRKx48LHruy.JPG) @livinguktaiwan mostrando orgullosa su captura. ![IMG_2287.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/palomap3/Eoc921sKNn67C9hiCGmLzfAMMgu2Wf3vNojjtVssxHzxhnMYC3k5EUQfp1cvhcr6zXq.JPG) Los nuevos miembros de Hive @gissse y @juanmatrader con su encantadora sobrina probaron suerte en la zona de la playa. A juzgar por el volumen de su bolsa tuvieron más suerte que nosotras. ![IMG_2330.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/palomap3/EnuiJmf2tYVBxNRNCT2YtupwDuY5VPicNkoVYH5T4CQwaJXWtD8w1cMkFkYzWw9infF.JPG) ![IMG_2331.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/palomap3/EnYSqxrAi5on9NtuqTtetNrKR4bAS4gjRw1qqz4YNfGV9iTtjQE1s4tFpnm9sYkJ66j.JPG) Instintivamente nos fuimos agrupando y terminamos formando una pequeña brigada de limpieza. Mientras dábamos un paseo un sendero natural al que dedicaré un post continuamos recogiendo aquí y allá, sobre todo colillas de cigarrillos y pedazos de plásticos. ![IMG_2353.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/palomap3/EpJYcaWFZb8Pdz1J9p921BHuf4zcUJkGrDyxYn1s4uhn11ECEFNgYUzTZg4Pb4gdruR.JPG) ![IMG_2362.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/palomap3/Eq5FzChfCYydrD4LG8ELMrWp2D7ecZqQbGGPwq38UbYh9Vrjse3tiHYA9AZKBTJ6pm8.JPG) A mitad de tarde volvimos a embarcar de regreso a Alicante, donde un rato después quedamos para cenar en [La Mala Buena](https://www.instagram.com/malabuenabar/?hl=es). Fuimos allí a propuesta de @godfish y me gustó un montón. Los chicos que lo llevan nos atendieron de maravilla, las empanadas que tomé estaban muy ricas y fue un broche de oro perfecto para un día intenso entre navegar, compartir momentos divertidos y caminar en un paraje de ensueño al que ya quiero regresar. Hasta la próxima publicación. Mientras tanto, ¡cuídate!

> Herramientas: Cámara iPhone 13 Pro, editor de fotos Mac. Mis publicaciones en [Worldmappin pinchando aquí](https://worldmappin.com/@palomap3) Si te gusta lo que publico, únete a mi [Fanbase pinchando aquí](https://hive.vote/dash.php?fan=palomap3&i=2) ![B67FB7A6-2E4B-43FD-BE20-57543B8993A2_4_5005_c.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/palomap3/23tmerjFT3bacskjaLCHwJcKiNucG1oEiEzj9BNLMfBBevvri9W4G7eDRveawxvcGY472.jpeg) ©️Copyright 2026 Paloma Peña Pérez. Todos los derechos reservados.

> Hi, dear hiver. I’ll continue with my account of what’s happened over the last few days. This time I’m writing from home, with the convenience of my computer rather than my mobile phone. I have hundreds of photos to go through, which will later form the basis for detailed posts about some of the experiences I’m telling you about today. ![IMG_2228.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/palomap3/EowJXVmpN6yGHPNYwEsS3GhBdYZBgsP3bkg8eBPivtfHAjJY4gqhunyN87QWKK8Ruwy.JPG) ![IMG_2230.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/palomap3/EogNJuVA837SoNByXpWNagRKT6SoMwvpZv2k1ap1TJMsSGBvT8zWwYAfpuKC6BKRSyX.JPG) I started the third day with this delicious breakfast at [Swallow Specialty Coffee](https://www.instagram.com/swallow_specialtycoffee/). I really liked the quiet, cosy atmosphere of this café and the service was unbeatable. From there we headed to the meeting point to walk together to the harbour. Before reaching the jetty, I stopped for a moment to take a photo of Alicante’s most famous promenade. ![IMG_2231.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/palomap3/EqFsWYpJM4H5tFVUa6cq1j9UxmcmtniEeNKoe9tUTZrfZdNKkbTcQFwrQ9nXUbPCbGW.JPG) ![IMG_2244.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/palomap3/Ep5nG9wKwQ6QAhnUfQ3QUfDDhk49QUif9jEYxYukW68weCndRZBzwnSW7fZTNzxxw4B.JPG) This image by @ninaeatshere sums up perfectly how we felt during the trip: thrilled to be out on the water and enjoying some stunning views. The wind did its best to muffle the sound of the boat’s engine, and our excitement at being out on the water meant the hour-long trip flew by. ![IMG_2255.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/palomap3/EqUdp94u8Kh2FsZwgToDYeaX6bqpfSxmtwq5rt5whG8CfvbUFy9QoWRPqWFQpiPYtz4.JPG) ![IMG_2267.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/palomap3/EqhQkLgHUp9Kydca34zVns6ZgkSCWYrfjeaoP5F5Fq79FT8bs9Uf5YRU8L4oSKa4qGB.JPG) ![IMG_2269.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/palomap3/Eq9Vo9qApJ55xF81Y5fKVvcYDQZRFCC1nEErwty6KPoYzmHxdbYVFjqKhCkDa4Nxkmi.JPG) Hivers disembarking on the island of Tabarca, eager to document what their eyes were seeing. The first thing we did was eat at the restaurant where we’d booked a table, and afterwards we had great fun playing a Trivia game organised by @ninaeatshere. ![IMG_2273.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/palomap3/Eq9WAML4fKn1YVpfFbyGmejrPSeyzUHzgRqoJKar7H37gvSSbPvFMsNFey3JAJiVAkG.JPG) This was my team; we came third – bronze medal! It was easy to achieve... as there were only three teams. 🤣 The important thing is that we had a laugh and learnt new things. From left to right: @juanmatrader @gissse @ninaeatshere @livinguktaiwan @edje @enraizar @sinochip @igormuba Paula @palomap3 and @ratona After this, we’d arranged to watch a video at the Nueva Tabarca Museum, but the person in charge of showing us round didn’t turn up. 🤷‍♀ That meant we had more time to take part in the next activity, the walk dedicated to the @cleanplanet initiative. ![IMG_2282.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/palomap3/EopvMeyooMdJZqN36dP6EkVbhC7cxYcLQy6DgjbKcjucojb89deFvHaxFzu63GyxNbQ.JPG) I teamed up with @ratona and, to be honest, it wasn’t easy to find any rubbish. We were surprised at how clean the island was, considering it’s a place dedicated almost exclusively to tourism and visited by so many people every day. ![IMG_2283.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/palomap3/EpGSCWirJfYSQxUDAKcXb7B8CW6YRjmXkUMzPAz8zyKjKixz2jz1km4aRmVQf7aJq5P.JPG) @igormuba and @edje hard at work. ![IMG_2286.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/palomap3/Eq9XG24g1B6U6ch64kQrJvgMfRzZZ1XRFEANxJ3hRN5UTqm1NctgoUGPhRKx48LHruy.JPG) @livinguktaiwan proudly showing off her catch. ![IMG_2287.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/palomap3/Eoc921sKNn67C9hiCGmLzfAMMgu2Wf3vNojjtVssxHzxhnMYC3k5EUQfp1cvhcr6zXq.JPG) New Hive members @gissse and @juanmatrader, along with their charming niece, tried their luck on the beach. Judging by the size of their bag, they were luckier than us. ![IMG_2330.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/palomap3/EnuiJmf2tYVBxNRNCT2YtupwDuY5VPicNkoVYH5T4CQwaJXWtD8w1cMkFkYzWw9infF.JPG) ![IMG_2331.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/palomap3/EnYSqxrAi5on9NtuqTtetNrKR4bAS4gjRw1qqz4YNfGV9iTtjQE1s4tFpnm9sYkJ66j.JPG) Instinctively, we started to gather together and ended up forming a small clean-up crew. Whilst we were walking along a nature trail – which I’ll be writing a post about – we kept picking up litter here and there, mainly cigarette butts and bits of plastic. ![IMG_2353.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/palomap3/EpJYcaWFZb8Pdz1J9p921BHuf4zcUJkGrDyxYn1s4uhn11ECEFNgYUzTZg4Pb4gdruR.JPG) ![IMG_2362.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/palomap3/Eq5FzChfCYydrD4LG8ELMrWp2D7ecZqQbGGPwq38UbYh9Vrjse3tiHYA9AZKBTJ6pm8.JPG) In the late afternoon, we boarded the ferry back to Alicante, where a little later we met up for dinner at [La Mala Buena](https://www.instagram.com/malabuenabar/?hl=es). We went there on @godfish’s recommendation and I loved it. The lads who run the place looked after us brilliantly, the empanadas I had were delicious, and it was the perfect finishing touch to a busy day of sailing, sharing fun moments and walking in a dreamlike setting that I already want to return to. Until the next post. In the meantime, take care! [//]:# (!worldmappin 38.16587 lat -0.47849 long d3scr)

></center>

title.title: \ndCrops: A Farming Game with an Uncertain Future\n
title.body:
/>

My screen

La versione in Italiano è subito dopo

In the world of Hive games, I’ve recently started my adventure as a farmer. I really enjoy it—having been a huge fan of FarmVille in the past, playing this felt like a natural choice.

However, lately I’ve been having doubts about how the game is being managed. The lack of information from the developers is making me question its future.

Missing Rewards
---------------

For a few days now, the game hasn't been updating rewards. With over 25,000 Crop Power, I should be receiving approximately 0.012 HIVE, but that isn't happening. I can understand synchronization delays, but this isn't the first time payments have been missed.

Investing in the Game
---------------------

I had big plans for this game, like acquiring more land and developing buildings. But how can I trust a platform that doesn't follow its own rules? Looking at the rankings, I see about a hundred players on average selling their harvests and staying active; this is a sign that the game isn't dead. Yet, it feels like the developers themselves no longer believe in it.

Potential Updates and a Possible Rebirth
----------------------------------------

There are so many ways this game could grow: new plants and seeds, more recipes to cook, or even the introduction of livestock management. In short, there are many development paths available, and I’m convinced that many former players would return—in fact, I’m sure it would attract plenty of new ones too.  
I’d love to hear your thoughts on this, and if possible, I would appreciate some direct information from the @@dCrops team.

Thanks for reading

Yours,  
Zumzulik

Versione italiano

Nel mondo dei giochi **hive** ho iniziato l’ avventura da contadino, mi diverte, poi, sono stato un appassionato di Farmville, e quindi, mi è venuto spontaneo giocarci.

Oggi però ho dei dubbi sulla gestione del gioco, poche informazioni da parte degli sviluppatori mi portano ad aver dubbi sul suo futuro.

Le ricompense mancanti
----------------------

È qualche giorno che il gioco non aggiorna le ricompense, avendo più di 25.000 crop power dovrei ricevere circa 0,012 hive, ma questo non succede.  
Capisco dei ritardi sulla sincronizzazione, ma non è la prima volta che mancano il pagamento.

Investire nel gioco
-------------------

Mi sono fatto dei programmi su questo gioco, tipo arrivare ad avere molti terreni e sviluppare le costruzioni, ma come posso fidarmi di una piattaforma che non rispetta le proprie regole. Nelle classifiche vedo che in media un centinaio di giocatori vendono i propri raccolti e continuano a giocare, segno che il gioco non è morto, però, sembra che siano gli sviluppatori a non crederci più.

Novità possibili e rinascita
----------------------------

Ci sono tante possibilità di far crescere ancora questo gioco, ad esempio, altre piante e semi, altri piatti da cucinare, ma anche un futuro con gestione di animali da fattoria. Insomma, ci sono molte strade di sviluppo e sono convinto che molti giocatori tornerebbero a giocare, anzi, sono sicuro che ci possano essere molti nuovi giocatori.

Mi piacerebbe sapere cosa ne pensate, ma vorrei anche, se possibile, qualche informazione direttamente da @dcrops .

Grazie di avermi letto

Il vostro  
Zumzulik
