title.title: Uninspired Motivations
title.body:
>

> What inspires you?

A friend and ex-colleague was recently on a work retreat \

for being one of the top sellers in the company, along with other top performers and of course, various management who had done very little. 60 employees and their plus-ones spent a week in the Virgin Islands at an exclusive resort for what he described as a *one in a lifetime* experience. He said that if he and his partner got away with a lunch under 200 dollars, he felt lucky. The rooms to the public were around 3000 dollars a night, meals and everything else were crazy expensive, and all this while the company is getting rid of people. 

> Typical.

---


![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/tarazkp/242DA8gDkJdq2hHnu3QnfknUPmPTdrhkmVLAxy4BN9hxgnb3CvJvh2wohi7SsioxHmccP.png)


---

At the end of the trip, the president of sales gave a very American speech about how the people back home aren't happy for them, are jealous, and next year they will be gunning to take their spot at the table etc. My friend (who is an American in Finland) was pretty uninspired by this call to competition, and the Finns were even less impressed. 

It is an interesting situation though, because what it highlighted is the difference between personal motivations, and how some people believe that the only inspiring factor is money. Sure, most people like to have money and more is better than less, but the majority of people are *not inspired* by making more money, especially when it is obvious that like this guy (who is part of the venture capital buyer group) benefits directly from it. His motivations are clear, but he hasn't put much thought into what inspires others. 

> A common problem for sure. 

For instance, I often write about various health improvement areas, because it is an area that both interests me and I am keen to develop myself in. Yet, while I wish more people would take their health seriously, I understand that many people aren't inspired by the journey to good health, even if they want healthy outcomes. Perhaps, for me it is important because I have spent so much of my life in ill-health, that I value the scarcity of good health. Perhaps it isn't important for others because they haven't yet experienced a huge amount of poor health. Or maybe it isn't because they are unable to connect the outcome they want strongly enough to motivate them to take the journey toward it. 

It is similar with most things I assume, where people who have never known what it is like to not have money, needn't focus their attention too much on making it. And perhaps as a result, they make it more easily because they are doing what they do to make money, engaging in the journey, not the destination. 

I have the opposite experience with health and money, where I have developed a scarcity mindset, so the outcome is important, and while I try to focus on the journey, it can get very difficult, because it is not where my true interest lays. But the journey requires investment, consistency, and adjustment. It needs to be taken seriously in the sense that it is these things we do, that lead to all the results we have. Because even though there is a lot of random interventions that can take place, the general trend is going to align to our general activity. 

## Is motivation important?

> **motivation** 
>/ˌməʊtɪˈveɪʃn/
>Motivation is the internal or external driving force that initiates, guides, and maintains goal-oriented behaviors. It is the process that fuels, directs, and sustains effort toward achieving a specific outcome, acting as the \

for actions. It includes activation (deciding to act), intensity (vigor of effort), and persistence (continuing despite obstacles).\n\nAs some one who has had the majority of theirs taken away in an unexpected medical event, *I believe so.* Yet it is also interesting, because while a lot of people want to \

of life, motivation can't be derived from the moment. Even though the actions are all performed in the moment, motivation requires a pressure from the past that pushes, or a gravity from the future that pulls. For it to be an internal force, it really has to be part of the process prior to the action. > Are you motivated? For many, I think motivation is a bit more like a passing infatuation, it doesn't last. It is the passion of attraction, but not enough to build the consistency that turns it into love. As they say, do something you love and you will never work a day in your life. But that is of course bullshit, because when you love something, you will work like a slave for it. When you are motivated to do the work consistently for something one loves, there is more than just the reward of accomplishment, but there is also the feeling of purpose. > Is purpose important? Again, I think so. I reckon a lot of the problems we have in the world today at the societal level are caused by a lack of *meaningful* purpose. People are chasing all kinds of things, but very little of it is truly relevant enough to make us feel part of something larger than ourselves in a way where we are advancing humanity. Most of it is instead adversarial, where people's meaning comes from being in a movement against something, rather than a series of actions that grow something. And I think this takes us back to the start, where the sales leader was trying to motivate people, but fell flat because he assumed their motivations. He expected that it is enough for them to feel purpose in making him richer, and themselves, for the potential of a fancy holiday for a few days. Nothing he said spoke to the growth of the individual needs, just money. Maybe that isn't his job to motivate people, but these days, when everyone just about is working to fulfil the dreams of an owner they will never meet, personal purpose is being lost. And a holiday doesn't make up for a life of meaningless activity. title.title: Hard work is mandatory to achieve success.
title.body: > ![1777457804672.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmR9gfTAtRFzDt5zUjMZ5zdKCBZqDqTQCSSLqVYenZdESB/1777457804672.jpg)[From My Facebook Profile](https://www.facebook.com/share/18WvPPfxvs/) This world cannot count how many people disappear in the pursuit of success. Even people who constantly work hard for success end up falling on the brink of success. Unless luck helps us, circumstances can never lead us to our destination. But it is also true that luck will help us when we strive for success. The Creator not only created humans and animals, but also the Creator of the earth and everything outside of it. Our destiny in this world is a kind of creation from the Creator's perspective. And this destiny has been created and determined for us, the present, future, and past are all written down. We do not have the power to change our written destiny. However, the Creator of this destiny has the power to change it. The funny thing is that fate is something that will take you to the edge even if you don't want it to. The constant effort we make to reach the threshold of success is a kind of path of destiny. Fate is the only way to make the path determined by fate and our life path easy or difficult. Basically, we move forward by taking fate as a sign, and perhaps at some point, after traversing various inaccessible paths, a better wheel of fate will emerge. All people who rely on luck may achieve success at some point. But one truth is that a person who relies on luck can never be lazy. Basically, a person who believes in fate becomes more determined and hardworking to move forward by believing in fate. And the hard work that people put into moving towards success, determined by fate, is essentially a reflection of fate. Life, death, success, achievement, everything is in the hands of the Creator. But God does not change our destiny until we want our destiny to change. That is, people want a change in fate when they want to achieve success through their tireless work. And it is through the hard work and perseverance that one puts in to achieve that success that the wheel of fortune is developed. This is basically the reality, may God help us. Thank you all...

title.body:
👑 The Kingdom and the Spirit of the Poor Girl

Long ago, in a forgotten land, there was a mighty kingdom ruled by a king and queen who lived in luxury while the poor suffered in silence.

Among the people was a poor girl, beautiful yet powerless, living with nothing but whispers of hidden strength said to run in her bloodline. One night, she was accused of sorcery and treachery. Without mercy, the rulers sentenced her to death.

Her blood spilled on the soil before the palace gates. That night, the skies darkened, the winds howled, and voices rose from the earth. The girl did not die as mortals do—her soul transformed into a vengeful spirit, a jinn bound by rage.

From that day, the kingdom was cursed. Each night, the spirit appeared in the royal palace, her eyes burning like fire, her voice echoing:
\

⚔️ Her Revenge

• The spirit haunted the king and queen, whispering in their dreams, forcing them to relive the moment of her unjust death.
• Soldiers heard phantom commands, their courage broken, until many fled the palace in terror.
• The spirit drained the life of those who had taken part in her execution—one by one, they vanished, leaving only silence behind.
• The palace itself began to crumble: walls shook, torches died without reason, and doors opened to shadows that swallowed men whole.

The once-great kingdom fell into ruin, abandoned by its people. And still, the legend says, the spirit of the poor girl roams the castle walls, waiting for the day she will finish her vengeance against all who thrive on cruelty and injustice.

title.title: Princess of the Sun [Solara]- Original artwork and Speed drawing Video
title.body:
Hi friends, I hope you’re doing well. Today I’m here to show you a drawing of this girl; I named her The Princess of the Sun. Her presence is always followed by the sun, illuminating her path wherever she goes.

In a kingdom plunged into eternal darkness, where sunlight was nothing more than a forgotten myth, there was a prophecy about a celestial figure destined to bring back the light. This figure was Solara, the Princess of the Sun.

One day, a young woman named Pilar, possessed of an indomitable spirit and a special connection with nature, began to have visions. She saw a radiant being, crowned with a diadem of gold and brilliant gems, sitting in a meditative pose. An aura of pure light enveloped her, and her presence radiated warmth and hope. Pilar knew it was Solara.

Following her visions, Pilar embarked on a journey toward Dawn Peak, the highest point in the kingdom. There, according to legend, lay the Temple of the Sun, hidden behind centuries of shadows. After an arduous journey, Pilar found the temple ruins and, inside, a stone altar with an ancient inscription.

Upon touching the inscription, the altar lit up, and the figure of Solara emerged from the stone, exactly as she appears in the drawing. Her beauty was celestial, and her expression serene and wise. Solara revealed to Pilar that she was not just a figure from the past, but the very essence of the sun, dormant and waiting for the right moment to be reborn.

Solara explained that the kingdom had been cursed by a dark entity that fed on despair. To break the curse, an act of pure faith was required. Pilar, with her heart full of hope and her unwavering belief in the prophecy, had been chosen to awaken Solara.

With Pilar’s help, Solara began to radiate her light throughout the entire kingdom. The darkness dissipated, and the fields burst into life. The people, awestruck and grateful, celebrated the return of light and the dawn of a new era of peace and prosperity.

Solara, the Princess of the Sun, became a symbol of hope and light for the entire realm, and Pilar, her guardian and friend, remained forever by her side, reminding the people that even in the darkest moments, the light will always prevail.

---

ESPAÑOL

Hola amigos, espero esten bien, hoy vengo a mostrarles un dibujo de esta chica, la llame la princesa del sol, su presencia siempre es seguida por el sol para iluminarla siempre en su camino. 

En un reino sumido en la oscuridad eterna, donde la luz del sol era solo un mito olvidado, existía una profecía sobre una figura celestial destinada a devolver la luz. Esta figura era Solara, la Princesa del Sol.

Un día, una joven llamada Pilar, de espíritu indomable y una conexión especial con la naturaleza, comenzó a tener visiones. Veía un ser radiante, coronado con una diadema de oro y gemas brillantes, sentada en una pose de meditación. Un aura de luz pura la envolvía, y su presencia irradiaba calor y esperanza. Pilar supo que era Solara.

Siguiendo sus visiones, pilar se embarcó en un viaje hacia el Pico del Amanecer, el lugar más alto del reino. Allí, según la leyenda, se encontraba el Templo del Sol, oculto tras siglos de sombras. Tras un arduo viaje, Pilar encontró las ruinas del templo y, en su interior, un altar de piedra con una inscripción antigua.

Al tocar la inscripción, el altar se iluminó, y la figura de Solara emergió de la piedra, exactamente como en el dibujo. Su belleza era celestial, y su expresión, serena y sabia. Solara le reveló a Pilar que ella no era solo una figura del pasado, sino la esencia misma del sol, latente y esperando el momento oportuno para renacer.

Solara explicó que el reino había sido maldecido por una entidad oscura que se alimentaba de la desesperanza. Para romper la maldición, se necesitaba un acto de fe pura. Pilar, con su corazón lleno de esperanza y su creencia inquebrantable en la profecía, había sido la elegida para despertar a Solara.

Con la ayuda de Pilar, Solara comenzó a irradiar su luz por todo el reino. La oscuridad se disipó, y los campos se llenaron de vida. El pueblo, asombrado y agradecido, celebró el regreso de la luz y el amanecer de una nueva era de paz y prosperidad.

Solara, la Princesa del Sol, se convirtió en un símbolo de esperanza y luz para todo el reino, y Pilar, su guardiana y amiga, siempre estuvo a su lado, recordando al pueblo que incluso en los momentos más oscuros, la luz siempre prevalecerá.

title.body:
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmXx5VZzmVMx9JPZUQjypTJUyvU5EMYP571B4a7v4JBFnA/foodologyllc_mother_8305922_640.jpg)
Fuente [Pixabay](https://pixabay.com/photos/mother-daughter-kitchen-bonding-8305922/)

---


🇪🇸 En Español

# Donde ella falta: lo que nunca dijo mi madre

---

A veces el amor no se dice.  
Se sirve en un plato… y se queda incompleto en otro.

---

Hola querida comunidad @holos-lotus,

Hay recuerdos que no llegan como imágenes claras, sino como preguntas que aparecen con los años.

Yo era pequeña durante el llamado “Período Especial” en Cuba. No conservo muchos detalles propios de aquella etapa, solo lo que he escuchado repetir: que fueron tiempos duros.

Aunque, siendo honesta, en este país los tiempos difíciles no han sido una excepción… sino una constante que se repite con distintos nombres.

Hoy, en medio de otra etapa marcada por la escasez —falta de corriente, de alimentos, de transporte— hay una pregunta que vuelve a mí con más fuerza que nunca:

> ¿cómo hizo mi madre para criarme en medio de todo eso?

---

## Lo que no vi entonces

No recuerdo el hambre como tal.

No recuerdo la angustia.

Pero ahora entiendo algo que en aquel momento era invisible para mí:

alguien estaba sosteniendo todo eso en silencio.

Alguien estaba resolviendo lo imposible para que yo no tuviera que enfrentarlo de frente.

---

## El gesto que lo explica todo

Hace no mucho, viviendo ya otra etapa de mi vida, ocurrió algo que me hizo entenderlo todo sin necesidad de explicaciones.

Mi madre me dijo, con total naturalidad:
“toma, ya te serví la comida”.

Fui a la cocina.

El plato estaba listo para mí.

Pero cuando miré con más atención, entendí algo que no estaba dicho: no había quedado nada para ella.

No fue un accidente.  
No fue descuido.

Fue una decisión.

---

## El sacrificio que no se anuncia

Ese tipo de gesto no se dice.

No se explica.

No se pone en palabras como sacrificio.

Se hace… y se normaliza.

Durante años, probablemente hizo lo mismo sin que yo lo notara.

Y como ocurre con muchas cosas importantes, lo esencial pasó desapercibido hasta que tuve edad suficiente para entenderlo.

---

## Cuando el amor aprende a ponerse límites

Hoy soy una mujer adulta.

Y aunque ese gesto sigue teniendo un valor inmenso para mí, ya no puedo aceptarlo de la misma manera.

Porque hay algo que también he aprendido:

el amor que cuida no debería desaparecerse a sí mismo.

Por eso ahora, cada vez que algo así ocurre, hago lo posible por cambiar la escena.

Busco que haya para ambas.

Y si no hay suficiente, entonces se comparte.

Pero en partes iguales.

Sin silencios.

Sin renuncias invisibles.

---

## Las madres que sostienen sin ser vistas

Hay una realidad que muchas veces no se nombra:

en contextos de crisis, las madres no solo cuidan… sostienen.

Sostienen la casa, la comida, la estabilidad emocional, la continuidad.

Sostienen incluso cuando no hay casi nada que sostener.

Y muchas veces lo hacen desde un lugar donde ellas quedan en último plano.

No porque alguien se lo imponga directamente.

Sino porque han aprendido a colocarse ahí, casi como una forma natural de amar.

---

## Lo que el cuerpo también guarda

Desde mi mirada como médica, hay algo que no puedo dejar de observar:

ese tipo de entrega constante, silenciosa y sostenida en el tiempo no desaparece sin dejar huella.

El cuerpo guarda.

El cansancio se acumula.

Las emociones que no se expresan buscan otras formas de salir.

Y muchas veces, cuando finalmente aparecen, ya vienen cargadas de años de silencio.

---

## Cuando celebremos… que también sepamos mirar

Por eso, cuando el próximo domingo celebremos el Día de las Madres, tal vez no se trate solo de flores, palabras bonitas o gestos visibles.

Tal vez también sea un momento para detenernos y mirar con más profundidad.

Para reconocer no solo lo que se ve… sino todo lo que quedó fuera del plato.

Todo lo que no se dijo.

Todo lo que se entregó sin testigos.

---

Porque hay amores que no se anuncian,  
pero sostienen vidas enteras.

Y quizás, el verdadero homenaje no esté solo en celebrar lo que hacen…

sino en aprender a no permitir que tengan que seguir haciéndolo solas.

---

Source [Pixabay](https://pixabay.com/photos/mother-daughter-kitchen-bonding-8305922/)

---

🇬🇧 In English

# Where She Is Missing: What My Mother Never Said

---

Sometimes love is not spoken.  
It is served on a plate… and left incomplete on another.

---

Hello dear @holos-lotus community,

There are memories that do not come as clear images, but as questions that emerge over time.

I was a child during what was known in Cuba as the “Special Period.” I do not remember much from those years, only what I have heard repeatedly: that they were difficult times.

Although, to be honest, in this country difficult times have not been the exception… but something that returns under different names.

Today, in the middle of another stage marked by scarcity—lack of electricity, food, transportation—one question comes back to me more strongly than ever:

> how did my mother manage to raise me in the middle of all that?

---

## What I could not see back then

I do not remember hunger itself.

I do not remember distress.

But now I understand something that was invisible to me at the time:

someone was silently holding everything together.

Someone was solving the unsolvable so that I would not have to face it directly.

---

## The gesture that explains everything

Not long ago, already in another stage of my life, something happened that made me understand everything without the need for explanations.

My mother said to me, naturally:
“here, your food is ready.”

I went to the kitchen.

The plate was there for me.

But when I looked more closely, I realized something unspoken: there was nothing left for her.

It was not an accident.  
It was not neglect.

It was a decision.

---

## The sacrifice that is never announced

That kind of gesture is never declared.

It is not explained.

It is not labeled as sacrifice.

It is simply done… and normalized.

For years, she probably did the same without me noticing.

And like many important things, the essential went unseen until I was old enough to understand it.

---

## When love learns to set limits

Today I am an adult woman.

And although that gesture still holds immense value for me, I can no longer accept it in the same way.

Because there is something I have also learned:

love that cares should not erase itself.

So now, whenever something like that happens, I try to change the scene.

I make sure there is enough for both of us.

And if there isn’t, then we share.

Equally.

Without silence.

Without invisible sacrifice.

---

## Mothers who sustain without being seen

There is a reality that is rarely spoken about:

in times of crisis, mothers do not just care… they sustain.

They sustain the home, the food, emotional stability, continuity.

They sustain even when there is almost nothing left to hold on to.

And many times, they do so from a place where they themselves come last.

Not because someone explicitly forces them.

But because they have learned to place themselves there, almost as a natural way of loving.

---

## What the body also keeps

From my perspective as a physician, there is something I cannot ignore:

this kind of constant, silent, long-term giving does not disappear without leaving a trace.

The body keeps it.

Fatigue accumulates.

Unexpressed emotions find other ways to surface.

And many times, when they finally appear, they come carrying years of silence.

---

## When we celebrate… may we also learn to see

So when we celebrate Mother’s Day next Sunday, perhaps it should not be only about flowers, kind words, or visible gestures.

Perhaps it should also be a moment to pause and look more deeply.

To recognize not only what is seen… but everything that was left off the plate.

Everything that was never said.

Everything that was given without witnesses.

---

Because there are forms of love that are never announced,  
yet they sustain entire lives.

And perhaps the truest tribute is not only to celebrate what they do…

but to learn not to let them keep doing it alone.

---

title.body:
Publicado en Español, Inglés y Portugués.


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmbPRvutiS24gXvxaVHerJhKJk4yufiw9agvaMYywzSHfk/1777980023439.jpg) *Editado en PhotoCollage*

Imagen de Pixabay 

[Fuente](https://pixabay.com/es/images/download/x-2084321_1920.jpg)


Un saludo Ladies.
Me interesa reflexionar sobre la primera pregunta de esta semana de @monachta.

Llevo veinte años con esa persona, todo ese tiempo amando hasta lo inexplicable. Y un día, en treinta y cinco segundos, el mundo se desvaneció.

Las razones que me dio fueron banas. Tan absurdas que nunca pude encontrarles una explicación loable. Pasé meses buscando, dándole vueltas a un por qué que no existía. Me culpé, sí, pero al mismo tiempo sabía que no era así. Que no todo era mío.

Romper esos lazos nos deshace. Porque cuando vives en pareja, en familia, en sociedad, no es solo un querer o no querer. Forma parte de tu vida, es imprescindible. Y arrancarlo de golpe es implacable con la cordura.

Pero un día decidí algo, asumirlo. Sin explicación. Sin justicia. Sin cierre bonito. Solo asumir que pasó y que no iba a entenderlo nunca. Ahí solté la preocupación. Ahí recuperé de a poco la tranquilidad.

Hoy soy libre, plena, feliz. No porque haya olvidado, sino porque entendí que amar no es prisión. Es dejar ir cuando toca y quedarte con la enseñanza clara y es que el amor verdadero no te ata, te libera. Y si no, no era amor. Era costumbre con nombre de sentimiento.


---
---

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmPioZKWPc3STML2a1iV8y8o3y7Ayv6wXZdNk6AeXJaENj/1758503903035.jpg)

---
---

# *ENGLISH*

---
---


Hello ladies.
I’d like to reflect on the first question of this week from @monachta.

I’ve been with that person for twenty years, loving even the inexplicable all that time. And one day, in thirty-five seconds, the world vanished.

The reasons they gave me were trivial. So absurd that I could never find a praiseworthy explanation. I spent months searching, turning over a \

that didn’t exist. I blamed myself, yes, but at the same time I knew it wasn’t like that. That not everything was mine to carry.

Breaking those bonds undoes us. Because when you live as a couple, in a family, in society, it’s not just a matter of wanting or not wanting. It’s part of your life, it’s essential. And tearing it away suddenly is merciless to your sanity.

But one day I decided something: to accept it. Without an explanation. Without justice. Without a nice closure. Just accept that it happened and that I was never going to understand it. That’s when I let go of the worry. That’s when I slowly regained my peace.

Today I am free, whole, happy. Not because I’ve forgotten, but because I understood that love is not a prison. It’s letting go when it’s time and keeping the clear lesson: true love does not tie you down, it sets you free. And if it doesn’t, then it wasn’t love. It was habit with a feeling’s name.

---
---

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmPioZKWPc3STML2a1iV8y8o3y7Ayv6wXZdNk6AeXJaENj/1758503903035.jpg)

---
---

# *PORTUGUÉS*

---
---

Olá, ladies.
Tenho interesse em refletir sobre a primeira pergunta desta semana da @monachta.

Estou há vinte anos com essa pessoa, todo esse tempo amando até o inexplicável. E um dia, em trinta e cinco segundos, o mundo desapareceu.

As razões que ela me deu foram banais. Tão absurdas que nunca consegui encontrar uma explicação louvável. Passei meses procurando, remoendo um porquê que não existia. Culpei-me, sim, mas ao mesmo tempo sabia que não era assim. Que nem tudo era meu.

Romper esses laços nos desfaz. Porque quando se vive em casal, em família, em sociedade, não é só um querer ou não querer. Faz parte da sua vida, é imprescindível. E arrancá-lo de repente é implacável com a sanidade.

Mas um dia decidi algo: assumir isso. Sem explicação. Sem justiça. Sem um final bonito. Apenas assumir que aconteceu e que eu nunca iria entender. Aí soltei a preocupação. Aí recuperei aos poucos a tranquilidade.

Hoje sou livre, plena, feliz. Não porque esqueci, mas porque entendi que amar não é prisão. É deixar ir quando é hora e ficar com o ensinamento claro: o amor verdadeiro não te prende, te liberta. E se não, não era amor. Era costume com nome de sentimento.

---
---


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmcAhAKwyNZZUJMUA7vdruF54aTShX8Mq1ZCs7xYD3C5Sp/1758337351053.jpg)

---

title.title: Polish Hive Power Report March 2k26
title.body: >\n\nPrzepraszam Was podwójnie bo post nie dość, że spóźniony to jeszcze w ogóle nie na temat. Pewnie większość z Was pomyślała po kolejnej obniżce APR na HBD 'OK, te 1514% i tak było nie do utrzymania w dłuższej perspektywie czasu, a teraz dobro całego systemu wymaga, żeby obniżyć, bo inaczej Hive się zawali'. Prawda? No problem w tym, że to gówno prawda. Mam wrażenie, że Hive stało się odbiciem naszego kraju, gdzie Jaśnie Państwo w obronie swoich przywilejów dowaliło podatki i inne utrudnienia klasie średniej, która dodatkowo obrywa również inflacją. Dlaczego jestem zły? Bo obniżenie APR dotyka między innymi mnie, ale rozumiem, że to jest działanie podjęte w celu ochrony systemu. Przy czym, chciałbym zwrócić uwagę na pewien fakt - **NAJWIĘKSZYM ŹRÓDŁEM DODATKOWEJ INFLACJI HIVE JEST DHF**. I bulwersujące jest to, że nic z tym nie zostało zrobione. **Proposal, który wyda HBD na Hive i je spali potrzebny na wczoraj!** W zeszłym miesiącu pisałem *Moim zdaniem to system należy unowocześnić, bo spójrzcie realnie kto zainwestuje, albo będzie trzymać Hive, czy HivePower jeśli inflacja tego tokena wynosi 12.71% (YoY) a w DHF znajduje się jeszcze 20 milionów HBD gotowych do konwersji na Hive. Oczywiście poza wariatami. (...) Czy naprawdę problemem są użytkownicy, czy może jednak to, że w ciągu miesiąca do gospodarki trafia 10 milionów Hive a spala się 10 tysięcy...* I wiecie co? Jest jeszcze gorzej, inflacja wzrosła do 13,51% (YoY), a będzie jeszcze gorzej. Jeżeli nie burn proposal, to może przynajmniej zmuszenie beneficjentów DHF, żeby zamiast konwertować otrzymywane środki kupowali Hive na rynku wewnętrznym albo przynajmniej skorzystali z Magi (hue hue o ile będzie w ogóle działać). W każdym razie, sama zmiana APR bez zmiany dotyczącej DHF nie przyniesie oczekiwanych skutków i w dalszym ciągu będziemy poruszać się po linii pochyłej do końca Hive - Dlatego odwołuje się do polskiego przysłowia, zgodnie z którym \

- DHF zawinił APR HBD zmniejszyli. > I owe you a double apology, because not only is this post late, it’s also completely off-topic. Most of you probably thought after the latest APR cut on HBD: *“OK, 15.14% was unsustainable in the long run anyway, and now the good of the entire system requires a reduction, otherwise Hive will collapse.”* Right? Well, the problem is—that’s complete bullshit. I get the impression that Hive has become a reflection of our country, where the “nobility,” in defense of their privileges, has piled taxes and other burdens onto the middle class, which is already getting hit by inflation. Why am I angry? Because the APR cut affects, among others, me—but I understand that it’s an action taken to protect the system. However, I’d like to point out one fact: **THE BIGGEST SOURCE OF ADDITIONAL HIVE INFLATION IS THE DHF.** And it’s outrageous that nothing has been done about it. **A proposal that spends HBD on Hive and burns it is needed yesterday!** Last month I wrote: *“In my opinion, the system needs modernization, because realistically—who is going to invest in or hold Hive or Hive Power if the token’s inflation is 12.71% (YoY), and there are still 20 million HBD in the DHF ready to be converted into Hive? Obviously, no one except lunatics. (...) Is the real problem the users, or the fact that 10 million Hive enters the economy every month while only 10 thousand is burned...?”* And you know what? It’s even worse now— inflation has risen to 13.51% (YoY), and it will get worse. If not a burn proposal, then at least force DHF beneficiaries to buy Hive on the internal market instead of converting the funds they receive—or at the very least use Magi (lol, assuming it even works). In any case, changing APR alone, without addressing the DHF, will not bring the expected results. We will continue sliding downwards toward Hive’s eventual decline. Which is why I’ll invoke a Polish proverb: *“The blacksmith sinned, and the gypsy was hanged.”* The DHF is at fault, but HBD APR gets cut. ![Gemini_Generated_Image_hz923xhz923xhz92.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/polish.hive/23ynWxWx1SPPQervGGqC7GKGpKz4PYCeVgAhXdBsUAw7t6sMEHzGHzT8mr8WK4kTLsQwy.jpg)

title.body: The auto vs quartz debate is old. Mechanical watches have soul but cost more and need upkeep. Quartz is accurate and low maintenance. Either way, prices change. I keep an eye on [Watch Prices](https://watchpolice.com/watches/price-change) because microbrands raise or drop prices all the time. I ended up with a quartz daily beater and one automatic for weekends. No regrets. Just don't overpay. Watch the market and buy smart. Both are fine if the price is right.

title.title: Brutal Fight At Underground Bar.
title.body:
[![](https://images.3speak.tv/images/1777980263496-e244bcf1c0259c59.webp)](https://3speak.tv/watch?v=yakubnoyon/c6948dda)

▶️ [Watch on 3Speak](https://3speak.tv/watch?v=yakubnoyon/c6948dda)


---

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmVRPJo7n5jhe44xkdojaJzLNcPjUuQhhXyJXEuyr8qfVr/gaming_photography_2_.gif)

The journey to save Commissioner Gordon continues. Batman reached the downside of the fan but the switch of the fan wasn't there. That means he had to search deep inside the building. He climbed up a broken wall and got inside.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmbu36iY7U98ybPVVJh9xs7iWZrEYSMH9UUKSbKdu4En1W/snapshot.png)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmbCxV8BNX9S4tWSFeUryfWYUkSpMN8utyUx8L1MJj9sLr/snapshot_1.png)

He saw some soldiers waiting at that place for him. Batman was thinking of a fight but suddenly he noticed something. Those soldiers were standing on a wet floor. If he powered up the generator, those soldiers would be electrocuted and killed. So he used that trick and he didn't have to fight with them at all.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmQY6ok5QFqt18NaeSsqUWfsdkAio6dA7SKMQFseCJCGSm/snapshot_2.png)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmRgUrXSEb8megRo68hg5pUPjEcChT78K77aN3vh9fM8No/snapshot_3.png)

Then using an elevator, Batman went deeper inside the underground area where he found a huge group of soldiers gathered in a place and waiting for him. There were a lot of soldiers with different types of weapons and powers. The fight wasn't going to be easy.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmaqFAF5dNbirQNMdn5XjdDZdciFJSfsaKtHKQKPDG3Mvt/snapshot_4.png)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmUHatjTAsGz6xBfUYZcso9j94ERTFmsrDQ6vhFR364GP3/snapshot_5.png)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmTvXAGr6Gymt6qrdgwQJz2AG2HxDB3zAzP6CUbaRkEson/snapshot_6.png)

First Batman had to take down their leader because he was wearing an explosive vest. He blew that, everyone here will die. So silently Batman reached into his back and disabled the vest first.

After the main threat was gone, Batman started to fight with the other soldiers. It was getting harder with all those soldiers attacking him. Some were firing at him, some had an electric stick in their hand, the situation was kind of out of control.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmW6TzNN4MjH7gJFk974Cvg2Th9HcytTRb3cczoX55Nx8f/snapshot_7.png)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmdSkS7mGzV5XDzrtBL99hEBeAnUjYR4wEcZxkwPkZcUV8/snapshot_8.png)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmShTPGxr6Q3S7nztP8TdAtBG49criBXpGKMiNt2ArbvSc/snapshot_9.png)

But Batman found a way. dropped a smoke bomb to blind the closer soldiers and then he targeted the soldier with a gun. He knocked those gan men first because they were keeping a distance and kept shooting at him. After that he went for the other soldiers, knocked them out using the battering. His move was fast and unstoppable, so all those soldiers couldn't keep up with him.

I saw new soldiers in this group who worked as doctors or something. Batman knocked down soldiers and the enemy was recovering all those knocked out soldiers. It was very annoying but Batman realized that after a long period. That's why this fight long time to finish.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmRiPfLyU8uFwU38RDw98MUg8FPFHn6dS5AHjo8TwGMVFX/snapshot_10.png)

Batman had to find the switch to stop the fan so that he could bring his Batmobile down. He opened a new gate that led him to another floor. Let's see what is waiting for him.

---

* **Thank you for reading. See you all on my next blog.**

---

---

▶️ [3Speak](https://3speak.tv/watch?v=yakubnoyon/c6948dda)

title.body: > Hola a todos los que me acompañan en mis posts; qué genial que hayamos visitado esta zona de la costa para hacer las fotografías de reflejos para participar de esta maravillosa <a href=\

> ¨ShadowHunterscontest¨: Es increíble cómo pasan los meses de rápido, y las estaciones cambian; en pocas semanas estaremos disfrutando del invierno, pero este verano pasó tan rápido que no he tenido el tiempo de publicar todas las fotografías que hemos hecho.
> Hello to all those who accompany me in my posts; How great that we visited this area of the coast to take the reflection photos to participate in this wonderful <a href=\

> ¨ShadowHunterscontest¨: It's incredible how quickly the months go by, and the seasons change; in a few weeks we'll be enjoying winter, but this summer went by so fast that I haven't had time to publish all the photos we've taken.

title.title: 和朋友去看车
title.body:
话说和朋友逛完劳动公园以及仙女湖公园并美美地饱餐一顿苏氏牛肉面之后，他们要去看车。

![20260502_152002.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmcqsjxDs7ZXAMwUsE4JCLGXBdUPeeQ22A7Kb3JLr7S4Mp/20260502_152002.jpg)

虽然我又累又困，但是还能怎么办，只能舍命陪君子喽，哎，感觉自己上了贼船。

其实我对看车也不感兴趣，早些年还对牧马人罗宾汉长草，但是这些年已经提不起兴趣啦。

现在正在开的车，虽然有些老，但是由于没咋跑，公里数低的可怜，才不到五万公里，也就是别人一年跑的里程数。

大概是因为跑得少，我感觉现在的车子开起来还是十分顺滑的，又因为这几年钱包紧张，暂时没有换车的计划了。

而且我还是更倾向于油车，或者换电车的话，我大概会选特斯拉吧，其它的车，让我感觉眼花缭乱的，有些接受不了。

北二路是沈阳4S店集中之处，宜家和星摩尔也在这里
![20260502_150645.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmURxZsAzwky9ZvDq7Ytqaytb1d2ir5dkEqNBg4co1gPUr/20260502_150645.jpg)

总觉得宜家的这个配色还是很有特点的
![20260502_150748.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmRpziw49jUh4cBBh9Q7eQ1W2wtpNvdKkaaDVS752Q9eF4/20260502_150748.jpg)

除了宜家、星摩尔、红星美凯龙，道路两边都是4S店
![20260502_151117.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmYyjtMHemVvRvmtcYWy1LVh8o4VQFnHk5NmEL6c7zwe5q/20260502_151117.jpg)

星摩尔
![20260502_151701.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmatWEGzbZoZCcrLiVid8oZCW75ZMoQyc2U9QNjCu9DSAT/20260502_151701.jpg)

方程豹的展厅（对面是长城炮，哈哈）
![20260502_151910.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmZiz9dxhdwc46aMwrYgHKF49jKVgAGBBsVw7HeVZYrdDx/20260502_151910.jpg)

这车看起来还不错
![20260502_152002.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmcqsjxDs7ZXAMwUsE4JCLGXBdUPeeQ22A7Kb3JLr7S4Mp/20260502_152002.jpg)

随便看看拍拍
![20260502_152018.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmWnfLVwAagRoodTzhSRaiqcJBdy52h7sxo1odH5tmRX1g/20260502_152018.jpg)

拍一下侧颜

![20260502_154904.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmTF5cnPkWEryLD9FgRXg7tiJFf7yRGVwfMvcbxm5G7PDn/20260502_154904.jpg)

这车颜值也能大，适合小女孩开
![20260502_155157.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmPEQse7nJ9GuToWLT7AZZ8aD9Z1zif4fmoP88vcb2dSnv/20260502_155157.jpg)

这个也不错
![20260502_155217.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmQVSuqHSn5tw7YfUP8R7DYdPGRHGqJseNnByY33FS7kV9/20260502_155217.jpg)

拍拍这小车的正脸
![20260502_155230.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmeRp7zLKhf1S5sXjH7gLDCBj6sDzZjh7MCftJwzXyzR26/20260502_155230.jpg)

大众4S店
![20260502_155612.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmSyEPEqHf2HuioTY5RedMhp8aMT3mPjuq3CjG1Uh8axH6/20260502_155612.jpg)

零跑汽车
![20260502_155909.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmWXa3mcamMwMTo4qZV7BH5qViaWEpGt5hfHMvgoQfvV3n/20260502_155909.jpg)

小车都不错
![20260502_155944.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmNqwXG7y2wAVaVhjA2K1uoahyDxRQPL4qRt7PNwVozsaZ/20260502_155944.jpg)

我坐着休息一会
![20260502_160026.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmXoGkRUhtrw9PGAQwAARm8QgVbTJxFFt7wFxXXPsHz18z/20260502_160026.jpg)

话说坐着的时候有美女过来问我们想喝什么饮料，有咖啡、玉米汁、西瓜汁类的可选，我们说不喝，美女说免费的，但是都不喝，哈哈哈，美女好气。

朋友们还想要试驾，我实在是困得睁不开眼睛，就打车回家啦。朋友们选择继续去逛万达、看电影，我真是羡慕他们的体力呀。

title.title: Un buen trato marca la diferencia/ Letras Inspiradoras: Cuando el buen trato es la excepción [ESP/ENG]
title.body: > Hola queridas amigas de @Womentribe, saludos y bendiciones, en esta ocasión vengo para participar en la [Iniciativa](https://peakd.com/hive-139925/@syllem/letras-inspiradoras-cuando-el-buen) de @syllem, un gusto invitar a @yaslenysofia a particpar. --- ![REVIEW (1).jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/yasmarit/23ywkfH7emx2jjfB5FEVuRXvMwY8AuzE84zbFo99NtMAzJSxeAn7pWrmNBQZsGVpR3pXa.jpg) **Diseño en CANVA** ---

>Hablando de buenos tratos a los clientes, ciertamente el simple hecho de vender no es suficiente, ya que ir a un lugar que aunque te vendan a buen precio o tengan el servicio a una buena comodidad, el trato sea como sea es importante, no solo porque te anima a regresar, sino porque mientras estas en el lugar te sientes cómodo en lo que estas comprando o esperando para ser atendido si es un servicio, en mi caso he pasado por experiencias buenas como otras no tanto, ya que así como he tenido personas que desde que entras hasta que sales de tu negocio te atienden o ven lo que necesitas, hasta te dan sugerencias, todo para que estés lo más cómodamente, así mismo he tenido lugares que cuando entras con su simple cara de bueno de pocos amigos definitivamente te desanima a estar ahí. ![separadoryasma1.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/yasmarit/23tRzwswFj7sdCJKFgW2jsAWvCyEzuv6zxT8pCrVwXa8ePqRSdQWi3P6ZbtsyGmy6y4G2.png)

>Claro entendemos que todos tenemos problemas, a veces no nos sentimos bien sea que estemos enfermos o en el caso de las mujeres tenemos malestar de la menstruación, pero ante los demás hay que mostrar la mejor cara, tener las ansias de prestar el mejor servicio o apoyo para vender lo que se está ofreciendo, porque eso a la final ayuda a que las cosas fluyan mejor y las personas como dije antes quieran regresar, es por ello que decir de que si me sorprender cuando alguien me atiende bien, bueno no realmente porque en realidad eso es lo que espero ya que siempre pienso que atender al público correctamente es la clave para que el negocio surja y se mantenga, ciertamente es muy importante y necesario tener en cuenta. --- ![pexels-apples-1841132_1920.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/yasmarit/23vsWzAZ8cKBfYpkHdRrwdPBGFjyh9aFAtZykaErFeeXSwKLb9g1WGAtTVq56jB6CE3eo.jpg) [Fuente](https://pixabay.com/es/images/download/x-1841132_1920.jpg) ---

>Lo que más me sorprende es cuando el trato no es el adecuado jeje, porque pienso que así como quieren que el cliente regrese o que sus ventas florezca, ciertamente difícil ps, quizás buenos algunos por sus precios ok dirán bueno me importa más ello que el trato, pero a la final puede resultar malo para el propietario del negocio porque tantas ofertas con algunos clientes viendo que no puede aumentar porque eso es lo único que atrae a los clientes ps no resulta del todo beneficioso, pienso que ambas cosas deben trabajar en conjunto, ofrecer buenos productos y servicios pero también tratar bien a sus clientes, mostrar un ambiente agradable, capaz de hacer sentir la comodidad y las ganas de querer regresar, es necesario que eso vaya de la mano, porque no hay como ir a un lugar que hasta te pueden aconsejar de lo que estas recibiendo como ofrecer algo de buena calidad. ![separadoryasma1.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/yasmarit/23tRzwswFj7sdCJKFgW2jsAWvCyEzuv6zxT8pCrVwXa8ePqRSdQWi3P6ZbtsyGmy6y4G2.png)

> **Muchas gracias por leerlo. Espero sea de su agrado. Cualquier comentario con gusto estaré para responder y si quieren saber más de mi les dejo mis:**
![EL FINAL DE POSTHIVE (1).jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/yasmarit/23tmBcG1dhAWXHSeTXHGahwcGe8eAbcEpZutQrCnSNiXxDwJJ31QA17giTgLpxPgJtEqN.jpg)
![separadoryasma1.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/yasmarit/23tRzwswFj7sdCJKFgW2jsAWvCyEzuv6zxT8pCrVwXa8ePqRSdQWi3P6ZbtsyGmy6y4G2.png) **ENGLISH**

> Hello, dear friends of @Womentribe Greetings and blessings. Today I’m here to take part in the [Initiative](https://peakd.com/hive-139925/@syllem/letras-inspiradoras-cuando-el-buen) From @syllem, it's a pleasure to invite @yaslenysofia to join us. --- ![REVIEW (2).jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/yasmarit/23ywkfH7emx2jjfB5FEVuRXuuCscpEza8ckE6TifnSZCJtamfrrmoyXEQSb9PkEpP5Csz.jpg) **Design in CANVA** ---

>Speaking of good customer service, simply making a sale isn’t enough. Even if a place offers good prices or convenient service, the way you’re treated matters—not just because it encourages you to come back, but because while you’re there, you feel comfortable with what you’re buying or, if it’s a service, while you’re waiting to be attended to. In my case, I’ve had some good experiences and others not so good. Just as I’ve encountered people who, from the moment you walk in until you leave, attend to you, see what you need, and even offer suggestions—all to make you as comfortable as possible—I’ve also been to places where, the moment you walk in, their unfriendly, unwelcoming demeanor definitely discourages you from staying there. ![separadoryasma1.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/yasmarit/23tRzwswFj7sdCJKFgW2jsAWvCyEzuv6zxT8pCrVwXa8ePqRSdQWi3P6ZbtsyGmy6y4G2.png)

>Of course, we understand that we all have problems; sometimes we don’t feel well—whether we’re sick or, in the case of women, experiencing menstrual discomfort— but in front of others, we have to put our best foot forward, be eager to provide the best service or support to sell what’s being offered, because in the end that helps things run more smoothly and, as I said before, makes people want to come back. That’s why I’d say that yes, I’m surprised when someone treats me well, well, not really, because that’s actually what I expect—since I always believe that serving the public properly is the key to a business thriving and staying afloat. It’s certainly very important and necessary to keep in mind. --- ![pexels-apples-1841132_1920.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/yasmarit/23vsWzAZ8cKBfYpkHdRrwdPBGFjyh9aFAtZykaErFeeXSwKLb9g1WGAtTVq56jB6CE3eo.jpg) [Source](https://pixabay.com/es/images/download/x-1841132_1920.jpg) ---

>What surprises me the most is when the treatment is not adequate hehe, because I think that just as they want the customer to return or for their sales to flourish, it is certainly difficult ps, maybe good, some because of their prices ok will say well I care more about that than the treatment, but in the end it can be bad for the business owner because so many offers with some clients seeing that they cannot increase because that is the only thing that attracts customers ps it is not entirely beneficial, I think that both things must work together, offer good products and services but also treat them well to their clients, showing a pleasant atmosphere, capable of making them feel comfortable and wanting to return, it is necessary that this goes hand in hand, because there is no way to go to a place that can even advise you on what you are receiving, such as offering something of good quality. ![separadoryasma1.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/yasmarit/23tRzwswFj7sdCJKFgW2jsAWvCyEzuv6zxT8pCrVwXa8ePqRSdQWi3P6ZbtsyGmy6y4G2.png)

> **Thank you very much for reading it. I hope you like it. I will be happy to respond to any comments and if you want to know more about me, I leave you my:**

title.title: Are we Financially responsible to other people? // MCGI TOPIC REVIEW
title.body:
https://youtu.be/aHC7rhMHhZc?si=uuXHOKLWSsrbdseM

All of our possessions are gifts from God. If God didn't provide us with the means to accomplish anything, we couldn't. We are fortunate to be able to bless others. The purpose of God's financial blessings is not to raise our level of living but rather to raise our standard of giving. 

Unfortunately, however, many people make mistakes. We should assist others in every way we can. People ought to gain from us. We shouldn't have to focus solely on ourselves. God's word commands us to love our neighbours as much as we love ourselves. When we have this kind of mentality we won't think twice before we help people.
‎

***

水煮牛肉是一道令人垂涎欲滴的川菜，鲜嫩的牛肉在热气腾腾的汤底中煮制，吸收了浓郁的香辣味道。每一口都是肉质的鲜美与香料的碰撞，辣味恰到好处，令人回味无穷。特别是那一层红油，融入每一片牛肉，提升了整道菜的风味，让人忍不住一口接一口。无论是寒冷的冬天，还是与朋友团聚的时刻，水煮牛肉总能带来温暖与满足！

***

title.title: 오늘은 마지막(?) 어린이날!
title.body: 자라면서 서운(?) 했던 몇번의 순간들이 있었습니다. 그 첫번째가 중학생이 되면서 어린이날에 소외(?) 된 존재가 되었다는 사실이었습니다. 공휴일이어서 학교에 가지는 않았지만 그래도 뭔가 아쉽고 서운하고.. 그런 느낌이었습니다. 난 아직은 어린이라고 생각되는데 중학생이라고 해서 학교에서나 집에서 더 큰 기대도 하고 중학생답게 라는 말을 듣곤 했는데 왠지 모를 부담이 있었던 것 같습니다. 2년전 첫째가 6학년 이었을 때, 어린이날을 맞으면서 제가 경험했던 얘기들을 해주면서 우리는 어린이날을 막내가 중학생이 되기 전까지 함께 어린이날을 보내자고 했었습니다. 그리고 오늘은 막내가 6학년이니, 저희 아이들이 마지막(?)으로 보내는 어린이날 입니다. 지난주 노동절부터 오늘까지 아이들은 연휴입니다. 저는... 오늘만 빼고는 매일 출근을 했었지만요.. 그래서(?) 어제 아내가 아이들을 데리고 집에서 멀지 않은 헬로키티에 다녀왔습니다.
/> 제주시에 오고가는 길목에 있는 곳이어서 항상 궁금하긴 했었거든요. 입장료도 입장료지만, 이런 곳에 가면 소품으로 사는 즐거움(?)이 있어서 조금은 부담스럽지만 그래도 마지막(?) 어린이날이니!

/>

아빠 없이 세자매(?)가 너무 신나게 놀고 왔습니다.  
그래서 오늘은 아무곳도 안나가고 집콕했구요.. ㅠ

이젠 저도 다음 어린이날은 손주 볼때까지 기다려야 하나요? ㅠ

title.title: Television Review: Three Sundays (Mad Men, S3x04, 2008)
title.body:
![(source:tmdb.org)](https://image.tmdb.org/t/p/original/hGbNZ6sGJoVJQt0Jy7pm67J5oar.jpg)


**Three Sundays (S2x04)**

Airdate: 17 August 2008

Written by: Andre Jacquemott & Maria Jacquemott
Directed by: Tim Hunter

Running Time: 48 minutes



The structural rhythm of *Mad Men* has often been described as episodic vignette, a series of finely observed “day in the life” slices that advance the overarching plot with deliberate, often glacial, slowness. Each episode typically confines itself to a narrow temporal window, deepening character through mundane ritual and subtle interaction rather than through sweeping narrative leaps. *Three Sundays*, the fourth episode of the second season, represents a slight but significant deviation from this established pattern. As the title overtly signals, the episode’s plot is spread across three consecutive Sundays—Passion Sunday, Palm Sunday, and Easter Sunday—encompassing the period between 8 April and 22 April 1962. This tripartite structure allows the writers, Andre and Maria Jacquemetton, to trace the gradual accumulation of pressure and revelation in their characters’ lives with a novel sense of weekly ritual, using the Christian liturgical calendar as both a narrative scaffold and a potent source of thematic resonance.

The choice of Eastertide is far from incidental; it ensures that questions of faith, guilt, redemption, and resurrection permeate the storylines. The episode is bookended by the high holy days of Christianity, and the script deftly explores how these abstract concepts collide with the messy, secular realities of early 1960s America. The most explicit engagement with faith is found in the storyline centred on Peggy Olson. Visiting her devoutly Catholic family for Sunday dinner, Peggy is pressured into attending Mass, an experience that visibly discomforts her. Her flight from the service—feigning illness—leads her to a chance encounter outside the church with Father Gill (Colin Hanks), a young, tall, and disarmingly handsome priest. In a beautifully ironic twist, his earnest, unintentionally charismatic presence inadvertently draws her back into the fold, setting in motion a complex dynamic that blends spiritual guidance with unspoken attraction and professional exchange.

Father Gill’s subsequent visit to the Olson home, where he learns of Peggy’s career as a copywriter on Madison Avenue, allows the episode to forge a fascinating connection between the pulpit and the pitch meeting. He recruits her to help craft his Palm Sunday sermon, a request that Peggy, ever eager to prove her utility and perhaps intrigued by the priest, accepts. This collaboration culminates in one of the episode’s most quietly devastating moments: during confession, Peggy’s sister Anita confesses to Father Gill that she “hates” Peggy. Anita, who has followed the traditional path of marriage and motherhood, seethes with resentment that Peggy, who bore a child out of wedlock, has simply abandoned that life for a career and acts like nothing happened. The Church, traditionally a bastion of the very morality Anita embodies, is here represented by a priest who is not a figure of judgement but of confused, slightly hip compassion. His final gesture—giving Peggy a painted Easter egg “for the little one” on Easter Sunday—is a masterpiece of ambiguous kindness. It is both a recognition of her secret and a gentle, painful reminder of the life she has chosen to suppress, highlighting the impossible gap between her modern aspirations and her family’s (and faith’s) traditional expectations.

Whilst Peggy grapples with the personal implications of faith and family, Don Draper  is embroiled in a professional crisis that mirrors the episode’s themes of disaster and forced resurrection. Sterling Cooper is tasked with salvaging the American Airlines account after a recent, devastating air crash. The assignment is a public relations nightmare, and the pressure is ratcheted up when Duck Phillips  informs Don that the airline wants concepts before Easter. This forces Don to summon his creative team for an emergency meeting on Palm Sunday—a violation of the Sabbath that underscores the agency’s secular devotion to commerce. The scenes of the team working in a near-deserted office are among the episode’s most striking visual departures; the men, usually icons of tailored perfection, are dressed in casual sweaters, slacks, and even shorts, creating a comical yet revealing contrast. Their dishabille mirrors their mental state—stripped of their professional armour, they are forced to think rawly. Don’s solution, when it comes, is pure Draper alchemy: to ignore the disaster entirely and pitch a future-oriented campaign asking “what 1963 will look like.” It is an act of audacious denial, a secular form of resurrection. Yet, in a cruel twist of corporate fate, Don’s perfect pitch is rendered useless when Duck reveals that Shel Keneally, their key contact at American Airlines, has been fired. The executives will attend the meeting merely out of courtesy. Don’s creative resurrection is stillborn, and his bitter reaction contrasts sharply with Roger Sterling’s world-weary consolation that “these things happen.”

Don’s professional frustration is expertly paralleled with his domestic turmoil. Most of this stems from his five-year-old son, Bobby (now played by Aaron Hart), whose childish irresponsibility causes minor but resonant chaos. Betty, overwhelmed and increasingly detached, demands that Don discipline his son. Don’s refusal, and his subsequent, raw admission to Betty, provides one of the season’s most poignant character insights: he confesses that he was savagely beaten by his own father and cannot bring himself to replicate that violence. This moment fractures the façade of Don as the omnipotent patriarch, revealing the traumatised child within who is desperately trying to forge a different, better fatherhood—even if he has no model for how to do so.

The episode’s focus on these two major arcs is disciplined, but it allows minor storylines to weave through the narrative with natural ease. Bobbie Barrett appears at Don’s office, using a flimsy business pretext to reignite their affair, highlighting Don’s continued moral drift. More notably, Roger Sterling, preoccupied with his daughter’s upcoming wedding, encounters a call girl named Vicky (Marguerite Moreau) in a hotel bar. Impressed by her brazen resourcefulness (she poses as a client’s wife to dine in a restaurant), he hires her services. In a telling moment of self-rationalisation, Roger tells Vicky he hasn’t been with a prostitute since his Navy days, framing this transaction as a tidier, less emotionally fraught alternative to an affair. It’s a sad, funny commentary on the compartmentalisation of his life, and the actor John Slattery delivers the line with perfectly dry irony, especially when Vicky dismisses his health concerns by stating “nobody ever died doing this,” prompting Roger’s wry smile at the memory of his own near-fatal heart attack.

The episode’s strength lies in this nuanced, structurally sound scripting and its acute sensitivity to the cultural shifts of its time. 1962 represents a pivotal moment where the old, established world begins to subtly erode. Peggy Olson is the embodiment of this change—a woman prioritising career over family in an era where such a choice was socially anathema. The episode cleverly contrasts her with the older, plainer, more “square” women in her family, framing the conflict not as a simple battle between progressive and conservative, but as a more tragic clash of mutually incomprehensible life paths. The casting of the youthful, attractive Colin Hanks as Father Gill adds a fascinating twist: the Church, the institution most associated with tradition, is here represented by a face that looks almost *cool*, blurring the lines and suggesting that even organised religion is not immune to the changing tides.

The use of humour is equally deft. Kiernan Shipka, as Sally Draper, steals her scenes with a child’s unfiltered curiosity, asking awkward questions and even sipping a cocktail in Sterling Cooper’s offices—a moment that is both charming and faintly unsettling. The visual joke of the creative team in casual weekend wear punctures the series’ usual aesthetic of rigid formality, reminding us that beneath the suits and slicked hair are fallible, tired men.

*Three Sundays* is a particularly finely crafted episode. It uses its expanded timeframe to explore themes of sacrifice, failure, and the hope for renewal—both personal and professional—against the backdrop of a fading, yet still potent, American Protestant ethic. It doesn’t advance the season’s plot in giant leaps, but in doing so it offers something richer: a profound, moving, and critically astute examination of its characters straining against the confines of their era, their faith, and their own deeply flawed natures.


RATING: 7/10 (+++)

title.title: A Peregrine Falcon...
title.body:
...perhaps my best shots of this famous predator yet.
![122.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/papilloncharity/23wCG6Cebyy6bELbkxTGtatGh33ggTtbzPYcR82nVJy1h54ukEax3aTKk8EmEYo5e48qF.jpg)

But why is this bird famous, you ask? This bird holds the worldwide record of the fastest diving speed.

He has left his signature under the high tree twice now for us to see. Two registered racing pigeons that he plucked out of the sky, and I managed to get the rings of the two dead birds. We took the rings of the first bird to our local vet, and on the second day there was another dead bird below the tree. I now also have to take the second set of rings to our vet. Thankfully for the bird's owner, we have not seen more birds of his, and I hope that he is flying his birds in another area.

Let's see what the Guinness World Record has to say about this bird. 

*The fastest dive by a bird is that of a peregrine falcon (Falco peregrinus), which has been estimated at reaching a terminal velocity in ideal conditions of approximately 320 km/h (200 mph) when in a diving stoop hunting prey on the wing. Some experimental dives have suggested that even higher speeds are possible by this species, perhaps up to 389 km/h (242 mph).*

[Source](https://www.guinnessworldrecords.com/world-records/70929-fastest-bird-diving) 

 He certainly gave me his death stare :) 
![072.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/papilloncharity/23xVVgXCGdXDf9HVBtZJ8jAAgqGPZZbuAmWNcrLCBCFTLoojHKwWdTtjsCFgV3avg7Y6c.JPG)

![069.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/papilloncharity/Ep3h9Y8dasrqaTCW18z6ELaAJqs4fGPqSjc7YRMAbjiVdAwZjafjUGShZ5D3mXRLr1Q.JPG)

![088.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/papilloncharity/23wWw3DjnMJRCs2pf5rk5CJe4TKAbnwwnKhSZimFPr1Z4c3SHenyZCd9yXJVXws8xoTcT.JPG)

A first for me to see him preening.
![076.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/papilloncharity/23xpD9Z6u7ZDZJnEzDTva6G5nNQsZgGtmNBjHTm5rD3ccccvMtUEMX4ktWqEA3kiqNeiJ.JPG)

I hoped that he would lift his tail to get his beak to the oil pot in order to oil his feathers, but sadly no go, as he only worked at the top of his back. But then again, one cannot have everything in life one's way, and as I so often say, such is life. 

Then the wind came up and it flared his feathers.
![112.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/papilloncharity/23w2sdsvJAseoiSRAYteyV4H6xreg57ubbuyo2x8p4gMFMUnnTuLs4qjQ5kX6ud5TJoJV.JPG)

![136.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/papilloncharity/EonkvRWF6SmKMZDRD57pgMhWaQotrdZ7PdieGBvBaLFFqGthbTfxCBSxqqjnwP6SMVL.JPG)

Just have a look at his claws, and no prey stands a chance at his grip.
![108.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/papilloncharity/23zS36Q3Tq38nPNiehZq8Npsi8dQj5EXETofgMWueQPQKjEjDNs58wXq25v92Qee3JRQh.JPG)

That tall tree at the right belongs to the Peregrine, and he sits near the top of the tree. Able to scout for miles around in a search for prey.
![143.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/papilloncharity/2423uvXpfWd7Mcaeg9Bw4QWvZWosmqvfaRMF9rrkqVq96PgTsTkwoWeynUKZs6CedUFwe.JPG)

I have done a few posts in my blog of the peregrine over the years, and I know that I will get him on camera every time that I see him in the future, as he simply fascinates me. It is said that the falconers (Bird handlers) are also fond of keeping the peregrines, and in fact his speed was clocked for the world record by a falconer. I don't keep birds, and if I did, then it would be a peregrine.

Maybe I can make friends with this one, and invite him to our place near the river, as we frequently see rats running around. I am sure that he will get so fat that his speed will drop to 10kph :) Only joking, as usual and I am really showing you one of nature's masters of flight. A thought came to me to submit the second photo in this post to bird publishers, as I have never before seen a peregrine stare like that. Maybe, maybe not. 
Such is life. 

I hope you enjoyed the pictures and the story.

Photos by Zac Smith. All-Rights-Reserved. 

Camera: Canon PowershotSX70HS Bridge camera.

Until next time, cheers!

title.title: One State, Three Songs, One Artist
title.body:
<center>![20240708_102722.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bozz/EpLeUzgeCfxPqGGA8vhtL5mHu7LorkYNkajbbJfdzoXoJmqeitNsp3sMzmE3NfUze3c.jpg)</center>

-------------------------

A few years ago when my wife and I were driving home from Colorado, we made a stop in St. Joseph Missouri.  We could have easily just passed on through St. Joseph without stopping, but I wanted to be able to say we at least saw or did something as we crossed the state.  The reason we stopped in this town versus some other town was the fact that the Pony Express originated here.  As you might expect, there are all kinds of historic sites in the town that you can stop and check out.  

The Pony Express Motel in the opening photo for instance.


<center>![20240708_102528.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bozz/EpA1yJ4ojuNgAuYfbfGq6xmbFvqppbrp5aavgY5ZgbgBnPZ9XpgkpJdzxtN8nbC7wrH.jpg)</center>

-----------------------------

Despite having driven across it recently, I can't say as though I have ever spent a lot of time in Missouri.  It's possible we camped there when I was a kid.  I know for a fact we passed through St. Louis on our way to Oklahoma when I was younger.  Like the scene from National Lampoons Vacation, I can still remember riding on highway 64 and seeing the famous Gateway Arch in the distance.  

I have friends who live in St. Louis, but as I said, I have never really spent any time there.  Which is a shame, because it seems like a pretty cool town.  If nothing else, they hold pork steak in high regard there and if that is all I need to know about the city, that is enough. As an avid griller, I have said for a long time that pork steak is a very underrated cut of meat. 

But I digress.

As you have probably figured out by now, our alphabetic journey through the US for #threetunetuesday sponsored by @ablaze has brought us to the great state of Missouri.  This was actually a kind of hard one.  There are a lot of country songs with Missouri in the title or lyrics, but none of them really stood out to me.  They are all pretty obscure, so I figured if we are going to go with obscure, we might as well go all the way.


<center>![20240708_095709.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bozz/EoXrgHSWbUSPdDF5Sror4fdAmPLCuxW4CfnVx5Qn4TsT4p9pcuZG58uXzfFJZH59LMr.jpg)</center>

----------------------------

In fact, with that in mind, I am going to try and share three songs with you today that are not only all about Missouri, but they are also all by the same artist.  Yep, you heard that right, in my research for this post, I was able to find not just one, or two songs, but three different songs with the word Missouri in them all by none other than Mr. Bob Dylan.

It's honestly kind of crazy the amount of material that Dylan has out there.  Even the demo's and \

stuff is quite good.  It might not be as polished as some of the more mainstream stuff.  If anything, the only Dylan I didn't really care for was when he went country for a bit, but that was more of a one off thing.  If I were to go back and listen to it again, I might feel differently.\n\n<center><iframe width=\

was originally included on the Minnesota Tapes album and the reference to Missouri doesn't come until much later in the song.  Almost the last line to be exact.  In fact, the reference isn't even about the state if I am reading it right, it is more about a man who had the last name of Missouri. Nevertheless, it is there if you take the time to listen to it.  \n\nI still want to see the movie that was recently released about Dylan called \

. It looks like it was pretty good and that Timothy Chalime guy seems to be a good actor.  I know I probably spelled his last name wrong there.  My apologies.  Anyway, let's move on to the next Dylan tune.\n\n<center><iframe width=\

allowfullscreen></iframe></center>

------------------------

[Direct Link](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AkUJjEbMXSc&list=RDAkUJjEbMXSc&start_radio=1)

------------------------

I may have forgot to mention, that until I did this post, I have never heard any of these Dylan songs before.  You might consider that cheating, but the fact that I was able to share three songs by the same artist for one state trumped the fact that I wasn't super familiar with the songs.  The reference to Missouri in \
is a bit sooner than it was in \

.  The video I found is just something that someone threw together.  You don't really need to watch it to appreciate how good the song is.  I think one of the things I like so much about Dylan is how he can tell a story with his lyrics.  

Even if you don't like his voice that much or his delivery, the lyrics are often quite poignant.

<center><iframe width=\

allowfullscreen></iframe></center>

------------------------

[Direct Link](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=O2ej3B4xUKY&list=RDO2ej3B4xUKY&start_radio=1)

-----------------------

Finally, I am going to leave you with the song \

by Bob Dylan.  Not much more to say here.  When you do a search of songs with Missouri in the title or lyrics, this is one of the first ones that actually shows up.  This and some songs by Eminem apparently.  I can't say I am super familiar with those either.  

I should point out, that this song refers more to the Missouri River than it does to the actual state and though in the past that may have been a violation of my unwritten rules, I am willing to bend it in this case, just for the coolness of having all the songs by the same artist.

Actually, I was thinking about it the other day and it is quite possible that just about every state  has at least one Bob Dylan song that references it.  Don't hold me to that of course, but it sure does seem like it.

Check back next week when we head to Montana (I think), and I believe that should be the last of the \

.

👉 Watercolor Paper, sketching Paper, or stretched canvas
👉 Pencil and Eraser
👉 Coffee Powder 
👉 2 small cups ( lighter and darker shades)
👉 Ruler
👉 Clean Water
👉 Rag
👉 Paper napkin or paper towel

👉 Flat Brush /small #10, 10/32 / 8.0mm
👉 Liner Brush #2 / 2/32\

body.title: La Mala Buena Alicante
body.body:
**We didn’t land in Normandy, nor did we have our D-Day. It was more of a B-Evening, for #beersaturday. And it definitely wasn’t any B-list kind of fun. Quite the opposite; it was the liveliest night of the entire Hive Open Days. A little bit impromptu. Then again... when traveling with me, can a craft beer session ever truly be unexpected? I think not! But let's take it from the top.**


![IMG_3187.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/godfish/EoGxSLyq3cuJ9iwHD5DnpDWvMmEEK1JSPymvPnVMgMAmAX1bLQae9fFh6hBH53WYyBg.JPG)

![IMG_3189.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/godfish/EoAbBGWvAD4penPG4BNqUpYBwKfcLDh9KzaKwPbJbNpxA7SveCeZKpfXBW5aHQFacQm.JPG)


Others have already covered the program in Alicante. In the style of professional reporters. Or festival enthusiasts. Or just however their pen happened to flow. Look up the reports from the Clean Planet Walk if you're craving the details of that very day. I took advantage of a sleepy moment on the boat back to Alicante (and the fact that @tibfox doesn't stomach these sailings all too well) and began pulling strings like a seasoned puppeteer. Or pub-peteer. How about we head out for a beer tonight? We'll grab a shower, catch a little siesta, and meet up at La Mala Buena in an hour and a half. I’m sure it’ll be much more buena than mala.


![IMG_3188.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/godfish/Eokd7CD4BU7fu32uDcYY6ZUz4BhtqfPNjuJjKiZbpWmKP4Y68MiJW5TuP4J7BNcsbDH.JPG)



It worked like a charm. Whoever wanted to come raised their hand. And apparently, even those who kept their hands down showed up. For twenty hands, we needed nearly thirty chairs. Luckily, both camareros were way more chill than the staff on the pirate island (wouldn't you expect it to be the other way around?). Or anywhere else, for that matter. We didn't even spook them with our rather unusual request for a reservation for twenty thirsty throats in fifty minutes flat. Perhaps because @honeydue and I stopped by in person.

![IMG_3186.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/godfish/Eokccu8uqS618pMCZqWFm9qq1wJvXYrWA1CjpcmCaficVSwdp4TW8jsism7D4r5RBG8.JPG)


Then a shower (we had, after all, actually been picking up trash) and back we went. The tables seemed inflatable; there was always room for one or two more Hiveans. After all, in Spain, there is simply no such thing as a full bar. Which is exactly why physicists from all over the world flock here, trying to describe this phenomenon for future generations. But when it comes down to that spacetime paradox, even the sharpest minds of Nobel laureates fall short against all those cañas, pintas, jarras, chupitos, and mostly, the liquids contained within them. But that's a story for another time. Or space.



![IMG_3196.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/godfish/23uR1EmwqQAuNoFhGDTCqFk27fCtYWaPJEww2ukPuwP6DFMJk1hGYgdkbmBUBQwuG4i3J.JPG)


The evening stretched out until closing time. Some took my recommendation and tasted a beer they hadn't even known existed. Among the ladies, various Gelato Sour Ales from the Polish microbrewery Funky Fluid were a massive hit. @honeydue and @ninaeatshere spread the beer gospel, while @livinguktaiwan, @alessandrawhite, and @mipiano tasted with gusto. The gentlemen stuck to more conservative beer styles, but everyone found their sweet spot. Or bitter, most people leaned towards the bitter brews.


![IMG_3193.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/godfish/23vsWz2pF1GMhRZHC5jNCzSoG4XgYdYuVtMMbLwacMeXXW41mg6wTyk6EanKtJ2fAeQi6.JPG)


But above all, had there been a physicist in the bar, they would have appreciated our Brownian motion around the pushed-together tables; everyone mingled with everyone, toasting and tasting. The food was worth it too, though Nina might write more about that.


![IMG_3190.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/godfish/2432UVubQyTVYbKh1fBoGCTxaFaA7oUPNfCqJEAGRErjseRdCoWeyvGvVG1KFUrZzDmDX.JPG)

> Porter

![IMG_3191.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/godfish/23w345mzkwKgVu2QAexeUisjjAwuMiT4YPyjCXc481Dc1XEwm4BvCDmiXaf5BiUPKZCpK.JPG)

> APA

![IMG_3197.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/godfish/Ep7w49sMQLMjNAU2ADD9PxuytafUG7a99Gv16RqnXyAto99WX3gsdg1xcUSaJcq44Wc.JPG)


And as the evening leaned toward its end, it was time for a sweet finale. For @honeydue, an Imperial Stout with a fish on the can; for me, a DDH TIPA fittingly named Looking for More. We shared these drinks with the last castaways of our pushed-together table archipelago, and then simply boarded our lifeboats and set off for home.


![IMG_3199.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/godfish/23yTqVcukHHGzx9Hqy8p6b2hHWRH1gew1r73wgBHpGQSDNe2jPcKeMJddwcvEQ8rjRpVo.JPG)

![IMG_3194.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/godfish/23xep3AatiC1HENmHoREt4DWVofFZBbSWCgFUBWyfhttkPLGB6hkfXz96G4K9N9orXWU5.JPG)



The best night, the greatest memories. Thanks to everyone who braved \

as my love called this hoppy excursion into the land of flavors and aromas.

Till the next time!


![IMG_3198.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/godfish/EoiXAkhRPHUE5SG9YQrZtZ477MLWGTnN3526tvGtEkHmanabFKUyRe8WQbTmw2EAxU8.JPG)

*I’d love to invite... well, everyone to participate in #BeerSaturday hosted by @detlev. What's your take on La Mala Buena?*

body.title: To Hive or not to Hive
body.body: Recently in Alicante, my husband and I attended an event that left an incredibly warm mark on our hearts. It was a landmark meeting with the ambassadors of the Hive platform, where the atmosphere was so pleasant and relaxed that inspiration simply overflowed for everyone present. Speaking personally with the creators allowed us to truly feel the spirit of this project and discover new horizons in the digital world. What struck us most is how much Hive differs from the giants we are used to, such as Facebook. This is a space where the fear of toxicity or hate, which so often permeates other resources, finally disappears. A sincere respect for authors and intellectual property prevails here, and community support is felt in every comment. It is deeply gratifying to realize that our thoughts and creativity hold real value. The reward system on Hive allows you to do more than just collect virtual likes; you receive genuine financial support in the form of tokens for every publication. This provides an incredible incentive to create high-quality content, knowing that your efforts will be worthily appreciated by the community. A vital feature that grants a sense of true freedom is the complete decentralization of the network. On Hive, there is no central server or administrator who can block an account or delete content at their own discretion. Since all data is recorded on the blockchain, it remains immutable and transparent, which guarantees protection against censorship and unfairness. This is a platform that belongs to the community itself rather than corporations, where everyone has the right to free self-expression. After the event in Alicante, we felt a sincere desire to try our hand at writing specifically for this audience. Hive is a safe and constructive environment where sincerity becomes the primary currency, and the possibility of monetizing creativity turns into a wonderful bonus. It is a place for those seeking a space to grow their blog without borders or limitations.

body.title: A Scenic Journey to Chandrika lake– Beauty in Every Turn
body.body:
Among the many enjoyable trips we have taken, our visit to Chandrika lake remains a truly memorable experience. The journey itself was filled with breathtaking views, making it just as special as the destination.

As we traveled along the route, we were lucky to witness a series of beautiful mountain ranges stretching across the horizon. The sight of these rolling hills, covered in greenery and touched by soft mist, created a peaceful and refreshing atmosphere. Every turn of the road revealed another stunning view, making us feel deeply connected to nature.
![WhatsApp Image 2026-05-03 at 13.09.41.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/hive.samadi/23ynWfzby2wkFQjDjsX7nYZ1W6QxpVuLvYANeVk8fJY4AJnak5UwTjSosgty6tzkps8Jm.jpeg)
The environment around Chandrika lake was calm and picturesque. The combination of water, mountains, and fresh air made it a perfect place to relax and unwind. The natural beauty of the area was truly captivating, offering a sense of serenity that is hard to find in busy city life.

One of the most memorable moments of our trip was when we stopped at a special viewpoint where we could see a full circle of mountains surrounding us. It was a breathtaking sight that left us in awe. While enjoying this incredible view, we decided to take a short break and treat ourselves to some ice cream. Sitting there, enjoying a simple ice cream while being surrounded by such magnificent scenery, felt like a small but perfect moment of happiness.
![WhatsApp Image 2026-05-03 at 13.06.32.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/hive.samadi/243qK9kWiGiQEHTrzka9uqfQbto54P8VsQQtZmKHffRaC81S8eXnXULdFvrdzwe2iK2NK.jpeg)

This trip to Chandrika lake was not just about sightseeing, but about enjoying the journey, appreciating nature, and spending quality time together. It is a place that truly touches the heart and leaves lasting memories.

body.title: DOES GOD ALLOW POLYGAMY// MCGI TOPIC REVIEW
body.body:
Yes in the old testament polygamy was accepted because many followers of God married multiple wives. People like Abraham, Solomon and David married more than one wife and they are all strong men of God who teaches people to follow God. However, these situations often came with conflict, jealousy, and family struggles, suggesting that while God permitted it at certain times, it was not His perfect design for marriage.
https://youtu.be/fK9Fo0xgtlE?si=TEWL7Zar3oc9YyvX
But from the begining of this world, God have made it to be one man and one wife. In Genesis, a man is described as leaving his parents and becoming one flesh with his wife, which points to a singular, committed relationship. This standard is reinforced in the teachings of Jesus, who emphasized faithfulness and unity in marriage rather than multiple partners.

We all know that in the new testament, the idea of marriage changed during the times of Jesus Christ where we are instructed to marry only one wife so as to promote monogamy. While God may have allowed polygamy in earlier times due to human circumstances, the overall biblical direction points toward one man and one woman as the model that reflects God’s intention for marriage.

body.title: I would call this a correction, not a pump, on the HIVE price
body.body:
/>  
  
The HIVE price is up around 50% in the past 24h. Each one of those huge green candles has around 15 to 20 million HIVE in volume. I wouldn't dare trying to predict the future so I will limit myself to saying that at around 50 million market cap HIVE feels heavily undervalued. I will limit myself to that because nobody knows if anything will go up, down or in circles. An overpriced coin can go up and an underpriced coin can go down.  
  
  
But it is exciting to imagine the possibility of a bull market returning to Hive and its ecosystems. The timing was great, just after Hive Open Days, which could or not have been a coincidence.  
  
  
With a higher price comes healthier funding for Hive projects. If we are to keep going up I hope we do not forget the lessons learned in such a long and strenuous bear market. Devs and the DHF need to be responsible with financing and need to think of income streams beyond the DHF.  
  
  
I hope I am not annoying for touching in such a subject in such a happy day of amazing gains for HIVE, but our ecosystems are too reliant on the DHF. We have projects that have been running for years and still have no income source beyond the DHF and no matter how much I love your project, if your only income is the DHF then you are developing a paid application and the price is the dumping you have to do to finance servers, devs, promotion and whatever else your expenses are. A project financed by the DHF is paid by everyone regardless if they use and like the application of not and that is unfair and that is why projects need income streams beyond the DHF.  
  
  
  
Anyways, the 50% price increase is a welcome surprise. Specially after I have just recently powered up. Hope it keeps the momentum!
