```
body.title: Hmburguesas casera, arroz y ensaladaºººººHomemade hamburgers, rice, and salad
body.body:
Hola a todos, para degustar el almuerzo de hoy consiste en hamburguesas de lentejas, arroz hervido y ensalada, para preparar la hamburguesa es de la siguiente manera, la lenteja la dejamos del dia anterior con agua, luego la hervimos bien, le quitamos el agua y la pisamos como si fuera para pure, le agregamos, sal a gusto, un poco de zanahoria rallada, cebolla morada reahogada, harina leudante y huevo lo amasamos como si fuera para pizza, luego le vamos dando la forma de hamburguesa, una ves cocinada queda como se ve en la fotografia, bueno para darle mas sabor le agregamos el queso blando o fresco arriba de la misma.

![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/comandoyeya/23tSWrGYrA7eaUe5AxKn6bcDFq37LmXVoK9GFxHsXtxpnKtR9YkobUXuH2pJAcjF5XP87.png)

Para cocinar el arroz agregamos una olla con agua en la hornalla de la cocina, cuando la misma comienza su hervor, le vertemos un poco de aceite y luego vamos agregando el arrzo y vamos revolviendo despacio para que no se forme grumos, cuando esta cocinado lo colamos, lo agregamos en un volts y le vertemos un poco de aceite de oliva, el cual le da un sabor muy especial y de esamanera todo sale muy exquisito.

![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/comandoyeya/23wMYTC1LuNJtngxjB4gxD8AmU5bqkLem4MyuhcER2bZAzmVwKFawbrvHAm6ACFBLcx3T.png)

Para preparar la ensalada la cual se trata de lechuga, aguacate o palta, tomate y pepino, para lo cual cortamos todo en trozos pequeños, luego le vertemos un poco de aceite de oliva y sal a gusto, lo mesclamos y de esa manera ya la podemos degustar.

![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/comandoyeya/Eonm2RgnTnwGdxB9SkA4QHWCYgzfxXLtNkJ7CCriTPa65XEEQFuyvBo7sBWYxgHMAF9.png)

La verdad degustar un almuerzo de esta manera, lo concidero especial por el solo hecho de preparar este manjar.

MUCHAS GRACIAS POR SEGUIRME Y LEERME, QUE TENGAN BUEN DIA.

ENGLISH

Hola a todos, para degustar el almuerzo de hoy consiste en hamburguesas de lentejas, arroz hervido y ensalada, para preparar la hamburguesa es de la siguiente manera, la lenteja la dejamos del dia anterior con agua, luego la hervimos bien, le quitamos el agua y la pisamos como si fuera para pure, le agregamos, sal a gusto, un poco de zanahoria rallada, cebolla morada reahogada, harina leudante y huevo lo amasamos como si fuera para pizza, luego le vamos dando la forma de hamburguesa, una ves cocinada queda como se ve en la fotografia, bueno para darle mas sabor le agregamos el queso blando o fresco arriba de la misma.

![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/comandoyeya/23tSWrGYrA7eaUe5AxKn6bcDFq37LmXVoK9GFxHsXtxpnKtR9YkobUXuH2p

To cook the rice, we place a pot with water on the stove, and when it starts to boil, we pour in a bit of oil and then gradually add the rice, stirring slowly to avoid lumps. Once it's cooked, we drain it, add it to a bowl, and pour in a bit of olive oil, which gives it a very special flavor, and in this way, everything turns out very delicious.

![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/comandoyeya/23wMYTC1LuNJtngxjB4gxD8AmU5bqkLem4MyuhcER2bZAzmVwKFawbrvH

To prepare the salad, which consists of lettuce, avocado, tomato, and cucumber, we cut everything into small pieces, then drizzle a bit of olive oil and salt to taste, mix it, and that way we can enjoy it.

body.title: PLANETS IN THE 12TH HOUSE AND EXPERIENCES ABROAD IN VEDIC ASTROLOGY
body.body: In Vedic astrology, the 12th house is traditionally associated with foreign lands, separation from familiar environments, isolation, spirituality, loss, and life lived behind the scenes. Because of this symbolism, many people assume that having planets in the 12th house automatically means struggling as an outsider or facing cultural difficulties when living abroad. However, this interpretation is an oversimplification. The 12th house does indicate experiences away from one’s birthplace or comfort zone, but whether those experiences are difficult, neutral, or even beneficial depends on several important factors within the full horoscope. Vedic astrology always emphasizes holistic chart analysis rather than judging outcomes based on a single house placement. The nature of the planets occupying the 12th house plays a crucial role. Benefic planets such as Jupiter, Venus, or a well-placed Moon can indicate comfort in foreign lands, spiritual fulfillment, or success in international environments, including work in multinational settings, research, or charitable institutions. These placements may even suggest that a person feels more at ease away from their homeland, finding personal growth and emotional peace abroad. On the other hand, malefic planets like Saturn, Mars, Rahu, or Ketu especially if afflicted can point toward feelings of isolation, loneliness, cultural disconnection, or being misunderstood. Even in such cases, the struggle often reflects an internal sense of detachment rather than consistent external rejection by others. Equally important is the condition of the 12th house lord. If the lord of the 12th house is strong, well-aspected, and placed favorably, it can significantly reduce challenges and instead support productive foreign experiences, spiritual maturity, or financial gains from overseas sources. Conversely, a weak or afflicted 12th lord may manifest as difficulties adjusting to foreign environments, emotional exhaustion, or a sense of rootlessness. The sign occupying the 12th house also modifies results, as some signs are more adaptable and open to change, while others seek stability and familiarity. It is also a misconception to attribute cultural issues abroad solely to the 12th house. In Vedic astrology, cultural adaptation and belief systems are more directly connected to the 9th house, which governs philosophy, traditions, and worldview. Emotional comfort and a sense of “home” are seen through the 4th house, while social integration is reflected through the 7th and 11th houses. Therefore, challenges related to feeling like an outsider often arise from a combination of factors rather than 12th-house placements alone. Additionally, planetary periods (dashas) are crucial, as the same 12th-house placement may manifest very differently depending on the timing in a person’s life. Ultimately, the 12th house is less about punishment or exclusion and more about inner transformation, detachment, and growth beyond familiar boundaries. While some individuals with strong 12th-house emphasis may experience moments of loneliness or cultural adjustment abroad, others may thrive precisely because distance from their roots allows them to reconnect with their deeper self. Vedic astrology views foreign residence as a karmic experience shaped by the entire chart, not as an inevitable struggle determined by the 12th house alone. #12thHouseAstrology #astrology #horoscope #vedicastrology #indianastrology #vedicastrologer #astrologer #predictions #destiny #psychic #kundli #jyotish #remedy

body.title: The Man I Built in My Head #287
body.body:
While I was still young and growing, I had this belief that my father could solve anything; this was something I held on to for a long time. He never said this to me; I just created that version of him, maybe because I was still very little and he was tall, brave, outspoken, and very confident in a way that his presence makes rooms feel smaller. I didn't know he was also human because he always knows what to do, who to call, and what to say in all situations. And I won't lie, I kept going on with this version because it made me comfortable and always made everything less frightening. I am always safe if he is unshakable. The day I saw a crack in this version. It was nothing dramatic because there was no single discussion, no misunderstanding, or anything brutal. I just saw him one evening sitting quietly and almost looking at nothing. It looks like he has a heavy heart, and he can't share it with anyone. He was looking in a way that I have almost never seen him in before. It was a much deeper thing, and I was not physically tired. I got to know that I have been seeing him every day without actually seeing him. I was just busy going around with that version of him that I have created only in my mind. It was very hard to let go of that version I'd created in my mind because I never expected it. I wasn't even angry. It was just painful, that type that comes unexpected. Because it was painful letting go of that part of him keeping me together. That idea had to let go because he's also a human, a father, and a man who had tried hard, made mistakes too, and knew to bow down because he keeps showing up. ![225222.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/goldenproject/23tGc5XsxXDjRECYx9AwD4HjekZLmNyZ2Vff4VnbCPSG6vFDH6aMcgBCsGBJDXeLwKQxu.png) And what I was surprised at was that immediately I stopped seeing that version of him, and I began knowing him more. The true him turned out to be a person I should know more than that previous version I created. Letting go of the old him just had to be painful first, and that is best for me in a way because sometimes some things have to end so that a new thing can begin. ----- ##### 🔗 Apps which I recommend body.title: Authenticity in Music, & Jeff Buckley for Three Tune Tuesday
body.body:
'I feel gross' a good friend says in response to me telling her that the music she sent me for Samhain blessings was generative AI. 'Violated.'

I felt bad. The link to the song on Spotify was well intended, and I could see why it appealed to her. The persona seemed authentic. There's a bio. Photos of the women - let's call her Lou Raven, because I don't *want* to push traffic her way because I too feel *gross* and *violated* for listening to music which has been AI generated. Her whole person seems to be about interacting with nature and ravens, which is why my friend probably got sucked in, being her thing and all. 


![b384e77d-7665-4142-bdf7-633989d2a67d-1_all_8627.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/riverflows/EpC8stVAFZJVTCcBsZaE1kUYFSkDAKJwzKC5Gm1KbW3BPsCt61UnHo2RSkPaBdrN3PW.jpg)


**A magpie, not a raven. Nothing to do with this post. I just didn't want to use AI. I try!**

Here's the fine line - she *says* her lyrics are written by her, as part of a healing process. Scroll down, and realise that somewhere in the fine print it says 'generative AI' - that is, the instruments and lyrics are created by Suno, an AI music generator. Plug in your lyrics, choose your genre, and create - and earn money for doing so. 

A few AI checkers were only *moderately* convinced it was *partly* human written. We all know they aren't accurate, particuarly as AI is shaping the language we use and thus even human generated content will sound AI. But it's enough to create some doubt. Is she *outsourcing all her creativity*? Look at her website, and it seems so - her images are clearly AI generated, though it doesn't say so. My friend may have been decieved because she doesn't deal with AI to the extent that I do. 

The 'artist' calls it *co-creation*, as if that lends a humanness to her process and the generated content. Let's not be bamboozled by such pretty terms. Spotify has created new laws against content farming - I mean one guy famously made millions before he got done for fraud - which helps us figure out which content is AI. I'd like a toggle switch to remove *any* AI content coming up in my feed. If it's not entirely human, can it be truly music, who by design takes our deepest emotions and turns them into something moving?

My friend asked how I could tell. Jamie thought the song was *terrible* but that wasn't really an answer. Perhaps it was my gut, but I'd like to think I understand music enough to realise there was something off about it. Some repetitive riffs that felt formulaic, perhaps. An inauthenticity between the bars. 

All the brilliant music out there, and we're now navigating AI slop music? 

Yeah, I feel gross. 

#### Meanwhile...

I've been listening to Grace by Jeff Buckley again this week. I used to really love him back in the mid 90's when we were travelling Australia, and had the luck to see him play in a natural ampitheatre in Western Australia before he died swimming in the Missisipi. It's one of those perfect albums of the '90s worth listening to. 

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EcaxrqhUJ4c

These days of course you could create music *in the style of Jeff Buckley*, lyrics and vocals including. I wonder what he would think of that. 

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ywEByqEVQRk&list=PLyernWk5UpgMNFINbivsL9EvyrWFWokXS

And certainly, I wouldn't have *drooled* over him so much if he was 'co-creating' or if he was *created*. Here's a guy who was known for resisting pressure to create what they wanted and instead sung from this place of vulnerability and pure emotion. I'll never forget the *intensity* of his performance on that stage under the full moon. Sent shivers down my spine. 

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3MMXjunSx80

A new documentary [It's Never Over](https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-04-30/jeff-buckley-movie-its-never-over-documentary-michale-tighe/106517122) purports to explore the music behind the myth - I think it's on Netflix which I don't have a sub for but I'm looking forward to seeing it at some point. I wonder if any of these generative AI artists will have a doco made about them twenty years after their death. Maybe, by generative AI. God help us.

I will give him exaggeratedly large boots, pants and a vest like in the card, and his guitar, which of course cannot be missing. > Mi primer boceto fue para definir rasgos básicos y su ropa. Le haré botas exageradamente grandes, un pantalón y chaleco como en la carta, y su guitarra, que por supuesto no puede faltar. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmVWE72ssWQXqKspXujKbpgXsGjy9bG4iAMoaUxk95S99s/298_sin_t_tulo_20260502174101.jpg) By deactivating the sketch layer, I can now work more on my line art until I am satisfied with the result and have everything ready for coloring. > Desactivando la capa de bocetos, ya puedo trabajar más en mi lineart hasta estar satisfecho con el resultado y dejar todo preparado para colorear. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmb5Vy1oacqnboj1y8ctdR3s9WD5JcFEsTFZknctA6D4iy/298_sin_t_tulo_20260502175257.jpg) To color, I will begin with the hair, skin, and pants, so that once they are finished, I can move on to the following clothing items and the guitar. This will be the most difficult part since there are many dark colors together in a small area. I will work with some lights and shadows to differentiate volumes and heights, as well as avoid using black everywhere; I will combine it with some very dark blue tones. > Para colorear comenzaré por el cabello, la piel y los pantalones, para, a la vez que estén terminados, seguir con las siguientes prendas de ropa y a la guitarra. Esto será lo más difícil ya que hay muchos colores oscuros juntos en una pequeña área. Trabajaré con algunas luces y sombras para diferenciar volúmenes y alturas, así como evitar usar negros en todo; lo combinaré con algunos tonos muy oscuros de azules. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmPu2FCSNSAbv7Ph8yqC75YbabWevMsSrwKsfDVjVc8E94/298_sin_t_tulo_20260502175532.jpg) So my whole character turned out colored, I really liked it and I think it has a lot of my style and the kind of drawing I like. In fact, I think that from today on, Duke will be my favorite legendary card in Rising Star Game. > Así quedó todo mi personaje coloreado, me gustó mucho y creo que tiene mucho mucho de mi estilo y del tipo de dibujo que me gusta. De hecho, creo que Duke será a partir de hoy mi carta legendaria favorita de Rising Star Game. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmfLxZTm9TA4SmeAmSx1anAAfiTun7si5KWQ1CovV2Vnmg/298_sin_t_tulo_20260502183153.jpg) Thank you for joining me another day of drawing. > Gracias por acompañarme un día más dibujando. --- ***About:*** ==*Sketchbook and Journal of a Learner*== **If you like my content, join my [Fanbase clicking here](https://hive.vote/dash.php?fan=nestodibuja&i=2)**

body.title: Three new VF3's
body.body:
I have only ever purchased one car in my life that was new and it was close to $20,000 and that was many years ago.  The fact that there is a brand new car that a person can purchase today for $10,000 is pretty remarkable and I don't think that people can be too fussy about the quality of it at that price point.

These little cars are yet to see the long-term and in all honesty, they can't really be that durable or long-lasting but you never know!   I suppose a miracle could happen.

In the meantime these silly little cars have become kind of a designer things for the middle-class because especially since it is a Vietnamese brand, it is really easy to get financing for them.   In the meantime, customizing your VF3 has become quite popular and no other car seems to have this sort of tradition going on with it.

<center> 
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/gabe.radke/23wWpJBDEQLM8HUEJLurKe4zKepYuDKG2UeR4oKtT7zWVAZeYyoaZbQkYhWTSMPWVzCQg.png)
</center>

I’ve seen a number of variations of this sort of accessories and I always find them amusing.  We have a roof rack that is quite sporty and also has a ladder leading up to it as if this was some sort of massive SUV.   If you are over 5 feet tall, you can probably reach halfway across the roof of this vehicle without a ladder and I really wouldn’t want to test the load-bearing capabilities of the ladder anyway.  I think it is probably more likely to crumple the windows or collapse the roof if anything larger than a child was actually trying to use the ladder.   

<center>  
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/gabe.radke/23xySz3VSeXsbVx8Pf8ChD3MZNt3EB2v4hattRKBfm21JgLgrsHqFxR3urq9RGxiKQZ1X.png)</center>

This one might not seem that special on first glance, but the owner had the roof removed and painted a different color so that his (or her) car is slightly different than all of the other yellow ones.  I got up close to check to see if the white was a decal and it is not.  Whoever had this done had a custom paint job done on it and it is CLEAN.   There are no wayward marks that would suggest this was anything other than a very professional paint job.   

<center> 
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/gabe.radke/23wgHdVaNvPuN4Tpkysdo1CgCdNaLwL1gyip4VKnYzkW34szcJSJU5FN83LYpxR5TC3MC.png)
</center> 

Lastly, we have this blue one with custom decals.  This is the first one of these cars that I have seen that is also an advertisement for some company but I am quite sure it will not be the last.  If you were going to put your logo onto something it may as well be the cheapest car on the market.  

These vehicles are turning heads a lot more than vehicles that are considerably more prestigious and the main reason is because they are a new thing and they are within the grasp of most anyone’s budget.   As of yet they are not available as taxis and I don’t think we will come to that point either since the back seat is remarkably small.   

But for a single person or even someone with small a small child this could actually be a pretty good car.  I wouldn’t want to be in an accident in it though, that is for sure.

It will likely be many years before we know or not if this has all been a colossal mistake.   It could be that the car is so cheap because that lithium battery is built to fail and while I haven’t heard of this happening yet, it really wouldn’t surprise me if in a few years there are a lot of really pissed off middle class people that have to pay $5000 for a replacement battery.   

I have no desire to own a car with streets as chaotic as Vietnam’s, but for the time being I am really enjoying seeing new and different versions of this car.   Apparently they are available in some markets in Europe and USA as well.  I can’t imagine they are very popular there though.

Hi @threespeak Please read the one paragraph introduction and one page  executive summary of my Proposal #374 HiveComunityBank and I would appreciate it if you could consider supporting the proposals 71 day trial. : [Link](https://inleo.io/@shortsegments/hive-comunity-bank-dhf-proposal-v2-revision-gda?referral=shortsegments)

HiveComunityBank (HCB) is a community lending protocol that lets serious HIVE stakeholders access real spending power without selling their HIVE. Borrowers deposit HIVE as collateral, receive HBD loans, and use those proceeds to spend, invest, or earn — while their HIVE remains powered up and appreciating. Every HBD the DHF allocates enters savings on day one, earns 15% APR immediately, and the principal is never spent. This is not a grant. It is a capital injection.

The protocol solves three problems simultaneously. First, it gives large HP holders liquidity access without exchange exposure. Second, it removes HIVE from liquid circulation — at 10 simultaneous loans with 50,000 HIVE minimum collateral, 500,000 HIVE leaves exchanges for approximately 15 months per lending cycle. Third, it generates guaranteed savings interest regardless of whether any loans are made — at 10,000 HBD per day for 71 days, the pool earns approximately 20,671 HBD in savings interest before a single borrower applies.

The manager is paid exclusively from curation rewards on collateral HP — not from DHF HBD. There is no liquidation mechanism, no oracle dependency, and no scenario in which the pool loses capital. Borrowers who deposit loan proceeds in HBD savings at 15% APR earn more in interest than they pay in loan interest — the net carry position is +7.5% APR on a 12-month term. The 71-day proposal duration gives the community a clear evaluation window before renewal. If the protocol underperforms, do not renew. If it works, expand it.

body.title: Retro Wspomnienia - Elwro 800 Junior
body.body:
Historia powstania Elwro 800 Junior jest mocno związana z realiami Polski lat 80. i ambicją, by wprowadzić komputery do szkół – mimo ograniczeń technologicznych i politycznych.

Wszystko zaczęło się we wrocławskich zakładach Elwro, które od lat 60. zajmowały się produkcją komputerów. Początkowo były to duże, profesjonalne maszyny używane w przemyśle i administracji, ale wraz z rozwojem mikrokomputerów na świecie pojawiła się potrzeba stworzenia czegoś mniejszego – sprzętu, który mógłby trafić do edukacji.

Na Zachodzie popularność zdobywały komputery domowe i szkolne, takie jak ZX Spectrum czy Commodore 64. W Polsce dostęp do nich był ograniczony, a import kosztowny i trudny. Dlatego podjęto decyzję: trzeba stworzyć własny komputer edukacyjny.

Tak narodziła się koncepcja Elwro 800 Junior, który był w dużej mierze inspirowany brytyjskim ZX Spectrum. Nie był to jednak prosty klon – konstruktorzy musieli dostosować projekt do dostępnych w Polsce podzespołów, co często oznaczało kompromisy i kreatywne rozwiązania.

Projektowanie rozpoczęło się w połowie lat 80. Zespół inżynierów pracował w trudnych warunkach – brakowało nowoczesnych układów scalonych, dokumentacji i narzędzi. Często korzystano z tego, co było dostępne lokalnie lub w krajach bloku wschodniego. Mimo to udało się stworzyć komputer oparty na 8-bitowym procesorze zgodnym z rodziną Z80, wyposażony w grafikę i interpreter języka BASIC, który był kluczowy w nauce programowania.

Najważniejszym celem nie była wydajność, lecz funkcjonalność edukacyjna. Komputer miał być prosty w obsłudze, tani w produkcji i odporny na intensywne użytkowanie przez uczniów. Dlatego zdecydowano się na charakterystyczną obudowę typu „all-in-one” z wbudowaną klawiaturą oraz możliwość podłączenia do zwykłego telewizora.

Pod koniec lat 80. rozpoczęto produkcję seryjną. Elwro 800 Junior trafił głównie do szkół w ramach programów informatyzacji edukacji. Dla wielu uczniów był to pierwszy kontakt z komputerem. Nauka polegała często na pisaniu prostych programów w BASIC-u, zapisywaniu ich na kasetach magnetofonowych i eksperymentowaniu z grafiką oraz dźwiękiem.

Choć komputer miał swoje ograniczenia – niewielką pamięć, prostą grafikę i stosunkowo wolne działanie – odegrał ważną rolę. Wprowadził całe pokolenie młodych ludzi w świat informatyki w czasach, gdy dostęp do technologii był bardzo ograniczony.

Po 1989 roku, wraz ze zmianami ustrojowymi i otwarciem rynku, do Polski zaczęły napływać nowocześniejsze komputery z Zachodu. Produkcja Elwro 800 Junior stopniowo traciła sens ekonomiczny, a same zakłady Elwro zakończyły działalność w latach 90.

Mimo to Elwro 800 Junior zapisał się w historii jako jeden z najważniejszych polskich komputerów edukacyjnych. Nie był najbardziej zaawansowany technicznie, ale spełnił swoją rolę – nauczył tysiące osób podstaw programowania i pokazał, że nawet w trudnych warunkach można budować własną technologię.

body.body:
<liketuimages>
<center>
![e6Aa7MFqkmK2Xjqd_3.webp](https://cdn.liketu.com/media/love5200/images/e6Aa7MFqkmK2Xjqd_3/e6Aa7MFqkmK2Xjqd_3.webp)
![08RC8oUhnuhUdvwE_4.webp](https://cdn.liketu.com/media/love5200/images/08RC8oUhnuhUdvwE_4/08RC8oUhnuhUdvwE_4.webp)
![z5eHLKBedWJ97ix6_2.webp](https://cdn.liketu.com/media/love5200/images/z5eHLKBedWJ97ix6_2/z5eHLKBedWJ97ix6_2.webp)
![jmDgtN8kO5lG3FrJ_1.webp](https://cdn.liketu.com/media/love5200/images/jmDgtN8kO5lG3FrJ_1/jmDgtN8kO5lG3FrJ_1.webp)
![bQtqIcsNrv6cskYM_5.webp](https://cdn.liketu.com/media/love5200/images/bQtqIcsNrv6cskYM_5/bQtqIcsNrv6cskYM_5.webp)
</center>
</liketuimages>

哈，美好的时光总是过得飞快哈，不知不觉中这五一小长假已经来到了最后一天，话说，这老天奶属实是给力啊，原本以为会是在阴雨绵绵的假期，没想到啊，天气预报都不准了，哪怕是提前一天知道次日是阴天或下雨，到了第二天，太阳公公又出来作伴哈。。真有趣。

一大早我给自己煮了大份的鸡腿排骨面，补啊，是真的很补，美味也确实美味，嘻嘻嘻。。加上今天是立夏嘛，据说还要吃蛋来着，那必须来两笨鸡蛋，反正每天吃鸡蛋不可少，知道说吃鸡蛋补头发，每个月特殊日子期间，我都会吃两蛋，看着自己黑长直的秀发啊，那一个劲的美啦美啦。。

不过呢，上周六晚，我那个手一抖，把秀发剪短了5公分左右，夏天到了嘛，头发太长，洗头发实在是麻烦了点。我的动手能力特别强，都等不及次日去找发型师了，只是，这一次我没发尾剪好，还是得找发型师帮忙继续修剪一下，夏日的头发长度到肩膀即可啦。

蝴蝶兰啊，一开始我还以为放置在入口处的蝴蝶兰是假花来着，直到我上手摸一下蝴蝶兰的花瓣，好家伙，这居然是真花，不得不说，机场还是很有心了，毕竟这人来人往的，蝴蝶兰养殖貌似也娇贵，养护的这么好，需要工作人员精心养护才行。

被店里的一只粘毛狗狗吸引住了，拿到手里把玩的感觉，触感相当真实，店里的小姐姐说这是用动物真毛手工制作而成的，难怪了。。现在手工制品，只要质量中上层，如果再有品牌加持，价格自然就贵，买回去还得注意护理呢。

OK，今天先分享到这儿哈，抓紧假期的小尾巴，继续HAPPY去。。发现生活中那开心的一二事，嘿嘿。

**感谢大家的阅读和喜欢，您的点赞给予我莫大的鼓励，感恩❀**

body.title: From Job Hunt to Comedy Scene in Minutes
body.body:
<div  class=text-justify>

I was searching for a different community to explore today and comedy came to mind. It's been a while here but I've not stopped hearing or reading jokes and laughing so here I am to share my experience with you. I love the prompt because I have two experiences I can't forget.

I'll share just one of my interview experiences I had, and it was an offline interview. Before the main story... No, I didn't get the job and here is why I didn't and why I don't even regret I didn't.

**My First Ever Interview at a school.**

![IMG_20260505_082915.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/merit.ahama/244A93QuwWDzvaQkct8x8ucpna2nxSzTkuCjzqymrpmEiitUmDW8CJ2uaa1nBkMAuDsqB.png)

I had just finished a 1 year program and while waiting for admission, I thought I should go do some teaching job. I saw a vacancy sign at a big school and I immediately went in and asked about the opening, what I did not plan for at all happened, A quick interview with the principal.

*Yes, I know I should have expected that but I honestly didn't. It's just to teach children, isn't it?*

**Here's how our conversation went when I woke up to reality to face an unprepared interview.**

*Principal: Have you taught in a school before?*

*Me: Yes, I taught a nursery class for a term after secondary school.*

I messed up there, I shouldn't have told him the exact class I taught and for how long. Because he automatically began to see me as a daycare or nursery potential teacher, I just couldn't point how I could actually see it all over his face. 😩

*Principal: Good, here is a chalkboard and I am your nursery kid, teach me any subject.*

*Me: (feeling lost and wanting to just go home and sleep, I acted deaf briefly). Sir, you said?*

He repeated himself without mincing word or at least changing the part where I'll have to actually see a grown man as a kid to teach him. My heart cried when I realized what I had gotten myself into. I picked up the chalk and stood in front of him with confidence I didn't even know I had.

If you can picture this very well, you'd see how funny and crazy it was for a young girl to teach an old man in nursery style. I even said *\

* when I got to the part where I ask the kids questions. And that wasn't even the craziest part. *Principal: Please don't flog me, I will tell my mummy to answer it when you give us homework.* I burst into laughter immediately and I knew then that I wasn't taking the job even if he calls me back as he promised. I can't explain it but I felt a lot of awkwardness to walk out of the school back home, because the office to the gate was a distance long enough for that awkward feeling. **Image used is AI body.title: Probably spring is coming :)
body.body:
Probably spring is coming :) Probably, spring is coming soon, the word “probably” should hedge my modest assumption, so as not to seem like a forecast that someone can believe, but no one can be trusted in such a matter, not even me lol. Yes, I’m not a weather forecaster, don’t even believe weather forecasters, I only know that you shouldn’t rush to change your car’s winter tires to summer tires, because ice can occur even in May, I checked. But, nevertheless, the rain outside the window and obvious warming gives me some right to say that spring, if not in a hurry, is definitely in its plans that, one day, it should visit us. The soulless, with some reservations, benches in the park have not felt pressure on their steel and wooden structures for a long time, except for the layer of snow on them, which, apparently, has begun to subside today and, with all the cold snow on the lifeless wood, the warmth of park visitors will soon come, who, sitting on the benches, will warm the tiny creatures living in the wood, all sorts of caterpillars, bark beetles and maybe some other nematodes ![1skaDSC00460.png](https://cdn.steemitimages.com/DQmbXbe2PM8qEVGxAbXTGVZdSfXq8Nn89FjbaiVtPZ8BGfg/1skaDSC00460.png) I hope that the rain will really reveal all the hidden places of winter and spring will show us its appearance like this cat in the thick of flowers... did you see the cat? ![1ap1dasDSC06918.png](https://cdn.steemitimages.com/DQmaKnwxL73eFUyhXjS6jbsn9MHhpWmypsEbemjZvDTNq2d/1ap1dasDSC06918.png) It would be good to lose the reason to talk about winter and start talking about the warm sun, which will definitely make its own adjustments to the active life of city parks, and not only that. ![1hgfDSC06193.png](https://cdn.steemitimages.com/DQmTJiFHgjEK2jVsTYDi5zGxL9YQTFphLYEU2ch6Qgk9ya7/1hgfDSC06193.png) --- Below you can see my containers with data that I collect in INLEO and always have quick access to them it is very convenient. links.title: ‎When Giants Stumble: How Manchester City’s Slip Hands Arsenal the Title Momentum
links.body:
‎Before Manchester city take on Everton yesterday, i thought to myself that it is now time for city to return the pressure back to arsenal after playing two games more with 6 points separating both side. I Thought it's city time to close the gap. But it's something else that happens and that's shows funny football can be. 
‎  

https://img.leopedia.io/DQmdDMqMA4Zf3RS7PqdCuXEPWGQoUFuJZzqNcNBKkZrctiE/img_4e150e69.png
‎[Source](‎https://baonghean.vn/fr/jeremy-doku-ruc-sang-giup-man-city-gianh-lai-1-diem-kich-tinh-truoc-everton-10335475.html)

‎
‎Initially, I thought Manchester city will easily got the win and walk  over everton but it's different ball game entirely.  The reason why I love the premier league us the fact that any team can pull a suprise and that's what Everton did. 
‎
‎Even though Manchester city shows some quality in the later stages of the game, but it's not enough to win them the three points they actually needed to close the gap on Arsenal as they eventually have to battle for a point. 
‎
‎This kind of result is what Arsenal really need to keep up their hope of securing the premier league title after a decade. 
‎
‎Even despite city going 3:1 down to Everton as moment in the match, they still don't give up. They show resilience, composure and reason why they are one of the best in the league as they later fought back to secure a 3:3 draw. 
‎
‎My question now is what does the result means? Does it mean the title has already slipped away from Manchester city? Does this mean is now Arsenal chance to grab and win their remaining games? 
‎

links.title: Spring bells.
links.body:
Spring bells. Alarm is probably the most appropriate word for those days when, after a long winter, I begin to hear spring bells trying to outshout each other. Yes, copper sounds a little different, but what else can you call the sounds made by heavy drops of water falling from the icicles that decorate the rooftops, encountering obstacles in their path, which emit a monotonous boom-boom-boom! ![1f1DSC04331.png](https://cdn.steemitimages.com/DQmSYkpJxic4xv7ZFy7JF1J7Z9wzqMousCvZkqgjvx99oxt/1f1DSC04331.png) These sounds are pleasant to the ear, but after quiet winter nights, you need to gradually get used to such sounds, and after a couple of days, these sounds, like the clatter of a train's wheels, begin to lull you to sleep. ![1grifDSC02759(1).png](https://cdn.steemitimages.com/DQmbfLq1FV6XrDbuabYegDzKP5wz21Bvoc4YBSXag89XqQd/1grifDSC02759%281%29.png) This is not the first February when warm weather wakes up the bees wintering in their hives, but I don’t know if they woke up so early this year; I haven’t seen them yet, but I think that they too hear these sounds of spring coocols and are getting ready to go out for their first meeting with the sun in the new year. ![1ytrDSC01353.png](https://cdn.steemitimages.com/DQmTJn2ukAU7xCCaiMLHHbNKtZkvFWHBr92tsz95p6vbk93/1ytrDSC01353.png) --- Below you can see my containers with data that I collect in INLEO and always have quick access to them it is very convenient. Hoy fue un día perfecto para caminar por la ciudad. Comencé mi ruta temprano en la mañana, cuando el aire estaba fresco y la luz del sol empezaba a asomarse. Mientras avanzaba, noté un grupo de artistas callejeros que estaban creando un mural vibrante en una de las paredes de un edificio antiguo. La energía y la creatividad que emanaban me hicieron detenerme un momento para disfrutar de su trabajo. Más adelante, conocí a una mujer mayor que estaba alimentando a las palomas en un parque. Su sonrisa y su amabilidad me hicieron sentir una conexión instantánea. Me contó que venía al parque todos los días desde hacía años y que cada paloma tenía su propio nombre. Era increíble escuchar sus historias sobre cómo había visto crecer el parque y la ciudad a su alrededor. A lo largo de mi caminata, también pasé por una pequeña feria de artesanías donde había puestos con productos locales. Me detuve a mirar y terminé comprando una pulsera hecha a mano que capturó mi atención. La artesana me contó la historia detrás de su trabajo y cómo cada pieza tenía un significado especial. Al final del día, regresé a casa con una sensación de alegría y conexión, no solo con el lugar, sino también con las personas que conocí en el camino. links.title: Iroha Karuta 20a: The Japanese Virtue of Double-Checking Everything
links.body:
![Kotowaza20Angel.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/hirohurl/EoK6p8yjoxb5c9asdmPUZtXhz36XmSTVz5y65QC1rfwHw1KJirwSVoxbmL7wvszTJHF.jpg)


It’s been a while since I last posted about the *Iroha Karuta* here on Hive. In fact, this is my first post in the series this year. I'm chilling out at home during the Golden Week season of consecutive national holidays, avoiding the crowds and all that, so today feels like a good time to revisit one of my back-burner projects and move on to the twentieth proverb in the deck.

The *Iroha Karuta* is a card grabbing game in which a \

of cards, and the players compete to grab the equivalent picture card from the tatami mat or table top. \n\nHowever, Iroha Karuta was never just a children’s game. Traditionally, they served several purposes at once: helping children learn the hiragana script, passing down folk wisdom, and providing moral instruction through short memorable proverbs - \

(諺) in Japanese. In that sense, they functioned as a compact introduction not only to literacy, but also to the values and practical wisdom of Japanese society.

The twentieth proverb in the Angel™ deck is a good example of that moral and practical dimension:

**念には念を入れよ**
(*Nen ni wa nen o ireyo*)

The accompanying Angel booklet glosses it as:

> **注意した上にもなお注意せよということ。**
> Chūi shita ue ni mo nao chūi seyo to iu koto.
> “Even after taking care, continue to take care.”


![Kotowaza20Setsumei.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/hirohurl/23vi6PKrmqVjYm7yRc4C3XdWHJnkchFBCd93rKzHRanwyD91N2F57S7hXXievAgAopuNG.jpg)


That captures the spirit of the proverb well. It is one of those sayings that sounds unmistakably Japanese in spirit. It's an exhortation to be thorough, careful, and not to assume that “good enough” is ever good enough.

## 念 - A Couple of Examples of \

in Daily Life in Japan

The kanji **念** is one I was already familiar with from a few other common expressions. 

One is **念のため** (*nen no tame*), a phrase I have always liked for its slightly non-committal quality. It is often translated as “just in case,” but it carries the sense of taking precautions as circumstances may yet prove uncertain because, in effect, all always does depend on uncertain circumstances in this contingent life.

The same kanji also appears in **残念** (*zannen*), the common word for regret or disappointment. Here too one can still sense the underlying idea of **念** as lingering thought or mental preoccupation: the chagrin felt when things do not work out as hoped, and the lingering regret that remains in the mind after a missed opportunity.

It also appears in more commemorative and religious contexts. A 記念 (kinen) is a memorial or commemoration, something kept in remembrance of an event or occasion. 

A 念珠 (nenju) is a Buddhist rosary or set of prayer beads, used in devotional practice, and in explicitly Buddhist usage, 念仏 (nenbutsu) refers to the recitation of the Buddha’s name (仏) in mindfulness and devotion.

Taken together, these usages suggest that 念 is a richer word than simple “care” or “attention.” At its core lies the idea of something held deliberately in the mind: careful attention before an action, regretful reflection after an event, remembrance of what has passed, or recollection in religious practice.

Seen in that light, 念には念を入れよ is not merely telling us to “be careful.” It suggests applying one act of \

attention on top of another, bringing deliberate thought and consciousness to one’s actions.

Let us now break the proverb down piece by piece.

### 念 (nen)

The kanji **念** means thought, care, attention, mindfulness, or caution. In this proverb, it carries the sense of carefulness or prudent attention, as we can see in the illustration of the chap who is carefully doing his accounts, with an accounts book, abacus, and what appear to be counting tokens, while the items being counted are carefully arranged on a cloth by his side.

### に (ni)

The particle **に** means “into,” “onto,” or “upon.”

### は (wa)

The topic marker **は** adds emphasis, giving the phrase a sense of “when it comes to” or “even upon.”

### 念 (nen)

The same word is repeated for emphasis.

### を (o)

Marks the second **念** as the object of the verb.

### 入れよ (ireyo)

An imperative form of **入れる**, meaning “put in” or “add.”

Taken literally, the proverb says:

> **“Put caution into caution.”**

Or more naturally in English:

> **“Be extra careful.”**
> **“Better safe than sorry.”**

Its force lies in the repetition of \

echoes the original though neither really catches anything more than the shallowest sense of the proverb. The point is that however careful you think you are being, the proverb advises you to add yet more care.

## Chatgpt versus Google Translate

I asked Chatgpt to give us its best version - just ONE translation - and it came up with this:


![Screenshot 2026-05-05 3.55.40 PM.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/hirohurl/23u6YyrukB8YnnAeFwAs8zAmTmHSER8cFbmRmiZkkknFhg1kuqtXJJbTXVvsHQvJfYRVN.png)

> Take every precaution

Not bad at all. It is a \

that catches the essential meaning and expresses it in natural idiomatic English.

On the other hand, Google Translate bungled it with this more literal attempt:

![Screenshot 2026-05-05 3.59.25 PM.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/hirohurl/23tmm5sZEzidmzk5Tnv9PA74bHZz8qoNAhwpVbGeGve7Y6SMi44h2AzRPFmbrGmHqR25R.png)

Google Translate seems to have mistranslated the first \

(it depends, just in case), and translated the second part of the proverb more accurately to come up with a sentence that sounds natural, but is off the mark.

So, once again, Chatgpt beats Google Translate.

For my final translation, I feel like channelling the Corsican Upstart, who once is said to have said:

> Si vous voulez prendre Vienne, prenez Vienne.
> If you would take Vienna, take Vienna.

And so,

> If you would take care, take care.

Well, it is not quite right, but then neither was Napoleon.

Well, however you choose to translate it, as a karuta proverb, it neatly illustrates the educational purpose of the deck. A child learning the kana **ね** is at the same time being taught a practical virtue: caution, diligence, and thoroughness.

It is also worth noting that while this proverb appears in the more culturally traditional Angel deck I am using for this series, it differs from the proverb chosen for **ね** in the more popular Daiso deck, which I will discuss in my next post on the *Iroha Karuta*.

For now, though, **念には念を入れよ** stands as an excellent example of how the karuta taught not only language, but also habits of mind and conduct considered worthy of admiration in Japan.

Cheers!

DH

links.title: The Racial System Relies On Egos
links.body: In 2026 America's polarized racial climate, being mixed-race feels more humorous than anything else. Having skipped the era of genuine violent tensions gives a clarifying distance: people routinely sensationalize their experiences, turning bullshit into existential drama.\n\nRacial prejudice still exists. However, social media has inflated egos to the point where likes and views are mistaken for intellectual validation. The emotional clumsiness that surfaces in these conversations has little to do with one-sided \

—a meme that writes itself—and everything to do with plain ignorance.
The answer is clear: drop the performance and confront reality without the filters.

Without bullshit, the system crumbles.

body.title: Women by Nature: We All Need Love, Care, and Affection
body.body:
Women, by nature, are deeply emotional and sensitive beings. Just like we cannot live without food or air, we cannot truly thrive without love, care, and affection. These aren’t just nice-to-have things, they are essential for our happiness and well-being.
 https://img.leopedia.io/DQmeUKR7PojWdEfoZPDZVbRH4nQFpQWKD6pgKwHtN4uLoKe/1000211657.jpg 

[Pixabay](https://pixabay.com/illustrations/women-sisterhood-support-friendship-7913460/)

From the moment we are born, care and love shape our world. A mother’s hug, a father’s kind words, or the support of family and friends teaches us that being loved matters. This early care doesn’t just make us feel safe, but it helps us grow into women who can love and care for others in return.

As we grow older, this need for love doesn’t disappear, rather it only becomes more important. Women are naturally empathetic and sensitive. We notice the feelings of those around us and often put others’ needs before our own. But we also need to feel seen, valued, and cared for. Without it, even the strongest woman can feel lonely or drained. Love and affection give us energy, confidence, and the courage to face challenges. They help us be the best versions of ourselves.

It’s important to understand that this need isn’t limited to romantic relationships. Women crave love and care from everyone in our lives, family, friends, and even colleagues. A simple word of encouragement, a thoughtful gesture, or just someone listening sincerely can make a huge difference. These small acts feed our hearts and minds in ways that material things never can.

When women feel loved and appreciated, we flourish. We become more resilient, more creative, and more compassionate. But when the emotional support is missing, it’s easy to feel drained or undervalued, no matter how much we achieve in life. Love, care, and affection are not weaknesses, they are our fuel.

Let not forget that every woman deserves to feel nurtured and appreciated. But know that because love and care are as essential for us does not make it a sign of fragility, it’s a recognition of our humanity. When women are supported emotionally, they not only shine in their own lives but also uplift the people around them.

So, let’s remember, a little love, a little care, and a little attention can go a long way. For women, these things aren’t just nice, they are life.

It also leans hard on capital preservation — the “no capital loss” argument is the cleanest part of the pitch — while creating a measurable, easy-to-track outcome around HIVE locked, HBD earned, and proposal efficiency, which is exactly why proposals like this get attention in [DHF value-plan discussions](https://hive.blog/dhf/@threespeak/how-to-reduce-hives-inflation-problem-our-new-dhf-proposal-voting-criteria-hbd-apr-and-a-proposed-value-plan-sop). The weak spot, honestly, is that strength #5 cuts both ways: it’s financially elegant, but voters still need to believe the proposal helps Hive more than simply funding builders directly, and that debate shows up a lot in broader [HBD/DHF analysis](https://inleo.io/@dalz/hbd-in-2026-supply-slightly-down-dhf-payouts-dominant-and-hive-absorbing-the-pressure).

body.title: Time and patience.
body.body:
Time and patience. I don't know if patience depends on time, or time on patience, but I do know that often, I lack both, lol. Yes, I'm filled with a certain envy for people who have the patience for long experiments, or, for example, who can devote several years to working on a drawing. That's not the case with me; everything has to be done quickly, in the shortest possible time. Even when I go mushroom picking in the forest, or when I used to go hunting, I tried to get what I wanted as quickly as possible and return home with my catch. Being quick didn't always mean the quality was low, but patience is something you need to learn, although sometimes it's hard to tell whether patience is justified or not. [![1aDSC06063.png](https://cdn.steemitimages.com/DQmPuyPs9sdrsPxyJwSc4pX4Q4hUHr693AwExqPDnvEbeNg/1aDSC06063.png)](https://steemitimages.com/p/6VvuHGsoU2QBt9MXeXNdDuyd4Bmd63j7zJymDTWgdcJjnzfMn17ecM5NV6tdQ91CbqLca1QtkVvp2miiucr4aYyo5hXCShfNsKdPDUmPh9p5ct8Dx2seYHQ1D3ZuNv?mode=fit&format=match&width=640) ![image](https://waivio.nyc3.digitaloceanspaces.com/6ca808abccb50a65c5eec8b947664980de5e5983b7828388921739ae38251fe4) In mushroom growing, patience is also a valuable asset. It's one thing to wait a month for an oyster mushroom harvest, but it's quite another to succumb to the temptation to grow wild mushrooms in your own garden. Producers of such mushroom mycelium claim you'll have to wait about four years, which is a hefty wait. Although, if you plant a fruit tree seedling, you'll have to wait the same amount of time for a harvest. Trees are understandable, but mushrooms are. Furthermore, some renowned mycologists claim that wild mushroom mycelium, for which you'll pay a pretty penny, is a scam, as each mushroom species has its own unique relationships, connections, and symbioses with forest vegetation, making it extremely difficult, if not impossible, to achieve in a garden plot. ![1aDSC06080.png](https://cdn.steemitimages.com/DQmXp7XbAL7Xb1dfLz6yvPCUDdzH2xtJPZv77w3CzgScDZG/1aDSC06080.png) ![image](https://waivio.nyc3.digitaloceanspaces.com/0da1a44bf68ff20d47c6557a6e81f1a123bb747c380cbef991b6fc3a53df6199) That's why I try to treat many experiments like a cake: eat it, enjoy it, and move on :) ![1aer024.png](https://cdn.steemitimages.com/DQmcQZFYQvwnWRpYigf88SHYR1YTWjZHyhN9t1R5WsA1F4D/1aer024.png) ![image](https://waivio.nyc3.digitaloceanspaces.com/5a94454d3cb59af8fd8ce7c7bb0ef07809b1d8f74cad6beb2f3d72d76373b55a) *** Below you can see my containers with data that I collect in INLEO and always have quick access to them it is very convenient. ## Statistical language models: n-grams
```

Before neural networks dominated NLP, language models counted word sequences in large text corpora. An **n-gram model** estimates the probability of a word based on the previous n-1 words:

- **Unigram** (n=1): `P(word)` based on overall word frequency. No context whatsoever.
- **Bigram** (n=2): `P(word | previous_word)`. \

```python
import random

def generate_from_bigram(model, start_word, n_words=15):
    current = start_word
    result = [current]
    for _ in range(n_words):
        if current not in model:
            break
        next_words = model[current]
        words = list(next_words.keys())
        probs = list(next_words.values())
        current = random.choices(words, weights=probs, k=1)[0]
        result.append(current)
    return ' '.join(result)
```

N-gram models dominated NLP for decades. They're fast, they're interpretable, and they work reasonably well for short-range patterns. Speech recognition systems in the 2000s relied heavily on trigram models. But they have fundamental limitations that no amount of data can fix:

**Sparsity**: most n-grams never appear in the training data. Even a corpus of 1 billion words can't cover all reasonable 5-word sequences. There are simply too many possible combinations. Smoothing techniques (adding small counts to unseen n-grams) help, but they're band-aids on a fundamental problem.

**No generalization**: an n-gram model that has seen \

-- the model doesn't know they're both animals.\n\n**Fixed context window**: a trigram uses exactly 2 previous words. But consider this sentence: \

. You need context from 20+ words back to make a good prediction here. No practical n-gram model can capture this (a 20-gram model would need impossibly large training data).

## Neural language models: the paradigm shift

Neural language models solve all three problems by representing words as dense vectors (**embeddings**) rather than discrete symbols. We covered embeddings back in episode #31 -- now you'll see exactly why they matter so much.

**No sparsity**: in stead of storing counts for every possible n-gram, a neural model learns a continuous function that maps any context to a probability distribution over next words. It can assign meaningful probabilities to sequences it has literally never seen, because it operates in continuous space. The function interpolates between training examples.

**Generalization**: because \
develop similar embeddings (they appear in similar contexts during training -- \

. Similar embeddings produce similar outputs. This is a direct consequence of the distributional hypothesis we discussed in episode #31.

**Variable context**: a transformer language model attends to ALL previous tokens (up to its context window length). That president sentence from 20 words ago? Self-attention connects it directly to the current prediction position. No fixed window -- every position can attend to every earlier position.

The architecture is exactly what we built in episode #56: a **decoder-only transformer**. The input is a sequence of tokens, and the output at each position is a probability distribution over the entire vocabulary for what the next token should be. The causal mask ensures each position can only see earlier positions -- exactly the autoregressive constraint that language modeling requires.

Let's build a simple neural language model to make this concrete:

```python

import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

class SimpleNeuralLM(nn.Module):
    \

def __init__(self, vocab_size, d_embed=64, context_size=5, d_hidden=128):
        super().__init__()
        self.context_size = context_size
        self.embedding = nn.Embedding(vocab_size, d_embed)
        self.fc1 = nn.Linear(context_size * d_embed, d_hidden)
        self.fc2 = nn.Linear(d_hidden, d_hidden)
        self.out = nn.Linear(d_hidden, vocab_size)

    def forward(self, x):
        # x shape: (batch, context_size) -- token indices
        emb = self.embedding(x)            # (batch, context_size, d_embed)
        emb = emb.view(x.size(0), -1)     # (batch, context_size * d_embed)
        h = F.relu(self.fc1(emb))
        h = F.relu(self.fc2(h))
        logits = self.out(h)               # (batch, vocab_size)
        return logits
```

## Perplexity: measuring language model quality

How do you measure whether a language model is good? You can't just check accuracy (\
) because language is inherently stochastic -- many words could validly follow any given context. \
has dozens of legitimate continuations.\n\n**Perplexity** is the standard metric. It measures how \

the model is by test data on average. Formally:

```
PPL = exp( -1/N * sum( log P(w_t | context) ) )
```

Intuition: if the model assigns probability 1.0 to every actual next token, the perplexity is 1 (perfect, zero surprise). If it's choosing uniformly among 100 options at each step, the perplexity is 100. Lower is better -- it means the model is less \

by the data.

```python
import math

def compute_perplexity(model, data_tokens, context_size):
    \

model.eval()
    total_log_prob = 0
    n_predictions = 0

    with torch.no_grad():
        for i in range(context_size, len(data_tokens)):
            context = data_tokens[i - context_size:i].unsqueeze(0)
            logits = model(context)
            probs = F.softmax(logits, dim=-1)
            target = data_tokens[i].item()
            prob = probs[0, target].item()

            if prob > 0:
                total_log_prob += math.log(prob)
            else:
                total_log_prob += math.log(1e-10)  # avoid log(0)
            n_predictions += 1

    avg_log_prob = total_log_prob / n_predictions
    perplexity = math.exp(-avg_log_prob)
    return perplexity

# With a transformer model (from episode #56):
def compute_transformer_perplexity(model, data, block_size=64):
    \

model.eval()
    total_loss = 0
    total_tokens = 0

    with torch.no_grad():
        for i in range(0, len(data) - block_size - 1, block_size):
            x = data[i:i + block_size].unsqueeze(0)
            y = data[i + 1:i + block_size + 1].unsqueeze(0)
            logits = model(x)
            if isinstance(logits, tuple):
                logits = logits[0]
            loss = F.cross_entropy(
                logits.view(-1, logits.size(-1)),
                y.view(-1)
            )
            total_loss += loss.item() * block_size
            total_tokens += block_size

    avg_loss = total_loss / total_tokens
    return math.exp(avg_loss)
```

## The scaling hypothesis

One of the most consequential empirical findings in AI: language model performance improves predictably with scale. More parameters, more data, more compute leads to lower loss. And not in some vague handwavy way -- it follows precise mathematical relationships called **scaling laws**.

In 2020, Kaplan et al. at OpenAI published a paper showing that language model loss follows power laws in three variables:

- **N** (parameters): Loss ~ N^(-0.076)
- **D** (dataset size): Loss ~ D^(-0.095)
- **C** (compute budget): Loss ~ C^(-0.050)

The **Chinchilla scaling laws** (Hoffmann et al., 2022) refined this further, showing that many early large models were actually undertrained. The optimal balance is roughly: scale parameters and training tokens at the same rate. A 70B parameter model trained on 1.4 trillion tokens (Chinchilla) outperformed a 280B parameter model trained on 300 billion tokens (Gopher). More data, properly matched to model size, beats raw parameter count.

The scaling hypothesis goes even further: as models scale, they develop **emergent abilities** -- capabilities that appear to not exist in smaller models and then suddenly work at a certain scale. Few-shot learning (learning from examples in the prompt without updating parameters) emerged around GPT-3's scale (~175B parameters). Whether these abilities are truly discontinuous or just cross a usefulness threshold on a smooth curve is debated among researchers. But the practical implication is clear: bigger models can do things smaller ones simply cannot.

## Vocabulary size tradeoffs

The choice of vocabulary size creates a fundamental tension that every model designer must navigate:

**Small vocabulary** (1K-10K tokens): each token is a common character or short subword. Sequences become long -- the model needs more positions to represent the same text. The context window fills up faster. But the embedding table is small and every single token gets plenty of training data, so each embedding is well-learned.

**Large vocabulary** (50K-200K tokens): many full words get their own dedicated token. Sequences are shorter (more efficient use of context window). A 4000-word article might be 3000 tokens with a small vocab but only 1500 tokens with a large one. But the embedding table is massive and rare tokens (obscure technical terms, foreign words) may appear only a handful of times in training, so their embeddings are poorly learned.

Modern models typically land on 30K-100K tokens. GPT-4's ~100K vocabulary handles most English words as single tokens, plus common multi-word code patterns (\

## Putting it together: from n-grams to transformers

Let me make the connection explicit. The evolution from statistical to neural language models mirrors the evolution we traced through this entire series:

1. **N-grams** (1980s-2000s): count word sequences. Fast but sparse, no generalization, fixed context. Like a lookup table.

2. **Feed-forward neural LMs** (Bengio, 2003): embed words as vectors, predict next word from fixed context window through a neural network. Generalizes via embeddings but still fixed context.

3. **RNN/LSTM language models** (2010-2017): process tokens sequentially, maintain hidden state that theoretically captures unbounded context. In practice limited by vanishing gradients and sequential processing. We built these in episodes #48-49.

4. **Transformer language models** (2017-present): attend to all previous tokens in parallel. Unbounded context (within window), no sequential bottleneck, scales well on modern hardware. This is what powers everything today.

Each step solved specific limitations of the previous approach. The transformer didn't appear from nowhere -- it solved the parallelization and long-range dependency problems that made RNNs impractical at scale. And the key realization that drove the LLM revolution: once you have a good enough architecture (transformers) and a good enough objective (next-token prediction), you can scale it up and emergent capabilites appear without being explicitly programmed.

## What this means for the rest of Arc 4

Everything in this arc builds on what we covered today. Language modeling is the **pre-training objective** -- the task that teaches a model about language before it ever sees an instruction or a conversation. The model learns grammar, facts, reasoning patterns, code syntax, and world knowledge, all from the single task of predicting the next token on internet-scale text data.

The questions that drive the rest of this arc are:

- How do you design a model architecture specifically optimized for language modeling? (decoder-only transformers, the GPT family)
- What happens when you train an encoder model with a different objective? (masked language modeling, BERT)
- How do you scale training to trillions of tokens across thousands of GPUs?
- How do you turn a raw next-token predictor into something that follows instructions and behaves helpfully? (instruction tuning, alignment)
- How do you use these models effectively through APIs and prompting?

The foundation is in place. The transformer predicts the next token. Everything that follows is about making that predictor bigger, training it on more data, and then teaching it to be useful.

## Did it click? Let's check

- A language model assigns probabilities to sequences: P(next_token | all_previous_tokens). That's the entire foundation.
- N-gram models count word sequences but suffer from sparsity, zero generalization, and fixed context windows -- fundamental limitations that no amount of data fixes.
- Neural language models solve all three problems through continuous embeddings and learned functions over those embeddings.
- Perplexity measures how surprised the model is by test data. Lower = better. But low perplexity alone does not mean the model is useful -- it's a necessary but not sufficient condition.
- Scaling laws show predictable power-law improvement with model size, data, and compute. The Chinchilla insight: balance parameters and training tokens, don't just scale one.
- Subword tokenization (BPE, WordPiece, SentencePiece) balances vocabulary coverage with sequence efficiency. Most models use 30K-100K tokens.
- Tokenization artifacts (token boundaries, multi-char tokens, inconsistent number splits) affect model capabilities in subtle but real ways.
- The evolution from n-grams to transformers is the same trajectory we traced through this whole series: from discrete counts to continuous functions, from fixed to adaptive, from sequential to parallel.

## Exercises

**Exercise 1:** Build a complete trigram language model with Laplace smoothing. Train it on a paragraph of text, compute its perplexity on a held-out sentence, and generate 5 random sentences from it. Compare the perplexity and output quality to an unsmoothed bigram model.

**Exercise 2:** Implement BPE from scratch as a class with `train(text, n_merges)`, `encode(text)`, and `decode(ids)` methods. Train it on a few paragraphs of English text with 200 merges. Then tokenize the sentence \

and show how many tokens it produces at different vocabulary sizes (50, 100, 200 merges).

**Exercise 3:** Take the transformer model from episode #56, train it on a text corpus, and compute perplexity on a held-out test set (use the last 10% of the data). Then vary the model size (number of layers: 2, 4, 6, 8) and plot perplexity vs parameter count. Does it follow the predicted power-law scaling?

### Thanks for reading, see you in the next one!

The biggest strength of this card is its magic damage that cannot be easily blocked by normal armor or defense. As a result, it often becomes very effective in situations where other cards are not so successful. When talking about the good aspects of this card, the first thing to mention is its reliable damage output. It usually attacks safely from the backline and consistently weakens the opponent. It can also coordinate well with other cards in the team especially when you are using a strategy where you want to gradually defeat the opponent. This card can often play an important role towards the end of the match. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmcZZwPDMyBUVz4rHWHeQEwFzuuvPkpBXTAHckDphWVZAu/image.png) However, Water-Lagged Wizard also has some limitations that are important to keep in mind. Its health and defense are not very strong, which can easily make it an easy target for the opponent. Especially if the opponent has snipers or fast attacking units, this card can be quickly out. Therefore, proper positioning and support are very important when using this card. All in all, an effective and strategic magic card that can make your team much stronger if used correctly. It is especially useful for those who want to ensure victory by weakening the opponent through magic damage. body.title: Some Kind Of Wonderful (1987) Is One Of The Most Underrated Teen Films Of The Eighties. It Has The Heart Of A John Hughes Story, But With A Little More Edge And A Lot More Emotion.
body.body:
Released in 1987 and directed by Howard Deutch, Some Kind of Wonderful often gets overshadowed by bigger John Hughes titles like The Breakfast Club and Pretty in Pink, but it absolutely deserves to be mentioned alongside them. Written by Hughes, the film takes familiar teen movie territory and gives it a sharper emotional honesty.

![IMG_1165.webp](https://images.hive.blog/DQmfFDqt4EBTHC5vNJKbWEPReVUPUBATADVyXYeQ6y39zGA/IMG_1165.webp)

The story follows Keith Nelson, played by Eric Stoltz, a smart but working class high school student who develops a crush on Amanda Jones, the beautiful and popular girl who seems far out of reach. Keith decides to take his shot, even though nearly everyone around him thinks it is a bad idea.

Lea Thompson plays Amanda with far more depth than the typical “popular girl” role would suggest. She is not simply shallow or unreachable. Thompson gives her vulnerability and self awareness, making Amanda feel like a real person rather than a stereotype.

Then there is Mary Stuart Masterson as Watts, one of the best characters in any eighties teen film. Watts is Keith’s best friend, drummer, and the person who understands him better than anyone else. Masterson gives the role attitude, humor, and emotional depth, making it impossible not to root for her.

The real heart of the movie is not the obvious romance, but the emotional tension between Keith and Watts. He is chasing an ideal while completely missing what is right in front of him. That dynamic gives the film its emotional weight and makes it much stronger than a standard high school romance.

Craig Sheffer plays Hardy Jenns, Amanda’s controlling ex boyfriend, bringing just enough arrogance and menace to keep the stakes real. His presence reminds you that the movie is also about class, reputation, and the pressure teenagers feel to fit into social expectations.

Howard Deutch directs the film with a strong sense of intimacy. He does not rely on flashy scenes or exaggerated comedy. Instead, he lets the emotions sit where they need to. The quieter moments often hit harder than the dramatic ones.

John Hughes’ writing is what gives the movie its staying power. He always understood that teenage emotions feel huge because, in that moment, they are huge. The script respects that instead of mocking it. It treats heartbreak, insecurity, and self discovery like they actually matter.

The soundtrack also deserves praise because, like most Hughes related films, music becomes part of the identity of the movie. The songs capture that late eighties emotional energy perfectly and help define the tone.

What makes Some Kind of Wonderful stand out is how grounded it feels. It is not overly polished or cartoonish. The characters feel like real teenagers making messy choices rather than movie versions of them.

Watts especially became iconic because she broke the mold. She was not written as the glamorous obvious choice. She was tough, funny, loyal, and emotionally honest. For a lot of viewers, she became the character people remembered most long after the credits rolled.

The final act works because it earns its emotional payoff. The movie understands that growing up often means realizing you were chasing the wrong thing. It is not just about getting the date. It is about understanding yourself.

Over time, the film has gained more appreciation as people revisit it outside the shadow of Hughes’ bigger hits. Many now see it as one of the strongest examples of his writing because it feels less manufactured and more sincere.

In the end, Some Kind of Wonderful is an excellent film because it combines romance, heartbreak, and character growth without losing its authenticity. It is funny, emotional, and honest in a way that still connects decades later.

![IMG_1164.webp](https://images.hive.blog/DQmTnbVe7o88TQFsFwFrC1q7FJuWaYLJxGYfAdMghjVwKeq/IMG_1164.webp)

It may not always get the same spotlight as other eighties classics, but for many people, it is one of the best of them all.

body.body:
<liketuimages>
<center>
![lcohgL3VULonjTnY_IMG_20260504_164012.webp](https://cdn.liketu.com/media/trina77/images/lcohgL3VULonjTnY_IMG_20260504_164012/lcohgL3VULonjTnY_IMG_20260504_164012.webp)
![61TazfghX4kqAjJG_IMG_20260504_163945.webp](https://cdn.liketu.com/media/trina77/images/61TazfghX4kqAjJG_IMG_20260504_163945/61TazfghX4kqAjJG_IMG_20260504_163945.webp)
![6FrRH6CKdNA4ruah_IMG_20260504_163943.webp](https://cdn.liketu.com/media/trina77/images/6FrRH6CKdNA4ruah_IMG_20260504_163943/6FrRH6CKdNA4ruah_IMG_20260504_163943.webp)
</center>
</liketuimages>

由于我的领导客户没有提前预约八一纪念馆和江西省博物馆的门票，官方渠道早已约满，就连滕王阁的门票也全部售罄了。
 
情急之下我又想到了闲鱼，之前订海世界门票就是走的这个渠道，性价比很不错。想着这类免费参观场馆没约上，说不定闲鱼上也能找到预约的办法。
 
最先咨询的一家，报价一人六十元，两个人就得一百二十元。场馆本身都是免费开放的，额外花这笔钱，着实觉得不太划算。可领导难得过来一趟，总不能连人家想去的景点都安排不上，心里左右为难。
 
就在我准备下单的时候，继续翻看找到了更实惠的店家，一人只收二十元，性价比一下子就上来了。当即敲定下来，两张门票一共花费四十元，同行的孩子身高不足一米四，符合免票标准，不用额外花钱。搞定之后，我第一时间把好消息告知了客户一字不提花钱的事。
 
紧接着我又着手预订滕王阁门票，每张比官网原价贵了十元，单张六十元，两张一共一百二十元。忙活许久，总算把两处景点的预约全部安排妥当。随后我又问了江西省博物馆的门票，卖滕王阁门票的黄牛告知我说没预约上不要紧，临时到现场的自助机上预约就能进。

一家三口2日下午一点半抵达南昌，我提前等候迎接。原本规划好行程，先前往八一纪念馆参观，傍晚再去滕王阁。客户想傍晚五点左右进滕王阁，这个时间段夕阳西下，刚好能亲眼见证“落霞与孤鹜齐飞，秋水共长天一色”的绝美景致，这是唯一的有备而来呢！
 
算上接站等候与路上行程，我们赶到纪念馆大概要两点多，时间本就比较紧张，但为了满足大家的心愿，我还是尽力配合安排。
 
万万没想到意外突然发生，我刚接上客人行驶在路上，闲鱼商家突然发来消息，说5月2日当天游客数量爆满，下午无法安排入园，只能等到晚上才能进去。不知是否真实总之是遇上不靠谱的商家，被骗了。
 
我们已经在去往场馆的路上，临时告知无法入园，实在让人措手不及。商家没有过多解释，直接原路退回了费用。事已至此别无他法，我只好如实把突发状况告诉客户，临时更改出行路线。

2日没有预约上，3日又有别的安排，我就计划排到4日他们出发这天去纪念馆。“神奇的咸鱼”再一次验证了它的神奇。

我担心遇上和上次一样不靠谱的商家，这次找了导游，配上导游讲解两个人150元，果断订下。


---

body.title: The Power of Sacrifice: How Others Shape Our Journey in Life.
body.body: There are lots of times we need to think and reflect about our lives. What we want to do and why we have gotten into the current state and position we are in. One thing I want us all to know is that when thinking about what we have done in life or what we have been able to acquire in life at the current stage we are at. Just know that there has always been something that is very paramount in life, which is that someone has given up their own self for you to become what you are today. There is a saying that says that a tree doesn't make a forest. Without a tree in a bush, no way a forest can be made.\n\n

>Source When we were young, our parents asked us questions about what we wanted to become, and one thing they did for the serious parents was that they made sure they followed our dreams accordingly and guided us so that we could be able to acquire these dreams we had in mind. Some parents even go as far as giving up their own dreams for their children's to come to fruition because they believe their children can still do better if they give them the chance. Alot of people do underestimate the power of a parent, and besides, not just parents but those that stood by you and gave up their lives for you to become a reputable person in the world. Take, for instance, some people who pursue a career of becoming a better version of themselves, like those who become a lawyer, doctor, and so on. Sometimes, their parents might not be financially buoyant enough to foot the bills of those careers, but what they will do is pause their own career and allow their children or younger ones to go forward. I got the inspiration for this post from a video I saw this morning. What does the video say? There was a water burst on the highway, and lots of vehicles and motorcycles were passing, and no one could hold the water back to allow people to pass freely. But there was this large truck that went to park right in front of the water pipe and ensured that he blocked the water pipe pressure so that others could pass through and be free without getting injured. I imagined this case, and I thought within myself that amongst all that were passing, why is it just a man that went to sacrifice his time and energy? Normally, the vehicle driver will surely have urgencies to attend to, but he was just assured that he could help in his own little way and not that if he had not waited, something was going to happen to him. Plus, he had a better chance of escaping the water burst, but he just decided to save some lives at his own expense. This is just life and him helping others to be safe. In everything we do, we should not only think about ourselves alone in some cases. We should think about others too because a little help can go a long way in people's lives. And always remember that just a person sacrifice can make a way for others to become who they want to become in life. body.title: Танцювальні рухи Трампа під пісню Y.M.C.A. - не випадкові
body.body:
Всі вже мабуть звикли до чудасій президента США Трампа. Присвоєння собі світових досягнень інших входить до його промов завжди. І часто проявляється досить несподівано для авторів. Як-от сталося нещодавно із танцювальними рухами Трампа на мітингах.

Як повідомляє Billboard, Президент США Дональд Трамп стверджує, що його танцювальні рухи під пісню Y.M.C.A. гурту Village People сприяли поверненню цієї композиції до чартів Billboard.
Так, 1 травня цього року Трамп сказав таке [під час виступу](https://twitter.com/i/status/2050663567922192523) в містечку Вілледжес у Флориді. Історія треку ж така: хіт 1970-х років очолив чарт Billboard Top Dance/Electronic Digital Song Sales ще наприкінці 2024 року, через понад чотири десятиліття після його випуску. Трамп же переплутав все на світі і заявив, що
32 роки тому пісня була на 5-му місці, а тепер піднялася на перше. І трималася на першому місці протягом кількох місяців, завдяки його  передвиборчій кампанії.
Автор пісні Віктор Вілліс вважає, що ця танцювальна мелодія лише \

у плані продажів та позицій у чартах, відколи Трамп почав використовувати її у своїй кампанії. Бо з самого початку існування, після виходу в кінці 1978 року пісня Y.M.C.A. піднялася на друге місце в чарті Billboard Hot 100.\n\nТрамп також назвав незаслужено цю пісню \
, проти чого вже висловився її автор. Сам Трамп розповідає всюди, що його дружина Меланія не любить його реакції на Y.M.C.A. під час виступів: \

.
І от знову, нещодавно, виступаючи зі зверненням в будинку для пенсіонерів Флориди, Трамп закрутив стегнами і помахав кулаками під пісню Y.M.C.A.

body.title: Are We Financially Responsible To Other People?(Part 2)//The Old Path.
body.body: https://youtu.be/aHC7rhMHhZc?si=O9bimLajrrUiPcwm\n\nMost people often ask this question whenever they encounter or meet those who are begging for money, food and other things. But the answer to this question is \

we are financially responsible for the welfare of others.

As christians, it is part of our obligation to look into the welfare of our brethren. We were taught by our Lord Jesus Christ always to assist those in need whenever we are in the position to do that. Most people think that it's only when they have everything in excess that's when they will render help to those in need, but the bible made us to understand that we can assist our brethren with the little we have by sharing it in love with the needy.

body.body:
https://img.leopedia.io/DQmSmeHjXH354bXiQnpjz7RDa8KcUWkYzgTd2PE2tGAMtQK/Gemini_Generated_Image_h3h1sgh3h1sgh3h1.png 
image generated using Gemini AI


Before I entered a higher institution, I never knew what it meant to hustle; everything I had ever spent was provided to me by my parents, and sometimes we got gifts from visitors or during celebrations. This was so because my parents completely frowned upon it. They will claim that if we start earning money early in life, it will discourage us from completing our schooling, since the reason we were in school in the first place was to make money. As such, my father saw to it that I never learned any skill or craft before graduation.

Side hustle simply means something one could do on the side to make a living. This is to say that for someone to have a side hustle, one must have full-time activities that occupies his/her time. It was in my second year that some friends introduced me to the idea of engaging in an activity for the purpose of earning wages for the first time in my life. My friend Mesh, who was a chemistry student then, told me about waiting on tables at weddings on weekends, since I was not really in it for the money. What he used to lure me was when he said that food was going to be in excess, and we would get as many drinks as we wanted after the event.

The amount we were paid was two thousand naira, but we will have to use about six hundred naira for transport, leaving us with one thousand four hundred. It was my first earning in my life, and I felt like I was a grown-up because of the earnings I made. After the first time, I kind of enjoyed the work because it lets me go to the town every weekend, and I was assured of eating different varieties of meals and drinking different varieties of drinks, even the ones I never knew existed.

body.title: My Entry for Reflection Hunters Contest SMARP
body.body:
Hello friends!

Today, I used a forest road to go to a village.
In fact, I could have used a car-road to go to that village.
However, there were sometimes some terrorist soldiers on the car-road, so I took a detour to avoid meeting them.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmfXzBXKWPn8s7hE2uRMkRVvd44kXFLQVBWfTEKAqtm8J7/img_20260504_075101.jpg)

I saw a natural pond on a forest trail I visited.
It was a pond that had collected rainwater from the previous week.
Trees were growing on the edge of the pond, creating reflections on the water's surface.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmRbnqZ67pjiwgEBffHAXA4HKJksuPiJbLGKjDdRT6LC2y/img_20260504_075118.jpg)

So I stopped my motorcycle, turned on my phone camera, and took some photos.
That's why I was able to participate in this week's Reflection Hunters Contest.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmPHL4jkXzLPuLymys8YakmBxouqwuixHKkHSiW8JEqKqd/img_20260504_075044.jpg)

မင်္ဂလာပါ မိတ်ဆွေတို့ရေ။

ယနေ့ ကျေးရွာတစ်ရွာသို့ သွားရာ တောလမ်းကို အသုံးပြုခဲ့သည်။
တကယ်တော့ ထိုကျေးရွာသို့ ကားလမ်းကို အသုံးပြု၍ သွားလို့ရပါသည်။
သို့ပေ့မယ့် ကားလမ်း တနေရာ၌ အကြမ်းဖက်စစ်သားအချို့ ရှိနေတတ်သောကြောင့် ကျွန်တော်သည် ထိုသူတွေနှင့် မတွေ့ရန် တောလမ်းမှ ရှောင်ကွင်းသွားခြင်း ဖြစ်သည်။

ကျွန်တော် သွားရောက်ခဲ့သည့် တောလမ်းတနေရာ၌ သဘာဝရေအိုင်တစ်ခုကို တွေ့မြင်ခဲ့ရသည်။
လွန်ခဲ့သော ရက်သတ္တပတ်အတွင်း ရွာချခဲ့သော မိုးရေများ စုမိနေသော ရေအိုင် ဖြစ်ပါသည်။
ထိုရေအိုင် နဘေး၌ သစ်ပင်များ ပေါက်နေကြသည်ဖြစ်ရာ ရေမျက်နှာပြင်၌ အလင်းပြန်ပုံရိပ်များ ကျရောက်နေကြသည်။
